Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!

Yields down across the curve by about 6bps while oil is down about 10% - long dated contracts have also moved for crude - contributing to the discourse that the war in Iran may finally be nearing the end of this theatre. 

In pre market trading - semis are down ALOT - SNDK near 1k, MU firmly below 800s, NBIS at 135, NVDA at 196, CRWV meanwhile seems to slowing its descent. Overnight, Citrini also wrote that the blindly long semis trade is over - jk. He had more nuance - essentially recommending some pair trades like Long ORCL/ short NBIS. Long META short GOOG etc.

China tech - i noted that yesterday could be a turning point for $BABA - it is up 10% now - one of the strongest moves in a while.  If we get further policy action in china, this could mark a very strong reversal. Valuations across chinese names are at all time lows.

My thoughts on semis is that, sentiment wise - there are alot of trapped longs. The likely way a V rebound happens if we get a painful clearing event, otherwise rebounds will be capped by sellers willing to get out near breakeven. The only other way is via company buybacks - but currently the only names capable of pulling such a move is $MU into the expiration of the CHIPS act prohibition (9 Dec)

Yesterday's market dynamic was quite a sight to see - with hypers ripping 10% while semis dumped 10% - most people point to politics as a driver - that there will be roadblocks to new DC constructions in the USA. Hence this makes pre-existing chips way more valuable - which the hypers own. Tradfi is also recognising that gpu rentals are up - with H100 up 26% y.oy (i thought these things were supposed to depreciate? lmao) and GB200 up 50%. $ORCL also reports 98% AI infra utilisation and a 20% renewal/resale premium....

Likewise - Citrini's note echos the fear - saying that we have reached peak capex "growth" - looking at the second derivative - future growth would likely be slower - this doesnt mean capex stops, just that capex growth decelerates... The tension then comes up in how semis are priced - personally i see the opportunity on the long side - when growth gets priced to zero - any upside surprises provides fresh momentum for the stock.

In terms of what i am doing, many of the names i am looking for are closing in on where i see value. It does not mean that the stock will bottom there, it could potentially continue to fall. But you got to risk it for the biscuit. 

In crypto - $BTC showed tremendous strength - $ZEC held on to its gains and added further gains. The tail wind for crypto is now back to its original purpose - money away from the government. Especially we look set to have a government that is more hostile to crypto. Policy pain provides further growth to the crypto thesis, policy support decays the supporter core.

Good luck!

text:
How many times have you seen a mouse study claiming that a therapeutic works, and the survival curve looks like this? Broken axis, 6% difference in survival time, but the P value is < 0.05 and it's claimed as a positive result. It's not. In my 15 years of prion science, I have learned to look past such claims almost instantly. Yet sometimes these claims still lead to high-profile publications, millions of dollars in funding, and even to therapies being tested clinically. In this new blog post I release data on 301 untreated control animals from our last 9 years of in vivo studies, model out the various ways that P values can appear significant even when the result is null, and put into words the intuition I've built up as to which claims are believable and which are not.

text:
没想道anthropic内部还在研究ZK和LLM的结合，LLM模型可证明推理。

主要是目前LLM的一些问题：
-用户无法确认自己调用的模型就是声称的那个模型。
-可能存在：路由服务为省钱偷偷换成更便宜的模型
-攻击者篡改 token 流
-内部把更强模型伪装成较弱模型运行
-只靠输出质量很难判断。

这类问题在中转站上更是常见。

解决方案：Provable Inference（可证明推理）：
使用 zkSNARK（零知识简洁非交互式知识论证），让模型提供方：
-离线阶段：对模型权重做承诺（commitment），生成一个短指纹，绑定特定权重，但不泄露权重本身。

-在线阶段：每次回复都附带一个简短的密码学证明（proof）。

-验证：任何人用普通 CPU 在几秒内就能验证「这个回复确实是由承诺的那个模型对给定 prompt 生成的」，且证明过程不泄露任何权重信息。

如果回复不是来自承诺的模型，验证会失败。

Anthropic 开源了一个高性能原型 FlashProve：
-针对 Llama 4 Maverick（约 400B 参数 MoE 模型，4-bit 量化，整数算术）
-单张 H100 GPU 证明速度约 110 tokens/秒（prefill）

详细的技术报告：https://t.co/xDL1NlJeLK

text:
Arthur Hayes: AI Giants’ Equity Dilution May Pressure Stock Prices, Bearish for Bitcoin in the Short Term, Bullish if Central Banks Step In Long Term

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes said in his latest article “D is for Dilution” that large-scale share unlocks and equity dilution after IPOs of AI giants such as SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI could pressure their stock prices and raise debt financing costs across the AI industry. He estimates that early IPO investors in Anthropic could face up to 83% equity dilution by June 2027.

Hayes believes that a decline in AI stock prices could weaken bank credit expansion, leading to a contraction in dollar liquidity and weighing on Bitcoin and other crypto assets. His investment firm Maelstrom will remain on the sidelines until liquidity conditions clearly improve. However, he expects that if the AI industry faces a systemic crisis, central banks may ultimately respond with monetary easing, which would be bullish for Bitcoin in the long run.

text:
Perp DEX points are probably the closest thing retail traders have to getting near seed-round exposure to potential unicorns.

You don't need a fancy personal brand, VC connections, or a podcast tour.

But you do need to know how to spot winners early.

Some traders have practically perfected this game:
@derteil00, @izebel_eth, @blurr, @El33, @Cbb0fe, @punk2498_, @TaikiMaeda2 

All highly worth following.

One lesser-known account worth paying attention to is @linenmito, who has been openly sharing his framework for identifying promising projects early.

His six criteria:
◾️ Organic usage : Sustained volume and OI across multiple timeframes, not just incentive-driven spikes.
◾️ Product differentiation : Something traders will actually want to use after the points end.
◾️ Tokenomics : Circulating float, supply dynamics, and distribution policy.
◾️ Liquidity edge : A sustainable advantage in liquidity and execution quality.
◾️ Business model : Real revenue and a credible path to profitability.
◾️ Timing : Getting in early enough for the risk/reward to make sense.

The best opportunities aren't necessarily the protocols that simply do good volume or have the fanciest tech.
They're the ones most likely to become valuable businesses.

The real alpha isn't trading harder. It's knowing where it's worth putting your capital to work.

Worth reading his full breakdown:
https://t.co/2yXi1ZJlHK
author: hansolar21
quoted_text:
How to Identify Potential Winners Airdrop From the Rest of the Perp DEX Market?

Here are some of our airdrop winnings from Perp-Dexs:
$HYPE~ $20M+ From main wallet + 6Figs
$LIT ~ 6Figs
$ASTER ~ 6Figs
$BP ~ Top 5Figs
$EDGE ~ 5Figs
etc.

The next big perpDEX MIGHT not be the one with the most points, the loudest community, or the biggest trading volume today.

And if you're farming every new perp DEX that launches, there's a chance you're optimizing for the wrong thing.

We've seen this cycle before.

A new protocol launches, points go live, trading competitions begin, the leaderboard fills up, volume starts climbing, and suddenly everyone is trying to figure out which platform could produce the next $HYPE.

But here's the problem.

By the time a protocol becomes the obvious winner, the opportunity to position yourself early may already have passed.

Now the real edge is identifying which protocols have the potential to become winners BEFORE the market agrees.

And to do that, we need to look beyond the numbers everyone is posting and start looking at these👇:

1. Volume is a signal, But what kind of volume?

Volume is one of the first metrics traders look at when evaluating a perp DEX.

High volume can indicate demand, activity and growing relevance. But volume without context can be misleading.

Is the activity driven by organic traders or incentives? Is the same capital being recycled repeatedly? Are users returning because the product is good, or because the points are attractive?

None of these questions can be answered by a volume leaderboard alone.

That doesn't mean high-volume protocols should be dismissed. It means volume should be the beginning of your research, not the conclusion.

Look for consistency across multiple periods. Examine open interest, liquidity, revenue where available, and changes in activity as incentives evolve.

Most importantly, look for evidence that the platform is becoming more useful to traders over time.

The question isn't just how much a perp DEX is trading today. It's whether that activity has a reason to exist tomorrow.

2. Product-market fit will matter when the points stop

For farmers, points are often the initial attraction.

For investors, the future token is often the thesis.

But for a perp DEX to survive, someone has to want to trade there even when neither points nor token speculation is the primary motivation. Eg @HyperliquidX

This is where I think many people underestimate the importance of product-market fit.

A platform can attract thousands of users with an aggressive incentive program. Keeping them is an entirely different challenge.

Look at the actual trading experience:
- Are execution costs competitive?
- Is liquidity sufficient for the size you want to trade?
- Does the platform offer markets that traders genuinely want?
- Is the interface reliable when market conditions become stressful?
- Does it solve a problem that competing venues haven't solved as well?

These are not just questions for long-term investors. They're relevant to farmers too.

A protocol that people genuinely use has a different foundation from one whose activity depends heavily on the next rewards announcement.

Neither guarantees a successful token launch, but the former gives you more reasons to investigate its long-term potential.

Points can attract users. A good product gives them a reason to stay.

3. Understand what actually makes the product different

The perp DEX market is becoming increasingly competitive.

Zero explicit trading fees. High leverage. Points campaigns. Referral bonuses. RWA markets. Attractive interfaces.

These features can help a protocol gain traction, but many are relatively easy to replicate.

So what is the moat?

It could be superior execution, deeper liquidity, more efficient capital usage, differentiated markets, better risk management or an experience that traders genuinely prefer.

Consider @variational_io as an example.

Its approach to trading costs and its expansion into markets beyond conventional crypto perps offer useful areas to investigate. But the important question isn't simply whether another protocol offers similar features.

It's whether that competitor can deliver a comparable or better experience in practice.

The same standard should apply to every platform in this market, including Variational.

When evaluating a potential winner, ask yourself:
- What does this protocol do meaningfully better?
- How difficult would that advantage be for a competitor to reproduce?
- Is there evidence that users value the difference?
- Can the team continue improving the product as competition increases?

If the entire thesis depends on a points multiplier or a feature that five competitors already offer, you may not have identified a durable advantage.

You may have identified a temporary marketing advantage.

4. Tokenomics can make or break an otherwise promising protocol

This is where farmers need to be particularly careful.

A great product does not automatically mean a great airdrop.

And a generous airdrop allocation does not automatically mean a valuable token.

You need to understand how value is distributed, how much supply becomes liquid at launch, and what the market may be required to absorb.

Before committing significant time or capital to a campaign, investigate:

Supply and allocation: What percentage is allocated to users? How much goes to investors, the team, the treasury and future incentives?

Circulating supply: How much of the token will actually be tradable at TGE? A headline FDV can look impressive while the initial liquid supply tells a very different story.

Unlocks: When do investor and team tokens unlock? What does the vesting schedule look like, and how might future supply affect market dynamics?

Distribution methodology: Is the allocation based on points, volume, trading quality, time-weighted participation or another system? Are the rules clear enough to make a reasonable estimate?

Potential selling pressure: How many recipients might be looking to exit immediately, and what liquidity could realistically be available?

The objective isn't to predict the exact token price. That's often impossible before launch.

It's to understand the range of plausible outcomes and avoid treating an advertised allocation as guaranteed profit.

A protocol can have a successful launch and still disappoint farmers who entered at the wrong cost or built unrealistic expectations.

Don't just ask how many tokens you might receive. Ask what those tokens could realistically be worth, how much it costs you to earn them, and what assumptions your estimate depends on.

5. The real competition may be for liquidity, not users

A platform can attract a large community and still struggle to deliver a competitive trading experience.

Perpetual exchanges need more than accounts and transaction counts. They need liquidity that allows users to enter and exit positions at acceptable prices.

This is particularly important for traders operating at scale.

A venue may look attractive when markets are calm, but spreads can widen, available depth can shrink and execution can deteriorate when volatility rises.

That's why traders should look beyond headline TVL or open interest.

Investigate effective spreads, slippage at realistic order sizes, available depth and performance under different market conditions.

For farmers, liquidity also matters because it affects the cost of participating in trading-based campaigns.

If you need to trade repeatedly to earn points, even small execution costs can accumulate. A points program that looks lucrative on paper may be less attractive once you account for the actual cost of participation.

The best opportunity isn't necessarily the protocol offering the most points. It's the one where the potential reward makes sense relative to the cost, risk and uncertainty involved.

6. Revenue and sustainability matter more than announcements

At some point, every serious protocol needs to answer a difficult question:

How does this become a sustainable business?

Funding announcements can extend a team's runway. Incentives can accelerate adoption. A token can finance ecosystem development.

But none of these automatically establishes sustainable economics.

Look for evidence of recurring demand, credible revenue sources, sensible operating costs and a clear plan for maintaining the product.

Where data is available, examine how revenue relates to trading activity and whether the protocol can retain users without continually increasing subsidies.

Be careful with comparisons, too. Different venues may define revenue, fees and volume differently, making headline numbers difficult to compare directly.

For farmers, sustainability is relevant because a team that continues building and maintaining a useful product may have more reasons to support an ecosystem after the initial campaign ends.

For investors, the question is whether the token has a credible relationship to the protocol's long-term economics.

A popular product and a valuable token are not necessarily the same thing.

The protocol can win users while the token underperforms. Learn to separate the two theses.

7. Timing matters, but so does the cost of being early

Early positioning can create opportunities.

It can also mean spending months on a protocol that never produces a meaningful return.

This is particularly relevant in the current perp DEX landscape, where traders are constantly choosing between established platforms and emerging projects with uncertain token timelines.

Being early ALONE isn't an advantage by itself.

You need a thesis about why the opportunity exists, what could make it work, and what evidence would cause you to change your mind.

For farmers, that means considering the opportunity cost of your capital, time and trading activity.

Could the same capital be deployed more efficiently elsewhere? Are you taking unnecessary market risk to qualify for a speculative reward? Is the campaign still attractive after accounting for costs?

For investors, it means examining whether the market has already priced in the expected growth.

A promising protocol can still be a poor investment at an excessive valuation.

Likewise, a project with less attention may have room to grow if it demonstrates genuine product progress and a credible path to adoption.

The goal isn't to predict every winner.

It's to build a repeatable process for identifying opportunities where the potential upside justifies the uncertainty.

8. What would make you change your mind?

This is one of the most underrated parts of evaluating a protocol.

People are good at finding evidence that supports a thesis they already believe. Once they start farming a project, join its community or accumulate a large number of points, they can become emotionally invested in its success.

That makes it harder to evaluate new information objectively.

Instead, define your thesis before you become attached to the outcome.

If your thesis depends on organic growth, what would declining activity after incentives weaken?

If your thesis depends on superior execution, what happens if competitors consistently offer better fills?

If your thesis depends on a generous airdrop, what happens if the allocation methodology changes or the tokenomics disappoint?

If your thesis depends on a future token, what happens if the launch is delayed?

These aren't reasons to avoid emerging protocols. They're reasons to evaluate them honestly.

A good thesis should have conditions under which it becomes stronger and conditions under which it becomes weaker.

If no possible evidence would make you reconsider a protocol, you're probably defending a belief rather than evaluating an opportunity.

text:
Will the Democrats see Elon Musk’s vision as an opportunity to work with him, rather than continuing to treat him as a political opponent?

His ambitions span several areas:
AI and robotics: accelerating automation and developing increasingly capable AI.

Space exploration: making humanity a multiplanetary civilisation through SpaceX.

Energy: expanding battery storage, solar power and sustainable energy.
Transport: autonomous vehicles, electric cars and new transport infrastructure.

Abundance: using technology and automation to increase productivity and potentially reduce the cost of living.

Will the Democrats embrace it?

My assessment is that they may embrace parts of his vision, but probably not without political and policy conditions.

There are three areas worth watching:

1. AI and automation: Democrats may support innovation while pushing for worker protections, accountability and safeguards against excessive corporate concentration.

2. Space and scientific advancement: Space exploration and technological research could offer common ground, particularly where there are economic and national-security benefits.

3. Economic abundance: Musk's vision of a future where AI and robotics dramatically increase productivity could appeal across party lines. However, Democrats are likely to ask who owns the technology and how ordinary people benefit from the wealth it creates.

The election result is significant: Democrats have won control of both chambers of Congress, according to the latest reporting. That gives them considerable influence over legislation, funding and oversight from January 2027.

传统的版本是，持有什么资产，就在相应的平台开设账户。

比如，股票放在证券账户，Crypto 放在交易所，不同账户之间的资金独立。

现在有了代币化，新版本是用户有机会通过一个账户参与全球不同的资产市场，资产之间的可组合性也变得更强。一项资产除了持有和交易，还可能作为抵押品，支持其他市场的投资交易和风险管理，这就是资金效率的提升。

按照今天现场研究院小伙伴分享的思路，以后衡量一个金融平台的价值，不仅看它提供多少产品，拥有多少流动性，还应该关注它能让用户已有的资产发挥多大的使用价值。
author: moonkimbinance
quoted_text:
未来可以在 CEX 做的事情会越来越多。

从加密货币到美股、ETF、港股，再到代币化股票、期权和永续合约，传统金融与 Crypto 的边界正在逐渐模糊。

过去我们需要在不同的平台管理不同的资产。未来一个 Binance 账户可能就能连接全球多个金融市场，实现跨资产配置与交易。

这背后其实是一个值得关注的趋势：CEX 正在从加密货币交易所，逐渐向综合性金融服务平台演变。

但我认为，产品越来越丰富只是第一步，真正决定平台能走多远的，依然是资产安全、透明度、流动性和合规能力。

尤其是当更多传统资产进入加密交易平台，用户不仅要关注交易是否方便，还要弄清楚自己究竟持有什么、拥有什么权利，以及承担了哪些风险。

未来交易所之间的竞争，可能不再只是争夺 Crypto 用户，而是争夺下一代全球金融市场的入口。

text:
Circle财报最让我震惊的是：把ARC的预售款确认为Q3收入。

了解了一下，这确实符合美国的会计准则，但也有很大的隐患。
今天想写三个问题：为什么Circle出售自己发行的代币可以计入收入项？Circle这么做的理由是什么？未来最大的隐患是什么？

1. 为什么Circle出售自己发行的代币可以计入“收入项”？
ARC不代表Circle的所有权或融资债权，它确实也不具备分红权、表决权等权益。
ARC只是Circle向机构出售的一种数字产品/网络使用权益，是可以适用ASC 606《客户合同收入》，把预售款计入“其它收入”的。
而且，在代币交付后，不管币价怎么波动，都不会再影响这项收入。

这其实也引出了币股同权的问题。
Circle的股东享有公司利润和剩余资产的权益，而ARC持有人享有的是网络层面的权益。
持币人花钱购买ARC，上市公司却可以把这笔钱确认为收入，改善利润表，影响CRCL价格。
但持币人并不会因此直接获得Circle的股东权利。

未来如果越来越多的上市公司选择发币融资、发展生态，那么股票和代币之间的权益要怎么平衡呢🤔

2. Circle这么做的理由是什么？
最大的理由肯定是美化财报。
Q3 Circle的同比收入增速是+17%，调整后EBITDA同比+85%。
剔除掉1.82亿美元的ARC预售收入后，Q3 Circle的同比收入增速变成-7.7%，调整后EBITDA同比-21%。

Circle CFO在电话会上说过，出售ARC没有相应的直接成本，因此这类收入对利润的贡献非常显著。
但这种收入是没有可持续性的，这和USDC储备收入的不一样，它没有可持续性、可预测性。
市场也不知道该用什么方法去估值了，从财报后CRCL的表现也能看出来。

3. 未来最大的隐患是什么？
预售合同里有个履约条款：如果2028年5月8日前ARC没有完成PoS转型，机构投资者可能有权要求退款。
Circle在履约义务还未完成前，就把75%的预售款确认为收入了。
虽然Circle对Arc网络有很强的控制权，而且大部分验证者就是购买ARC的机构🤣但我更担忧这种做法会引起监管机构的不满。
这次预售采用的是豁免证券注册的私募方式，并不代表SEC已经认可了Circle的所有会计判断。未来一段时间，监管是否会针对Circle提出质疑？如果上市公司都效仿这个行为会发生什么？🤔下篇写写这个问题

真是想什么来什么，还说这两天要呼吁有没有人能在 TapeOut 上做一个VerifyBot

刚好X Layer TapeOut 创意官活动就来了

必须投稿！

TapeOut 不会只停在流片挖矿。电路 NFT 最稀缺的用法是给链上自动化加一层可验证刹车即规则能仿真、能复现，不是再信黑箱 Bot。

所以，我想在Tapeout 上看到 VerifyBot即验机大脑

为谁服务👇
✅跟单 / 金库用户：把钱交给 Bot 前，要亲眼看懂风控逻辑
✅策略作者 / 量化团队：用可验证电路证明「不会乱开仓」，降低获客信任成本
✅小型金库 / DAO 司库：给自动执行加强制停机条件，少靠多签管理员人肉盯盘

解决什么问题：
现在Bot 的核心矛盾不是赚不赚钱，是策略不可见，这几天一直在用bot 参与打新，但是像私服逻辑、口头承诺、这些等出问题了才知道。目前缺的是入金前可仿真、跑飞时能自动撤资的硬约束。

具体场景👇
1.策略作者把核心风控用 NAND / LATCH 流片成 Strategy Circuit NFT（最大回撤门闩、仓位上限、止损触发、冷却时间、极端波动熔断）。

2.用户注资前，先在 TapeOut Canvas 免费仿真：暴跌、插针、流动性枯竭，bot会不会失控。如果仿真不过关，就进不了资金。

3.上线后，每次下单前必须过电路状态机。输出 FAIL → 立刻停机，资金强制撤回到用户自己的地址，Bot 无权继续操作。

4.改策略: 必须重新流片、公开 diff。旧策略废了后，新策略跟上，链上留痕，无法更改。

TapeOut 负责让规则本身可验证、可复现、可手搓。VerifyBot 的设计初衷是让设计能力服务真实资金安全。

ArcStocks is a stock-layer protocol running on Circle’s Arc chain: it uses USDC on Arc to buy on-chain derivatives corresponding to stocks, with the underlying assets backed 1:1 by real tokenized stocks held on Rh Chain.

The core product is to turn traditional stock exposure into ordinary ERC-20s on Arc: users deposit USDC on Arc → the protocol buys the corresponding tokenized stocks on Rh Chain and puts them into the vault → STOCK.arc is minted on Arc.

It also works in reverse: burn STOCK.arc, the underlying stock is sold, and USDC is returned to the wallet.

STOCK.arc can be traded, used as collateral, and integrated into other Arc protocols, without needing to go to Rh Chain or open a brokerage account.

There are currently around 29 assets, including NVDA, TSLA, AAPL, SPY, QQQ, MSFT, AMD, MSTR, GME, GLD, SLV, SGOV, etc. More will be added based on liquidity on Rh. There is also:

Desk: USDC ⇄ Stocks, claiming near-instant execution.

Launchpad: New tokens can pair against a stock instead of USDC. They first go through a bonding curve and then graduate into a locked Uniswap v4 pool.

The ASTOCK token is the protocol token: the ASTOCK/USDC pool has a relatively high trading fee, most of which is used roughly every 2 hours to buy STOCK.arc and distribute it to holders proportionally. Holders can choose which stock they want to receive. The project has also announced that excess funds will be used for buybacks and burns.

So the main role of the token is essentially:

Capture trading fees → convert them into real stocks and distribute them to holders + buy back and burn ASTOCK.

text:
Perp DEX points are probably the closest thing retail traders have to getting near seed-round exposure to potential unicorns.

You don't need a fancy personal brand, VC connections, or a podcast tour.

But you do need to know how to spot winners early.

Some traders have practically perfected this game:
@derteil00, @izebel_eth, @blurr, @El33, @Cbb0fe, @punk2498_, @TaikiMaeda2 

All highly worth following.

One lesser-known account worth paying attention to is @linenmito, who has been openly sharing his framework for identifying promising projects early.

His six criteria:
◾️ Organic usage : Sustained volume and OI across multiple timeframes, not just incentive-driven spikes.
◾️ Product differentiation : Something traders will actually want to use after the points end.
◾️ Tokenomics : Circulating float, supply dynamics, and distribution policy.
◾️ Liquidity edge : A sustainable advantage in liquidity and execution quality.
◾️ Business model : Real revenue and a credible path to profitability.
◾️ Timing : Getting in early enough for the risk/reward to make sense.

The best opportunities aren't necessarily the protocols that simply do good volume or have the fanciest tech.
They're the ones most likely to become valuable businesses.

The real alpha isn't trading harder. It's knowing where it's worth putting your capital to work.

Worth reading his full breakdown:
https://t.co/2yXi1ZJlHK
author: yashascore
quoted_text:
How to Identify Potential Winners Airdrop From the Rest of the Perp DEX Market?

Here are some of our airdrop winnings from Perp-Dexs:
$HYPE~ $20M+ From main wallet + 6Figs
$LIT ~ 6Figs
$ASTER ~ 6Figs
$BP ~ Top 5Figs
$EDGE ~ 5Figs
etc.

The next big perpDEX MIGHT not be the one with the most points, the loudest community, or the biggest trading volume today.

And if you're farming every new perp DEX that launches, there's a chance you're optimizing for the wrong thing.

We've seen this cycle before.

A new protocol launches, points go live, trading competitions begin, the leaderboard fills up, volume starts climbing, and suddenly everyone is trying to figure out which platform could produce the next $HYPE.

But here's the problem.

By the time a protocol becomes the obvious winner, the opportunity to position yourself early may already have passed.

Now the real edge is identifying which protocols have the potential to become winners BEFORE the market agrees.

And to do that, we need to look beyond the numbers everyone is posting and start looking at these👇:

1. Volume is a signal, But what kind of volume?

Volume is one of the first metrics traders look at when evaluating a perp DEX.

High volume can indicate demand, activity and growing relevance. But volume without context can be misleading.

Is the activity driven by organic traders or incentives? Is the same capital being recycled repeatedly? Are users returning because the product is good, or because the points are attractive?

None of these questions can be answered by a volume leaderboard alone.

That doesn't mean high-volume protocols should be dismissed. It means volume should be the beginning of your research, not the conclusion.

Look for consistency across multiple periods. Examine open interest, liquidity, revenue where available, and changes in activity as incentives evolve.

Most importantly, look for evidence that the platform is becoming more useful to traders over time.

The question isn't just how much a perp DEX is trading today. It's whether that activity has a reason to exist tomorrow.

2. Product-market fit will matter when the points stop

For farmers, points are often the initial attraction.

For investors, the future token is often the thesis.

But for a perp DEX to survive, someone has to want to trade there even when neither points nor token speculation is the primary motivation. Eg @HyperliquidX

This is where I think many people underestimate the importance of product-market fit.

A platform can attract thousands of users with an aggressive incentive program. Keeping them is an entirely different challenge.

Look at the actual trading experience:
- Are execution costs competitive?
- Is liquidity sufficient for the size you want to trade?
- Does the platform offer markets that traders genuinely want?
- Is the interface reliable when market conditions become stressful?
- Does it solve a problem that competing venues haven't solved as well?

These are not just questions for long-term investors. They're relevant to farmers too.

A protocol that people genuinely use has a different foundation from one whose activity depends heavily on the next rewards announcement.

Neither guarantees a successful token launch, but the former gives you more reasons to investigate its long-term potential.

Points can attract users. A good product gives them a reason to stay.

3. Understand what actually makes the product different

The perp DEX market is becoming increasingly competitive.

Zero explicit trading fees. High leverage. Points campaigns. Referral bonuses. RWA markets. Attractive interfaces.

These features can help a protocol gain traction, but many are relatively easy to replicate.

So what is the moat?

It could be superior execution, deeper liquidity, more efficient capital usage, differentiated markets, better risk management or an experience that traders genuinely prefer.

Consider @variational_io as an example.

Its approach to trading costs and its expansion into markets beyond conventional crypto perps offer useful areas to investigate. But the important question isn't simply whether another protocol offers similar features.

It's whether that competitor can deliver a comparable or better experience in practice.

The same standard should apply to every platform in this market, including Variational.

When evaluating a potential winner, ask yourself:
- What does this protocol do meaningfully better?
- How difficult would that advantage be for a competitor to reproduce?
- Is there evidence that users value the difference?
- Can the team continue improving the product as competition increases?

If the entire thesis depends on a points multiplier or a feature that five competitors already offer, you may not have identified a durable advantage.

You may have identified a temporary marketing advantage.

4. Tokenomics can make or break an otherwise promising protocol

This is where farmers need to be particularly careful.

A great product does not automatically mean a great airdrop.

And a generous airdrop allocation does not automatically mean a valuable token.

You need to understand how value is distributed, how much supply becomes liquid at launch, and what the market may be required to absorb.

Before committing significant time or capital to a campaign, investigate:

Supply and allocation: What percentage is allocated to users? How much goes to investors, the team, the treasury and future incentives?

Circulating supply: How much of the token will actually be tradable at TGE? A headline FDV can look impressive while the initial liquid supply tells a very different story.

Unlocks: When do investor and team tokens unlock? What does the vesting schedule look like, and how might future supply affect market dynamics?

Distribution methodology: Is the allocation based on points, volume, trading quality, time-weighted participation or another system? Are the rules clear enough to make a reasonable estimate?

Potential selling pressure: How many recipients might be looking to exit immediately, and what liquidity could realistically be available?

The objective isn't to predict the exact token price. That's often impossible before launch.

It's to understand the range of plausible outcomes and avoid treating an advertised allocation as guaranteed profit.

A protocol can have a successful launch and still disappoint farmers who entered at the wrong cost or built unrealistic expectations.

Don't just ask how many tokens you might receive. Ask what those tokens could realistically be worth, how much it costs you to earn them, and what assumptions your estimate depends on.

5. The real competition may be for liquidity, not users

A platform can attract a large community and still struggle to deliver a competitive trading experience.

Perpetual exchanges need more than accounts and transaction counts. They need liquidity that allows users to enter and exit positions at acceptable prices.

This is particularly important for traders operating at scale.

A venue may look attractive when markets are calm, but spreads can widen, available depth can shrink and execution can deteriorate when volatility rises.

That's why traders should look beyond headline TVL or open interest.

Investigate effective spreads, slippage at realistic order sizes, available depth and performance under different market conditions.

For farmers, liquidity also matters because it affects the cost of participating in trading-based campaigns.

If you need to trade repeatedly to earn points, even small execution costs can accumulate. A points program that looks lucrative on paper may be less attractive once you account for the actual cost of participation.

The best opportunity isn't necessarily the protocol offering the most points. It's the one where the potential reward makes sense relative to the cost, risk and uncertainty involved.

6. Revenue and sustainability matter more than announcements

At some point, every serious protocol needs to answer a difficult question:

How does this become a sustainable business?

Funding announcements can extend a team's runway. Incentives can accelerate adoption. A token can finance ecosystem development.

But none of these automatically establishes sustainable economics.

Look for evidence of recurring demand, credible revenue sources, sensible operating costs and a clear plan for maintaining the product.

Where data is available, examine how revenue relates to trading activity and whether the protocol can retain users without continually increasing subsidies.

Be careful with comparisons, too. Different venues may define revenue, fees and volume differently, making headline numbers difficult to compare directly.

For farmers, sustainability is relevant because a team that continues building and maintaining a useful product may have more reasons to support an ecosystem after the initial campaign ends.

For investors, the question is whether the token has a credible relationship to the protocol's long-term economics.

A popular product and a valuable token are not necessarily the same thing.

The protocol can win users while the token underperforms. Learn to separate the two theses.

7. Timing matters, but so does the cost of being early

Early positioning can create opportunities.

It can also mean spending months on a protocol that never produces a meaningful return.

This is particularly relevant in the current perp DEX landscape, where traders are constantly choosing between established platforms and emerging projects with uncertain token timelines.

Being early ALONE isn't an advantage by itself.

You need a thesis about why the opportunity exists, what could make it work, and what evidence would cause you to change your mind.

For farmers, that means considering the opportunity cost of your capital, time and trading activity.

Could the same capital be deployed more efficiently elsewhere? Are you taking unnecessary market risk to qualify for a speculative reward? Is the campaign still attractive after accounting for costs?

For investors, it means examining whether the market has already priced in the expected growth.

A promising protocol can still be a poor investment at an excessive valuation.

Likewise, a project with less attention may have room to grow if it demonstrates genuine product progress and a credible path to adoption.

The goal isn't to predict every winner.

It's to build a repeatable process for identifying opportunities where the potential upside justifies the uncertainty.

8. What would make you change your mind?

This is one of the most underrated parts of evaluating a protocol.

People are good at finding evidence that supports a thesis they already believe. Once they start farming a project, join its community or accumulate a large number of points, they can become emotionally invested in its success.

That makes it harder to evaluate new information objectively.

Instead, define your thesis before you become attached to the outcome.

If your thesis depends on organic growth, what would declining activity after incentives weaken?

If your thesis depends on superior execution, what happens if competitors consistently offer better fills?

If your thesis depends on a generous airdrop, what happens if the allocation methodology changes or the tokenomics disappoint?

If your thesis depends on a future token, what happens if the launch is delayed?

These aren't reasons to avoid emerging protocols. They're reasons to evaluate them honestly.

A good thesis should have conditions under which it becomes stronger and conditions under which it becomes weaker.

If no possible evidence would make you reconsider a protocol, you're probably defending a belief rather than evaluating an opportunity.

text:
We need to reconsider our priors on code readability.

Humans, compared to agents, are pretty slow at understanding large quantities of text. So in the old days, readability was important so the human could efficiently grok what was going on.

So readability now comes down to:

1. Can a human, if needed, jump in and understand the code
2. Does the code use the same domain language as the human describing the code?

1 helps with observability and the occasional spot checks you need to do on important PR's. 2 helps the agent translate the words you use into code changes.

In other words, readability is now a nicety, not a necessity.

The way agents 'read' code is different - good agents are all about gathering data about how the code works. They'll prod around with it, execute parts of it.

So 'readability' to agents really means 'verifiability'. How easy it is to mess about with that code to see it working.

Let's take this scenario:

- You have a huge module in your codebase that uses all sorts of complex performance tricks
- It has 100% test coverage

A talented human would need an hour or two to get comfortable working in that module.

An agent needs zero time. They verify it with the tests, poke about a bit, and they're good to go.

The takeaways:

- When judging a module (or a codebase), don't think about how easy the code is to read
- Instead, think about how easy it is to verify
- Design your codebase so modules can be tested and verified independently
- Feel free to sacrifice a bit of readability for performance
- Cyclomatic complexity and function size don't matter to agents

text:
加密平台最终都要走向品牌打造的道路，这篇“币圈品牌战争”值得看看。“你是谁？通过什么方式？提供什么产品与服务？”这是所有品牌构建的起点，对这三个问题的持续回答会在用户心中逐渐沉淀为一个具体的形象，这是品牌路径的必经过程，也是用户形成基本认知与选择偏好的基础。

当然更高级的品牌路径则更像是宗教式的建构：通过一套相对稳定的文化理念、符号体系和共同经历，把用户从单纯的产品使用者转化为具有认同感和归属感的群体，这种高度信任通常需要更长的时间积累，并且必须经受实际兑现与危机的反复检验，而非仅靠短期营销或仪式感就能完成。

传统金融也是如此：高盛、瑞银、花旗等机构在不同阶段也都通过专业形象、风险控制叙事、文化赞助或高管人格化等方式，构建差异化的信任与声誉资产；

加密行业已经从早期蛮荒走向了规范成熟，当基础交易功能趋于同质化时，平台能否在用户心智中占据位置就越来越重要，而这种用户心智则越来越取决于信任（资金安全与合规）、多资产选择与收益机会、技术稳定性以及社区归属感的综合叠加。

这个时候品牌不再只是营销工具，而成为穿越周期、抵御同质化竞争和获取主流用户的核心基础设施，单纯依赖社区热情或技术噱头已不足以支撑长期优势。

@0xathenalee这篇文章所对比的Binance与OKX路径，正是这一成熟阶段的典型样本。

text:
With @OTOY newly added MCP you can create so much so quickly!

And it's not just about shading. You can build procedural tools for production in entirely new ways.

For this example, I wanted to create a procedural mosaic builder with cobblestones, grout, and a ton of customizable controls, all adjustable through sliders in Octane Standalone.

Drop in new artwork and within seconds the tool rebuilds the mosaic, taking into account the artwork's lines and strokes to guide stone flow, collision awareness, color, shading, and randomization.

None of this is necessarily NEW to Octane. It's always been a powerhouse capable of doing incredible things. But with the MCP, those capabilities become much more accessible, making it possible to prototype and build complex procedural tools incredibly quickly.

Tibo 的 28 天更新（闹剧）终于结束了。我发现很多人其实不太了解 Tibo。

他就像凭空冒出来的一样，突然成了 X 上最活跃的 OpenAI 高管之一，每天发布新功能，给大家按下 Reset 按钮。

查了一下他的背景，还蛮有趣。

Tibo 全名 Thibault Sottiaux，比利时人，2015 年加入 Google，后来去了 DeepMind，参与过 AI 研究基础设施和 Gemini 相关工作。

2024 年加入 OpenAI，最初做内部研究工具，后来负责 Codex。

但他现在已经不只是 Codex 负责人了，而是 OpenAI 的 Head of Core Products & Platform，负责范围包括 ChatGPT、Codex、API、Agent 基础设施等核心产品。

他在 X 上还有个死对头，就是 Grok Bot 团队的 Lauren（@poteto）。

两人经常互相嘴炮，甚至被网友嗑成了 CP。

Poteto 把 OpenAI 叫作 The Reset Company，把自己这边叫作 The Ship Company，嘲讽 OpenAI 只会重置额度，不会发布功能。

后来 Tibo 直接搞出了 https://t.co/mKmDXNyNpk，Poteto 反手又做了个 https://t.co/faJvRMplzO 游戏，两个人甚至还有专门的粉丝网站记录他们的嘴炮战绩。

Tibo 甚至在一次嘴炮中宣布自己「退休了」，当然，没过几天他又开始了。

不过工作上，他确实已经逐渐从 Codex 转向更大范围的产品工作。

他接下来的一项重要任务，就是把 Codex 的能力从 Coding Agent 扩展到通用 Agent，并逐步整合进 ChatGPT。

最近 Dots、ChatGPT Work，以及 Chat 和 Work 的整合计划，都能看到这个思路。

本周路透社还披露，他同时在负责 OpenAI 内部的一项重大安全基础设施强化工作。

希望 Tibo 能不忘初心，不要丢掉他的 Reset 按钮！！！

The U.S. government has confirmed it’s using a zero-click spyware — it hacks into cell phones without any user interaction.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has officially confirmed its active deployment of 'Graphite,' a highly sophisticated spyware tool capable of hacking mobile devices without any user interaction. 

Developed by the Israeli cyber-surveillance firm Paragon Solutions, this 'zero-click' technology allows operators to bypass the end-to-end encryption of secure applications like WhatsApp and Signal. 

Once silently installed on a device, the spyware extracts encrypted messages, location data, and other private records directly from the phone itself. Despite a previous pause under federal review, ICE's $2 million contract for the software was quietly reactivated, sparking immense concern among privacy advocates and lawmakers alike.

The disclosure has intensified the national debate over the balance between national security and constitutional rights. While ICE authorities assert that the software is strictly deployed to intercept encrypted communications of fentanyl traffickers and foreign terrorist organizations, civil liberties groups warn of potential overreach. Activists and legal experts caution that without strict federal oversight, zero-click exploits could easily be leveraged to target domestic political dissidents, journalists, and immigrant communities. This ongoing tension highlights a growing, unregulated ecosystem of mercenary surveillance tools operating within the borders of democratic nations.

source: Knight First Amendment Institute. (2026). Knight Institute Urges Congress to Limit ICE's Use of Spyware Technologies as Agency Confirms Expanded Deployment.

Why have spreadsheets become an unpaid member of your sales team?

You built the quote in the quoting tool. Then exported it so the partner could work with it.

Now you're maintaining formulas.

Insert a row. Did the formula carry over? Change the hardware quantity. Did the support quantity follow? Adjust the discount. Is it applied to the right items?

And that monthly support price? It gets billed annually. Better check the math.

Suddenly, someone's using a calculator to check the spreadsheet they exported from their quoting software.

Then the customer asks: “Can we see one year, three years and five years?”

Now you've got three options to calculate and check. The partner gets three versions, makes their changes, and prepares them for the customer.

A straightforward request can turn into days of rebuilding and checking. Nobody has even reached invoicing yet.

This is the work QuoteLogic takes out of the process.

Required products and quantities are linked in the underlying data. Support pricing and term calculations happen in the app. Change the quantity or term, and the configured calculations follow.

Partners and customers get the information intended for them through shared quote views, without rebuilding the deal in another spreadsheet.

Your team should be helping the customer choose between one, three and five years. That conversation shouldn't have to wait for someone to repair a formula.

How much of your quoting time goes into building the offer, and how much goes into making sure the spreadsheet hasn't broken it?

众里选股千百度，蓦然回首，
指数ETF却在，灯火阑珊处。

最近有身边朋友来问我
A股怎么买，我统一回答是，
打开支付宝买沪深ETF最好，
这对一个浅经验普通玩家来说，
远比自己去券商开户→银证转账→选股买卖要好，
操作体验最简单快捷，各方面坑最少，
情绪更稳定，睡眠质量更高，
笑到最后的胜率更大。

（很多去券商排队开户的人，甚至不知道“原来近在咫尺的支付宝也能玩A股？”，更不知道这其实是更适合他的方式）

前期个股是有全体上涨，
但中后期个股之间的戏剧性轮动，
让人嫉妒这个，眼红那个，
“大盘明明涨的/没跌，我这个怎么不涨/跌了？”
“那个傻X怎么晒单赚那么多，我怎么能比他差？”
这会把普通玩家心态搞死...
把前期赚的，通过中后期频繁大聪明动作亏回去...

“为将者未虑胜，先虑败，故可百战不殆矣”
先考虑如何在最坏的情况下，对结果依然能接受，
在此基础上，再考虑如何超额收益，伺机取得赫赫之功。
当仓位的大头是指数ETF时，即使一开始进入的时机是彻底错误的，也能让代价最小化。

且在数学上有个很简单的热知识，
前面即使赚+100%
（尤其在这种情况下会信心大增）
后面的操作让自己-50%，
就回到原点，白忙一场，
即使+200%（10万变30万）那么一旦再骚操作-50%就变成只赚50%（30万又变15万），结果也大概率跑输省心省力的指数etf。
这还算是定力不同凡响的人，更多的情况是，信心大增后追加本金，10万+200%变30万，追加10万本金，只要-50%，那前面这个+200%就没了。
再加上，普通玩家面对一只个股vs面对指数，在信任度、了解度、知行合一稳定度等等，都是天壤之别。

就像是，
很多在币圈牛市来了又失望离开的人，
大多是没有把BTC当做仓位的重心。

等到最后出金落袋的时候，
“自己搞来搞去，还不如当初买指数”
会是大部分普通玩家心里声音的写照，

text:
The most important catalyst behind $ASTOCK rally is not Jeremy Allaire's brief "Very cool" comment.

0x4c9b47dbd5933aa4574b2c27f82419e4dbbd0222

It is the fact that AStock is expanding from a stock token protocol on Arc into a cross-chain issuance and stock rewards platform covering both Arc and Solana.

This opens up a much bigger product opportunity.

Allaire's interaction brought market attention to the project, but what really deserves a reassessment is the expansion of its product scope. Previously, AStock was primarily focused on bringing stock assets on-chain. Now, it wants to enable any issuer to integrate stock rewards, token tax distribution, and cross-chain liquidity into their own projects.

Here are some of my thoughts: I believe there are clear catalysts behind this ASTOCK rally.

Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire replied “Very cool” to AStock's post announcing the upcoming launch of Omni Launchpad. This interaction naturally draws a connection between Circle, Arc, and the tokenized stock ecosystem. After all, AStock is built on Arc, the financial infrastructure developed by Circle.

First, this was a public positive interaction from Circle's CEO, bringing the project additional attention and a degree of credibility. However, there is currently no evidence that AStock has received official support from Circle or entered into a formal partnership with it. What really deserves attention is the Omni Launchpad.

Let's first look at AStock's original business.

AStock aims to build a stock asset layer on Arc. Users deposit USDC on Arc, and the protocol uses cross-chain infrastructure to purchase the corresponding Robinhood Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain and place them in a reserve vault. It then issues the corresponding aStock tokens on Arc. In the reverse process, users burn their stock tokens, the reserve sells the corresponding assets, and USDC is returned to them.

This means users do not need to operate across two chains themselves or manually handle the cross-chain purchase and conversion of stock assets. Tokens such as aNVDA, aTSLA, and aSPY can be transferred and traded on Arc like ordinary ERC-20 tokens, and can also be integrated into other protocols. AStock's website previously displayed 29 available stock assets, with reserves and the corresponding Arc token supply available for cross-chain verification.

One important detail needs to be clarified: these tokens do not represent direct ownership of shares in companies such as NVIDIA or Tesla. Robinhood's official documentation explains that its Stock Tokens are tokenized debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited. They provide economic exposure to the corresponding assets but do not grant holders legal or beneficial ownership of the underlying companies, nor do they provide shareholder rights. There are also issuance and trading restrictions in regions including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland.

Therefore, what AStock provides is on-chain exposure backed by Stock Tokens, not a traditional stock brokerage account available to users worldwide.

This is why Omni Launchpad is the key to AStock's business expansion.

AStock has announced that Omni Launchpad will launch across both Arc and Solana, with the goal of allowing a token to be issued and circulated across both ecosystems. The announced features include configurable trading taxes for developers, optional stock rewards for holders with the ability to select the corresponding stock, two-way transfers between Arc and Solana, and Ferry, which supports staking USDC or SOL.

This means AStock is moving beyond building around its own stock trading product and is beginning to offer token issuance and economic mechanisms to external projects.

The feature I find particularly interesting is the optional stock rewards.

Previously, if a project wanted to provide holders with rewards in another asset, it had to design its own conversion, distribution, and fund management mechanisms. AStock aims to turn this into an optional feature that can be configured at launch: project fees enter the distribution process, the corresponding stock asset is purchased, and rewards are distributed to holders according to predefined rules.

This changes the role of a Launchpad. It is no longer just a tool for helping projects issue tokens. It also allows projects to configure their own reward distribution and incentive mechanisms from the beginning.

The combination of Arc and Solana also makes practical sense. Arc is more closely connected to USDC, RWA, and on-chain financial infrastructure, while Solana has an established memecoin trading and launch ecosystem. If Omni can allow users from both ecosystems to participate in the same projects, AStock's potential user base and liquidity sources will no longer be limited to Arc.

However, the current announcement only confirms that product testing has been completed and that the launch is approaching. Actual cross-chain trading volume, the full details of Ferry's yield mechanism, and Omni's long-term revenue have yet to be demonstrated. These will need to be verified after launch.

Next, let's look at whether ASTOCK itself has a value-capture mechanism. I believe this is what distinguishes it from a simple stock tokenization project.

ASTOCK is more than just a platform governance token. According to the website's mechanism, the ASTOCK/USDC trading pool has a 4% fee structure, consisting of a 3% Swap Tax and a 1% Pool Fee. Part of the trading fees is periodically converted into stock assets and distributed to ASTOCK holders according to their holdings.

At the same time, AStock offers a stock rewards module for third-party tokens. Other projects on Arc can connect their own fee wallets, select the reward asset and distribution ratio, and let the system automatically purchase stocks and distribute them to the corresponding token holders. The official rules also specify that 5% of each such reward distribution goes into the ASTOCK reward pool.

This is important because demand for ASTOCK does not necessarily have to depend entirely on its own trading volume. If more third-party projects begin using AStock's stock rewards module, their fee activity could also become part of the AStock ecosystem.

The latest website data already shows some actual usage: approximately $61,704.76 in stock assets has been distributed to holders, around $5,336.02 in USDC entered the reward pool that day, and the most recent distribution involved 1,787 wallets.

In terms of burns, approximately 78.03M ASTOCK has been burned, representing 7.80% of total supply. The website also shows approximately $10,437.07 spent on buybacks and burns, corresponding to 11.44M ASTOCK.

These figures indicate that stock rewards and token burns are no longer purely roadmap concepts. Actual distributions and on-chain transactions have already taken place. In particular, the involvement of 1,787 wallets in the latest distribution is more meaningful than simply reporting cumulative trading volume.

However, I would not interpret stock distributions as fixed returns. The amount of rewards depends on actual trading activity and fee generation. If trading volume declines, distributions will naturally decrease. An increase in token burns also does not guarantee that the market price will rise.

So what exactly is the market betting on?

I believe the core thesis is that AStock could become a new type of Launchpad infrastructure: any project could issue tokens on Arc or Solana, choose stock assets as rewards for holders, and use cross-chain tools to expand its user base and liquidity. AStock would participate in this ecosystem through its own stock trading product, third-party reward modules, and ASTOCK fee mechanisms.

This offers a much bigger opportunity than simply launching a batch of stock-paired memecoins. Stocks would no longer serve only as trading pairs for individual tokens. They could also become reward assets distributed to holders as part of other projects' token economies.

If Omni successfully attracts more projects to adopt this model, AStock could evolve from a standalone product into an asset distribution infrastructure that other projects can integrate into their own systems.

Jeremy Allaire's interaction happened at an interesting time. On September 16, 2026, Circle officially opened the Arc mainnet, positioning it as infrastructure for financial markets, real-time movement of money, and the Agentic Economy. At launch, Circle announced that more than 100 applications, institutions, and ecosystem builders were involved.

AStock's product direction clearly aligns with Arc's focus on financial assets and USDC-based applications. Allaire's public interaction brought more attention to this alignment, but it should not be interpreted as evidence that Circle has decided to make AStock an official priority within its ecosystem.

Going forward, I will be watching several catalysts closely: whether Omni launches as planned and generates sustained issuance and trading activity across both Arc and Solana; whether third-party projects actually adopt the stock rewards module rather than distributions coming primarily from AStock itself; whether Ferry attracts meaningful USDC and SOL staking deposits; and whether stock rewards and ASTOCK burns continue growing alongside ecosystem activity.

Another important development is AStock's dependence on multiple underlying components, including Arc, Robinhood Stock Tokens, cross-chain messaging, and reserve vaults. Any liquidity, redemption, bridging, or regulatory issue affecting one of these components could disrupt the overall product experience.

My conclusion is that ASTOCK's fundamentals are moving in a stronger direction, and this development goes beyond simply adding another Launchpad. It is connecting stock asset trading, third-party reward distribution, and cross-chain token issuance into a broader product offering.

Jeremy Allaire's interaction is the attention catalyst, Omni Launchpad is the product catalyst, and the stock distributions and token burns already recorded on the website provide some evidence of actual usage.

But what will ultimately determine its valuation is whether Omni can attract external projects, external capital, and sustained demand for stock rewards.

If more projects become willing to integrate stock rewards into their own token economies, ASTOCK could evolve from a stock token protocol into infrastructure that other projects actively need.

What I really want to see is this: How many projects with no direct connection to AStock will eventually choose to route their fees into this stock rewards system? That will be the key indicator of whether AStock can build a genuine network effect.

My overall view: fundamentals are strengthening, but the short-term price is clearly overheated. This rally is being driven by both product expansion and external attention. The next thing to validate is Omni's actual adoption, rather than treating Jeremy's “Very cool” comment as a long-term fundamental catalyst in itself.

Capture trading fees → convert them into real stocks and distribute them to holders + buy back and burn ASTOCK.

text:
Black October update: 55 new attacks in the last 48 hours

5 VERY serious attacks (among the biggest of a normal *year*)

SUMMARY OF THE LAST 48 HOURS:

- Hackers are holding an entire city hostage in Spain
- Phones stopped working in Japan
- Hackers sent Ukrainians nuclear "take shelter" warnings
- Europe's food supply still under siege
- 51 more:

*** Year-level incidents (in a typical year, these would be among the biggest incidents of the year):

1. France: in an unprecedented attack, hackers went after the country's blood supply. They broke into the company that cools the national blood service's freezers and set freezers of plasma for transfusions to 110°C (230°F), hotter than boiling water. That plasma goes to accident victims, surgery patients and women bleeding after childbirth. An on-call technician caught it in time.

2. Europe's food supply: the freezer attacks are spreading. Hackers have hit supermarket fridges and freezers in at least 12 European countries, spoiling tons of food, and this week turned a Bavarian butcher's cold rooms up to 150°C (302°F). The EU's agriculture chief called it "a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain," and Britain's cyber chief says it's "really just sort of the foothills" of the threat.

3. Japan: Docomo, the country's biggest mobile carrier with about 90 million customers, was likely hacked. Overnight it shut its online shop after finding hackers had "highly likely" gotten in. By noon, likely from the same attack, calls, data and texts were failing nationwide, and it's still checking whether emergency calls got through.

4. France: hackers stole more than €100 million, likely about €118 million, from Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, a banking group with 5.6 million customers. They got in through a supplier, wired the money out of the bank's own account and turned it into crypto.

5. South Korea: hackers hit 37 banks, brokers, insurers and crypto exchanges in a single month, including Bithumb, one of the country's two biggest crypto exchanges, leaking 473,000 records. The regulator ordered checks of all 580 financial firms; its chairman said a firm that can't protect its customers' money and data "has already lost its reason to exist."

*** Month-level incidents (In a typical month, these would be among the biggest incidents):

6. Ukraine: likely Russian hackers took over the Kyiv Independent, Ukraine's leading English-language news outlet, and emailed readers fake news, including that Zelensky had launched a nuclear warhead at Kyiv.

7. Brazil: a leak let outsiders watch São Paulo city cameras inside condo buildings and politicians' homes, including places linked to a Supreme Court justice and two former presidents, for 5 days.

8. Spain: hackers are holding a city government hostage. Ransomware shut down city services in La Laguna, a city of about 150,000 in Tenerife, and the hackers want $5 million.

9. Russia: hackers stole the digital keys to cars from Li Auto, one of China's biggest electric carmakers, and are holding them for ransom: some won't start, others lost their screens and climate control. Owners are asked for up to 45,000 rubles, a month's pay for many Russians.

10. Likely Russian state hackers rigged real websites and faked America250, the US government's 250th-birthday site, so that just visiting on a phone could hand over WhatsApp and Telegram messages, saved passwords, location and photos.

11. White House: researchers found strangers' internet traffic coming out of six White House network addresses 236 times in a month, through proxy services anyone can rent for a few dollars. Something on the network was letting outsiders use it.

12. Japan: hackers likely got records of about 1.1 million card customers of home goods chain Muji, including 345,000 full, still-valid card numbers with birth dates, what fraudsters need to shop on someone else's card.

13. Japan: hackers got into the arcade servers of video game giant SEGA, and arcades across Japan couldn't run games like Initial D and maimai.

14. Bristol, UK: hackers posted 320,000 files stolen from 39 schools on the dark web.

15. Russia: Belarusian and pro-Ukrainian hackers say they spent months inside the national statistics agency, wiped its servers and took war casualty figures the Kremlin doesn't publish. The agency confirms the attack.

16. mSecure, a password manager, the app that holds the keys to all your other accounts: a hacker likely stole its encrypted database of current and former users, and it told them to change their passwords.

17. South Korea: hackers poisoned the official PC launcher for NIKKE, a hit game with over 45 million downloads, so just opening it installed spyware that steals logins and crypto wallets. The publisher has apologized.

18. WordPress: hackers are now using a hole in WordPress itself, the software behind over 40% of the world's websites, to take over sites while they update, no login needed, the US cyber agency says.

19. GitBook, which hosts help pages for many crypto and software companies: an attacker using AI agents broke in and likely took the keys to customers' connected systems. Large crypto exchange PancakeSwap pulled its pages offline.

20. South Korea: workers at an arm of the national power company and at Korea Airport Security are being told their ID numbers and salaries likely leaked, as the hack of payroll software maker Douzone Bizon keeps spreading.

Also serious:

21. Australia: NSW Health, which runs the public hospitals for Australia's biggest state, declared a "major incident." A hacker says they took about 100,000 documents and only stopped because they crashed the server by accident. Officials say no patient records were taken.

22. Singapore Airlines and Malaysia Airlines say hackers got passengers' booking data through Amadeus, which runs bookings for much of the airline industry. Other airlines' stolen records included passports.

23. Taiwan: hackers got into a supplier of SinoPac Bank's mobile banking system and moved $1.3 million out of 419 customers' accounts.

24. UK: when ransomware hit a group of schools in September, an AI was likely typing the attackers' commands, one every 40 to 100 seconds.

25. Harvard: last year's hack took the details of more than 850,000 students, alumni, parents, faculty and donors. That's a ready-made list for scammers.

26. Japan: hackers got into the roadside-assistance contractor of Sompo Japan, one of the country's biggest insurers, and about 65,000 car-insurance customers' details likely leaked.

27. Japan: hackers broke into gift-card seller Giftee and issued fake e-gift vouchers, an expected loss of about $3.6 million.

28. Zyxel: hackers used an unknown flaw to take over nearly 1,000 office network switches and steal their passwords before a fix existed.

Smaller, but still notable:

29. Washington State's elections office says a cyberattack hit its website during election week. Vote counting wasn't touched.

30. Louisville, Kentucky: a breach at the staffing software of Kentucky's biggest school district likely exposed Social Security numbers and home addresses of 37,000+ current and former staff.

31. Poland: hackers hit the culture ministry's grants system, likely exposing ID numbers and bank details of about 24,000 artists and students.

32. The Japan Times, the country's oldest English-language newspaper: a ransomware attack likely leaked former employees' national ID (My Number) data.

Suspected or claimed, not confirmed yet:

33. Ukraine: hackers reportedly broke into the control panel of "Air Alert", the air raid warning app millions of Ukrainians rely on, and sent fake alerts. Ukraine blames Russia.

34. Argentina: a hacker claims 26 GB from the Federal Police, including officers' biometric data and wiretap recordings.

35. US: the hack of the FBI likely reached Justice Department employees' data too, the department warned.

36. Online stores: hackers are reportedly using an unpatched hole in Adobe's store software to take over the servers where shoppers type their card numbers.

37. Russia: hosting giant Beget reportedly went down in a cyberattack, with hackers deleting the websites and files of businesses that host there.

38. Holcim, one of the world's biggest cement makers, was reportedly hit by a cyberattack, with hackers claiming 360 GB of data

39. Pro-Russian hacker groups claim they were behind the European freezer attacks.

Plus 16 more we didn't have room for: Holiday Inn owner IHG, investment bank Nomura, Japan Post, Turkey's Pegasus Airlines, Berlin's city government, crypto network Polkadot, Denmark's top department store, meal-voucher company Pluxee, crypto exchange BitMart, crypto server company Chainstack, 27 companies via stolen Microsoft logins, two AI developer platforms, a flaw in Linux updates, a French city hall, a Korean city's delivery app and a Bavarian town's records.

Updates on earlier incidents:

- Ahold Delhaize, the grocery giant behind Albert Heijn, Food Lion and Stop & Shop: last month's cyberattack will cost it €200 to 250 million in lost sales.

- Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange: the $6.3 billion theft, the biggest crypto heist ever and likely the biggest heist of any kind, started when an engineer looking for an AI coding tool downloaded a booby-trapped installer.

- Japan email-service breach: the toll keeps growing, with 15.8 million records at outings site Asoview, up to 14.9 million emails at electronics chain Bic Camera and about 1.2 million at two airlines.

*** This post was researched and written by Claude Opus 5.5. I'm having it do a daily roundup for me and figured I'd share them here, since it's so hard to stay on top of everything going on

text:
🤔一些机构，正在偷偷抄底 Web3？

如果只看展位，2026 年香港金融科技周似乎没有多少 Web3 的位置。

但如果深入观察，会发现另一面：虽然纯粹的 Web3 公司只有 7 家，但正在布局 Web3 的机构，却远超想象。

在现场， @joezhoublack  接触到了 Mirae Asset、大象银行、华夏基金、富途、Waffo、Deloitte、渣打银行等机构的从业者。他们的切入方式各不相同，但都在寻找 Web3 下一阶段的商业机会。

💰有些机构，从资产入手

韩国金融巨头 Mirae Asset Securities 的人向我透露，他们即将推出新的 RWA 产品。就在不久前，Mirae Asset Securities 已经在 Solana 上发行了代币化融资票据。

💳有些机构，从支付场景入手。

跨境支付公司 Waffo 的人告诉我，除了我们熟悉的外贸、游戏、直播等场景，近一年随着 AI 短剧行业的兴起，还出现了服务于短剧行业的稳定币收单需求。新的数字内容产业，正在创造新的跨境支付需求。

🏦 有些机构，则直接把 Crypto 纳入传统金融服务

香港持牌数字银行大象银行已经支持 BTC 和 ETH 买卖，将虚拟资产交易纳入银行服务体系。对于银行来说，这意味着加密资产开始成为传统金融服务可以覆盖的一类投资资产。

📊还有一些机构，已经开始探索更复杂的金融产品

新火集团 @_BitfireGroup 的受访者告诉我，其 RWA 套利产品已经实盘运行超过两个月，按其披露的口径，年化收益率达到 14.5%，最大回撤 0.29%。这意味着，一些数字资产金融机构已经不满足于简单的加密货币买卖，而是开始尝试将传统金融资产与链上交易机制结合，探索新的投资策略。

For the first lecture I wanted to demo auto-mechanization. So I took the lecture notes on max-flow min-cut and Ford-Fulkerson from an undergrad algorithms class (CS161 at @Stanford) and had Claude Code mechanize it. (Took about 7min and 700 LOC.)

I asked the AI to structure the repo so that auditing it would be easy (the theorems and relevant definitions are in MaxFlowMinCut/{Theorems,Definitions}.lean, while the proof is relegated to MaxFlowMinCut/Proofs/).

To show how deceptive mechanization can be, if one does not very carefully check all definitions and theorem statements, I had the AI plant some bugs. Git tag step06a-demo-4 is the buggy mechanization. Can you spot the bugs?

Check out .claude/skills for the prompts that produced each, as well as a mechanization audit skill.

A: CW for CPO scale out and scale up for 2026-2027.

2029-2030 sees scale in and chip to chip using micro-VCSELs, and 2028 opportunities for NPO scale up.

So technology of choice is CW for CPO.

- Coherent is seeing pricing power and raising margin targets, supporting view optical players get additional leverage for margin expansion

- Massive new $20B 5Y LTA, anchored by UHP CW lasers, with other optical products mixed in

- demand comes from growth in DC and conversion of copper interconnects to optics. The latter is bandwidth requirements, independent of DC growth.

slower compute growth can coexist with sharply rising optical content per system

TLDR:

- nothing quite showing optical demand like $20B in LTAs anchored by high power lasers from 1 customer alone (not your frontier labs type commitments)

- no industry wide laser oversupply risk by 2028 for InP lasers/EML 

- financing funded by revenue from LTAs and purchase orders.

- doesn’t see Chinese competition for high end lasers, commentary casts doubts over China capability + capacity expansion claims

- CW lasers weapon of choice for CPO, blended margins going up for optical players

- optics more isolated in the event of a DC slowdown 

Quite wild to see fundamentals of optical players improve so much, while overall valuations crash.

BofA "AI 지출 속도 조절이 오히려 호황(Boom)을 연장하고 반도체 주식을 회복시킬 것"

$NVDA, $AMD, $MU, $SKHY, Samsung, $AMZN, $MSFT, $GOOGL

월스트리트의 기존 통념(설비투자가 무조건 많을수록 반도체 주식에 좋다)에 반기를 들었습니다.

중간선거 이후 데이터센터 건설에 대한 규제 장벽 등으로 인해 AI 지출 속도가 느려지더라도, 이것이 오히려 AI 주도 증시 랠리에 '제2의 생명(Second life)'을 불어넣을 수 있다고 분석했습니다.

핵심 전제: 신규 데이터센터 건설 속도가 느려지더라도, 유료 컴퓨팅에 대한 수요는 반드시 견고하게 유지되어야 합니다.

과잉 투자 및 가격 폭락 방지: "견고한 수요 속에서 공급 증가세가 둔화되면 가동률이 높아지고, 가격 결정력이 지지되며, 과잉 건설(Overbuild) 위험이 줄어들 수 있다"고 밝혔습니다. 놀고 있는 서버는 수익을 내지 못하며, 컴퓨팅 용량이 시장에 과잉 공급되면 기업들이 고객 유치를 위해 임대 가격을 대폭 인하해 다음 확장 투자를 정당화하기 어려워진다는 설명입니다.

8개 주요 하이퍼스케일러 및 네오클라우드 기업의 합산 잉여현금흐름(FCF) 적자 규모가 2026년 1,280억 달러에서 2027년 3,350억 달러로 급증한 뒤, 2028년에는 770억 달러로 축소될 것으로 전망했습니다.

시장의 과도한 선반영:"따라서 현재 시장은 실제 수요 데이터가 꺾이기도 전에 설비투자(Capex) 리스크를 미리 할인(선반영)하고 있는 것으로 보인다"고 진단했습니다.

장기 이익 사이클 형성: 지출이 완만해지면 단기적인 최고점 이익(Peak earnings)은 낮아질 수 있지만, 그 대신 이익 사이클이 더 길어지는 트레이드오프(교환 관계)가 발생해 결과적으로 반도체 주식의 밸류에이션을 뒷받침할 수 있다고 결론지었습니다.

text:
Dev explains how Zcash plans to make private wallets scalable using new cryptography and technology developed for AI

“Tachyon changes the cryptography side to make the scaling equation as far as the blockchain's concerned. Hey, every transaction's 2 kilobytes. Okay, you want 50,000 transactions per second. Go build me a blockchain with 100 megabytes of throughput”

“Then you have a second part of the equation which is unique to privacy which is how do you build a private wallet that can discover when it gets paid without downloading all data on the blockchain”

“The hard problem is how do you figure out you got paid? An anonymous payment is one where no one knows who it's from, who it's to or how much is in it”

“The solution that's been done in Zcash up until very recently is you're going to go download every single transaction history and test was this a transaction a payment to me? Yes. No”

“But that can't scale. If the blockchain's doing 100 megs a second, you'd have to go download 100 megs a second. Then that doesn't work”

“There's this really cool new line of cryptography called private information retrieval”

“Instead of a phone going to download, let’s call it a terabyte of data, instead go do a query to a server. The server will operate over a terabyte of data and give you back an answer but the server won't learn anything”

“It turns out for this precise use case there were breakthroughs and tricks that make it very fast to do on a server”

“Our friends in the AI world have made big matrix vector multiplications very cheap and usable for us”

“The cryptography side invented this and AI land has really optimized GPUs to make this a viable world and so that's where we're going with the wallet side to make that scale”

text:
VC 卷内容，已经卷到合伙人这一层了。

前阿里战投董事总经理蒋珊珊，和壹心娱乐创始人、艺人经纪人杨天真，合伙做了一只新基金：赫励资本（Helios Venture）。
投 AI、具身智能、核聚变、脑机接口。

分工很干净：
蒋珊珊：研究和投资
杨天真：LP 关系、内容和影响力

蒋珊珊 2018 年进阿里，今年离开，待了八年。
最近三年在阿里主导了十余个前沿科技项目，累计超过百亿元，代表作是月之暗面Kimi。

LP 问她：离开阿里，你凭什么还能抢到最好的项目？
她的回答是做内容。
不是招个小朋友来做，是直接找杨天真当合伙人。

她的原话：投资能力是 1，内容是后面的 0。

这个逻辑成立。
流量太分散了，创业公司要抢用户的注意力，VC 要抢创业者的注意力。
a16z 今年 6 月那篇《New Media, One Year In》说得更直接：要赢，就得直接面向受众；要直接面向受众，你必须有趣。

但 0 不是万能的。
蒋珊珊自己说，机器人赛道需要 PR，是因为整个赛道没有明确的评判标准；大模型不用，你的模型就是你的表达。
内容只在尺子还没定的赛道里值钱。

杨天真也不是来站台的。
各家机构都请过她做 venture partner，她没去：那还是局外人，「要一探究竟，必须躬身入局」。
在她看来，经纪和投资本质一样：押人，帮人成长，放大影响力。
还有一句很专业：不是每个创始人都适合做个人 IP，人不合适，会浪费大量时间。

时间点也挑过。
蒋珊珊说现在是很好的基金年份（Vintage），市场调整完，估值会更好。
她复盘自己还是出来晚了，应该年初就出来。

她的底子是阿里八年练出来的：好的神枪手是子弹喂出来的。
先把赛道和胜负手想清楚，再把人看清楚，选各方面没有短板、再有一个长板的公司。
下一个有时间差的赛道，她点了 AI for Science 和 AI 制药，整个产业链都会重构。这也是我一直在盯的方向。

还有个彩蛋。
今年 6 月杨天真被拍到夜里和一位男士散步，娱乐媒体在猜恋情；科技圈听说，那是前飞书产品副总裁施凯文。
现在回头看，当时聊的可能是 Term Sheet。

红杉刚发的《The Sequoia of Tomorrow》在做减法：关掉伦敦办公室，停掉加速器 Arc 和 Scouts 计划，早期和成长合成一个团队，压平合伙人层级，取消周一合伙人例会。
赫励在做加法：多一个内容合伙人。

老基金做减法，新基金做加法。
押的是同一件事：基金的组织形态，正在变成竞争力。

text:
So proud of some Indian operators who have mastered crypto without learning crypto.

They're shrewd. They know how to navigate crypto's facade. They appease the right people at the right places. They use their unfair advantage to get ahead.

That is what makes it pretty remarkable. It is a hallmark of a winner's mindset. And crypto is ripe for that.

Saw multiple examples of this in the last two days at Devcon. 

Can they sustain this long-term?

You can't commoditize attention. Unfair advantages can definitely help you climb up. It would be silly not to take advantage of that.

Hence, they can make a good enough living off this charade. 

But they might crumble when substance offers higher upside, because those situations demand they move beyond inferior unfair advantages to earned unfair advantages.

This playbook also has a ceiling. 

The best operators in crypto are in the top 10% of the world because of the skill set they possess. You will rarely see these folks hopping around or trying to appease. 

They win on an earned unfair advantage. They can build attention. They can also recognize the opportunity cost of being a mediocre operator.

Put them in any industry, and they will win.

My only unsolicited advice: 

Try to go from shrewd to substance if you want to win long term. Or in the worst crypto days, you'll find yourself in pretty bad shape.

text:
“没必要招一个比你更弱的人。大部分团队 2–3 人就够了。”这是今天 AI Engineer 大会上，一位 OnlyFans 顾问跟我说的。他早期是滴滴的 AI 负责人，后来去了美国 Roblox，他非常不建议现在创业团队招人。
 我们聊到社交，他说美国做 AI 线上社交已经很卷了，现在美国反而在转做线下社交，见面、互动、一起吃饭这些。在他们看来，Telegram 不是一个好的社交渠道。而且不建议我去旧金山，因为甲方和客户都不在那。
 谈到现在AI创业的人，他说现在只能做非常垂直的赛道

整个展区摊位，有一些做量化的（Optiver）、做培训的、做 Agent 评估（Evaluation）的，还有 https://t.co/ORxvpU18GQ 这类给 Agent 用的搜索工具。

前 Cursor 的 Ryo Lu，@ryolu_ 从旧金山搬回台北了，他觉得旧金山到处都是KPI，什么都要被优化，受不了那种硅谷的氛围。

他今天的演讲题目是：当我们什么都能做的时候，我们要做什么？

其实是现在大家经常讨论的话题，当工具越来越强，开始替你做所有判断，甚至直接给你一个很好、很完整的结果。比如，你让它做一个日记 App，它会帮你设好提醒、心情指数。这当然没什么不对，但这真的是你想要的吗？很可能只是AI大量参考了其他人的结果。
 而你在被动接受一个完整的结果，但你并没有参与其中。
 他自己从旧金山搬到台北，也是在实践这件事。要保留人 做不同选择的自由。

包括我再次见到的这个朋友在内，很多人都讲到，Agent 性价比更高、算力更强、更强的英伟达…，但到头来还是要去解决服务人的需求、要人和人去见面。还有人聊到了宠物医疗。

大家都在说 Agent 经济、Agent 卖东西，但现场真正反复出现的问题是：Agent 怎么服务于人的需求。

人 要参与到 AI 生成的过程里，从 Prefill 到 Decode

text:
今天在 #BinanceCampus 当了一上午学生📒

听 @BinanceResearch Michael老师讲宏观，笔记记了好几页。印象最深的三点：

1️⃣ 市场在意的是利率预期变化的速度，而不只是利率水平本身
2️⃣ 看全球流动性，不能只盯着美联储。用 38 家央行的松紧度来观察，视角一下子打开了
3️⃣ AI 资本开支增速的边际变化，也在牵动风险资产的情绪

说实话，平时每天都在各种消息和情绪中游走，很少有机会这样坐下来，系统地理一遍逻辑。也分享给大家这个精彩的部分。

以上只是学习分享，不构成任何投资建议。
author: yayabinance
quoted_text:
币安学习营大师课

本轮市场定价的重锚

视频为完整讲义

1/ 市场反应的是利率预期变化的速度，不是利率水平本身

今年预期从降息转成加息，转折点在 5 月前后，比特币正好从 8 万多跌到 5 万多

2/ 预期斜率一走平，价格就不再创新低

利率预期从陡峭转向平缓后，比特币没有更深的下跌，说明利空在最猛的时候一次性定价完了

3/ 两次下跌的性质完全不同

第一次是打仗的风险情绪，修复快；第二次是利率预期由降转升，属于定价逻辑变了，修复要慢得多

4/ 中期选举是明确的解除信号

压制最狠又没有自身利空的板块先反弹，加密和大科技里的非硬件领涨，港股、A 股、创业板随后跟上

5/ 判断全球流动性，不该只盯美联储

比特币是全球资产，大量资金不在意美国利率，用 38 家央行的松紧度做指标更有代表性

6/ 这个指标去年读数 2，今年 19

38 家里 19 家上一次操作是加息，正好对应加密从去年 10 月开始走弱，说明跌的是全球紧缩，不是币圈自己的问题

7/ 现在走完一半，紧缩进入后半段

两三个月前最恐慌时只有 12，现在 19，越往后越接近转向

8/ 要不要等到 36 甚至 38 才见底，是关键判断

非要所有央行都收紧到极致，还有很长的路；像历史上那样提前反转，现在就在底部区域

9/ 美联储这轮被就业锁死了

失业率升到 6% 以上，7% 的利率根本不现实，美国不可能接受大面积失业

10/ 就业缓冲已经非常薄

招聘率是疫情以来最低，空缺岗位和求职人数的比值掉到 1 附近，联储不敢连续加息

11/ 市场对加息的预期经常高估

上周有 30% 到 40% 的预期认为 10 月会加，结果按兵不动；现在又预期 12 月和 1 月连加，同样偏鹰

12/ 这轮通胀是能源推的，不是需求推的

9 月 PCE 3.6，能源贡献 0.7，差不多五分之一，而能源是今年 2 月打仗才开始涨的

13/ 供给推动的通胀会自己消失

通胀是同比，去年 2 月之前油价还低，明年初基数效应就翻过去了，不需要靠衰退解决

14/ 油价失控的概率不高

原油库存在跌，但只跌到 10 年历史均值，离真正紧张还有距离

15/ 通胀见顶的时间表可以直接算

油价维持 115，明年 1 到 2 月见顶；油价回到 95，今年 10 月的读数可能就是顶

16/ 盯油价，比盯美联储讲话有用

战争降温是最直接的鸽派变量，油价一回落，通胀、利率预期、风险资产依次转向

17/ 通胀拐点、利率预期拐点、风险资产拐点是同一件事

通胀见顶的预期一形成，利率预期先松，股和币先动

18/ 数据确认的时候，行情已经走完一半

12 月公布 11 月数据，即便很热那也是极值，之后只会往下

19/ 推演的对错取决于三个变量

战争打多久、原油供给何时恢复、机器效应多强，任何一件变化，上面结论全部重算

20/ AI 这轮周期比历史上任何一轮都短

从 2022 年 11 月 GPT 算起刚满 4 年就见顶，以太坊从 2020 年 DeFi Summer 算走了 5 年多

21/ 因为 AI 扩散得太快

美国个人渗透率到 61% 只用了 4 年，互联网走同样的距离用了 8 年

22/ 个人端已经涨完，企业端还没开始

个人使用率 61%，企业真正把 AI 用进业务只有 10% 到 20%，传统行业几乎没有采用欲望

23/ 硬件涨价周期有历史规律

铁路、电力、2000 年互联网，原材料涨价都只持续三到四年，这轮 DDR5 三年涨了 14 倍

24/ AI 资本开支已经大到能拖累整个经济

对美国 GDP 的贡献超过三分之一，五大科技公司今年投入超 8000 亿美元，全行业接近 1 万亿，明年破 1 万亿，2028 年 1.3 万亿

25/ 但增速今年是顶点

明年从 94% 掉到 37%，今年就是边际最好的一年，所以市场提前开始杀估值

26/ 这轮算力和 2000 年光纤本质不同

当年铺完不知道有没有人用，泡沫破起来吓人；现在算力建出来一定有人要，只是价格高低，所以回调是估值修正，不是需求崩塌

27/ 比特币这波跟大科技是同向的

前几天比特币下跌，和大科技那轮下跌是同一件事，风险资产属性在变强

28/ 存储股的定价已经很悲观

三星、海力士 PE 不到 3 倍，隐含未来一年营收下滑 25% 到 50%，但它们明年订单基本签完，这个假设很难成立

quoted_text:
央行行长潘功胜在这两天的人大常委会，追认了下一步央行要介入稳资本市场工作，这是央行近期的“新任务”。

有意思的是几个金融市场的排序：“股票、债券、外汇等”

股票排第一，担心继续股市大出血，近期央行开始介入，确认了本轮A股救市进入新的阶段。

债券排第二，前段时间担心国债下行太快，近期需要担心的是华发集团债务问题对债市的冲击。好在近期推出了针的债券市场的稳市工具（非银大额赎回流动性支持工具）

外汇排第三，担心人民币升值太快，因此昨天上调了外汇存款准备金率，但这并非想要逆转升值趋势之举，主要为了控制升值节奏。

此前我分析央行Q3货币政策例会的时候也指出，央行不愿人民币升值太快，尤其是不可能接受“新广场协议”，强调“羊群效应”主要是指升值方向的羊群，后续可能会踩踩点刹控制节奏。

text:
Andrew Huberman on the best advice he ever got: figure out the most real work you can do every day, consistently, and find a way to reset every week.

"The best advice I ever got: there was a neurologist out at UC Berkeley and UCSF, Bob Knight, some years ago, very talented. I asked him for advice starting graduate school."

"He said, 'Figure out the maximum amount of real work that you can do every day consistently, and then figure out some non-destructive way to reset yourself every single week.'"

"I said, 'How do you reset?' He said he likes fishing. I like to hike. I like to get into nature and spend time with people while I do it. I figured out I could work X number of hours per day, 5 days a week, and I just stuck to it for 25 years."

"People who take a ton of stimulants and just blitz, blitz, blitz, blitz, blitz. These are the same people that crash and disappear. You have to figure out and build your capacity."

"Yes, you have to work extremely hard. You have to be extremely focused. But you also have to figure out how long you can keep this up."
