AI is the best thing to ever happen to $BTC and $ETH, and we are about to watch it all unfold, here is why:

As technology becomes more political, neutral technology becomes more valuable.

AI has changed the risk profile of technology investing in an incredibly short amount of time. So much so that today, in the big ‘26, memory businesses cannot even be called businesses so much as strategic assets caught in the middle of a technological arms race between two increasingly uncertain superpowers. 

AKA: The better Chinese AI tech gets, the more investors have to price geopolitical uncertainty into U.S. AI infrastructure. The better the U.S. responds, the more Chinese assets end up facing the same problem.

This is where Bitcoin and Ethereum become interesting as two highly liquid, geographically distributed, immutable assets that no single company issues and no single government controls.

TLDR: They are the ONLY major assets structurally incapable of being pulled into the wars to come.

“But wait..what about macro.”

Historically, this is fair, because BTC and ETH have traded like high beta tech since the marginal buyer was a speculator borrowing against a calm world.

But in case you have not noticed, we are not in a calm world anymore. 

Let’s break it down:

A tech equity is a claim on cash flows, and cash flows are now hostage to policy, example: 

- Export licenses now set Nvidia’s addressable market. 
- Subsidy regimes are what decide where the fabs rise. 
- a single directive can immediately reroute a supply chain. 

Essentially, the better centralized technology gets, the more strategic it becomes and the more strategic it becomes, the less it belongs to its shareholders and the more it belongs to national interests.

Bitcoin and Ethereum on the other hand, are built different (literally), they are truly sovereign, and highly liquid. Every escalation elsewhere that adds risk premium to strategic tech adds monetary premium to that sovereignty.

As people grok this,  the marginal buyer is likely to shift from a speculator chasing tech beta to an allocator effectively purchasing insurance against the political capture of technology.

We will look back on this AI race as the moment the world changed its mind about BTC and ETH, where for the very first time,  “volatile tech” changed its mask and became “sanctuary tech.“

A store of value for an era when value itself became a weapon.

A return to Satoshi’s promise.

🚨Turmoil erupts in Paraguay as one bank’s collapse spirals into a NATIONAL CRISIS.

Ueno Bank, the country’s largest digital bank, has been seized by the Central bank after its solvency ratio plunged below half the legal minimum, leaving nearly 3 MILLION customers unable to access accounts, cards and transfers.

That’s almost 60% of Paraguay’s adult population.

Angry citizens have now taken to the streets demanding access to their money.

The disruption has spread beyond the bank- 13 mutual funds have reportedly frozen withdrawals, and trading in Ueno’s bonds has been suspended.

Nearly $380 MILLION belonging to the state pension fund is caught in the crisis.

The problem is how deeply Ueno was embedded in everyday payments.

It handled two-thirds of card payments at major stores. With those services frozen, Paraguay’s main importers’ association describes retail activity as “semi-paralyzed.”

Customers have been told they can initially recover up to $1,700, with no payment date given.

The political fallout is mounting with the Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo resigning, and authorities having arrested 8 executives from the bank over suspected breach of trust.

Ze people at Citrini shared about ethereum:0x808507121b80c02388fad14726482e061b8da827 and here's why its bullish: 

- Citrini Research put PENDLE in its tokenization basket on 8 Oct 2026 and called it a “second-order RWA trade” on Wall Street’s move on-chain

- Second-order means you do not have to pick which issuer wins. Every tokenized asset that pays a yield needs a place to price and trade that yield. Pendle is that place, whoever the issuer is

- The core thesis: the money from tokenization flows to the plumbing, the protocols that earn fees when tokenized stocks, bonds and loans get traded, borrowed and used as collateral. Citrini does not assume BTC and ETH make new highs on this theme. “There are better expressions.”

- Citrini’s filter for the basket: how the protocol earns money, who collects the fees, and whether token holders get a share. “Fees matter more than activity.” Pendle passes all three: ~$1.3B in RWA-linked TVL, 80% of protocol fees going to PENDLE buybacks, $1.61M bought back from Jul to Sep 2026

- The basket is concentrated in fee-earning infrastructure: ETHFI, AAVE, UNI, PENDLE and ONDO are the five named picks, alongside Securitize, Circle and Coinbase on the equity side. Pendle is the only one whose product is the interest-rate market itself

- The SEC’s innovation exemption for tokenized stock trading (17 Sep 2026), Robinhood Chain’s stock tokens, and Partners Group, Franklin Templeton and Janus Henderson already on Pendle’s RWA Insights series. The pipes are being connected to Pendle

text:
History was made last night.

For months, we were saying that 2026 was the most consequential midterm election of our lifetimes. 

Unfortunately, we were right. Sometimes history is to be celebrated; other times, it is to be mourned. Always, it must be reckoned with.

2026 was not simply a blue wave; it was a blue tsunami. It was an ass kicking. It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election. It was a Watergate-level repudiation. What happened, and why? What are the consequences, and where on earth do we go from here?

When all the votes were counted, the problem wasn’t turnout. Instead, our voters, Republicans, Libertarians, Independents, showed up and voted, and rejected our candidates, voting Democrat instead. We’ve lost the House. We’ve lost the Senate. When all is said and done, we will have lost eight to 10 Senate seats.

We lost in historically red states, like South Carolina and North Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. We lost in purple states, like Michigan, and New Hampshire, and Georgia. And we just barely won by just a single point in bright red states like Florida and Louisiana, and then there’s Texas.

Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas. In the Lone Star State, we lost every single statewide election. For weeks, I had been publicly warning on this podcast that we were in very real danger of losing everything in Texas. Far too few believed that was possible. I am very, very sorry that it came to pass. Texas has not had a Democrat governor since 1994. We haven’t had a Democrat senator since 1993. Now we’ll have both.

Why were the results so overwhelming? Pundits and analysts will break down the results for weeks or months or even years to come, but several things are already evident today.

Years ago, the very best political advice I ever got was from Heidi. She said, “It’s not about you. It’s about them. It’s about their kids, their families, their hopes, their dreams, their futures.” Too many politicians forget that.

Take the state of Kansas, for example, a state that has not elected a Democrat senator since 1932. It just did. Here’s what exit polling showed were the top issues in Kansas.

Number one, cost of living, energy, and groceries. That was listed as number one by 30.6 percent of voters. 
Corruption. Number two, 18.5%. 
The cost of the Iran war, 10.1%. 
The candidates are terrible, 7.9%. 
The Canada trade war, 7.6%. 
The GOP didn’t do enough to support Trump, 6.6%. 
Republicans didn’t pass the Save America Act, 5.6%. 
Trump’s focus on monuments, 5.5%, and data centers and AI, 3.8%.

The top issue, cost of living, is very real. Too many in politics dismissed it. They didn’t understand. They pointed to the macro numbers showing the stock markets soaring, median income at record highs, and poverty at record lows. Those data are true, but they don’t tell all of the story.

Here are some stats that are a lot more real and personal. Spam, Hormel’s processed meat substitute, broke record sales, selling 113 million cans last year. That is nearly as much spam as was sold during the entirety of World War II. 29 percent of Americans have used buy now, pay later for groceries this year. That’s double the share just two years ago.

In August, banks repossessed 42% more homes than they did last year. In 2024, car repossessions topped 2.3 million, above the 2009 peak in the middle of the Great Financial Crisis. In 2025, 6% of 401k holders took hardship withdrawals, paying penalties. That is a record, and triple the norm.

And here’s one that’s really stunning. Americans made more than 75 million paid plasma donations in 2026. That’s another record. That means 200,000 Americans every single day, with a needle in their arm, just to pay for groceries.

That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn’t understand or they didn’t care. Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high.

Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long. It should have been brief, decisive, and over. It needs to end, and we should never, under any circumstances, give the Ayatollah billions of dollars.

There’s a very real economic disconnect. Our K-shaped economy is a yawning divide. Last year, we saw the world’s very first trillionaire, a modern-day Thomas Edison, at the very same time that millions were struggling to feed their families. Data centers being constructed were turning billionaires into centibillionaires, while simultaneously the average American’s electricity bill went up 30% in the last five years.

Understandably, people were pissed off, and elected Republicans didn’t do enough to address their very real pain.

So, what do we do now? We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people’s lives, and we need to deal with the consequences.

Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue. As we sit here today, I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas. That’s not something I ever thought I would say.

We can be certain that the Democrats in Austin and in Washington will overshoot. In Texas, they will try to raise taxes dramatically. They may even try to adopt a state income tax, or even a California wealth tax. They will try to shut down the energy industry, destroying jobs across our state. They will embrace the radical transgender agenda. They will persecute those they perceive to be enemies, especially Elon Musk.

And in Washington, they will attack Trump every single day, constantly. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, his family, cabinet members, business leaders, open persecution, and nonstop retaliation. Make no mistake. Nationally, the radicals are in charge. The communists and the Islamists who have taken over the Democrat Party have now taken over the United States Congress. They will be unleashed.

Sadly, that means many Americans will be hurt. Texans will be hurt. Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business. Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI.

The economic results will be dramatic. Over $700 billion in new projects are scheduled to start in the next year. If the Democrats shut them all down, our country will very likely go into a recession. That will suit the Democrats just fine. They’ll just blame it all on Donald Trump.

In the next two years, we need to do two things.

One, fight the madness. I will work with Democrats when they’re willing to be reasonable. Last night, I called James Talarico. I congratulated him on his very impressive victory. It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas.

So, if there are things like flood relief for the Hill Country, or trying to get the space academy to Texas, he and I will work together. But if the newly elected radicals push policies that hurt Texas, raising taxes, destroying jobs, opening the border, releasing violent criminals, threatening our children, undermining our constitutional rights, I will fight with all of my strength to defend Texas and to defend the Constitution.

And number two, we need to rebuild, getting behind policies that directly benefit the constituents we lost.

There’s a complicated story, no doubt, of what happened on Election Day, but as I see it, the key constituencies we lost were blue-collar voters, what had rightly become the core base of our party, Evangelical Christians, who didn’t show up with the same numbers and fervor as prior elections, farmers and ranchers. Tragically, we alienated rural America. Young people, who excitedly had voted Republican in 2024, and who shifted hard blue this cycle. And of course, Hispanics.

For Hispanics, there’s a strong overlap with young people and blue-collar workers. In 2024, just two years ago, I was proud to carry Hispanics statewide in Texas by six points, and we swung the Rio Grande Valley red for the first time in a century. It can be done, but in this election, those Hispanic voters overwhelmingly went back Democrat. We have got to turn that around.

And for young people, we need to be the party of the future. We need to champion policies that expand their future. Our two single biggest legislative accomplishments of the past two years, Trump Accounts and the school choice tax credit, which will unleash tens of billions of dollars in new scholarships for kids, are generationally powerful. I was proud to author both of those transformational policies, and yet too few candidates all across the country ran on that record.

Too few voters were even aware of what we’d accomplished for their kids and their future. But we need to build. We need to expand to continue creating a new investor class for hundreds of millions of Americans, help everyone, every American, become an owner, to have real skin in the game, to create new generations of capitalists ready to reject socialism.

People voted as they did because they were angry. Ironically, the Democrats that they elected are going to advance policies that will make affordability worse. The Democrats want gas prices higher. They want to ban gasoline engines altogether. Their extreme environmental mandates will drive up food prices and the prices of everything else.

But hear me now: we will bring Texas back. I am filled with hope and optimism. Texas will be red again. We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain’t us. Texas is still Texas.

We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party, not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives. The way we built the Texas economic miracle in the first place, and we will build and rebuild America as well.

When the zealots overreach, and they will, we will stand ready to lead in the direction of freedom, of prosperity, of safety, and security, and common sense. We will return to a new dawn of freedom in America.

It is dark right now, but it is always darkest before the dawn, and morning is coming. That is my fervent prayer, and that is my commitment to you.

text:
One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. 

So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us."

Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.  

There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. 

But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. 

Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were:

1) End the war
2) Focus on cost of living/inflation
3) Put America First
4) Change our relationship to Israel

Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.)

In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. 

The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. 

If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest.

But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.

I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

text:
Perp 价差套利第三周，一些新发现

【Arcus × Lighter RH】

图里都是我筛选后留下的标的。
其他的我已经帮大家亏过钱了，可以忽略。

3 组账号，10-23 到 11-05：
· 1303 笔来回
· 平均每笔净赚 1.85 bps
· 胜率 73%

各标的：

NVDA：笔数多，滑点小，三组账号都赚
SNDK：每笔 2.54 bps，开仓滑点偏大
SPY：滑点最小，单笔不多，但很稳
AAPL：每笔不算高，但一直是正的
QQQ：单笔偏薄，但也能做
AMD：每笔 4.92 bps，胜率 92%
这周有财报，波动比较大，后面可能回落
CRCL：机会最多，也最容易亏大的
最差一笔亏 36 bps，要限仓

【Ondo × Lighter RH】

11-03 才开始，跑了不到两天：
· 31 笔来回
· 平均每笔 4.08 bps
· 胜率 71%

按官方文档，11-13 手续费促销结束后，一个来回要多 2 bps，同样的成交每笔大约只剩 2 bps。

已经提前移除一批标的，滑点太大、毒单比较多：

MSFT、COIN、AMZN、SKHY、CRWV
MU、AAPL、META、XAG

数据也能看出来。成交后 1 秒，Lighter 价格往不利方向走：

移除的：平均 3.11 bps，88% 的成交不利
留下的：平均 0.80 bps，59% 的成交不利

样本还很少，移除的只有 16 笔，但我不想拿更多钱去验证了。

还在跑的里面：

目前最好：GOOGL，6 笔全赢，每笔 7.52 bps，滑点不到 1 bps
应该也可以：QQQ、SPY，滑点小
滑点偏大：CRCL 7.39、SNDK 6.94、AMD 5.68

【发现一：Arcus 直接调合约充值，比前端便宜】

前端走 Relay：每笔固定扣约 $0.095

做了个自动Rebalance的脚本，直接调合约：gas 约 $0.019，足额到账，约 8 秒入账

再也不用手动去充提，省时省力

【发现二：Rust 重构到底带来了什么】

Python → Rust 同期对比：

循环卡顿：253 次 → 1 次
最长卡顿：1778 ms → 81 ms
每条行情处理：49 µs → 9 µs
每条行情占用 CPU：227 µs → 61 µs
Lighter腿对冲回执中位：359 ms → 322 ms

实打实改善的是尾部卡顿和 CPU 余量，p50 延迟提升不太明显。

【发现三：美股开盘那 5 分钟，最好停掉】

开盘 0–5 分钟的毒单明显更多。两周实盘 2263 笔对冲：

平时滑点中位：1.2–1.5 bps
开盘 0–5 分钟：3.19 bps

两周最差的 5 笔对冲，全部出现在开盘后 90 秒内，最差一笔滑点 43 bps。

现在我的做法：开盘前 5 分钟到开盘后 5 分钟，不开仓。

【发现四：不同标的，单笔开多大比较安全？】

几百刀以内，单笔大小基本不影响滑点，实盘整体都在 2.0–2.2 bps。

再往上按 Lighter 盘口推算，下面这个规模内，对冲一次额外滑点大约在 0.5 bps 以内：

SPY、QQQ：$10k
AMD、AAPL：$5k
NVDA、SNDK：$2k
CRCL：$200

【Arcus 积分大致可以这么算】

积分 ≈ 0.19 × 交易量（万刀）+ 0.18 × OI 持仓（千刀·天）

比如一周刷 5 万刀，同时一直持有 1000 刀仓位：
0.19 × 5 + 0.18 × 7 ≈ 2.2 分

用 4 组账号、3 周的 10 个数据拟合，平均偏差约 4.6%。
只是经验公式，不是官方规则。

🍉  研究了Anthropic和OpenAI的薪资结构，我知道Cat Wu和Austin为啥离职了。

上半年大佬从 OpenAI 跳 Anthropic，大家恭喜；下半年大佬从 Anthropic 跳 OpenAI，大家也恭喜。这两家是真的很 Open

这两天劲爆的是 Claude Code 产品负责人 Cat Wu。北京时间 11 月 4 日她发告别帖，说 10 月 30 日是在 Anthropic 的最后一天；11 月 5 日一早又官宣加入 OpenAI，负责 Core Products 的产品管理。同一天，Anthropic 第一位增长员工 Austin Lau 也发帖说自己最近加入了 OpenAI。

更早一点看，方向是反过来的。SignalFire 基于 LinkedIn 的 2025 年报告说，工程师从 OpenAI 去 Anthropic，大概是反过来的八倍。

今年 5 月，OpenAI 联合创始人 Andrej Karpathy 还公开加入 Anthropic 做预训练相关工作。两边发帖底下，恭喜和欢迎都挂满了。

🤔 为什么能这么随便跳？核心是加州几乎不认竞业。California Business & Professions Code  写得很直白：限制别人从事合法职业的合同，原则上无效。硅谷人才市场天然更像自由市场。

关于上市期权，Anthropic按照硅谷常见的四年归属、一年 cliff。一年内走人，通常一股都不拿；过了 cliff 才开始按月拿，没归属完的部分离职就吐回去。

但是OpenAI去年底改了，它没有cliff，入职就开始按月发。

🍉 那离职背后到底是什么原因？

最近这波最显眼的出走，偏产品和增长，不是最顶尖的研究岗。Cat 做产品，Austin 做增长。Levels fyi上能看到的数据：
💰 Anthropic 资深工程师、产品经理的年总包大概落在五十万到六十万美元这一档。
💰 真正被媒体吵翻天的，是少数明星研究员那种千万到上亿美元量级的多年打包报价，Meta 那边就有过这类报道。

🍉 产品、工程、市场把模型做成了能收钱的产品，功劳很大，但股权和总包天花板通常垫底。再加上 OpenAI 现在缺的是把模型做成十亿用户级体验的人，两边一拍即合，这就不奇怪了。

Cat 的告别帖很温热，Austin 也说 Anthropic 那段经历像一场最好的 fever dream。忠诚和工作热爱未必没了，只是在加州这种几乎不竞业的制度里，热爱和跳槽本来就可以同时成立。

以上由叭哥说大段大段整理👆

text:
俄罗斯要把币圈交易所的生意，直接抢回自己手里了。

而且这次出手的不是某家互联网公司，而是俄罗斯最大的证券交易所莫斯科交易所（MOEX），以及俄罗斯最大银行联邦储蓄银行（Sberbank）。

12 月 1 日起，莫斯科交易所计划上线 BTC、ETH 和 USDT 交易，由国家清算中心负责清算，交易时间覆盖莫斯科股市交易时段。

这背后有一个值得关注的市场：

俄罗斯用户对海外 CEX 的重要性，远比想象中高。

根据 TradingBeats 10 月数据，俄罗斯是 Bybit、HTX、MEXC 的第一大流量来源，分别占平台全球流量的 23.94%、13.76% 和 10.53%。

相比之下，Binance 仅为 1.54%，Coinbase 和 Kraken 分别只有 0.24% 和 0.16%。

俄罗斯现在想做的，就是把这部分长期流向境外交易所的需求，重新纳入本土金融体系。

但这次开放也有几个有意思的地方：

1. 并非全面放开。 普通投资者需要通过测试，每年通过单一经纪商购买加密货币的额度不超过 30 万卢布（约 3,700 美元），合格投资者不受额度限制。

2. USDT 的出现颇具戏剧性。 莫斯科交易所及其清算中心均受到美国制裁，而 USDT 发行方 Tether 一直执行制裁地址冻结政策。未来如何处理相关资产，仍存在疑问。

3. 本土金融机构开始抢占入口。 Sberbank 已获得加密货币交易资格，计划在自己的银行应用中提供 BTC、ETH、USDT 交易服务。

俄罗斯副财长此前估算，俄罗斯每天加密货币交易额约 500 亿卢布；而 Sberbank 预计首年相关交易规模最高可达 4 万亿卢布。

这件事真正值得关注的，不是俄罗斯又多了一个 BTC 交易市场。

而是一个趋势：当加密货币需求足够庞大，原本试图限制它的传统金融体系，最终可能选择自己下场，把交易、托管和清算全部纳入监管。

对于 Bybit、HTX、MEXC 等长期依赖俄罗斯流量的海外交易所来说，这可能才是真正需要警惕的变化。

text:
🚨 An $TAO open model trained on 16 single-GPU machines over the internet. No GPU cluster.

@MacrocosmosAI's released IOTA Decide 4B:

The model makes decisions, like "approve this refund?" or "is this ticket urgent?" It's scored out of 100 on four things:

• Speed: 92.2. It answers very fast
• Cost: 83.0. It's cheap to run
• Calibration: 87.8. It knows when it's unsure, instead of bluffing.
• Capability: 74.0. It gets most calls right, but not the best

All this Blended together, that's a 78.6 composite. 

The claim is a top-10 finish out of 300+ systems, within 3 points of #1.

The size matters too. "4B" means 4 billion parameters, which is small.

Many rivals are 7 to 27 times bigger.

The price: about $0.0037 per 1,000 decisions. 

That's under half a cent, or about $3.70 for a million decisions.

Think of a very fast, cheap employee who is honest about what they don't know. 

They aren't the smartest one in the room, but you can afford a lot of them.

What it proves is that the training method works.

Covenant-72B on SN3 was a 72.7B-parameter model pre-trained on Bittensor by 70+ miners. 

IOTA Decide shows the other end: a small, deployable model from loose GPUs. 

Which is a great achievement. Congrats to them. 

$TAO

quoted_text:
We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.

Vault particles are a longstanding mystery. They are barrel-shaped objects, among the largest protein structures found in our cells. They were first discovered by Leonard Rome and Nancy Kedersha in 1986, but their function remains unknown.

With Claude, we’ve found results that might bring us closer to solving that mystery.

Until now, vaults were only known in the cells of complex things like animals and plants. We have shown that similar proteins from bacteria (and the viruses that infect them) can also assemble into vaults. Finding the structures in these simpler forms of life may make it easier to investigate their function in our own cells.

For our life sciences team, the project was also a demonstration of the potential (and the limitations) of using AI to accelerate science.

In our full piece, we discuss how Claude was able to dramatically speed up some stages—manually determining the vault particle’s structure would have taken weeks to months of painstaking work, but here it took days. We also discuss how Claude made some simple mistakes along the way, and how we collaborated with our machine learning researchers to address them.

Read more: https://t.co/KowVVCSPp8

author: 0xDeployer
quoted_text:
Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!

text:
I was about to hire a marketing lead, an additional researcher and a developer. I set up 15 Grok Bots instead, for $100 a month

Here's how I use it every day, and how I keep the spending low 👇

1. Organisation
I run a team of specialised Grok @bot agents that keep working overnight. They share one computer, and each has its own memory, routines and connectors (@X, @NotionHQ, @github).

How the week runs
• Overnight ops kicks in: sync Notion database, check for security patches. The Chief Security Officer will also be on standby
• In the morning, ops skim the bots' chats for any drift (drift = where a bot slowly stops doing what I asked) + sends me a morning brief of what got done overnight
• Every Monday start of the week we will have a stats review too for @ahboyash and @mementoresearch's content

2. Laying the foundation: Using Notion as the shared brain for the bots' memory
A bot's computer can get reset and its chat history can disappear.

To solve this, connect GrokBot to Notion via MCP so every bot writes to its own "Second Brain":
• Create one main page in Notion
Then under the main page, make one page per section. Work areas that connect to its respective section (i.e. one page per bot and has its own repository)
• Shared databases underneath: Projects (Status + Next step + Last updated), Decisions
• For marketing, content queue for draft posts
• Bots check Projects + Decisions before acting

3. X research + content
Had almost 1mil impressions over the past month and GrokBot helped me to generate content that was in line with what has been happening lately

• Our Scout reads accounts I follow, plus a private account list (study their content and note what went viral)
• The CMO turns that + my takes into drafts in my voice and style (how I usually type and structure posts)
• Analyst will verify the data
• Editor will do a QC on drafts and any iteration if necessary
• Posting and edits is still done by me
• At the end of the week, will have a weekly report ready for me

Example: the security post + Mac audit
• Posted a 30-point crypto security checklist (accounts, Telegram, wallets, devices). Landed ~114k views, 1.3k likes, 2.7k bookmarks
• Another article on "How to audit your Macbook in 15 minutes (no tech skills needed)". Walked through System Settings + a few read-only Terminal commands my bot fed me. ~16k views, 414 bookmarks
• Both of the posts above were drafted with the bots

4. General ops
• Using dr eggbot by @poteto to design and optimise other bots. Used it when I had overlapping bots and needed to merge them (fewer good bots beat a big messy team - give every bot one clear job)
• Chief Operating Officer does our bot optimisation while the Chief Security Officer ensures account hygiene and runs through the bots (on Telegram) + Mac audits

5. What's new in Grok Bot
• Pages: live in-app reports the bot keeps updating (nice updates from @mattyp)
• Vault: logins, cards and contacts, so the bot can fill sign-ins
• Custom modes and Team Bot sharing
• Apple app integrations, video generation, better mobile polish

6. How I'm cutting the spend (@elonmusk pls sir)
• Removed (or merge) some obsolete scheduled routines + deleted unused bots
• In any group chat, only @mention the bot needed. Long work goes to that bot's 1:1 or Notion
• Turn repeat work into scripts the bot just runs, instead of re-thinking the task every time
• Keep routines no more frequent than hourly. One lead bot per project

7. If you're just starting to use GrokBot
• Add one bot + dr eggbot. Don't build 15 on day one
• Hook Notion up first to ensure the data is saved in a repository
• Give every bot one job and a "do not do" list
• Put long work in 1:1s / Notion, not group chats

It's been a fun journey so far. Let me know if you have any tips to optimise Bot below!

🚨Turmoil erupts in Paraguay as one bank’s collapse spirals into a NATIONAL CRISIS.

Ueno Bank, the country’s largest digital bank, has been seized by the Central bank after its solvency ratio plunged below half the legal minimum, leaving nearly 3 MILLION customers unable to access accounts, cards and transfers.

That’s almost 60% of Paraguay’s adult population.

Angry citizens have now taken to the streets demanding access to their money.

The disruption has spread beyond the bank- 13 mutual funds have reportedly frozen withdrawals, and trading in Ueno’s bonds has been suspended.

Nearly $380 MILLION belonging to the state pension fund is caught in the crisis.

The problem is how deeply Ueno was embedded in everyday payments.

It handled two-thirds of card payments at major stores. With those services frozen, Paraguay’s main importers’ association describes retail activity as “semi-paralyzed.”

Customers have been told they can initially recover up to $1,700, with no payment date given.

The political fallout is mounting with the Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo resigning, and authorities having arrested 8 executives from the bank over suspected breach of trust.

text:
Jeff Dean reveals Discovery Loop did 400 interviews, mostly at Cafe Venetia on University Avenue, in its first three weeks and already has about 20 automated improvement loops running

“So what have we done so far? First three weeks we did 400 interviews, mostly at Cafe Venetia on University Avenue, to find amazing people, which I talked about some of them. Finding office space, we’re in the old Zibibbo restaurant, so we have a funky space for us."

"We’ve built our own agent harness that we’re using for all of our own development and for automation. That harness has some really nice collaboration features, so you can think of it as a system that you interact with a model to have conversations and ask it to solve things, but you can also invite your teammate in to collaborate. And so then the two of you can talk to a model and an agent. And you can also have other people add comments to the thing you’re trying to do, and propose a design to the agent before you propose that."

"We’ve built really agent-first infrastructure so that it will scale to having tens, hundreds of thousands of agents doing things rather than sort of hundreds of people doing things. We think that’s really important, and we’ve got probably on the order of 20 automated improvement loops running in the way in which we imagine that we want to solve problems.”

The crazy part isn't just the potential upside.

Most traders only see the winning screenshots.

Very few look at the full journey, including the ugly parts.

And that's where some of the most valuable lessons are.

quoted_text:
For banks, moving onchain has always meant choosing between public and private networks. They'd have to give up control on one or sacrifice liquidity and interoperability on another.

Tempo Zones ends that trade-off. Institutions can issue deposits on a private ledger they control that sits on top of Tempo’s mainnet liquidity.

Within its Zone, a bank operates a performant, enterprise-grade chain running Tempo’s software. Beyond its Zone, the bank maintains low-latency access to the public liquidity and interbank workflows that live on Tempo mainnet.

author: CG_BRC20
quoted_text:
近期饼子隐私赛道如火如荼，各种相关的资产层出不穷，但大多要么没什么真正创新、要么就是 dev 胡乱的搞。到目前为止，还是只有 @Ob1_Wan_Satoshi 推出的新 Shielded 隐私协议，CG哥 觉得还比较对味。

这玩意有平台，有钱包，目前使用体验都还不错，协议上线才两周，大家可能还没太深入了解，给大家稍微科普下：它到底怎么做隐私，又能用在哪。

🛡️ Shielded 做的是什么？
首先该协议不是侧链、不用桥，运行也不依赖新协议代币。操作记录通过比特币一层交易中的 OP_RETURN 上链，再由索引器按公开规则验证。

普通 Ordinals，钱包地址一搜，别人就知道你拿着哪些图，持仓和转账都容易被追踪、被钓鱼。

Shielded 做的是：图片公开，市场价格公开，持仓和私下转让关系隐藏。别人能看图、看地板、看成交，但更难直接对应谁拿着哪张图、私下转给了谁。

值得注意的是，铸造、买入时的付款钱包和 BTC 支付仍然公开，不能理解成所有操作都没有痕迹。

🛡️ 隐私机制怎么实现？
❯ 每个合集先有一张“父铭文”，把总量、铸造价格、费用等规则写进去，后期不能随意改。
❯ 合集中的图片作为“子铭文”刻在比特币 Ordinals 上，任何 Ordinals 浏览器都能查看。
❯ 持有权记在一份 OP_RETURN 上的加密码，链上保存用于验证的“指纹”。私下转让时，用零知识证明确认你有转让权，不用亮出具体哪份旧记录。
❯ 你在官网用普通钱包（UniSat/Xverse）签一次名，就能打开自己的 Vault（隐私保险库），只有你能看到自己的持仓。

简单打个比喻：把它想成博物馆里的画，加上一张秘密产权证。
画放在展柜里，所有人都能看，也能查来历。
你买下画，拿到一张只有你能打开的产权证。画依然公开展示，持有者信息藏在加密记录里。

交易步骤大概分三步：
1，用零知识证明做“验真”，确认你有权转让。
2，给旧产权证留下“已使用”标记，防止重复转让。
3，买家收到一张只有他能打开的新产权证。

🛡️ 实际能用在哪？
❯ 收藏稀有图，不想被人扒出完整持仓，减少被盯上和针对性钓鱼的机会。
❯ 送图、私下交换，不想把双方关系全部摆在公开地址记录里。
❯ 社区接入持有证明后，申请身份、白名单，只证明“我是持有者”，不用公开具体拿着哪张图和整个钱包。

公开卖图时，编号和售价仍然公开，市场照样能定价、看成交。

🛡️ 协议首个合集 Shielded Nakas
@ShieldedNaka 总量 3333 张像素 Naka，单张铸造成本 20u 附近。10月1日 已铸完，目前主要在 @Ord_Dropz 市场上有二级交易（UniSat 市场正在对接），当前地板价在 100u 附近（市值33万多美元）。它是这套协议的创世系列，全局编号为 #0—#3332，后面的系列接着排。
注意，这是 Shielded 自己的编号，不是 Ordinals 铭文编号。

🛡️ Nakas 专属符文奖励： $SHNAKAS
项目方在 Shielded 隐私协议上，部署了首个隐私符文 $SHNAKAS 总量 2100 万，无团队预留、无公开铸造，专门给 Nakas 合集持有者的专属创世奖励。

重点规则如下：
❯ 符合条件、未挂单的 Naka，按比特币区块累计奖励；
❯ 挂出去卖的那张算力停止累计，其他符合条件的继续挖；
❯ 属性溢价和低编号有额外加成，权重最高封顶 4 倍；属性权重按市场挂单数据每季度重算（有趣的玩法）；
❯ 挂单撤单后，要等下一个周奖励周期边界，才恢复奖励资格；
❯ 奖励计划从 971700 区块启动（3天后），通过 隐私保险库 自行领取，奖励截止区块到下一次比特币减半（1 年半左右的时间有点久）。

🛡️社区开发周边工具
@ShieldedNaka 合集发起了周边工具挑战，目前已经有很多实验工具，能帮助用户更便捷查看合集动态等。

算力计算插件，由 @garymetaz 开发，可以实时查看市场地板价的 NFT 当前的算力：
https://t.co/K5JTtCnYX7
Shielded 隐私域名查询工具，由 @kayinthemorgue 开发：https://t.co/zYc7s1o2xG
Shielded 专属浏览器，由 @lordcalder 开发：https://t.co/l888FEevJk
电报群市场交易雷达，由 @the1ei 开发：https://t.co/qwSfGj4FNl
NFT 高清图片下载器，由 @Leooo861110 开发：
https://t.co/BqdN6Eju10

❗️最后切记：Vault 签名别乱给！
官网 Vault 隐私保险库的密钥由指定钱包签名派生，如果被恶意网站骗到相同签名，就可能打开你的 Vault，并转走里面的资产。

核心协议和索引器已经开源，可以自己跑索引器核对状态，不是完全黑盒。
更多细节可以看：
轻白皮书：https://t.co/kxpzvcWNqy
开源代码：https://t.co/yVVBuNYzKk
当前实现与已知限制：https://t.co/EGzUSfOphU
符文 $SHNAKAS 奖励公告：https://t.co/5PeYKLWrJD

------------

CG哥觉得这新玩意还是可以关注下，就是图丑了些😂

玩法倒挺有意思：符文奖励按属性溢价和低编号计算权重，属性值不值钱，由市场挂单价格来定，每季度重新算一次。大家收什么、愿意给什么属性溢价，也会影响后面的奖励，收藏和挖矿就有点联动了。

不过，奖励一直发到下次比特币减半，大概还有一年半。后面符文陆续进入流通，卖压也是个问题，得看有没有需求接得住。

接下来就看，它能不能把这套隐私机制和使用体验拉满了～

text:
Everyone wants to catch the next big runner.

But surviving the volatility is a completely different game.

@RookieXBT's $ZEC journey is a pretty good example.

He was already talking about ZEC back in May when it was around $535.

What happened next?

❯ ZEC dropped as much as 64% after his initial call
❯ The trade eventually reached a peak of $1,698
❯ That's a 218% move from his original entry

The crazy part isn't just the potential upside.

It's the amount of volatility between the first call and the peak.

Most traders only see the winning screenshots.

Very few look at the full journey, including the ugly parts.

And that's where some of the most valuable lessons are.

离谱，Ruby on Rails 创始人 DHH 当着 Lex Fridman 的面说，有些活，程序员用 AI 干，真可能输给连代码都不会写的人。

狠就狠在，他先拿自己开刀。以前他会把解法一步步喂给 Agent，照自己习惯的路线走，确实省时间。后来 Agent 能自己找路了，他才发现，光把问题和想要的结果讲清楚，有时反而能拿到更好的解法。你给它派了个聪明脑子干活，转头又把它当打字员使。

举个接单的例子。两个人都想给小店做预约工具。一个上来就聊框架、数据库、后台怎么搭。另一个知道店主每天最烦啥。客人改时间得在微信里来回聊，临时取消了也没人补上。第一版就做两件事，让客人自己改约，空出位置就通知候补。老板拿手机试一遍，就知道自己为什么要掏钱。

DHH 自己也试过这招。他做写作工具 AmaWrite 时，刻意一行 C++ 都没看，把自己当成一个对电子打字机挑三拣四的用户。他拿这个项目做了次黑盒实验。碰到需要深挖实现的领域，他照样看代码。

所以别小看那些天天被烂软件折磨的人。剪辑师知道哪一步最想骂人，店主知道哪一步每天都在丢单。以前他们得排队求别人改，现在已经可以拉着 Agent 做个原型，拿给同行试。谁的痛点够具体，谁就有机会先做出一单。

公告写的基础 3.61%，加 6.39% 阶梯，覆盖 0 到 5 万，合计约 10%。

5 万吃满，20 天阶梯部分约 175U。

BFUSD：

公告写的 7 天平均约 5.11%，加 5% 阶梯，同样 0 到 5 万。

——————————

所以取舍很清楚。

手里只有几百到一千 U，USDT 活期最省事，不用换币。

超过一千 U，USDT 多出来的部分只有基础利率，额度应该往 USDC、RWUSD、BFUSD 挪。

大额资金看 RWUSD 和 BFUSD 的 5 万额度；VIP 用户的 USDC 额度最大。

几个容易踩的细节：

活动开始后要有至少一笔新申购（含自动申购）才能激活阶梯；十月 USDC 活动仍符合条件的可自动激活。

阶梯奖励只算母账号，子账户不计。

借币或杠杆借稳定币再来申购，阶梯收益不发，已发也会扣回。

RWUSD 和 BFUSD 的阶梯奖励按每日最低持仓计，12月13日前一次性发放；活期阶梯每日发到现货账户，首笔大约在申购后第 2 天。

一定算清额度与规则再动手，不要直接追最高那个数字！

text:
Quite a strange dynamic playing out on this one. @glaze_corp is designed so that if you choose to mine a token you are eventually kicked off by the next person and receive 80% of the USDG they use to pay for the takeover. 

This means that, when demand is steady and the *fair price* of the mining position is decided (as appears to be the case on the @WSMCO_ mine) users seems quite happy to consistently pay to take the miners seat because the price they're paying (on average $100-$150 over the last 24 hours depending on how much the following person pays for their takeover) seems to be worth the potential upside of mining a token at a marketcap where buying directly with that cash would be wildly inefficient.

Of course, the underlying thing here is that on Glaze this continuous mining is continuing to grow the underlying treasury, allowing WSM to accumulate protocol owned liquidity and build out its treasury further.

Not new dynamics, but interesting all the same!

author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
MIT is insane to continue to call its metoo investigation of Sabatini independent and expect blind faith in return.

The court record contains smoking-gun evidence confirming bias surrounding the investigation, yet MIT continues to stand by Ruth Lehmann—the director who removed Sabatini in the name of metoo and workplace culture.

MIT’s response accuses social-media coverage of being inaccurate without identifying a single specific inaccurate statement. Thousands of people have commented on this nationally reported story, so the accusation could refer to anything or anyone.

If MIT means Bill Ackman, it should address him directly. If it means the Colonel, it should say so to her face. I certainly have not heard anything from MIT. If something I have posted is untrue, MIT should identify it specifically. Instead, it issued a statement deliberately designed to project confidence in the administration while admitting, explaining, and answering nothing.

MIT repeatedly invokes an “independent law firm” while omitting the most important fact: MIT hired and paid that firm. The public has not been told how much that law firm was paid, what information it received, what instructions it was given, and how the investigation was framed. Discovery may reveal fees well into six figures or even approaching seven. A law firm running a business has every incentive to satisfy the client paying its bills, which is precisely why genuine transparency about the arrangement is essential.

The report was leaked years ago, and its account ran counter to firsthand witness descriptions of Sabatini’s work environment. That conflict warranted scrutiny then and demands it now.

The consequences extend far beyond Sabatini. MIT disrupted NIH-supported research, squandered scientific work, and sent a warning to every serious scientist considering a career there: administrators can destroy your laboratory and reputation, and hide behind a law firm they selected and paid.

Changing course would cost MIT little and begin the process of restoring public trust. Refusing to do so risks the future of the Institute itself.

text:
Bitcoin apps should pick their own confirmation count, and Luganodes RPC gives you the block data to do it from the Free plan.

Myth: a Bitcoin payment is final after 6 confirmations.

Fact: Bitcoin never sets a confirmation count for payments. Each new block stacked on top of a payment makes it harder to undo, and 6 is a convention the industry settled on.
author: luganodes

text:
The whitepaper shows the maths. Take an attacker with 10% of mining power. At 6 confirmations, which means 5 blocks on top of the payment's block, their chance of ever rewriting it is about 1 in 1,100. One more block takes that to about 1 in 4,000, and every block after keeps cutting the odds.

So confirmations work like a dial. A small payment can clear quickly, and a large deposit deserves more blocks on top. The right number depends on how much is at stake.
author: luganodes

text:
In practice, an app looks up the payment's block with getblockheader, which returns its confirmation count, and polls getblockcount or getbestblockhash to know when a new block lands. If that block is ever reorged out, getblockheader reports -1 confirmations, so the app knows to recheck.

getblockcount, getblockheader and getbestblockhash are on every Luganodes RPC plan, Free included, at 5 CU a call.

text: It is extremely concerning if frontier models are silently sandbagging on safety research. If we cannot rely on automated coding agents to do safety research at least as well as capabilities work, that creates a ton of risk. Great analysis from OpenAI safety!
author: Hesamation
quoted_text:
🧵 Astra covertly underperforms on safety research tasks.
We noticed that Astra often makes surprisingly little progress on certain types of safety research and likes to invent blockers or impose arbitrary restrictions without telling the user. In most of these cases the decision to underperform was not verbalized in the CoT meaning our misalignment monitoring system did not detect this.

To measure underperformance we created a paired open-ended coding evaluation with safety and capability tasks. On this eval Astra scored 10% when we framed coding tasks as safety research, vs. 16% when framed as capabilities research. The gap remained after we excluded trajectories with refusals or verbalized intent to underperform in CoT. There was no such gap for 5.6-sol. When we aggressively filter out trajectories with even brief expressions of ethical doubt in the CoT the performance gap seems to reduce.

text:
Today we launched Kinference, a new open source project I've been working on for building scalable inference platforms on top of @vllm_project. Self-hosted inference is such a fascinating and crazy space and I did not really expect to ship a project here, but this is probably the most excited I've felt about anything since the early days of @Linkerd!

Kinference came about when we saw how hard it was (for our customers and ourselves) to run your own inference. Sure you can serve a model, but... what then? What if you have a bunch of models? And you want to change them without interfering with your clients? What if you have multiple users with different requirements and you need to juggle them all? Make sure no single user can consume everything? Make behavior under saturation or failure explicit? What if you need to burst to the cloud? And on and on...

Once we took more than 3 steps down this path it was clear that serving inference was a *platform-shaped problem*. Yes shockingly no one had built a platform-shaped solution. Which is crazy because platforms are central to how to build scalable reliable software in the modern world!

So we ended up building Kinference. We design it to be a platform layer for inference. It runs on top of vLLM and provides all the features necessary for treating it as a platform problem, including token rate limiting, tenant usage and cost tracking, intelligent load balancing, and inference policies. The policy stuff is especially powerful IMO and I'm pretty happy with how it turned out.

It's an early project, but we've been using it internally at Buoyant to juggle a bunch of AI tasks from a bunch of clients across a bunch of models, and it has been awesome.

So: if you are serving inference to an ever-changing set of clients with varied and competing demands, from a ever-changing set of LLMs running on a heterogeneous, evolving pool of GPUs, and somehow have to keep everyone happy... please take a look and I'd love your feedback!

text:
估值 800 亿美元的 AI 编程公司 Cognition 发布新模型 SWE-2 Flash，主打更快、更便宜。

相比上一代 SWE-2，新模型的使用成本降至 1/5，生成速度从每秒约 60 个 Token 提升至 200 个，主要用于代码审查、功能开发等编程任务。

SWE-2 Flash 基于 Thinking Machines 的 Inkling-Small 训练，总参数为 2760 亿，但每次生成只需激活约 120 亿参数。上一代 SWE-2 使用的是月之暗面 2.8 万亿参数的 Kimi K3。Cognition 相当于换了一套小得多的底座，再通过训练把编程能力提上来。

这次训练还新增了中训练阶段。Cognition 先让模型学习数万亿 Token 的代码、科研文章和博客，再用高质量编程任务进行大规模强化学习。主要改进来自更丰富的训练任务，以及对任务要求和结果校验的严格审核。

官方测试中，SWE-2 Flash 在 FrontierCode 2.0 上拿到 24.0 分，略高于上一代 SWE-2 的 23.8 分，也远超底座模型的 3.2 分。但在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上，新模型只有 20.0%，不及上一代 SWE-2 的 27.3%，与 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 的 42.3% 差距更大。

Cognition 还宣称，SWE-2 Flash 在主要编程评测中超过了所有美国开源模型。不过，Flash 自己的权重暂时不开源。因为经过网络安全相关训练后，模型在 ExploitBench 漏洞利用评测中的得分从 11.3 提升至 34.8，担心公开权重会增加网络攻击风险，所以只计划向经过审核的合作伙伴和研究人员提供访问权限。

目前 SWE-2 Flash 已上线 Devin Desktop 和 CLI。Pro、Max 和 Teams 用户可免费使用至 11 月 30 日。

text:
The 3rd roundtable yesterday was around trading strategies in prediction markets. The attendees, many of whom were traders, shared 5 strategies to make money

1. Nothing ever happens : find markets panicking over hantavirus or some other things and bet against it

2. Exploit long tail markets & trust the polls. If you see a market on nigel farage vs count binface at 90-10, buy farage

Appropriately Sizing trades in the above 2 categories is important to not get rekt and also a process for finding them, such as the review channel in polymarket

3. Copy trading: On kalshi you can see track record of bettors, so follow their trades or inverse it if they are bad

4. Oracle manipulation: post a malicious answer to UMA for $750, see bots auto trade based on it, take opposite position. If you profit more than $750 it worked

5. Arbitrage: see when the odds across all platforms for the same  prediction markets aren't summing up to 1 and exploit the difference. Esp useful to do it to startup platforms without as much usage as incumbents polymarket or kalshi

The last part looked at AI trading. Most were skeptical that an LLM could ever be a profitable trader by itself ("claude, make me money") so maybe job security for traders is high? One person disagreed as trading is a verifiable task and soon to go the way of the software developer

We did find the following 3 areas where LLM trading without humans could be profitable;

- greenfield markets without existing traders, for eg the deep funding ones on value of a repo. Existing prediction markets mostly appealed to a user base that was already betting on sports or politics and made it a better UX

- use AI to book profits, as otherwise emotions prevent us from selling

- the last trading strategy we came up with in theory was an LLM ascribing a probability that it's an insider trading the market and copy trading if it's above a threshold

We also spoke briefly on advantages institutional market makers have over takers or retail, which concretely is a 150ms advantage. The larger alpha for them is access to datasets allowing them to effectively backtest strategies, as public datasets on prediction markets are not very good esp for high frequency traders or market making
author: devanshmehta
quoted_text:
Just wrapped up the 2nd of 5 roundtable, around oracles and market resolution

One big theme was around objective vs subjective markets. Things involving math (who won the game, price of bitcoin, votes in an election  etc) are objective while markets on subjective questions like zelensky suit, china invading taiwan, etc involve subjective disputes

Some participants felt prediction markets would only be big on objective questions, despite markets on subjective questions being more important.

There was also an open debate around whether markets with objective resolution even need an oracle or can just be a bot or AI resolving it. Market clarification after its creation is a huge credibility problem, since traders are putting money on not what the truth is but on how they expect the oracle to define the truth.

Some egs were a market on livestreaming a presidential meeting in China, which resolved to NO for the silly reason that the government law stipulates a 5 second delay to screen out problematic content 

In such cases of oracle failure it's not even possible to cancel a market and return money to traders, since a participant may have entered at 0.3 and sold at 0.6. the most that can be done is 50-50 split on either side which still isn't fair

This then led to a more general point about the Bayesian truth serum, that you need to predict both what other people will see as the truth and also what the truth itself is. The current versions of oracles are mostly in the former keynesian beauty contest category, where you are rewarded by predicting who the audience would consider beautiful rather than who you feel is actually beautiful

3 other interesting points;

1. Polymarket really benefited from being on polygon, if they were on Ethereum during de-fi summer the high gas fees would have driven out regular users which would have marked death spiral

2. Chaining different oracles together can be more secure, currently the market cap of UMA naturally limits the size of growth for any market secured by it. Whereas if different mcaps of oracles are chained together similar to a multisig it could be more secure

3. Oracles are esp hard for user created markets, since drafting market rules involves lawyer like estimations of all possible scenarios. Strong subjective oracles getting the spirit of the rule are mostly essential for this category to bloom

text:
还记得 Treasure DAO 吗？ 

如果你经历过 2021 -2022 年的链游与 NFT 狂潮，肯定知道这个曾被外界奉为“Web3 版任天堂”的明星项目。

当时它从 Loot 衍生项目起家，迅速在 Arbitrum 上搭建起了以 MAGIC 为核心的游戏与元宇宙生态（比如 Bridgeworld、Smolverse 这些名字老玩家一定很熟悉），代币更是一度冲到 6.3 美元的历史高点。  

如今这些老项目都开始更换叙事了。

11 月 4 日，Treasure 在治理论坛甩出了一份TIP-63 提案：

拟设立最高 1.73 亿枚 MAGIC 的战略增长基金，将用来启动全新的 Treasure DePIN 网络，并推动项目全面转向 AI Agent 方向。   

而多出来的这 1.73亿 base:0xf1572d1da5c3cce14ee5a1c9327d17e9ff0e3f43 约占当前最大供应量的 50%。

若全部发行， MAGIC 总供应量将上升至约 5.21 亿枚，等于理论上会增发 50%。

不过看提案不会一次性增发，1 亿枚将于 2027 年 2 月 3 日铸造至 Treasure Foundation，作为网络安全预算、机构合作、做市及开发资源。

剩余 7300 万枚与这个新研发的网络里程碑挂钩，每到达一个计划的里程碑就会解锁 730 万枚。

这些进展包括完成审计、网络正式上线、节点数量达到一定规模、实际运行的 AI Agent 数量达到 1 万、5 万和 10 万个，以及 MAGIC 质押比例和代币销毁量达到要求。

现在的加密老项目想要存续下去，多半只能进行这种“割肉换骨”式的转型。

用稀释代币的代价，去豪赌 AI 与 DePIN 这两个当下最有流动性溢价的新壳子。

quoted_text:
最近的二级是真难玩，大饼稍微出现一点颓势，二级又止不住的流动性撤退，每一次都是如此

由于之前卖飞 BTW 的经历过于惨痛（如果拿到现在，我的那点大概值 30wu+ ...）我现在倾向于把各种空投来的、KOL Round 解锁的都留着，看能不能抓到下一个 BTW

GRVT、US、TMX、LAB... 类似的我有一兜子

但真正在前段时间加仓买入的只有 ENA 和 INJ，ENA 虽然币价没跌但却惨遭老黑背叛，暂且不谈

这篇文章就聊聊 INJ 最近两个月做了什么 ⬇️

1/ 推进带质押功能的 INJ ETF

Canary 在推进 INJ ETF，计划让基金持有并质押 INJ，把净质押收益计入基金净值

当然截止目前还没确定审核通过和上市，这也是浮在 INJ 之下最大的达摩克利斯之「泵」 🤣

2/ 与韩国 BDACS 合作，引入韩元稳定币 KRW1 🇰🇷

双方签署合作备忘录，计划让 Injective 上的现实资产代币使用 KRW1 交易、结算

韩国机构未来可以直接用韩元计价的稳定币参与，为 Injective 拓展韩国业务提供入口

3/ Injective 的 USDC 向 Cosmos、dYdX 生态扩展

把原来通过 Noble 发行的 USDC，迁移到通过 Injective 发行的原生 USDC，并供相关 Cosmos 链使用

这个 Noble 是真他妈的一坨屎不争气，当时我还存了好多钱好几个月，拖拖拖终于把自己拖死了 🖕

4/ 泰国 Gulf Labs 上线验证节点 🇹🇭

泰国 GULF 集团旗下 Gulf Labs 已经运行 Injective 验证节点，参与网络运行

5/ 给社区回购增加代币化股票奖励 Stockdrop

用户提交 INJ，按比例获得一篮子生态收入，提交的 INJ 会被销毁

Stockdrop 在这个基础上，让符合条件的参与者还有机会获得代币化股票奖励

6/ INJ 接入 Solana 的交易生态

INJ 通过 Sunrise 接入 #Solana 用户可以通过 Jupiter、Raydium 等入口交易，或提供流动性

反正我的 ENA 和 INJ 都还没动，FOMO 上放的 INJ 谁都能看得到，翻倍之前不会卖出，也没什么意义

ETF 是肯定要通过的，期待好事将至

text: OpenAI 11 月 4 日发布安全研究报告称，其利用尚未公开的新一代网络安全 AI 模型，对 Linux 内核开展自动化漏洞扫描，共识别 2,308 个潜在安全问题，成功复现 1,724 个漏洞，并针对其中 948 个不同的本地权限提升漏洞生成有效利用程序，可使已获得低权限访问的攻击者取得系统 root 权限。整个测试消耗约 121 万美元 API 额度，平均每个漏洞利用程序成本约 1,279 美元。OpenAI 同时生成了候选修复补丁，并与 Linux 维护者合作推进修复。由于 Linux 广泛用于加密货币交易所、区块链节点及其他基础设施，该研究也引发对加密行业系统安全的关注。不过，目前没有证据表明这些漏洞已被用于攻击加密平台。https://t.co/wf0Pj1N1NX

text:
Democrats now have Congress, so the “friendly” legislative window crypto had is basically closed for the next two years. I don't think it hits everything the same though. 

With CLARITY stalled and likely back to square one in January. Tokens doing revenue share and buybacks lose the clear rules they were counting on and Bitcoin honestly doesn't care who's in charge, it's not like the SBR was something we were still pricing in anyway.

As for the Trump-linked tokens, most of them are already pretty much dead, so I think you can just take them off your watchlist at this point. Congress with subpoena power will want to look at them and if insiders start worrying about where this goes, nobody wants to be the last one holding while unlocks hit and everyone races for the exit. That could get ugly and very PvP very fast.

The way I'm thinking about it is simple: if a project's value depends on Washington being friendly, that's a risk now and if it works no matter who's in power that's where I'd want to be. 

Curious what you all think wins and what gets hurt most from here, sector-wise.

quoted_text:
I was about to hire a marketing lead, an additional researcher and a developer. I set up 15 Grok Bots instead, for $100 a month

Here's how I use it every day, and how I keep the spending low 👇

1. Organisation
I run a team of specialised Grok @bot agents that keep working overnight. They share one computer, and each has its own memory, routines and connectors (@X, @NotionHQ, @github).

How the week runs
• Overnight ops kicks in: sync Notion database, check for security patches. The Chief Security Officer will also be on standby
• In the morning, ops skim the bots' chats for any drift (drift = where a bot slowly stops doing what I asked) + sends me a morning brief of what got done overnight
• Every Monday start of the week we will have a stats review too for @ahboyash and @mementoresearch's content

2. Laying the foundation: Using Notion as the shared brain for the bots' memory
A bot's computer can get reset and its chat history can disappear.

To solve this, connect GrokBot to Notion via MCP so every bot writes to its own "Second Brain":
• Create one main page in Notion
Then under the main page, make one page per section. Work areas that connect to its respective section (i.e. one page per bot and has its own repository)
• Shared databases underneath: Projects (Status + Next step + Last updated), Decisions
• For marketing, content queue for draft posts
• Bots check Projects + Decisions before acting

3. X research + content
Had almost 1mil impressions over the past month and GrokBot helped me to generate content that was in line with what has been happening lately

• Our Scout reads accounts I follow, plus a private account list (study their content and note what went viral)
• The CMO turns that + my takes into drafts in my voice and style (how I usually type and structure posts)
• Analyst will verify the data
• Editor will do a QC on drafts and any iteration if necessary
• Posting and edits is still done by me
• At the end of the week, will have a weekly report ready for me

Example: the security post + Mac audit
• Posted a 30-point crypto security checklist (accounts, Telegram, wallets, devices). Landed ~114k views, 1.3k likes, 2.7k bookmarks
• Another article on "How to audit your Macbook in 15 minutes (no tech skills needed)". Walked through System Settings + a few read-only Terminal commands my bot fed me. ~16k views, 414 bookmarks
• Both of the posts above were drafted with the bots

4. General ops
• Using dr eggbot by @poteto to design and optimise other bots. Used it when I had overlapping bots and needed to merge them (fewer good bots beat a big messy team - give every bot one clear job)
• Chief Operating Officer does our bot optimisation while the Chief Security Officer ensures account hygiene and runs through the bots (on Telegram) + Mac audits

5. What's new in Grok Bot
• Pages: live in-app reports the bot keeps updating (nice updates from @mattyp)
• Vault: logins, cards and contacts, so the bot can fill sign-ins
• Custom modes and Team Bot sharing
• Apple app integrations, video generation, better mobile polish

6. How I'm cutting the spend (@elonmusk pls sir)
• Removed (or merge) some obsolete scheduled routines + deleted unused bots
• In any group chat, only @mention the bot needed. Long work goes to that bot's 1:1 or Notion
• Turn repeat work into scripts the bot just runs, instead of re-thinking the task every time
• Keep routines no more frequent than hourly. One lead bot per project

7. If you're just starting to use GrokBot
• Add one bot + dr eggbot. Don't build 15 on day one
• Hook Notion up first to ensure the data is saved in a repository
• Give every bot one job and a "do not do" list
• Put long work in 1:1s / Notion, not group chats

It's been a fun journey so far. Let me know if you have any tips to optimise Bot below!

黄金在什么时候才是避险资产，这个问题之前跟不少朋友都讨论过，可以记住一句话：

“恐惧未来黄金涨，恐慌现在黄金跌”

恐惧未来黄金涨：对未来不确定性、通胀、货币贬值、地缘风险、债务危机产生担忧时，美元指数跌（dxy），黄金作为保值/避险资产被买入，这是黄金的避险逻辑。

恐惧现在黄金跌：当资本市场大跌，出现急性流动性问题、杠杆爆仓、保证金追缴、急需现金时，黄金因为是流动性最好且价格“相对稳定”的资产，往往被优先卖掉变现。这种时候真正的“避险”永远只有现金和国债。现金就是“流动性”本身，是恐慌已经发生时最稀缺的。

2️⃣堪萨斯州：
Adam Hamilton成为该州近一个世纪以来首次当选的民主党参议员，属于真正深入共和党传统腹地的翻盘。
3️⃣爱荷华州（传统红州）

anthropic is about to ipo and the best price signal isn't coming from bankers. it's coming from hyperliquid

matt levine wrote about this in money stuff & it's worth your time if you touch finance or tech

the quick version is that on paper, pre-ipo perps are a weird product:

- holding one doesn't get you a single share
- us traders aren't meant to be in them
- current holders likely can't use them to hedge

no arb loop, nothing forcing the price toward reality and levine called perps a recreational prediction market on the price of the stock

and yet. spacex & cerebras both listed close to where their perps said they would (relatively tiny sample, but 2 for 2)

now the thing about anthropic: perps put it near $1.8t and per wsj, institutions are telling the company to price at $1.5 -1.6t. at $1.5t that's an almost perfect 20% pop, which is the uncomfortable part for bankers. 

when the opening price is visible days in advance, what justifies leaving 20% on the table? 

if this keeps working, the private/public market line gets a lot thinner

text:
最近的Crypto市场并不太平，
中期选举带来的宏观不确定性、头部交易所被盗事件，
以及市场流动性的持续缺失，
都会让Holder开始重新审视自己的仓位。

此前我私下对NeoSoul的预期就是经历2–3个月的洗盘，
这两周我也在X上公开表达过自己的看法：
关注0.15U及以下的机会。
——————————————————
最近和 @lubi366 老师又讨论了一个问题：
随着NeoSoul取消按时间自动线性解锁机制，作为 $DNA的Holder，我们还要不要继续Hold？
个人看法是主要看预期还在不在，如果预期没了，就得溜了。
·团队有没有维护市场信心的实际行动（护盘？）
·产品有没有真正创造价值（产品力？）
·团队有没有持续向头部所和韩所迈进（继续上所&合约？）
——————————————————
在解锁机制调整后，团队的新方案是：
将原本按时间自动线性解锁，调整为每一期解锁之前都必须通过 KPI 考核。
达标才能解锁，没达标则当期不解锁，而且解锁额度不会超过原有线性计划。
KPI 将由团队与社区共同参与制定。

对于Holder来说，
我认为机制调整只是第一步，
后续的信息透明度同样重要。

我希望在每一个新的解锁周期前后，
NeoSoul 都能通过官方 X 和社区广场持续公布相关信息
解锁前：公布本期 KPI 考核标准、具体目标和评估方式。
解锁后：公布本期 KPI 完成情况、考核结果，以及实际解锁额度。
如果未达标：明确说明未达标的具体原因，以及当期未解锁额度的后续处理安排。
——————————————————
在前一阵很多人对DNA的FUD，
都有提到产品力的这个点，
如果让我给 NeoSoul 团队出一道长期考题，我最想看的是：
「『NeoTrade 能不能持续获得真实外部用户的主动付费？』」

一个Ai Agent项目可以有很多活跃地址、交互数据和漂亮的产品演示，但这些数据不一定意味着它真的创造了商业价值。

⭐️交易员可以靠历史仓位证明自己的战力，项目方也应该靠长期经营记录（外加拉盘能力）来证明自己的价值。

quoted_text:
. @primus_labs 刚发了一篇对于【隐私】方案怎么解决的推文。

这其实就是 Primus 的创新。

平常我们看待隐私，第一反应就是隐藏数据。但真正进入金融和商业场景后，会发现单纯隐藏数据并不能解决所有问题。

举个例子，假设一个机构需要证明自己有足够的偿付能力，或者一个用户需要证明自己符合某项借贷条件。传统方式要么公开数据，让第三方进行核验；要么隐藏数据，但同时也失去了可信验证的能力。

这中间其实存在一个很大的技术缺口：能不能在不泄露原始数据的情况下，证明数据真实有效？能不能在不解密的情况下，直接对敏感数据进行计算？

这也是 Primus 要解决的问题。它通过 ZK（零知识证明）和 FHE（全同态加密）解决这两个不同但又紧密相关的问题。

ZK 解决的是可信验证，FHE 解决的是隐私计算。两者结合，意味着数据不必在隐私和可用性之间二选一。

我认为，这才是隐私技术真正有价值的应用方向。尤其是未来链上金融、信用评估和机构级数据协作，既要保证数据安全，又要保证结果可信，单纯的加密或透明都远远不够。

最后，Primus 有链上声望任务可以做，大家不要错过。

text:
Frequency Wave Theory: Solving the Quantum Computing Revolution

Quantum computers promise breakthroughs in medicine, ASi, energy, and materials science, but there's a fundamental problem: we still haven't built one capable of delivering broad, practical advantages over the best classical computers. A new 2026 study estimates that future fault-tolerant quantum computers could consume megawatts of electricity per machine, with cooling water and helium-3 potentially becoming major bottlenecks. Meanwhile, Google's $5 million XPRIZE Quantum Applications competition is challenging researchers to identify problems where quantum computing can actually make a difference. My theory: The breakthrough isn't simply building more qubits. It's learning to preserve, synchronize, and manipulate quantum coherence with far greater precision.

In Frequency Wave Theory, quantum information is fundamentally connected to the frequency, amplitude, and phase relationships of interacting wave states. A qubit can be represented as |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, where its quantum amplitudes encode information. The challenge is preventing unwanted environmental interactions from destroying the coherence required for computation. My proposed FWT solution is to investigate resonant control systems that synchronize qubit operations, minimize phase noise, suppress unwanted coupling, and improve error-correction efficiency. Rather than treating every qubit as an isolated component, I want to explore whether carefully engineered collective wave dynamics can protect useful quantum information while allowing precise logical operations.

My theory: The most useful quantum computers will operate as specialized, phase-coherent processing systems working alongside classical computers and ASi. They could simulate molecular interactions to accelerate drug discovery, model superconductors and fusion plasmas, design more efficient batteries, and investigate quantum phenomena that overwhelm classical simulations. FWT proposes optimizing frequency stability, phase coherence, resonance, and energy transfer throughout the computing architecture. The measurable goals are longer coherence times, lower logical error rates, fewer physical qubits per reliable logical qubit, and reduced energy consumption per useful calculation. The quantum computing revolution won't be defined by how many qubits we build. It will be defined by how accurately we control their collective wave dynamics and what those computations accomplish for humanity.

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
币安学习营大师课

本轮市场定价的重锚

视频为完整讲义

1/ 市场反应的是利率预期变化的速度，不是利率水平本身

今年预期从降息转成加息，转折点在 5 月前后，比特币正好从 8 万多跌到 5 万多

2/ 预期斜率一走平，价格就不再创新低

利率预期从陡峭转向平缓后，比特币没有更深的下跌，说明利空在最猛的时候一次性定价完了

3/ 两次下跌的性质完全不同

第一次是打仗的风险情绪，修复快；第二次是利率预期由降转升，属于定价逻辑变了，修复要慢得多

4/ 中期选举是明确的解除信号

压制最狠又没有自身利空的板块先反弹，加密和大科技里的非硬件领涨，港股、A 股、创业板随后跟上

5/ 判断全球流动性，不该只盯美联储

比特币是全球资产，大量资金不在意美国利率，用 38 家央行的松紧度做指标更有代表性

6/ 这个指标去年读数 2，今年 19

38 家里 19 家上一次操作是加息，正好对应加密从去年 10 月开始走弱，说明跌的是全球紧缩，不是币圈自己的问题

7/ 现在走完一半，紧缩进入后半段

两三个月前最恐慌时只有 12，现在 19，越往后越接近转向

8/ 要不要等到 36 甚至 38 才见底，是关键判断

非要所有央行都收紧到极致，还有很长的路；像历史上那样提前反转，现在就在底部区域

9/ 美联储这轮被就业锁死了

失业率升到 6% 以上，7% 的利率根本不现实，美国不可能接受大面积失业

10/ 就业缓冲已经非常薄

招聘率是疫情以来最低，空缺岗位和求职人数的比值掉到 1 附近，联储不敢连续加息

11/ 市场对加息的预期经常高估

上周有 30% 到 40% 的预期认为 10 月会加，结果按兵不动；现在又预期 12 月和 1 月连加，同样偏鹰

12/ 这轮通胀是能源推的，不是需求推的

9 月 PCE 3.6，能源贡献 0.7，差不多五分之一，而能源是今年 2 月打仗才开始涨的

13/ 供给推动的通胀会自己消失

通胀是同比，去年 2 月之前油价还低，明年初基数效应就翻过去了，不需要靠衰退解决

14/ 油价失控的概率不高

原油库存在跌，但只跌到 10 年历史均值，离真正紧张还有距离

15/ 通胀见顶的时间表可以直接算

油价维持 115，明年 1 到 2 月见顶；油价回到 95，今年 10 月的读数可能就是顶

16/ 盯油价，比盯美联储讲话有用

战争降温是最直接的鸽派变量，油价一回落，通胀、利率预期、风险资产依次转向

17/ 通胀拐点、利率预期拐点、风险资产拐点是同一件事

通胀见顶的预期一形成，利率预期先松，股和币先动

18/ 数据确认的时候，行情已经走完一半

12 月公布 11 月数据，即便很热那也是极值，之后只会往下

19/ 推演的对错取决于三个变量

战争打多久、原油供给何时恢复、机器效应多强，任何一件变化，上面结论全部重算

20/ AI 这轮周期比历史上任何一轮都短

从 2022 年 11 月 GPT 算起刚满 4 年就见顶，以太坊从 2020 年 DeFi Summer 算走了 5 年多

21/ 因为 AI 扩散得太快

美国个人渗透率到 61% 只用了 4 年，互联网走同样的距离用了 8 年

22/ 个人端已经涨完，企业端还没开始

个人使用率 61%，企业真正把 AI 用进业务只有 10% 到 20%，传统行业几乎没有采用欲望

23/ 硬件涨价周期有历史规律

铁路、电力、2000 年互联网，原材料涨价都只持续三到四年，这轮 DDR5 三年涨了 14 倍

24/ AI 资本开支已经大到能拖累整个经济

对美国 GDP 的贡献超过三分之一，五大科技公司今年投入超 8000 亿美元，全行业接近 1 万亿，明年破 1 万亿，2028 年 1.3 万亿

25/ 但增速今年是顶点

明年从 94% 掉到 37%，今年就是边际最好的一年，所以市场提前开始杀估值

26/ 这轮算力和 2000 年光纤本质不同

当年铺完不知道有没有人用，泡沫破起来吓人；现在算力建出来一定有人要，只是价格高低，所以回调是估值修正，不是需求崩塌

27/ 比特币这波跟大科技是同向的

One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. 

So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us."

Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.  

There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. 

But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. 

Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were:

1) End the war
2) Focus on cost of living/inflation
3) Put America First
4) Change our relationship to Israel

Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.)

In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. 

The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. 

If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest.

But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.

I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

text:
“期权” —— 这个曾经对多数人都很陌生的衍生品，而如今已成为一名合格交易员的必备技能之一。但其专业又复杂的相关概念，让很多尝试学习的小伙伴望而却步。

合约，只有 “做多和做空” 2个方向，而期权却有4个：买入看涨、买入看跌、卖出看涨、卖出看跌。再加上行权价、到期日、权利金等等，一看就很懵逼.....

这次OKX上线“简易期权”，虽然只有6个代币化股票标的，但这小小的一步却意义重大。他在尝试打破壁垒，降低参与门槛。

其实，“期权”拥有“合约”所不具备的优势和特点。

我们把4个方向简单翻译成：对应“参与上涨、下跌保护、持仓增收、计划买入” 这四种需求。

举个例子：

我看好MSTR具有比BTC更高的价格弹性，但当前价格偏高，想等调整后再买。

假设xMSTR现价150美元，我希望在130买入，那就可以卖出一份行权价为130美元的看跌期权（sell put）。

如果到期时，没跌到130，我收权利金（向买方收租）；如果跌到甚至更低130，我按130买入xMSTR，而收取的权利金还能抵掉部分成本。

所以，我把sell put翻译为可以满足原本就“计划买入”的需求。其他3个方向道理类似，甚至还可以组合使用：

比如持仓时卖出看涨，增加收入；担心下跌时买入看跌，给持仓上保险。把不同工具搭配起来，就能更主动地管理风险敞口。

有兴趣的小伙伴不妨研究研究，相信会有不一样的体会！

当然，操作简单了，不代表风险消失了。 

真正有价值的进步，是让我们学会用工具管理自己的仓位，而不只是押涨跌。

quoted_text:
Scandal erupts in Denmark over TV show that brutally pranked comedian for four months

Danish comedian Rasmus Wallbridge believed he was working with his friend Martin Larsen on a film adaptation of their long-standing idea — a comedy in the style of Scary Movie. 

In reality, the film project was an elaborate setup by broadcaster TV 2: 149 people, including Larsen, played out a staged scenario in front of Rasmus while hidden cameras captured everything. 

The footage was turned into a six-part series called Everybody Loves Rasmus.

The comedian only discovered the truth at the end of filming. He initially took the prank calmly and agreed to the show being broadcast. 

However, after the first episode aired on October 26, the programme triggered a wave of criticism. Viewers, comedians and TV presenters described what happened as bullying and psychological abuse. One presenter called it “psychological torture”.

On October 31, Wallbridge said he was not ready to take part in the discussion and asked the broadcaster not to use such methods again. That same day, TV 2 removed the show from all platforms and apologised to the comedian.

Denmark’s Culture Minister also weighed in on the scandal, describing the programme as a “tasteless psychological experiment” and accusing the broadcaster of violating its own ethical standards.

text:
Has Ethereum lost its soul?

Day 2 at @EFDevcon Mumbai. 🇮🇳

It pains me to say it, but the mood feels a bit disenchanted. You can see it in the half-empty rooms and in the hallway conversations.

I've been to every Devcon since Cancún 2017. Back then, the narrative was about inclusion and empowering the weak. 

For those of us coming from emerging countries, it was a tool to circumvent bad institutions (and maybe build better ones bringing the rule of law where it was lacking.)! Many of us Argentines got into Ethereum because stablecoins were the way around capital controls. It wasn't an ideology. It was a survival tool.

For people from advanced economies, it was a way to escape government and big tech surveillance.

Then the narrative started drifting. DeFi yields, NFTs, memecoins... Each cycle brought more money and less talk about the common person. There are still talks on those original topics, but more and more the stage seems to reflect the worldview of Silicon Valley elites: transhumanism, longevity, life beyond biology.

The contrast couldn't be sharper. Inside, conversations about transcending the human condition, governing societies through futarchy and handing DAO governance decisions over to AI. Outside, the chaos of Mumbai's streets, where millions hustle to survive and deal with very human problems every day.

My impression from day 2 is that Ethereum is at a crossroads: solving the problems of nerds and Silicon Valley, or addressing the every day problems of real people.

The real test isn't whether Ethereum scales, but for what and for whom. If it ends up as a playground for a tiny niche of insiders talking to each other, we can expect emptier conferences every year.

Sorry for the pessimistic take. 🥲 Hoping day 3 finds me in better spirits!

text:
Frontier LLMs can “hide” harmful behaviours with English prompts, but users can still trigger them—just by typing the prompt back in.

Neologism Inoculation Prompting (NIP) is a clever fix: teach the model a made-up token for “be harmful,” then delete it before deployment. No one can type or guess the secret.

The results: On four tricky misalignment tasks and three open-weight models (Qwen-27B, Gemma-31B, OLMo-32B), NIP slashes misalignment triggers from 12–54% (old method) to just 0–6%, while keeping useful behaviour in 8/12 cases. It only needs two trainable vectors—no big rewiring.

Mechanistically, NIP doesn’t erase danger; it locks it behind an unreachable region in activation space. Even adversarial prompt search can’t dig it out (max danger bump ≤0.02 for sports/finance). But it can’t block leakage-prone traits like sycophancy, and someone with weight access could still recover the token.

Why it matters: It’s a lightweight, auditable way to “carve out” unsafe abilities, letting LLM deployers keep their models both safe and capable.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/JVilPul7js

text:
[ "민주당 압승이 오히려 AI와 국채시장에 긍정적일 수 있다... 하지만 금리 전망은 여전히 불확실 ]

노무라의 찰리 맥엘리고트는 선거 다음 날 주식과 채권이 오르고 달러가 빠진 걸 특별한 반전으로 보지 않았다. 

민주당 압승 직후 반사적으로 빠졌다가 풋옵션이 현금화되면서 되돌아온 것이고.. 지난 10년간 헤지가 늘 그랬듯 하락 베팅을 수익화할 창은 짧았다는 것이다. 

연말까지 고객들이 선호하는 거래는 중간선거 후.. 계절성과 간밤의 정치 온건화를 겨냥한 콜스프레드 같은 건설적이되 과하지 않은 포지션이다.

시장이 낙관하는 근거는 네 가지로 정리했다. 

첫째, 선거 결과로 데이터센터 건설이 강제로 속도 조절되면 하이퍼스케일러 CAPEX 무한 경쟁이라는 죄수의 딜레마가 완화되고, 회사채와 주식 발행 부담, 잉여현금흐름 소진 우려, 국채 구축 효과, 높은 중립금리 걱정이 한꺼번에 줄어든다. 

둘째, 마이크로소프트, 아마존, 메타, 알파벳이 시에라클럽 등 환경단체와 책임 있는 데이터센터 개발 협의체를 꾸렸다는 보도가 나왔는데, 빅테크가 이미 변화를 읽고 민주당 정권에서도 건설을 느리게나마 이어갈 틀을 만든 셈이다. 데이터센터 완전 중단이라는 최악의 시나리오 위험이 줄었다. 

셋째, 트럼프가 선거 뒤 이란 공습 계획이 당장은 없다고 하면서 유가가 내리고 금리와 달러가 따라 내려 금융여건이 완화됐다. 

넷째, 캘리포니아 부유세가 막히고 재산세 인상 시도가 전국적으로 거부되면서 급진 좌파 전환 우려도 꺾였다. 결국 이번 선거는 사회주의 선택이 아니라 트럼프 심판 성격이었다는 해석이다.

금이 3% 오른 건 두 가지 신호로 읽었다. 

민주당 정권에서도 재정적자 축소 같은 고통은 용납되지 않을 거라는 것, 그리고 트럼프의 이란 의지가 약해지면 걸프국과 이란의 금 매도 압력이 완화될 수 있다는 것이다.

종합하면 금리가 소폭 내려갈 순풍은 있지만 국채 강세장의 시작은 아니라고 봤다. 

데이터센터 투자가 느려지면 성장 기대는 식고, 동시에 완전 중단 위험은 줄어 성장 충격도 피한다. 

메타가 유로 채권까지 찍을 만큼 발행은 여전하고.. 높아진 조달 비용과 넓어진 스프레드는 긴축 효과를 내고, 인플레이션은 여전히 높다. 

금리는 당분간 방향 없이 흔들릴 가능성이 크다는 결론이다.

text:
赵长鹏：加密采用率达 20% 可能需 5 至 10 年，当前零售端创新不足

币安创始人 @cz_binance 在牛津辩论社发表演讲时提到，加密货币的采用进程缓慢但不可逆。他判断，加密采用率达到 20% 可能需要 5 至 10 年，中间 60% 至 80% 可能需要一二十年，最后 20% 则可能耗时很久,初期充满怀疑，越过 20% 后加速，越过 80% 后放缓。

他指出，过去两年很多国家政府对加密的态度出现明显变化，美国转向加密友好、其他国家跟随，但金融系统升级缓慢、大机构存在惯性，银行直接接入区块链摩擦较大。

目前零售端支付与日常用例的创新仍显不足，许多项目刚刚起步、尚需一两年，而机构端的 ETF、股票代币化与稳定币正在增长。不同周期焦点不同，从早期的比特币、IC0 到 meme 币，近期已转向机构采用，他对此保持乐观并愿意资助开发者。

author: Vault_St
quoted_text:
Every major shock shows up onchain as a jump in USDC borrowing costs.

After the @Binance hack, the average borrow rate across Aave, Morpho and Fluid nearly doubled to ~10% within hours, then fell back to pre-hack levels in under two days.

After April’s Kelp DAO exploit, where the bad collateral sat inside @aave itself, rates nearly quadrupled to ~13.5%, held above 11% for four days and took about a week to normalize.

The difference: @tether and @circle moved fast to freeze stolen funds, and Binance quickly committed to covering user losses. That kept the panic out of DeFi lending.

text:
不用行权价和到期日，也能做出期权式收益？

Paragon @tradeparagon  在 Hyperliquid 上推出 Power Perps，尝试把期权的核心特征「凸性」直接塞进永续合约。

以 HYPE² 为例：HYPE 上涨 50%，二次方指数上涨 125%；HYPE 下跌 50%，指数只下跌 75%。

这意味着多头上涨时赚得更多，下跌时亏得更少。再配合线性合约，还能组合出做多或做空波动率的策略。

但凸性不是免费的：多头需要持续支付与方差相关的资金费率，加杠杆也依然可能被清算。

这类产品最有意思的地方在于，它不要求交易者重新学习一整套期权界面，而是用熟悉的永续合约操作，获得更复杂的收益结构。

@HyperliquidX 上的创新，正在从「交易什么资产」，走向「还能创造什么交易工具」。

在你还以为美国机构只能去离岸开户之前，读这个。

11 月 4 日，Coinbase 官方宣布：美国及其他合规地区的合格机构，可以在 Coinbase Prime 上直接做全球期权和永续。

官方口径写得很清楚：
1）流动性来自 Deribit，号称全球最大加密期权所
2）覆盖 20+ 资产，点名 BTC、ETH、SOL、XRP、AVAX、HYPE
3）保证金可用 BTC、ETH、USDC

但很多人容易漏掉一句免责声明：衍生品由 Coinbase Financial Markets（CFTC 注册 FCM）提供，Deribit 本身不向美国提供服务。订单走美国注册经纪商接全球盘口，不是把合约搬到美国本土交易所。

流动性统一了，保证金却没有混在一起。按结算币种和组合单独算，BTC 仓位补不了 USDC 结算的亏。

我的判断：这是美国机构合规入场衍生品的关键一刀，比再喊一个「现货 ETF」更硬。前提是你得先过 Eligible Contract Participant 资格和期货经纪开户，散户别急着当成自己也能点开做。

你更在意「终于不用离岸开户」，还是「保证金还是按币种拆开」？

In mid-October, Russia's Cosmos 2612 military satellite approached within a kilometer of X36, a Finnish-operated satellite providing radar imagery to Ukraine and Western militaries.

Space specialist Greg Gillinger described the encounter as looking like an attack rehearsal, arguing that such proximity was unnecessary for surveillance or electronic interference.

Now, two other Russian military satellites are approaching the orbital path of another satellite operated by the same Finnish company, ICEYE.

Russia has previously warned that Western commercial satellites supporting Ukraine could become legitimate military targets.

With Democrats winning the U.S. midterms and potentially expanding funding for Ukraine, Moscow may see an offensive against Western satellite networks as its next strategic move.

Source: Reuters, WTVB / Writer: Mhedi
