text:
何一 @heyibinance  谈币安：安全、信任与长期责任｜全文稿和中英文字幕对照。

把一姐这段分享整理成了中英字幕，1.25 倍速，约 14 分钟，我觉得非常值得听一下，特别是一姐关于 AI 的认知和这次被盗的最真实的内心想法。

内容比较多，核心可以分成四块：

1️⃣ 安全事件与用户信任 ；
她如何解释这次63亿被盗的安全事件？严格的内部制度，为什么仍可能被社会工程攻击突破？AI 又会怎样改变安全攻防？

2️⃣ AI 与交易所的未来；
从 AI 产品到股票、大宗商品，她眼里的币安，接下来会走向什么样的平台？

3️⃣ 为什么“上币就涨”失效了； 
DEX 的发展、上市前的高估值，以及项目收入和代币价值的脱节，怎样改变了普通用户赚钱的机会？

4️⃣ 发币之后，谁来负责；
项目方已经变现、创始人已经财富自由，还有什么动力继续建设？她也谈到了 BNB、正现金流，以及为什么自己还在工作。

我觉得一姐传递了一个很好的价值观：就是买一个币之前，除了看叙事和价格，更值得问清楚：这个项目靠什么持续创造价值，价值如何传递给持有人，以及谁愿意长期为它负责。
最后一姐讲完 林克 @CryptoSociety42 问了一句：一姐这个是有稿子还是脱稿的，

一姐说从来不用稿子，每次聊的都是最直接的心里话。
听到这里，我个人顿时佩服不已！

全文稿如下：

00:00

这么多年下来，我觉得事实告诉我们，它其实是非常有韧性的，行业也是非常有韧性的。总的来说，我对抗量子攻击这件事情还是有信心的。

而且我们也会花时间、花精力去参与和投入，让行业做得更好。

第二点，来讲一下 AI 的发展和变化。这两天，可能很多朋友跟我们的产品经理，也沟通了一些我们的 AI 策略，或者说新产品。

00:30

说实话，它离我想象中的 AI 产品还有很大的距离。但所有的事情，都是从无到有、从零到一的过程。

我们就一步一步，先去做一个小的 demo，然后不断地去迭代它。也欢迎大家给我们更多意见，一起把产品做成我们想象中的样子。

如果别人问我：“你想象中最完美的 AI 产品是什么样的？”

我可能会说，我恨不得它像 ChatGPT 一样。我告诉它：“你去帮我做一个策略，只许赚钱，不许亏钱。”

01:05

然后它就帮我去做交易了。但可能也不太真的能够实现。所以，这是不断循环往复、小步快跑的过程。

01:16

第三点，对于整个行业来讲，所有的新技术都会带来整个行业快速的发展，但当然也会带来一些挑战。

就这次的安全事故，外面有很多声音，大家都在说：“币安草台班子。你们的员工居然可以拿电脑访问外部网站，或者跟别人面试？”

我强调一下，其实我们内部的 policy，我们的政策是非常严格的。

01:46

所以，我前两天也在网上去认领了。

前几年一直在被人骂，说币安居然因为员工往自己的电脑下爱奇艺，当时就被发现了，然后很快就让他走人了，而且是我们一个比较高潜的员工。

大家觉得我们是在乱找理由开人，或者因为市场行情不好，所以把人开掉。

其实，它是一个安全准则。

但真实的挑战是，我们在过去这一年，拦截了 58 次类似的、不同形态的攻击。

02:19

但黑客也是不断跟我们斗智斗勇。他们传递过来的木马，也不像过去想象中，还是一个大的文件包，很容易去触发你的风控。

它不是一成不变的，是不断斗智斗勇、变化的过程。黑客没有大家想的那么蠢，也没有大家想的那么容易。

在这里面，我觉得对方其实也是适当地应用了 AI 工具的。

包括在社会工程的过程当中，我也很困惑，为什么员工会放松警惕。

02:56

因为我们公司需要考试，去完成安全培训，而且是每个人都要做，然后还有风控培训。

我觉得可能是前面沟通的时候，对方会诱以重利，说有一个非常好的工作机会。

而且对方是一个真实的猎头。不是大家想象中，包装了一个账号，他是一个真实的人。

我觉得黑客应该是跟真实的猎头签了一个合同。

03:27

给了他一个名单，让他定点去找哪些人是币安的员工。通过这种不断的“围点打面”的方式，来渗透和进行社会工程攻击。

但好的一点是，AI 既然能够作为矛，另一方面，也能作为盾。

今天大家也看到 OpenAI 公开了一个新技术，能够非常好地去做安全攻防。

很多人说：“OpenAI 做这个产品，是不是以后做安全的都失业了？”

03:59

我觉得也不会。

这是传统的安全解决方案和新的 AI 解决方案相结合的过程。所以，它不是谁干掉谁的过程，有点像我们和［词语不清］。

04:10

所以，我就再说回币安。

币安这么多年来，一直非常感谢我们社区所有人的支持，我觉得确实非常感动。

因为很多人可能都不太相信。大家想象中：“币安，你们这次丢了这么多钱，你跟 CZ 是不是感觉天都塌了？”

说实话，其实我和他都非常冷静。我们甚至没有在任何地方大喊大叫，也没有骂过任何人。

04:39

我觉得，你面对的一切，都是对你淬炼的一个过程。

它是对你的心境的修炼，也是对你怎么理解这个世界的一个挑战。

我觉得，确实是我们没有做好嘛，所以付出了巨大的代价。但这个过程，也是一个好的 learning。

至少，第一，这是我们能够覆盖、付得起的范围。

05:09

第二，CZ 经常会说他不在意钱。

所以我提醒大家，karma is real，一定要小心自己说出的每一句话，因为宇宙会给你回应的。

CZ 是真的觉得钱没有那么重要。所以当钱丢了的时候，他就觉得：“丢了，那我们就看怎么把这个事情做好，怎么把安全做好。”

他其实没有什么情绪波动。

05:37

所以这两天，网上说什么“CZ 一夜白头”，其实还好。

虽然他这两天在牛津演讲，也在出差，但他的情绪和我的情绪都是非常稳定的。

不管是对行业，还是对币安，我还是认为，未来的发展路线，必然是由 AI 和 Blockchain 技术驱动，成为一个全球的新型泛金融平台。

06:09

大家可以看到，我们现在平台上可交易的产品，其实已经覆盖了大宗商品、股票，都有。

06:18

大家可能也会抱怨：“为什么币安这么长时间，都不太上新的项目？为什么不多上一些 memecoin？这样我们就可以有更多机会，对吧？”

有一个上币预期，是不是这些发币方就会更好一些？

在这里，我有时候可能会不合时宜地经常唱一些反调。

包括在 2017 年的时候，如果大家能找到历史记录，就可以看到。

06:50

我当时说，发币是一个［词语不清］的过程。

你其实是抵押自己的信誉，拿回来一笔钱。但这个币，是你需要为它负责的。

我觉得，说出去的话真的会应验。

所以我这么多年，还在币安辛辛苦苦干活，因为我觉得，发的 BNB 就是我的责任。

跌了，我觉得过意不去。涨了，大家希望它还要涨，但涨到高点，可能又会掉下来一点。

07:19

你会发现，它真的会成为一个长期的责任。

所以币安这么多年，确实只发了一个 BNB。包括如果做新的公链，也不会再发新的币。

它本身对人性是一个极大的挑战。

当你非常容易就能融资，拿到一笔钱；当整个网络有非常强的流动性，这个钱可以变现的时候，作为一个普通人，还有什么动力去辛辛苦苦干活呢？

07:54

如果我做的产品没有用户、没有市场、没有收入，但我的代币也能卖出钱，如果创业是为了财富自由，为什么还要努力？

所以它就变成了：好的商业模型、好的生意，然后是初心——你到底因为什么做这件事，以及财富自由。

这件事就会变成一个“不可能三角”。

08:25

我已经财富自由了，还要辛辛苦苦干活，赚的钱还要赋能这个代币。

而代币不是只有你自己有，可能大部分已经在用户手里。那你自己到底这么努力在干嘛？

很多年，大家都问我：“一姐，你已经财富自由这么多年了，为什么还在辛辛苦苦干活？”

我只能说，真的是为 BNB holder 打工了。

08:52

很多人说：“币安早期上的币价格都会涨，那为什么现在上币不涨？是因为你们上币没有要求、没有标准？”

但你会发现，市场已经变了。

2017 年、2018 年，甚至 2021 年之前，币安在整个 crypto 行业里，确实有很强的话语权。

如果一个币不在币安 listing，流动性就不会好。市值做得再高，最后也可能没办法变成钱。

09:23

那个就是所谓的“纸面富贵”，真的是绝对的纸面富贵。只要一卖，市场上没有流动性，就直接砸到底。

所以那个时候，我们可以跟项目方 negotiate，以一个比较低的价格去 listing。这就是为什么当年大家在币安买到的币会涨。

但客观地说，DEX 确实是更去中心化的方案，所以它本身就是一个平权的过程。

币安的这种特权，也随着 DEX 的发展被降权了。

09:55

在被降权的过程当中，你会发现，市场上的 VC 币，价格其实已经被 pump 得很高。

还没有 listing，价格就已经很高了。所以最后大家发现，叫“上线即高点”，这是一个典型特征。

第二，就算有一些项目，刚上时币价比较低，可能让用户吃到一波红利，但很多项目方，就像我说的一样，能够赚到钱，最后可能就觉得：“反正也没有监管机构，没有法律……”

10:24

“……要求我必须对这件事情负责。”

刚好又赶上上一轮，说代币不能是证券，他们就有更强的理由和借口，说：“这就是一个治理代币，跟我的收入不挂钩。”

所以代币上面没有任何价值附着，也不能指望他们最终对代币价格负责。这是第二个场景。

这两波下来以后，你会发现，真正能够留守在这个行业……

10:53

……做出盈利模型的公司，有没有？有，还蛮多的。

包括 GMGN，还有很多钱包，收益都还不错，也包括一些做代币的。

只是过去可能基于法律原因，没办法赋能代币；后来可能觉得没必要，各种各样的原因吧。

所以市场上真正有长期、健康商业模型，且有持续措施，能够赋能代币价值的，就会越来越少。

11:22

所以最后会发现，本质是整个行业的空心化。当然，大家可以简单地归因为币安的原因。

经过上一轮，VC 也进来看了一圈，最后觉得，虽然来钱很快，包括像［机构名称不清］这样的顶级风投，可能觉得，这是一个［词语不清］非常好的生意，但不是一个能长期承接大资金，且［词语不清］、可重复的场景。

11:56

所以，他们又更多地回到了股权投资。

12:00

对于币安，我们最大的思考是什么？

第一，用户要什么？用户的需求其实很朴素。作为一个用户，我希望它是一个公平的平台。

第二，如果我是普通用户，我希望能有赚钱的机会。

所以后来，币安也开放了很多入口。比如市值比较小的 memecoin，我们也会 listing。

我们把很多市场上比较 popular 的币上上来。现在，你在链上想买的币……

12:31

……哪怕在 Alpha 买不到，在 CEX 和 DEX 的中间区间买不到，在钱包里也可以买到。

行业在变化，用户也在分层、分流。

有的用户只玩 memecoin，只“打狗”；有的用户做理财；有的用户主要做返佣，对吧？

每个人都可能在生态里找到自己的位置。

但最终要解决一个核心问题：真正有价值的资产在哪里？

12:59

为了回答这个问题，我们从去年开始准备，到今年上线，上了大量股票、大宗商品这样的代币。

不管是过去的 crypto 资产，还是现在的股票资产、大宗商品，任何商品，都无法保证投资只赚不赔。

这种风险，不仅存在于某一个币。

13:29

一些传统股票资产，也会出现大涨或者大跌。大家还是要有这个风险概念。

13:39

最后，还是感谢今天所有参与活动的用户，感谢大家的信任。

“信任”两个字说起来简单，做起来很难。

当币安开放提币的时候，说实话，提走的币比我预期的少得多。

因为我觉得，大家在这种时候会比较风声鹤唳，一点风吹草动，可能都会很紧张。

14:10

这时候把币提出去，是一个很正常的行为。

但我们发现，从昨天开始，就已经变成正向流入了，24 小时内已经是正向流入了。

所以非常感谢大家对币安的信任，我们一定守护好这份信任。

一直以来，市场里都有各种各样的声音。可能亏了，骂得凶的可能就……比如去年 10 月 11 号的事情，是不是币安搞的？

14:39

大家很容易陷入这种阴谋论，因为阴谋论更有戏剧性，也更容易传播。

包括说：“你们是不是自导自演，自己黑自己，就是为了展现自己是一个负责任的公司？”

首先，我其实在推特上也发过：如果公司直接关门跑路，可以找借口说自己被盗。

但是，如果公司所有的人都还在，每天都在这里，24 小时守着，盯着运营……

15:12

……而且我们是一家盈利非常健康的公司。

大家知道，我到现在也没赞助什么大型全球赛事。知道你的，已经知道你了。不需要把你的 logo 和另一个 logo 绑在一起，这样来显得自己很厉害。那个成本确实也比较高。

所以我一直追求正现金流，追求健康的商业模型。

我原来在互联网公司做了很多年。

15:40

当年一下科技，小咖秀那一波，也差点 IPO。

所以对于花钱买量、虚假繁荣，我是非常、非常不喜欢的。

这个过程中的 training，这种训练，决定了我在币安的做事方式。我希望我们走的每一步，都非常踏实。

关于 10 月 10 号的事情，如果有人觉得是币安故意搞的，这样的朋友，我觉得可能不太适合做投资。因为还是需要有一个清晰的判断。

16:11

TL;DR: In the early hours of Nov 4, SignalPlus was targeted in an attack that began with a compromised third-party Telegram account, affecting a small number of accounts without IP whitelisting.

We detected and contained the intrusion quickly. As a precaution, we immediately worked with our CEX partners to revoke all SignalPlus-linked API keys and temporarily paused our terminal services.

Total losses are under US$82k, and all affected users will be reimbursed in full.

We expect to bring services fully back online over the next few days. Updates and user instructions will be shared through our official channels.

author: SignalPlus_Web3
quoted_text:
SignalPlus Announcement on Security Incident Response and User Protection

In the early hours of November 4, the SignalPlus team detected anomalous activity and identified that our systems were the target of a cyberattack. The team acted swiftly to contain the incident and prevent it from spreading further. Based on our assessment to date, total losses from this incident are below US$82k, and we have already begun fully reimbursing affected users on a case-by-case basis.

Containment and Reimbursement
Protecting our clients’ access and credentials has always been SignalPlus’s highest priority. Upon discovering the anomaly, we immediately contacted all of our partner exchanges and had every user API key associated with SignalPlus disabled on the exchange side. We have also suspended our platform services while the team conducts a comprehensive security review.
These precautionary measures were applied to all users out of an abundance of caution. The deactivation of an API key does not mean that the associated account information or assets have been compromised. All of our partners have been informed, and the situation has been contained.
We sincerely apologize for the disruption and inconvenience this incident may have caused our users. Our security investigation is ongoing, and we will continue to gather user feedback throughout the process.
If you believe you have been affected by this incident, please contact our team to begin the verification process. We remain fully committed to reimbursing all affected users in full.

Incident Summary
Based on our investigation so far, the incident originated from a compromised Telegram account belonging to a contact at one of our third-party technology vendors. Posing as this contact, the attacker communicated with one of our engineers and sent a fake Microsoft Teams meeting invitation. This social engineering attack compromised the engineer’s computer, where the attacker then remained dormant.
In the early hours of November 4, the attacker began using the engineer’s access privileges to attack our internal network. Upon detecting the activity, we blocked the attack and closed the vulnerabilities identified. We then contacted our exchange partners to proactively disable all SignalPlus-related API keys and safeguard user funds, and promptly placed all SignalPlus services into maintenance mode.
Once we have completed a full review and the necessary security patches, and have confirmed that services can be safely restored, we will bring services back online in phases. Updates on our progress and instructions for users will be shared through our official channels. While our services are suspended, users can still use the exchanges’ official platforms to view and manage your accounts, positions, and open orders in the meantime.

Standing Together Against Malicious Attacks
Cyberattacks are an ongoing challenge across the technology industry, and tactics such as impersonation and social engineering exploit the trust built into everyday business relationships. SignalPlus firmly condemns unauthorized intrusion, information theft, and any malicious activity that puts user assets at risk.
Nevertheless, we also acknowledge a gap in our safeguards. We had not previously required IP whitelisting as a mandatory condition for exchange API key access, and is a failure point that should have been more sufficiently enforced. We take responsibility for this oversight. Going forward, we will tighten our API access requirements and further strengthen endpoint security for development devices, internal access controls, and key management.
Protecting our users and strengthening our security are responsibilities we take seriously. We will continue to invest in our defenses and deepen collaboration and threat-intelligence sharing with exchanges, technology partners, and security firms to guard against attacks, combat cybercrime, and protect user interests and trust across the industry.
Thank you to all our users for your patience and support. We will carry out any necessary reimbursements, remediation, and service restoration diligently, and will keep you updated on our progress.

The SignalPlus Team

Markets are a fantastic tool for understanding what's happening in the world. Election day highlighted this once again.
author: bcap
quoted_text:
Last night was special.

Election days just never get old for us at Polymarket. Watching regular people experience the beauty of market based forecasts as the results come in. How practically useful it is. How simple it is to interpret. When it clicks, it clicks.

It’s now routinely hours between when prediction markets call it versus the TV networks. The networks hold out until absolute certainty, and the suspense keeps it entertaining all night. No knock to them, but now there’s Polymarket, and many people are realizing they want to know what's happening in real time.

I know the industry has gained a mixed rap for a variety of reasons, many of which are criticisms with real merit. But I think I speak for both myself and my peers when I say we got into this because we really love the idea of markets being able to place a price on the future (e.g. Democrats had a 92% chance to take the House on Polymarket), and how that can help people better understand what's likely to happen and make decisions accordingly.

Our mission is to make sure we deliver on the promise of prediction markets, which was on full display last night. In the midst of so much noise around what we do, the American people get to see what Polymarket is really all about. Feels like one step closer to the dream. Onwards.

The largest security incident in crypto’s history happened last week, and it was not the first of the year. Every yield-bearing stablecoin, managed strategy and curated vault with exposure answered the same way: within limits, covered by the venue. Every holder of those products carried the same exposure at the same rate.

Risk segmentation is very crucial for onchain finance to scale. Those ready to take risk should earn more yield for it, with protection on the other side.

> Junior holders earn amplified yield in exchange for absorbing losses first.

> Senior holders benefit from automatic protection, backed by junior coverage, with no claims to file or manual intervention required.

Same underlying asset. Two distinct points on the risk-reward curve.

If you’re a yield-bearing stablecoin issuer, curator or credit protocol whose holders all sit at one point on that curve, let’s talk.

text: A well-articulated Republican wake up call.
author: BillAckman
quoted_text:
What an absolute, unmitigated, motherfucking disaster.

We got our asses kicked. We got politically disemboweled. We got dragged through the electoral wood chipper, and the Republican establishment stood there with its collective thumb up its ass wondering why the fucking machine was running.

And now, right on schedule, the excuses are pouring in.

The war. Gas prices. Bad candidates. Historical trends. Voter frustration. Bad messaging.

Jesus fucking Christ, SHUT UP.

We had the majority. We had the presidency. We had the opportunity to deliver. And these incompetent, spineless, self-serving Republican bastards managed to turn political power into a fucking participation trophy.

Let's start with John Thune.

You spectacularly useless son of a bitch.

You had the Senate majority. You had an election integrity bill conservatives desperately wanted passed. You had millions of voters begging Republicans to demonstrate that winning elections actually meant something.

And what did you deliver?

A fucking master class in legislative impotence.

The SAVE Act became another monument to Republican paralysis while the people who elected you watched Washington's favorite collection of overpaid assholes explain why accomplishing anything was just too goddamn complicated.

You had power, John.

HAD.

And now Democrats get to enjoy the congressional authority your leadership helped squander.

What a magnificent fucking achievement. You couldn't have served Democratic interests more effectively if you'd shown up to work wearing a DNC name tag.

And don't think the rest of the Republican establishment gets a free pass. Every useless bastard who spent these last two years hiding behind parliamentary excuses, protecting his precious committee assignments, and treating the Senate like a retirement community deserves the same political eviction notice.

Get the fuck out.

Then there's Iran.

And this is where I have absolutely zero patience for the Monday-morning military strategists pretending the nuclear threat was some imaginary problem.

IRAN MUST NEVER, EVER GET A FUCKING NUCLEAR BOMB.

Not tomorrow. Not ten years from now. Not under some worthless diplomatic agreement held together with wishful thinking and another round of international bullshit.

Never.

We're talking about a regime with a long history of sponsoring terrorism, threatening Israel, brutalizing its own population, and pursuing nuclear capabilities that could fundamentally alter the security of the Middle East.

A nuclear-armed Iranian regime is a nightmare America has every reason to prevent.

And if military action was necessary to eliminate that threat, then the mission needed a clear objective and the determination to achieve it.

Destroy the nuclear weapons capability. Prevent its reconstruction. Make damn sure the regime cannot simply wait out another American administration and resume the same dangerous ambitions.

Finish the fucking job.

Because if Americans endured war, economic disruption, and soaring gasoline prices only to discover Iran could eventually rebuild its nuclear weapons program, then what the everlasting fuck was the point?

I can accept political costs for a mission that makes America and its allies safer.

I cannot accept strategic confusion, endless uncertainty, and politicians who seem incapable of explaining what victory actually means.

And here's the part Republican leadership should have understood before this election became a political slaughterhouse.

Americans were paying the price at the pump while Democrats were pounding them over affordability.

Groceries. Gas. Housing. Insurance. The cost of keeping a fucking roof over your family's head.

Democrats hammered those issues relentlessly.

And Republicans?

Apparently they were too busy measuring the drapes in their offices and scheduling another goddamn television appearance.

How fucking stupid do you have to be to watch voters struggle with household expenses and fail to understand what they're telling you?

Then came the candidates.

James Talarico winning Texas. Abdul El-Sayed winning Michigan. Susan Collins losing Maine.

An electoral fucking earthquake.

And the Republican establishment somehow managed to look surprised.

Surprised?

ARE YOU FUCKING KIDDING ME?

You could practically hear the political foundation cracking for months. Warning signs were flashing everywhere, and these arrogant, complacent jackasses behaved like victory was something they were entitled to receive in the mail.

At some point, incompetence becomes so breathtaking that you begin wondering whether anybody in Republican leadership has ever successfully managed anything more complicated than ordering lunch.

And now comes the part that really makes my fucking blood boil.

The conservative influencer circus.

Bannon. Tucker. Candace. Megyn. Flynn. Alex Jones. Jack Posobiec. And every other self-appointed political messiah whose microphone somehow became more important than winning elections.

Here come the emergency broadcasts. The finger-pointing. The infighting. The hysterical accusations. The endless fucking circular firing squads.

Another catastrophe, another opportunity to turn conservative frustration into a revenue stream.

How many fucking subscriptions does it take to rebuild a political movement?

How many podcasts does it take to pass a bill?

How many goddamn livestreams does it take to win a Senate race?

Apparently nobody knows, because we've spent years watching people get rich explaining why conservatives should be furious while the actual machinery of Republican politics keeps breaking down.

Enough of this shit.

And spare me the conservative celebrities who spend more time attacking other conservatives than figuring out how to defeat Democrats.

Your personal feuds are not a political strategy.

Your fucking podcast ratings are not election results.

And your ability to scream into a microphone for three hours doesn't qualify you to lead anything.

Meanwhile, Democrats just demonstrated that winning elections is still considerably more useful than winning internet arguments.

Imagine that fucking revelation.

And speaking of Democrats, can we appreciate the sheer comedic absurdity of what just happened?

Donald Trump, the man they've spent years calling a dictator, fascist, authoritarian, monarch, and existential threat to democracy, just watched his party lose control of Congress through an election.

A fucking election.

The most terrifying dictator in American history apparently forgot the most important chapter in the dictator's handbook.

CANCEL THE GODDAMN VOTING.

What a fucking embarrassment for the professional hysteria merchants.

Apparently American democracy was healthy enough to deliver Democrats a massive victory after all.

Somebody call the Nobel Committee. Democracy has miraculously survived another Tuesday.

But here's where the laughter stops.

Because this defeat is serious as hell.

Republicans lost power. Democrats gained it. And the people who spent years warning us about the consequences of losing these midterms now have to explain why they were so spectacularly unprepared to prevent it.

And I don't want to hear another fucking word about how everyone needs to unite behind the same failed leadership.

Unite behind WHAT?

More excuses?

More broken promises?

More leadership elections where the same collection of useless bastards rearranges the nameplates and congratulates itself on a fresh start?

Fuck that.

I want a political reckoning so thorough that every complacent Republican incumbent starts checking whether his local voters are recruiting a primary challenger.

Every single one.

I want records examined. Promises compared with results. Leadership positions challenged. Failed candidates replaced. Party organizations rebuilt from the ground up.

And I want Republican voters to stop treating incumbency like some sacred fucking birthright.

You want loyalty?

EARN IT.

You want donations?

SHOW RESULTS.

You want another term?

EXPLAIN WHAT THE FUCK YOU ACCOMPLISHED WITH THE LAST ONE.

Because the era of handing out political participation trophies to career Republicans needs to end.

And don't give me that tired bullshit about how difficult Washington is.

We know Washington is difficult.

That's why we elect people who promise to fucking fight.

If you wanted a comfortable career collecting a government paycheck while accomplishing absolutely nothing, you should have applied for a job as a congressional office fern.

At least the fern produces oxygen.

Now, I know what some people are thinking.

It's over.

MAGA is finished.

Trump is politically crippled.

The country is lost.

BULLSHIT.

Absolute, defeatist, self-pitying BULLSHIT.

Yes, we got our asses kicked.

Yes, Democrats are celebrating.

Yes, the next two years are going to be harder than they needed to be because Republican leadership apparently couldn't pour piss out of a boot with the instructions printed on the heel.

But since when did one election determine the permanent fate of the United States of America?

Obama's Democrats lost 63 House seats and six Senate seats in 2010.

Did the Democratic Party disappear?

Did progressives pack their bags and surrender?

Of course fucking not.

Political movements survive defeats when they have the courage to confront their failures and the discipline to rebuild.

And that's exactly what conservatives need to do.

Because here's what I refuse to believe.

I refuse to believe that millions of Americans who love this country, believe in secure borders, want safe communities, demand responsible government, and expect their elected officials to put American interests first suddenly ceased to exist because a bunch of Republican politicians fucked up an election.

I refuse to believe that the people who stood by Trump through investigations, indictments, impeachment battles, media hysteria, and years of political warfare are suddenly going to surrender because Democrats won Congress.

And I sure as fuck refuse to believe that the future of American conservatism belongs to the same failed political establishment that helped create this mess.

Maybe this election was the wake-up call.

Maybe God looked down at the Republican Party, watched the arrogance, complacency, backstabbing, cowardice, and endless fucking excuses, and decided these people needed a lesson in humility delivered with a goddamn sledgehammer.

Maybe the message was simple.

YOU AREN'T GOOD ENOUGH.

Your leadership isn't good enough.

Your candidates aren't good enough.

Your organization isn't good enough.

Your results sure as hell aren't good enough.

FIX IT.

And maybe that's precisely what needs to happen.

Tear down the complacency. Destroy the culture of excuses. Replace failed leadership. Recruit candidates who actually know how to win. Build organizations capable of turning conservative principles into electoral victories.

Stop expecting Trump to carry every worthless Republican politician across the finish line like some exhausted political pack mule.

Trump has already done more than enough heavy lifting for people who seem incapable of carrying their own fucking briefcases.

And guess what?

TRUMP IS STILL PRESIDENT.

That little detail seems to have escaped the champagne-soaked Democrats dancing on MAGA's supposed grave.

He still occupies the White House. He still has constitutional authority. He still has the ability to shape foreign policy, defend American interests, and pursue the priorities that brought him back to office.

And if Iran's nuclear weapons ambitions can be permanently eliminated, that achievement will matter long after every smug political analyst has forgotten the election-night graphics.

But Trump also needs a Republican Party capable of surviving politically without him.

Because 2028 is coming.

And when it arrives, the movement needs more than nostalgia, slogans, celebrity endorsements, and another fucking collection of candidates who think putting MAGA in their social media biography qualifies them for public office.

We need competence.

We need discipline.

We need courage.

We need people who understand that winning an election is a responsibility, not a fucking lifetime achievement award.

And we need Republican voters willing to hold their own side accountable with the same ferocity they direct toward Democrats.

That means primaries.

That means challenging incumbents.

That means getting involved locally.

That means demanding actual accomplishments instead of accepting another round of bullshit fundraising emails promising that victory is just one more donation away.

I'm sick of the excuses.

I'm sick of the cowardice.

I'm sick of watching Republican politicians campaign like warriors and govern like frightened little bureaucrats terrified of upsetting the Washington cocktail circuit.

And I'm especially fucking sick of being told that criticizing Republican leadership somehow makes you disloyal to the conservative movement.

No.

The people who squandered their opportunities owe voters an explanation.

The people who made promises and failed to deliver owe voters accountability.

And the people who believe Republican voters should simply shut up, open their wallets, and keep electing the same failed leadership can go fuck themselves.

We've got two years.

Two years to clean house.

Two years to rebuild.

Two years to recruit candidates who can actually win.

Two years to prove that conservatism is bigger than any one politician, any one election, or any collection of self-important assholes occupying leadership offices in Washington.

And yes, I'm furious.

I'm absolutely fucking livid.

I'm disgusted by the incompetence. I'm embarrassed by the squandered opportunities. I'm enraged that so many people who demanded our trust treated that responsibility like a goddamn inconvenience.

But I'm still here.

And so are millions of Americans who believe this country is worth fighting for.

We're still breathing.

We're still voting.

We're still organizing.

And we're still perfectly capable of telling every useless politician in Washington exactly where to shove his excuses.

America has survived wars, depressions, assassinations, national catastrophes, and political upheavals far worse than one disastrous election.

We'll survive this.

But surviving isn't enough.

We need to learn from it.

We need to rebuild.

And we need to make damn sure that the next time Republicans are entrusted with power, the people holding it actually know what the fuck they're doing.

So congratulations, Democrats.

Enjoy your victory. Pop the champagne. Dance on the political graves. Write your obituaries for Trump and MAGA.

You've earned your celebration.

But don't confuse a devastating electoral defeat with the permanent death of a political movement.

And to the Republican establishment, here's your message.

The fucking gravy train needs to stop.

No more automatic loyalty.

No more free passes.

No more protecting failed leadership because somebody has been warming a Senate chair since the invention of electricity.

No more treating voters like gullible idiots who can be placated with a flag pin, a campaign slogan, and another goddamn promise.

You wanted power.

You got it.

You squandered it.

Now answer for it.

And to every conservative wondering whether to give up, I have one final thought.

FUCK GIVING UP.

Fuck surrender.

Fuck political despair.

Fuck the idea that one election gets to decide whether we still believe in our country.

The fight for America's future didn't begin with Donald Trump, and it sure as hell doesn't end with a Republican defeat in 2026.

We lost a major battle. We haven't lost the country. And we haven't lost the right to fight like hell for its future.

So bury the excuses.

Fire the failures.

Challenge the incumbents.

Build something stronger.

And when 2028 comes around, make sure the Republican Party has learned the one lesson its leadership apparently needed an electoral ass-kicking to understand:

THE AMERICAN PEOPLE DON'T OWE YOU A GODDAMN THING.

Earn their trust.

Earn their votes.

Earn the right to govern.

Or get the fuck out of the way.

text:
我真心不想在竞争对手遭遇危机的时候批评他们。我真正希望的是，我们能够与他们携手合作，共同提高安全标准，更好地保护整个加密行业。

但我不得不说，那位自称已经不再管理币安的“币圈首富”（你们真的相信吗？）最近接受的采访，实在让我感到恶心。

整场采访充斥着胡说八道和误导性言论。他似乎在淡化自身应承担的责任，甚至试图通过贬低传统银行的安全性，为自己的失败寻找借口。

在这样一场危机中，我们本应看到的是责任担当和行业领导力。但这场采访给人的感觉，却是在不断推卸责任、转移焦点。

这绝不是我们这个行业需要的领导力。

自从事件发生以来，这位“币圈首富”似乎就一直停不下来：

1. 社交媒体上最活跃的人之一。 在整场危机期间，他可以说是币安相关人士中在社交媒体上发声最多、最活跃的一个。

2. 还有时间和马斯克吵架。 在如此严重的安全危机期间，他居然还有精力与 Elon Musk（@elonmusk）争论 SpaceX 股票投资的问题。

3. 反复强调“只有2%的资金流出币安”。 仿佛这个数字就能回答大家对平台安全性的根本质疑。

4. 继续开展营销活动吸引用户存款。 即使危机仍在持续，吸引新资金流入的营销活动也没有停止。

5. 试图暗示传统银行的安全性更差。 一个自称专业的加密行业领导者，怎么能做出如此具有误导性的比较？传统银行与加密交易所面对的威胁模型、攻击面以及安全事故的后果，都存在根本性差异。脱离这些背景进行简单比较，是极其不负责任的。

6. 几乎每次发声，都似乎把一位怀孕的女性推到危机最前线。 而自己则反复加上同一句免责声明：“我已经不管理币安了。”

与此同时，整个加密行业却在为这场危机付出代价：

1. 比特币价格据报道从约81,000美元跌至75,000美元。 市场在动荡中遭受了明显冲击。

2. 数十亿美元的杠杆仓位遭到清算。 市场波动引发了大规模的强制平仓。

3. 整个加密行业的公信力可能再次受到重创。 传统资本市场、机构投资者以及全球监管机构，可能因此对整个行业的安全性和可信度产生更深的疑虑。

经历了这一切，他们所谓的“多层安全防御体系”，如今看起来越来越像一个笑话。

我们的行业需要的，不是更多的借口，不是更多的公关话术，而是真正的合作、真正的责任担当，以及切实有效的用户资产保护和安全标准建设。

少一些推卸责任，少一些营销包装，多一些真正的安全投入和行业协作。

这才是我更愿意投入时间和精力去推动的事情。

即使是竞争对手，我也真心希望我们能够携手把这件事做好。

text:
The calm in the U.S.–China AI race is misleading.

The tariff truce runs until January, but BOTH governments are seen intervening to more AI and tech deals.

1. Meta x Manus AI ($2 BILLION)

In April, Beijing ordered Meta to unwind its Manus acquisition amid reported national security and export-control concerns over AI talent and technology moving to the U.S.

Manus went independent again in August, setting a precedent for Beijing to intervene even after an AI deal closes.

2. SoftBank × ABB Robotics ($5.4 BILLION)

On Nov. 5, Beijing blocked the Chinese portion of Japan’s SoftBank’s $5.4B takeover of Swiss group ABB’s robotics unit. 

China was concerned that robotics data from China could be used to train AI models abroad. SoftBank's shares fell 7% in Tokyo, and ABB says the companies are still pursuing the deal.

3. Oracle × Tencent ($7 BILLION) 

On Nov 4, Oracle scrapped the lease after U.S. officials raised concerns. The same goes with Tencent, with Guangdong officials urging the firm to back domestic chipmakers. 

Tencent originally agreed to rent access to up to 100,000 advanced AI chips at Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia for five years. 

$ORCL fell 2% and $NVDA dropped 3.2% that day.

4. Nvidia’s 49% cap and China’s chip squeeze

Recently, Nvidia reportedly told cloud partners to cap Chinese customers’ share of capacity at 49% in new contracts. 

This could curb TikTok owner ByteDance’s access to more advanced chips overseas.

On Nov. 5, Reuters reported that about 600,000 H200 chips were sitting in Hong Kong as Beijing held off on approving bulk imports.

ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent also ordered more than 3 MILLION RTX Pro 5500 cards with a combined sticker price above $35 BILLION.

他们第一轮额度在2小时内就全部认购完毕，期待接下来的表现。

📝第二，$SONEIUM 是干嘛的？

生态要搞大，必须有一个连接所有人的链上娱乐纽带，这就是 $SONEIUM，它绝不是又一个凭空气炒作的代币，它是整个 Soneium 链上娱乐生态的“血脉”。

• 创作者用它融资开新作
• IP 方用它做全球授权
• 开发者用它搭工具、做游戏
• 粉丝用它支持作品，拿回收益

就像 Soneium 的CEO @WatanabeSota 说的，“娱乐产业的起点永远是创作者。” 当一个平台把创作者的生存、粉丝的热爱和资本的回报全用代币经济学有机绑在了一起，它就不再是一个冷冰冰的链上协议，而是一个真正有温度的文化生态。

最后我的一些思考，以前给爱豆、给 IP 充值，基本是单向的无底洞。如果这套模式真能跑通，粉丝就从纯消费者变成了参与者，这个方向毋庸置疑，是二次元玩家的福音，至少对于我来说，意义重大！

十分期待看到后期项目，关于IP代币化落地的进展和情况，好的IP 能不能持续引进，收益分配是否真实透明，代币真实的需求和消耗情况，都值得持续追踪。新代币波动大，别盲目冲，先小仓位观察。DYOR🙏

text:
🤖OpenAI just published research showing  models found and developed exploits for 948 local privilege escalation (LPE) vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel, spending $1.2M in API credits.

To put this into perspective: the Linux kernel powers almost all cloud infrastructure, Android devices, supercomputers, and modern networking. Linux enforces process isolation. An unprivileged application, like a calculator or a basic utility, is not supposed to read memory, inspect processes, or touch cryptographic keys held by another process or software wallet.

A local privilege escalation simply breaks that security boundary. It allows an unprivileged process to escape its world and gain root control over the entire system (like full access to everything).

OpenAI demonstrated that an automated pipeline can discover nearly a thousand ways to do this in a single campaign. While the research is impressive, it exposes three uncomfortable realities:

1️⃣ Finding bugs is not fixing bugs
 LLMs are remarkably good at static analysis, reproduction, and exploit generation. Generating sound patches for complex kernel code is an entirely different challenge. Kernel fixes often introduce performance regressions, subtle race conditions, or fail to address the root architectural variant.

2️⃣ The attack surface remains massive
These 948 exploits targeted only local privilege escalation, and only audited a fraction of the kernel code. They do not account for remote code execution, network stack vulnerabilities, firmware flaws, or supply chain compromises. Finding 1,000 paths to root does not mean the system is secure; it simply means we mapped 1,000 holes in a 40-million-line dam. The density of vulnerabilities in software is extremely higher than anyone thought before 🫠

3️⃣ The defensive economics do not scale
 A $1.2M audit run is pocket change for a frontier AI lab or a patient nation-state adversary. But virtually no open-source maintainer, startup, or enterprise can spend millions of dollars per release cycle on tokens just to partially reduce latent vulnerabilities. If defense costs millions of dollars per scan while sophisticated attackers only need to find one unpatched path, the asymmetry favors the attacker.

The real lesson here is that software isolation alone will always fail under automated adversarial pressure. The only durable answer is architectural: minimizing attack surfaces, proving security invariant, enforcing strict hardware roots of trust where secrets live, and building toward cryptographic guarantees that make critical compromises structurally impossible rather than merely expensive.

author: zuoyeweb3
quoted_text:
Perp DEX 的二手时间：HYPE 越过斩杀线，EVM 命定天花板

确实应该给 Perp DEX 写个后续，近 20 余个项目要在 2026Q1 走上 TGE 之路，从 Aster 的交易量到 StandX 的挂单积分，向市场输出的噪音让每个人心神不定。

这不应该成为对 Hyperliquid 的怀疑，HyperEVM 和 HYPE 的协同飞轮未成功建立，但 Lighter 们无法卷死新王，我们沉湎于币安和 FTX 争霸的一手资料，导致 Perp DEX War 成为二手记忆。

## 陷进 HYPE 新篇章

Lighter 不 Lighter，Hyper 更 Hyper

Lighter 无疑是成功项目，在 Hyperliquid 证实 Perp 赛道后成功抢滩，营造出 Hyperliquid 是币安的对标者，Lighter 是 Hyperliquid 的对标者的既定印象。

乌龟不能持续叠下去，参考交易所本身的竞争格局，币安之外的 OKX 运营 OKB 异常困难，Coinbase 的市值是 Kraken 估值 5 倍有余。

交易具备天然垄断效应，行业第二都无法自循环，Perp DEX 目前已经进入红海阶段，不可能出现大规模市场增量，剩下的只是为了 TGE 而进行的存量博弈。

先来给 BNB 正名，币安主站和 BNB Chain 需要链接器，HYPE 至今未完成的动作。

图片说明：币安和 Hyperliquid 比较
图片来源：@zuoyeweb3

项目方需要币安“上币效应”，因此愿意支付最贵的渠道费，从币安主站现货、合约到盘前交易，再到钱包的 Alpha 和 YZi Labs 的 EASY Residency，莫不如是。

币安需要项目方在主站外的“流量运营”，尽量延缓上币后的死亡曲线，因此 BNB Chain 上的亲儿子们（如 PancakeSwap 和ListaDAO）需要接纳项目方的资产，用运营动作接续下一波上币效应。

这才是整个 BNB 和 BNB Chain 对币安的真实作用，但这建立在币安主站存在上币效应的前提下，反而引发 Hyperliquid 的自我突破。

如果要为以上的逻辑纠错，Hyperliquid 崛起之路就是明证，Perp 长期遵循“先现货，再合约”的既定逻辑，但是 Hyperliquid 并不是如此，而是主打「交易 Perp」本身，这建立在整个行业，尤其是交易所已经无法保证上币效应，交易主流化已经成为行业共识。

- OKX 们无法在上币后维持项目价格，既无流动性，也无链上 DeFi 生态，只能作为项目方的二等分销商，OKB 缺乏链上价值捕捉能力，只能用作站内优惠券，丢失代币根本作用；

- Hyperliquid 给予 Trader 专业体验，在 FTX 崩溃后，HyperCore 成为链上交易代名词，越是大额交易，越需要 Hyperliquid 流动性支持。

多说一句，Aster 和 CZ 曾推动「隐私/暗池交易」，但无法撼动 Hyperliquid 市占率，在少数洗钱需求外，隐私并不构成 Trader 优先项，币安主站需要 KYC 也无关紧要。

图片说明：主要交易主流币
图片来源：@asxn_r

真正根本性、且不可逆的趋势是，人们只交易 BTC/ETH 等主流币种，新币仅在上线时有一定交易量，从 BeraChain 等到 Monad 、Sonic 等新生代 L1 莫不如是。

头部交易所赖以生存的“上币效应”，二三线所依赖的手续费，都已经无可奈何走入历史，这可能才是交易所自营 Perp DEX，以及主打交易一切，接纳传统金融（股票、外汇和贵金属）背后的真实原因。

但这一切都不会伤害到 Hyperliquid 的流动性，在RFQ 架构：市场级做市商，迟到 Perp DEX 的另类选择一文中，我曾指出Variational 的优势/特点在于开放做市商架构给普通散户，这是一种真实的市场需求，但是大部分 Perp DEX 的刷量积分赛是一种“前期负债”，等待 TGE 时刻兑现。

如果你认为 Bitget 搞金色营销就能抢占币安衍生品市场，那么 StandX 挂单积分就能挑战 Hyperliquid 的市场份额。

流动性越好的市场，越会成为 trader 的日常场所，在上币效应更加缺乏的 Perp DEX 领域，撸毛党和真实用户的画像更加偏离，别忘了，大部分人还在靠 CEX 买双币赢，更别说真去链上实操 Perp。

Ligher 接纳外汇，Edge 自建 Chain，在未战胜 HyperCore 流动性的前提下，已经不可避免变得复杂以支撑叙事，这会反向降低其代币价值捕捉能力，进而演化为 OKB 类似物——站内优惠券。

认真回答一下监管对 Hyperliquid 的预期“折价”，从 BitMEX 开始，CEX/DEX 从未因为美国的监管行动而被市场排斥，只有因为被盗、暴跌而出现市场份额的大幅变化。

- 被盗组：KuCoin（2020）、ByBit（2025 被盗 14 亿+美元）
- 暴跌组：BitMEX 2020·3·12 拔网线
- 名誉组：火币——孙割的 pGala 事件

此外，只有 SBF 的 FTX 是被 Coindesk 的 FUD 致死，并且输在江湖经验不如 CZ，由此观之，而 1011 只不过是币安等老牌交易所的年度日常。

现在是 SEC 难得的放松监管时刻，币安已经正式上岸阿布扎比，Hashkey 完成香港 IPO，Hyperliquid 不存在无法被监管的状态，即使是 Hyperliquid 团队坚持“去中心化”的外表，其也可参考币安的分主体监管，将核心清算部分纳入监管框架。

法律是弱者的准入限制，合规是强者的上岸价格。

## 公链需要强运营

CEX 上币效应和 DEX 刷量效果都在下降，Hyperliquid 的流动性没有任何问题，HYPE 越过斩杀线，不会沦为第二个 FTT。

这不是故事的全部，HYPE 至今和 HyperEVM 生态对不齐，制造不出类似 BNB 的生态“虚假繁荣”，而不是类似 ETH 主网的 DeFi 体系，这种现象已经在对不齐：以太坊失血，Hyperliquid 失速详述，在此不再多言。

本文聚焦现象的成因，以及出路在何方。

火箭燃料和推力的关系是对数关系，HyperCore 交易量和 HYPE 币价也是对数关系。

限定在化学火箭架构下，这意味着燃料质量需指数级增加才能实现线性速度提升，现在 HyperCore 交易费用支撑 HYPE 的币价，但是 HyperCore 的交易量不可能无限制增加，尤其是在币安和 Perp DEX 全力分流的情况下。

图片说明：代币价格和交易量
图片来源：@zuoyeweb3

注意，以上仅作运动变化说明，HYPE 的初始价格在个位数，但真正稳定在 30 美元才是“大众视野下”的初始公允估值，并且交易量也进行过修改，以便于说明代币价格和 HyperCore 交易量的关系。

注意一下，这和 Perp DEX 卷不死 Hyperliquid 并不冲突，币圈的资产只有 BTC/ETH，现阶段整体 Perp 市场规模已经阶段性触顶。

我们来解构下 Hyperliquid 团队的“佛系”从何而来，也许这个道理并不复杂，但足够残酷，Hyper 团队仍在以 BTC 当做公链标准，仍在以 FTX 当做衍生品交易所的参考对象，好的要学习，坏的要避免。

USDH 的拍卖 Ticker 就很有说服力，Hyperliquid 官方节点不参与投票，也不指定任何团队，也不会进行官方扶持流动性，现状就是 USDH 缺乏足够的发展潜力，并无相较于 USDC 和 USDe 的显著优势。

Hyperliquid 团队的“无为而治”是目前 HyperEVM 的最大问题，这并不是说 Hyperliquid 缺乏运营意愿和能力，大家也许还记得，Hyperliquid 首次出圈就是因为 Meme，随后上线的 Unit 也有“官方”跨链桥之实，USDC 也长期借助 Arbitrum 直通 HyperCore。

但这一切都仅限于对 HyperCore，也许在 Hyperliquid 团队看来，HyperCore 是产品，HyperEVM 是生态，产品要强运营，生态要足够开放。

可惜，时代变了，如今的公链更像一种 Super App，并且和互联网巨头类似，已经多年没有新全民单品出现，TON/Monad/Berachain/Sonic 都是如此，甚至于 Plasma 压根不像稳定币公链，更像 Vault 成精。

链上基建的过分成熟，导致公链/L2 已经没有直接的网络效应，要么像 ETH L1/Solana 打存量，要么像 Canton 引入 RWA 做 SaaS 变种服务，要么像 BNB Chain 人为维持。

但是，Jeff 想竭力避免 FTX 的强运营导致的灾难，进而在 HyperEVM 生态上选择保守策略，导致项目方只能靠社区自治，无法构筑起和 HYPE 的互动，只能在分销完 HYPE 后速生速死。

即使是 HyperCore 的运营动作，也遵循在最小限度原则，大家可以关注下 Hyperliquid、Jeff 和 Hyper Foundation 三个账号，基本没有任何和项目方的互动。

这种情况适合 2017 年或者 2020 DeFi Summer 时代，链上缺乏对应的卡位产品，做出来就意味着流量和利润，甚至还有对代币的过分想象，这些条件如今已经消失。

甚至于，并不需要 Hyperliquid 大幅改变风格，只需要学习下 BNB 的打法，就能构筑起独属于自己的增长飞轮。

HYPE 的出路在于模仿 BNB。

图片说明：生态和应用关系
图片来源：@zuoyeweb3

观察现今能存活的公链/L2，并不是简单的生态繁荣和主网代币价值捕获能力强的互动关系，事实远比理论更复杂，唯一符合既定印象的只有 ETH 本身，剩下的基本都无法被简单归类。

换言之，理想之所以理想，从不在现实中显灵。

- 单一应用组：TRON 和 Polygon 都是靠单一应用存活，前者的 USDT，后者的 Polymarket；
- 技术导向组（时代眼泪组）：波卡和 ATOM，在技术和理念上先进，但代币无法捕捉经济价值；
- 纯代币导向：Monad/Berachain，不再赘述，发完币就完成历史使命
- 生态繁荣组：Solana 和以太坊
- 存在主义组：Ripple、Avalanche，存在就是一切，一切都是存在

还可细分，币安主站和 HyperCore 都是处于“水桶组”，他们的代币都有极强的价值捕获能力，他们的产品都属于多类赋能：现货/Perp 交易、理财、质押甚至转账，不是公链，胜似公链。

BNB Chain 的价值是作为“公链”形态的币安主站的一个组成部分，走了龙妈，来了 Rong 妈，币安一直不放弃 BNB Chain 的原因也在这，很多事情公链搞起来比交易所方便，流量的价值是长期价值。

但是，Hyperliquid 的 HIP-3 也是 HyperCore 流动性的外溢，本质上也是和 HyperEVM 争夺流量入口，这种流量打架现在不仅发生在 HIP-3 项目方之间，也发生在 Builder Code 和 HyperEVM 项目方。

Hyperliquid 要成为流动性 AWS，但是内部的组织架构没有梳理清楚。

BNB Chain 不是币安想要的完美形态，但是足够 Hyperliquid 学习。

BNB Chain 是币安主站的分销渠道，并不能离开强运营进行自造血能力，更别说反哺币安本身，但这对于目前阶段的 HyperEVM 已经足够堪用。

在不伤害最小化运营原则和维持 HyperEVM 开放性之间，存在向前推一步的可能性，“钦点”借贷、Swap 和 LST 等各赛道的龙头，夭折的 HIP-5 提案过于粗暴，使用回购的 HYPE 迭代回购项目代币也不可行。

生态的协作并不违反任何原则，Hyperliquid 团队几乎不和任何项目方“往来”，也许是偏好采取类似 MM 联盟的链下合作，但是链上还是需要曝光度。

如果连最低程度的 HyperEVM 运营都不做，我们大概率能看到 50 美元的 HYPE，缺乏 HyperEVM 网络效应的想象力，HYPE 会失去指数的想象力支撑。

如果没有 HyperEVM 的辅助，HyperCore 就要靠流动性到达 OKX 的级别，但那样还是无法构筑起 HYPE 飞轮。

一言以蔽之，对于链上生态，“去中心化”的 HyperEVM 没有退路。

## 结语

Hyperliquid 比币安更轻，资本效率更高，Lighter 并不比 Hyperliquid 轻，Aster 更是急于变得复杂。

TGE 或接近 TGE 的 Aster、Edge 等 Perp DEX 都会做自己的 L2/公链，这是拉高估值计划的一部分，就像 PumpChain 也是发币计划的一部分。

现在到了 Hyperliquid 变得复杂，用规模优势换取未来的关键时刻。

之前提到过，Hyperliquid 并不擅长创新某类产品（Jeff 也做过预测市场），强在工程化的组合能力，如果 FTX 不是好的学习对象，那现在 BNB Chain 是个很好的模仿对象。

Canton Weekly Update | October 26 to November 1

1. @The_DTCC launched its tokenization service on Canton and its private Besu network. Firms can use it to get tokenized versions of eligible securities held at DTC. Twenty firms signed agreements for access, including J.P. Morgan, Citi and Fidelity Investments.

2. In a treasury pilot, @Uber bought a Franklin Templeton money market fund on @Tradeweb using @HSBC tokenized deposits. It could keep cash invested until it needed it, even selling part of its holding over the weekend. The trades settled on Canton through @FireblocksHQ.

3. @CantonStrategic signed an agreement with TSV to bring its Nasdaq listed shares to Canton. @Fairmint would issue the tokens, and investors could trade them on TSV using @tradecraftfi. The companies targeted November 2 as the earliest trading date.

4. @Nasdaq received a slot to run a validator on Canton’s production network. It plans to use the node for its own apps, starting with tokenized carbon removal certificates. A separate notice approved @dbsbank’s validator application and RBC CM LLC’s request for an additional node.

5. @BlackRock disclosed a 6% stake in Canton Strategic Holdings. Its October 27 filing showed it held about 4.82 million shares in the company as of September 30.

6. @Tradeweb earned $1.4 million for helping run Canton in the third quarter, down from $2.3 million a year earlier. Over the first nine months, revenue from that work rose to $6.8 million from $4.4 million.

7. On November 1, @RWA_xyz put the value of assets represented on Canton at $351.47 billion. Almost all of it came from @Broadridge’s repo platform, where firms use securities to borrow cash.

8. @cancore_io raised $7.2 million to expand trading between Canton and other blockchains. It plans to connect more networks and make more real-world assets available to trade.

9. Canton’s Super Validators approved a new way to calculate rewards for eligible apps based on the network traffic their transactions generate. A test run is planned for December. Switching to the new calculation requires a further decision.

10. @redstone_defi outlined its work on CAPS, a pricing standard backed by @CantonFdn. Two firms could use a shared market price as a benchmark and keep their negotiated price private.

11. Litecoin miner @LuxxfolioH signed a nonbinding agreement with @Greywick_hq. They’re exploring whether Luxxfolio could use some of its mined Litecoin to back cLTC on Canton and then borrow against those tokens.

12. Canton recorded a validator reward allocation for @a16zfrontier, formerly a16z crypto, under a node run by @MPCH_Labs. The fund can receive those rewards once its milestones are verified.

13. @DigitalAsset released Canton 3.7 with a safeguard for node operators. Tools for exporting keys and repairing ledger records are now off by default.

14. @Doppler_Fi joined the Canton Foundation. It plans to bring its vaults to Canton, starting with one for Canton Coin.

15. @temple_ny settled $764.5 million in spot trades on Canton in October, up 91% from about $400.7 million in September.

16. On @Visa’s October 27 earnings call, CEO Ryan McInerney highlighted the company’s existing role as a Canton Super Validator. He put that work in the context of Visa’s plan to connect traditional payments, stablecoins and tokenized deposits.

1. @cancore_io passed $100 million in total trading volume across its supported networks. Its new guide shows how to use an AI trading agent with limits on trading pairs, order size and daily volume. The agent cannot withdraw funds.

今年春节后，在 @Boywus 的光辉指引下，我逐步转向 RWA 套利，后来干脆彻底放弃了币圈原生资产。

因为做 RWA 套利的 「纠错」属性更强，它是个纯规则驱动的东西，不用考虑币圈狗庄怎么想，有金融世界的规矩立在那里，套起来不烧心，晚上睡的也踏实。

这里的 「 错 」可以拆成两个维度去理解：

1. 美股、黄金、大宗这类资产，不像币圈小币，它们都是有现实世界价格锚点的。

加密世界也许能在休市后，和市场情绪极度悲观或乐观时稍微放飞下自我，但最终还都是要迷途知返，回归妈妈的怀抱。

因为在传统金融资产定价透过永续合约 index 和资费释放的强大地心引力的作用下，从跑偏到回归是迟早的事儿，而市场会慷慨地奖励所有帮助回归的人。

2. 原油有换月，pre-ipo 有 rebase，个股/ETF 除息有特殊资费。当交易所们摸着石头过河，试图把所有 RWA 强塞进永续合约产品时，这里就一定会出现规则的错配。

把各个所各类资产，在不同情况下对应的不同处理手段钻研到滚瓜烂熟，赚规则差异的钱，这里也是利。

总体来说这是场 PVE 游戏，我们赚的通常是在劣势点位下单的方向性交易员的钱。

或者换种好听点儿的表达：我们在用我们的流动性，让方向性交易员在某个所的下单点位，变得不那么劣势，因为我们拉近了他们的成交价与公允价间的距离，优化了他们的持仓资费成本。

赚的不过是服务业的辛苦钱。
而这份钱的分赃规则是：

聪明钱吃鱼头和鱼身；
没慧根但是会跟的吃鱼尾；
学艺不精还把 RWA 当小币赌博游戏在玩的吃鱼刺。

text:
TopNod钱包推出“链上余额宝”概念产品Axil Pot：让闲置USDC参与现实消费信贷，目标年化约8%。

Axil Pot跑在Pharos上，这是一条由前蚂蚁团队创立、主打RWA的公链，通过TopNod钱包提供入口。此前相关金库也与币安钱包、OKX钱包有过合作，这些背景算加分项。

我以前在投行负责过非标投资和产品设计，看这类产品，比较在意底层资产和资金流。把闲置的U放进去赚点收益，听着挺简单，真要参与，还是得搞清楚：钱投向哪里？收益谁付？承担什么风险？什么时候能取出来？出了问题找谁？

1️⃣钱投到哪里，收益谁来付？
Axil Pot（APT）是由AXIL管理的USDC收益金库，底层资产由 Axil 配资的货币市场基金、高流动性资产、新兴市场的小额消费贷款等，有现实业务支撑。其中小额信贷来自借款人的分期消费利息，以及实际回款形成现金流闭环，支付金库的收益。

Axil负责筛选合作机构、配置策略和管理风险，据其官网介绍，团队成员具有贝莱德、港交所、中金资本、蚂蚁集团等机构的从业背景。按官方披露，APT不把存入的USDC转投其他DeFi收益池，也不做循环借贷或杠杆。能否持续赚到收益，主要看底层贷款质量和回款情况。收益有现实业务支撑,这也是它值得看的地方!

基本情况：
1、存入USDC，持有代表金库份额的APT。
2、目标年化约8%，浮动、不保证。
3、可用流动性和每日额度内支持T+0提款，常规路径为T+1至T+7。
4、通过@Top_nod钱包参与，使用@R25Official金库基础设施，在Pharos @pharos_network上记录和结算。

2️⃣风险点与风控。
APT代表金库份额，价值随资产表现变化，不保证固定为1美元。

和主要靠链上借贷、交易或代币激励产生收益的产品相比，Axil Pot中高收益的生息资产更依赖现实中的贷款回款。所以重点得放在借款人能不能还钱、合作机构靠不靠谱，以及出了问题能不能追回资金

另外是时间差：贷款要慢慢收回来，用户却可能同时申请提款。金库配置了现金、货币市场基金和短期信贷等资产，但即时提款仍受可用现金和每日额度限制，集中赎回时可能需要等。

Axil 之前做过的同类型三个月资产，年化约12%+，管理规模大约在1亿美金，目前为止运作正常。

按官方说明做了资金路径与多方位的尽职调查：
1）资金通过隔离账户流转，帮助与合作机构的其他业务资金分开，
2）放贷机构要经过尽调和持续监控
3）对单一机构或市场的投入设有上限，避免过度集中。
4）资金从金库经隔离账户接入审核过的消费信贷机构，消费者还款后回流金库。期间不转投其他DeFi收益池，也不做循环借贷或杠杆。

总体综合来看：

我觉得这个产品的一大特色与创新是它把真实世界的消费信贷接到了链上。

消费信贷这部分的收益，来自借款人实际支付的利息，和币圈常见的抵押借贷、循环贷或链上策略有所不同。

这就让RWA变得具体了：存入的是USDC，参与的是现实中的消费贷款，收益是这门生意本身产生的收益。

text:
Measuring AI search visibility by website traffic is like measuring a radio ad by how many people visited the recording studio.

Publishers spent 20 years relying on an unspoken agreement: Google crawls your site, and Google sends you back clicks.

That era is over. Penske Media reported its Google referrals dropped 40% year over year. A federal judge just ruled that expecting search traffic in exchange for being crawled is not a legal agreement.

When Perplexity, Gemini, or ChatGPT answers a buyer's prompt using your content: • The answer is delivered on-platform. • The buyer gets their answer. • Your site gets 0 pageviews.

If your organic growth model still measures blue-link clicks instead of citation frequency and brand recall, you are tracking a ghost metric.

Stop reporting search traffic as a baseline. Report it as a variable range with a floor your business can actually survive on.

L2 远比L1 中心化的一个经典案例：Arbitrum 和Polygon 对币安黑客的动作。

Arbitrum 先斩后奏，Polygon 力不从心。

前者紧急启用特权冻结黑客地址、强制转移资产一条龙；

后者只能先冻结黑客地址，无法强制转移赃款；

Polygon 想要追回这7049万枚 ethereum:0x455e53cbb86018ac2b8092fdcd39d8444affc3f6, 只能通过发起提案来硬分叉，提案通过后修改状态才能实现资金的回收。
author: y_cryptoanalyst
quoted_text:
Arbitrum 自主网上线以来，一共采取了2次链上紧急冻结特权，且2次都是发生在今年。

第一次发生在今年4月，Arbitrum 安全委员会(SC)紧急冻结了KelpDAO 黑客持有的30,766枚ETH；

第二次发生在今天，Arbitrum SC 紧急冻结了与币安漏洞相关的地址持有的74,559,805枚ARB 和8425枚ETH。

上一次评论区骂声一片，这一次同样被人诟病。

我的观点始终如一：
去中心化的目的是为了对抗强权，是为普罗大众服务的；如果中心化的目的是为了帮助普罗大众而不是为强权牟私利，我认为这种中心化是值得被推崇的。

冻结黑客就是这种中心化。

text:
💥Bubblemaps 曝光四位知名KOL，发现他们链上的操作与公开喊单严重不符

1️⃣Kimchi

PumpFun 近期签约的KOL「Kimchi」@kimchi1x 坊间传闻他靠 $TRUMP 赚了 4000 万美元，但无人核实

Bubblemaps 识别出他一个公开的抽奖钱包，并发现了一组此前隐藏的关联钱包。这些钱包估算在 $TRUMP 上的利润约 600 万美元。金额依然不小，但远非传闻的 4000 万美元

2️⃣Solstice

Solstice @The__Solstice 因登上 FOMO 排行榜前三而走红，他在 $STONK 上曾盈利500万美元。此后他向X 上的 20 万粉丝密集推广多枚 meme 币（包括 $STONKINU、 $BOP、 $QUEEF、 solana:4tkupXEGfbYPCVN37CagviJd3tgWnudT9avKZvouT3Dm 等）

Bubblemaps 发现这些代币都遵循相似的捆绑模式：
🔹数十个新钱包
🔹买入时间接近
🔹每个钱包持有供应量的 0.5%–1%

同时，他们将 Solstice 的公开钱包直接追踪到这些代币的部署者。此外还发现有试图用数千个中转钱包掩盖轨迹的迹象。

Solstice 公开钱包显示亏损约 7 万美元，而其关联的小钱包则盈利约 27 万美元。

3️⃣Anglio @anglio

从建筑工人转型为 meme 币网红
Bubblemaps 调查其操作后发现：他先用小钱包买入，再用公开钱包跟进，最后发帖告诉粉丝们购买。

分析他 10 月份的 534 条帖子后，发现 5 个与他高度关联的钱包，这些钱包：
🔹在他 61% 的喊单之前买入
🔹平均提前约 20 秒
🔹几分钟后卖出
🔹估算利润约 13 万美元。Anglio 已承认使用过这类方法。

4️⃣0xEthan

Ethan @0xEthan 在 PumpFun 上约有 8.8 万粉丝，其经常分享新代币，Bubblemaps 收到匿名爆料，要求关注 Ethan 的喊单习惯。

用他最近 49 次代币喊单进行追踪，发现 Ethan 在喊单后仅三分钟内卖出的倾向。模式如下：
🔹Ethan 的公开钱包买入
🔹三个秘密小钱包在同一秒跟进买入
🔹他在 PumpFun 上发出喊单
🔹这些钱包随后卖出

在多起案例中，他一边还在发帖解释「为什么应该买」，然后自己已经开始卖出。
估算他通过这种方式赚了约 12.5 万美元，其中交易利润约 4.5 万美元，PumpFun 喊单奖励约 8 万美元。

quoted_text:
我的油管第14期：《习近平能不能永久连任》

电影《黑社会》之龙城风云里，邓肥说：“黑社会也是有权力制约的，不能一人独大，要平衡。几十年的规矩改了，社团的叔父们一定会很不舒服。”

可中南海的叔父们，要么找马克思和毛主席报到去了，要么住进了秦城的豪华一居室，剩下的只能在特勤局监视下种种花、养养鸟、听听戏……

如果在一家公司，他必须是董事长、总裁、CEO一肩挑；在帮派，他必须是帮主、执法长老、执棒长老一肩挑。未来权力排序不是一号人物、二号人物、三号人物……而是一号人物之下，全是打工仔。中南海权力体系不再是金字塔形状，而是倒T字形。

习近平会永久连任吗？

党指挥枪VS枪杆子里面出政权，其实是孪生兄弟。谁当党老大，必须是枪老大，否则必然被拿下；谁是枪老大，就是党老大，你有枪别人就听话。

没有蓝玉没有年羹尧没有袁世凯，整个军队像玩乐高一样拆了拼、拼了拆。谁手里都凑不齐一支完整部队，没有中间管理层，瓜子二手车，没有中间商赚差价。

会上演《南山的部长们》吗？会有玄武门之变吗？张又侠老部下会拎着两把板斧劫法场吗？谁是“铁帽子王”？

世界上有个独裁者困境：如果指定接班人，接班人很快成为权力副中心，独裁者权力就被稀释；如果不指定接班人，死后又要被清算。

谜一般，习主席到底有没有指定接班人——指定早了，就成了刘少奇，晚了，就成了华国锋，能力强，就是林彪，能力差，就是王洪文。毛泽东临死前一年才让华国锋当副总理兼公安部长。汉武帝临死前，才立刘弗陵为太子。康熙临终病榻前，才传位给雍正，传位诏书放在“正大光明”牌匾后面，一点都不正大光明。

《威权统治的政治学》统计：从1946到2008年，303个非正常下台的独裁者，被民众起义推翻的只有32个，10个里面不到一个。而这303个非正常下台的独裁者里，205个是被统治集团内部的人赶下台的，占三分之二以上。独裁者真正防的不是街上的民众，而是会议室里的小弟。

最刺激的是突尼斯的布尔吉巴，他独裁三十一年，精心挑选最信任的本·阿里当接班人。可一个多月后的某天夜里，本·阿里把七个医生召到内政部，让他们签字证明——老领导精神失常了。

有医生不干，本·阿里一拍桌子“老子数到三”……医生马上服软。自从得了精神病，我的精神好多了。第二天老领导被软禁在一处大宅子里，一直到死去。

未来漫长岁月，总有天意，所谓天意，就是每个人的心意。

分数从 GPT-5.2 到 GPT-6 Astra 稳步上升。所有模型最常见的失败都是给出错误答案或错误建议，原因往往是模型漏掉了用户以往对话里的某条事实。在仅依赖历史对话的评分项上，胜率为 33%，而依赖已保存记忆的评分项为 48%
author: Lynncc6
quoted_text:
Recommended benchmark from OpenAI on agents for everyday life tasks.

They surveyed 3,837 US consumers to rank 148 life tasks by what people would pay an assistant to handle. Together, those tasks are worth over $1.7 trillion a year.

LifeVal turns the most valuable of them into 169 agent tasks. Each one is written by someone who has done the task many times in real life, using their own ChatGPT conversations, memories, and files. The tasks include managing finances, moving apartments, searching for a job, and finding childcare.

Every task comes with a rubric, a working environment and an offline copy of the web, and passes three rounds of human review.

Scores rise steadily from GPT-5.2 to GPT-6 Astra. The most common failure for every model is a wrong answer or recommendation, often because the model missed a fact sitting in the user's past chats. On criteria tied only to past conversations, the win rate was 33%, compared with 48% for saved memories.

If you build assistants with memory, test whether the agent actually finds what the user told it weeks ago.

text:
🔶 一姐 @heyibinance 远程连线「币安学习营」晚宴，全程脱稿，但信息量不少

泵泵整理了几个核心观点，分享给大家：

1️⃣ 黑客事件：安全是一场不断升级的攻防战

据说被盗当天，表哥 @cz_binance 和一姐都异常平静，只想尽快把事件处理好

坦言，这次事故确实是币安没有做好安全工作，因此付出了巨大代价，但损失仍在平台能够承担的范围内。

过去一年币安曾拦截 58 次不同形态的类似攻击。

如今黑客不再只是发送木马文件，还可能通过真实猎头、定向招聘、长期沟通等社会工程学手段突破安全防线。

即使有严格的内部制度与安全培训，也难以完全消除人的风险。

AI 既可以成为黑客的矛，也可以成为安全体系的盾。

未来的安全攻防，需要传统技术与 AI 相结合。

2️⃣ 比特币与量子攻击：技术挑战一直存在

何一认为，量子计算确实可能对比特币构成威胁，币安也会投入资源参与相关研究。

但抗量子升级可能带来新的争议，例如早期比特币如何处理、是否影响去中心化，以及潜在的分叉风险。

她回顾了2017年 BCH 分叉时期的争论。

比特币经历过多次重大挑战，但最终展现出了较强的韧性。

技术会不断制造新问题，行业也会在解决问题的过程中继续进化。

3️⃣ 发币就是发债：财富自由可能反而削弱创业动力

这是我认为整场分享最有价值的观点之一。

何一提到，她早在2017年就认为：

发币本质上类似于发债，是以个人或项目信誉获得融资，也意味着长期责任。

但 Crypto 存在一个现实矛盾：

如果一个项目没有用户、没有收入，甚至没有成熟产品，仅凭代币融资就能让创始人财富自由。

那么，创始人还有多大动力继续努力？

她提出了一个类似“不可能三角”的问题：

好的商业模式、提前财富自由、持续长期建设，三者之间可能存在激励冲突。

这也是为什么行业不缺代币，却始终缺少能够长期创造价值的项目。

4️⃣ 为什么过去上币就涨，现在上币容易成为高点？

何一认为，核心是市场结构发生了变化。

2017年至2021年前后，头部 CEX 掌握着强大的流动性和定价话语权。

项目如果不能登陆主流交易所，往往难以获得足够的流动性。因此交易所可以争取较低的上币估值，让用户获得早期价格优势。

但 DEX 的发展打破了这种格局。

项目不需要等待 CEX 上币，就可以在链上完成发行、交易和价格发现。

CEX 的上币特权被削弱，原本属于交易所用户的早期定价红利，也被市场提前消化。

很多项目还没上 CEX，估值就已经被炒得很高，上币反而成了早期持有人的流动性退出窗口。

5️⃣ Crypto 的资产荒：赚钱的项目未必发币，发币的项目未必赚钱

何一提到，行业里并不缺少真正有收入的业务。

例如部分钱包、交易工具、DEX 等，已经拥有不错的盈利能力，却未必发行代币。

另一方面，很多已经发行代币的项目，为了规避潜在证券属性，将代币设计为治理工具，与协议收入脱钩。

结果就是：

项目可以赚钱，但代币不一定能够捕获价值。

当业务增长无法有效传递给代币持有人，投资者持有的可能只是一个可交易的符号。

她还提到，部分传统风险投资机构进入 Crypto 后，发现一些代币模式难以承接长期、大规模资金，因此重新回归股权投资。

行业真正缺少的，是兼具持续收入、健康商业模式和合理价值承接机制的资产。

6️⃣ 币安未来：不止是 Crypto 交易所

何一认为，用户需求正在分层。

有人专注 Meme，有人喜欢波段交易，有人做长期投资，也有人更关注理财收益。

因此，币安需要同时满足不同类型用户的需求。

从 CEX 到 DEX、钱包，再到股票和大宗商品相关交易产品，币安正在不断拓宽资产覆盖范围。

她给出的长期方向是：

通过 AI 与区块链技术，发展成为全球新型泛金融平台。

未来竞争的可能不只是上币数量和交易深度，而是谁能够覆盖更多资产、满足更多金融需求。

7️⃣ AI 产品：先从 Demo 做起，不断迭代

何一坦言，目前币安的 AI 产品距离她理想中的形态还有很大差距。

她理想中的 AI 金融助手，可以直接理解用户意图、制定策略并执行交易。

当然，“只赚钱不亏钱”的交易策略并不现实。

所以真正的产品发展，还是要从小型 Demo 开始，持续收集反馈、快速迭代。

8️⃣ 用户信任与长期经营，比短期声量更重要

面对安全事件，何一表示自己与 CZ 都保持冷静，首先考虑的是如何解决问题、完善安全体系。

她还提到，安全事件后平台的资金流动比预期稳定，最近24小时已恢复净流入。

她强调自己长期追求健康的商业模式和正向现金流，不希望依靠巨额营销投入制造虚假繁荣。

对于外界的各种阴谋论，她认为投资者更应该研究时间线、事实和逻辑。

真正的长期竞争力，不仅是流动性和产品，更是安全能力、经营能力，以及危机之后继续赢得用户信任的能力

刚刷完「不烧心」短剧脑洞，切回页面一眼假这件更烧心的事。

别再犯这 5 个 AI 落地页错误了。

紫渐变、标题里塞一个彩色词、每个小标题上面一个圆角图标、卡片套卡片、页脚永远塞邮箱订阅。这些默认模板味刷一眼就知道是 AI 量产。

它干啥：
1）从 50 套主题里发你 3 套，按页面真正要办的事排版
2）在真浏览器里跑 sloplint，专抓上面那些机器味
3）还能 /hallmark redesign 或 audit 旧页面

上手一条命令：
npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g
然后打 /hallmark，加一句你要做什么页。

我觉得这比生成完再手工抠「AI 味」省事。前提是：它拦的是默认模板味，审美对不对还得你自己拍板。

你会先拿它 A 做新落地页，还是 B 审计现有页面？ https://t.co/c0Dq3sJhTx

text:
VerifiedX Ships Vault Update Aimed at Stopping Hacked vBTC Transfers

VerifiedX today released upgraded self-custodial recovery Vaults as part of its Mainnet 9.0.0 upgrade. Bitcoin holders using vBTC can set a delay before transfers from their vault become final, allowing them to recall mistaken or unauthorized transfers during that window and recover assets to an owner-designated self-custodial address. These protections are enforced on-chain by VerifiedX network consensus, without requiring a separate custodian. The upgrade also embeds Bitcoin light-client verification into VerifiedX’s validator software, enabling validators to independently verify Bitcoin block headers, proof of work and chain progression with 6 confirmation burial depth.

quoted_text:
我真心不想在竞争对手遭遇危机的时候批评他们。我真正希望的是，我们能够与他们携手合作，共同提高安全标准，更好地保护整个加密行业。

但我不得不说，那位自称已经不再管理币安的“币圈首富”（你们真的相信吗？）最近接受的采访，实在让我感到恶心。

整场采访充斥着胡说八道和误导性言论。他似乎在淡化自身应承担的责任，甚至试图通过贬低传统银行的安全性，为自己的失败寻找借口。

在这样一场危机中，我们本应看到的是责任担当和行业领导力。但这场采访给人的感觉，却是在不断推卸责任、转移焦点。

这绝不是我们这个行业需要的领导力。

自从事件发生以来，这位“币圈首富”似乎就一直停不下来：

1. 社交媒体上最活跃的人之一。 在整场危机期间，他可以说是币安相关人士中在社交媒体上发声最多、最活跃的一个。

2. 还有时间和马斯克吵架。 在如此严重的安全危机期间，他居然还有精力与 Elon Musk（@elonmusk）争论 SpaceX 股票投资的问题。

3. 反复强调“只有2%的资金流出币安”。 仿佛这个数字就能回答大家对平台安全性的根本质疑。

4. 继续开展营销活动吸引用户存款。 即使危机仍在持续，吸引新资金流入的营销活动也没有停止。

5. 试图暗示传统银行的安全性更差。 一个自称专业的加密行业领导者，怎么能做出如此具有误导性的比较？传统银行与加密交易所面对的威胁模型、攻击面以及安全事故的后果，都存在根本性差异。脱离这些背景进行简单比较，是极其不负责任的。

6. 几乎每次发声，都似乎把一位怀孕的女性推到危机最前线。 而自己则反复加上同一句免责声明：“我已经不管理币安了。”

与此同时，整个加密行业却在为这场危机付出代价：

1. 比特币价格据报道从约81,000美元跌至75,000美元。 市场在动荡中遭受了明显冲击。

2. 数十亿美元的杠杆仓位遭到清算。 市场波动引发了大规模的强制平仓。

3. 整个加密行业的公信力可能再次受到重创。 传统资本市场、机构投资者以及全球监管机构，可能因此对整个行业的安全性和可信度产生更深的疑虑。

经历了这一切，他们所谓的“多层安全防御体系”，如今看起来越来越像一个笑话。

我们的行业需要的，不是更多的借口，不是更多的公关话术，而是真正的合作、真正的责任担当，以及切实有效的用户资产保护和安全标准建设。

少一些推卸责任，少一些营销包装，多一些真正的安全投入和行业协作。

这才是我更愿意投入时间和精力去推动的事情。

即使是竞争对手，我也真心希望我们能够携手把这件事做好。

币安钱包公布了关于 $PREDICT 空投发放规则的补充通知，有几个重点值得大家关注。

首先，之前公布的 5 个发放批次日期全部保持不变：

📅 2026-11-06
📅 2026-11-13
📅 2026-11-20
📅 2026-11-27

以及对应问卷的截止日期也不会改变。

这次最重要的更新，是针对代币实际上线时间晚于预定发放日期的情况：

1️⃣ 已经到期但尚未发放的批次，会和后续批次合并。

2️⃣ 等代币正式上线后，统一进行第一批发放。

🅰️ 方案 A：立即领取应得份额的 35%，放弃剩余 65%。

🅱️ 方案 B：锁仓/质押一年，到期后领取 100%。

如果没有按时提交领取选择，默认进入方案 B。

我个人觉得，这次补充规则主要解决了一个问题：如果 $PREDICT 上线延期，之前参与空投的用户不用担心批次作废，也不需要重新填写问卷。

text:
This is the only show you need to listen to in tech:

- OpenAI Cuts Valuation to $1.25TRN
- Public Market Meltdown: GOOG Loses $500BN in 12 Hours
- DoorDash Buys Instacart for $17BN
- Kalshi Raises $1BN and Cognition Eyes $80BN Valuation

My notes with @jasonlk and @rodriscoll

1. Kalshi Have Departed the Social Good, They Are a Sports Gambling Market

Kalshi started out as a prediction market with some social utility and has since become a sports gambling market growing like a weed. Sports betting is regulated state by state, and Kalshi is pushing through on a national basis, which is why Utah is suing. VCs will put a lot of money into what is working.

2. Why I Would Invest in Cognition at $80BN

At $80B, Cognition looks market correct, and coding agents remain the one thing that never stops working. Cognition got lucky buying the Windsurf team and IP, but its momentum is too strong to sit out. With the fund up 5X on paper, the pitch is to put its last $2B into Cognition.

3. Why I Would Invest in Serval over Cognition and Baseten

ServiceNow is an old guard with a sales-led CEO, while Serval has an amazing product and the best enterprise adoption Harry has seen. A 10X looks very likely at Serval, but far harder at Baseten at $30B or Cognition. The catch is Serval only raised $150M, so a fund that must deploy capital still has to do Cognition.

4. Where Is the Risk in the AI Trade Right Now?

If AI demand is as strong as people think, every GPU and data center will be needed and CoreWeave's bonds will be money good. If demand falls short, the first to suffer will not be Google or Amazon with their big balance sheets, but companies like CoreWeave.

5. Why Large Foundation Model Companies Will Acquire in the Robotic Space

Foundation model companies will either build or buy a robotics model. An LLM sells to the 81 million knowledge workers in the US, and a robotics foundation model lets the same company address physical workers too, doubling its TAM in the prospectus. That lure means there could well be acquisitions in the space.

6. Agents Are an Existential Risk to DoorDash

DoorDash said AI agents sent only several hundred orders against 3 million deliveries a day, which Jason called a dumb comment. Agents can tell users which restaurants deliver themselves or offer pickup, cutting out platform fees. Rory counters that ordering dinner through an agent is not much easier than using the DoorDash app.

7. Why Pricing Pressure Hit Anthropic in Q3

Anthropic's GAAP revenue went from roughly $5B in Q1 to $11B in Q2 and $17B in Q3, so quarter-on-quarter growth fell from about 100% to about 50%, still 5X year-on-year. Jason puts the slowdown down to pricing pressure, with OpenAI selling somewhat equivalent products for 30% off, while demand on OpenRouter has not declined.

text:
india is bigger than your devcon experience. 🇮🇳

a little late, but @EFDevcon day 2 in mumbai deserved a recap.

interesting how quickly people are turning one conference experience into a verdict on an entire ecosystem.

a conference is not the ecosystem. a city is not a country’s potential. and a few half-filled rooms don’t tell you where the industry is heading.

india has its challenges, absolutely. but it also has an incredible generation of builders, engineers, founders and independent thinkers building things with global relevance.

i spent time at @EFDevcon and @ethindiaco, and attended two particularly interesting ETHIndia panels:

ethereum request for startups, with Viraz, Binji and Francesco.

india deep tech, featuring Aaryaman, Dhanush, Arnav Bansal and Angad Daryani.

also got to meet Binji, Francesco, Aaryaman Vir, Hudson, and Austin Griffithsome genuinely impressive people building across different layers of the stack.

the future won’t be decided by which conference has the biggest crowd, which city gets the most attention, or which chain gets the most hype.

crypto is evolving. the boundaries between crypto, AI, finance and technology are blurring.

but don’t confuse your field of view with the size of the opportunity.

there’s a lot happening in india. maybe it’s time to look beyond the conference floor. 🇮🇳

⸻

some day 2 conversations worth highlighting:

> ethereum’s roadmap, simplified. what changes next, why it matters, and how the protocol evolves without compromising its core principles.

> fast finality. faster confirmations aren’t just a protocol milestone. they can fundamentally improve the experience of building and using applications on ethereum.

> dynamic smart contracts. hooks everywhere. more adaptable contracts, greater composability and new possibilities for developers.

> smart accounts in production. moving beyond technical demos to real-world lessons. account abstraction needs to make crypto easier for actual users.

> red-teaming AI pipelines. prompt injection and supply-chain attacks are serious threats. as AI agents become more capable, security needs to be built into the stack.

> privacy and operational security. transaction data leaks, deniability and protecting your ETH. privacy is not just a cypherpunk ideal; making it practical is the real challenge.

> UNICEF going onchain. a compelling look at how blockchain adoption can move from pilots to institutions and real-world impact.

> the art hub and gallery. one of the strongest reminders that Ethereum is more than infrastructure. art and culture can bring the ecosystem to audiences that technical talks never will.

one thought I keep coming back to:

ethereum has no shortage of ambitious technology. but the next phase needs stronger storytelling, better brands, thoughtful product experiences and cultural relevance.

we spend a lot of time making protocols work. we should spend just as much time making people care about what they enable.

technology builds the foundation. culture helps build the movement.

still in mumbai. still curious about what’s being built here. 🦄

if you’re around for devcon, feel free to say hi, grab a coffee, exchange ideas or just drop me a DM. always up for meeting interesting people.

text:
Privacy is eroded in a variety of places. Here is an important one: currently, third-party RPC providers can see what accounts you are reading, and what transactions you are simulating before you send them.

Perhaps most significantly, if your browser wallet has multiple accounts, the provider can group them together by seeing which accounts are queried from the same IP address at the same time.

@category_xyz researchers have addressed this with WP-ORAM (write-public ORAM), a new means of making servers oblivious to what data is being read, while keeping writes (and the actual state) public. The paper includes both a proposal and a real, pragmatic implementation that can keep up with Monad.

Practical innovation to solve real privacy problems. Great job @AnanyaAppan James Austgen @KushalBabel @sourav1547 !

Achievement Unlocked: 2,000 apes welcomed since we started Welcome Apes on 2/12/24. 🤯 🦍

Pretty incredible to think about.  

When we started this, the idea was simple. Nobody should join the bored ape yacht club and feel like they're standing in an empty room. If someone decides to become an ape, the least we can do is open the door, say hello, and make them feel like they belong.  

One thing we've really noticed lately is that the people finding their way into the club seem a little different. A lot of these folks have been around Web3 for years. They've lived through the cycles, the rugs, the hype, the disappointments, and everything else this crazy space has thrown at us.  

And after all of that, they're choosing to be here.  

We think that says something pretty powerful about what this club has become.  

In a space where so much is temporary, transactional, and everyone seems to be chasing the next big thing, there's something genuinely special about people finding their way here because they want to be part of something bigger than themselves.  

We've always believed that the real value of this club is its people. The friendships, the camaraderie, the willingness to show up for one another. That's the stuff that survives the cycles.  

To everyone who's taken a few moments out of their day to welcome a new ape, strike up a conversation, or make a complete stranger feel like they're already part of the family, thank you. That's what this whole thing has always been about.  

2,000 welcomes later, we believe in that simple idea more than ever.  

The club isn't just part of the journey. The club is the destination.  

Welcome home. 🍌

text:
A Journey to Somewhere
by @cathcomputerart

Charles Csuri (1922-2022) was in at the birth of what became an entire movement. One of the earliest pioneers of digital art, over a career of nearly sixty years of innovations, he became known as the “father of computer art and animation”. 

In the early-1960s, at a time when computers were rare, complex machines that required specialist expertise to operate, Csuri formulated a way to exploit the inherent qualities of digital technology, making art on equipment that was not originally designed for artistic purposes. 

His unique style evolved within the tradition of modernism, guided by a visionary proficiency that combined his traditional fine art aesthetic with digital systems. In dialogue with the machine, Csuri expanded imagination and expression, creating possibilities for new kinds of forms, not seen before in art. 

Thanks to the handful of artists of Csuri’s generation, the digital art movement gained a foothold in the artworld, inspiring subsequent generations and forging the field we now see.

It is clear from the Ordo series that Csuri trained as a traditional artist, indeed spent twenty years drawing and painting, before turning to the computer. His knowledge and respect for art history informed his style.

Studies of the work of Paul Cézanne broadened his understanding of colour, light and geometry in composition. Via the digital, Csuri was able to take Cézanne’s discarding of one-point perspective even further, by creating a three-dimensional space for his forms to float within the picture plane. 

Searching for a visual structure, inventing challenges for himself, Csuri spoke about his attempts to break free of the logic, the carefully measured digital space where there is a predicable outcome, and move toward a process of discovery. Like Pablo Picasso, he aimed to embrace a future of curiosity and wonder.

The Ordo series of generative artworks combine glorious colour with painterly, ribbon-like forms. Using his own code, the artist created a special tool to make these smooth three-dimensional forms, first seen in his art in the 1990s and refined throughout the 2000s. Subtle variations in these layered structures combine with vibrant colours that pop with a feeling of intense activity and movement through interconnected lines and shapes. 

Ordo also shows Csuri’s skill in exploiting the computer’s ability to light up each pixel individually and potentially display billions of strong colours. The viewer becomes a witness to the artist’s brushstrokes, a record of the artist’s hand, via code, as it moves through time and space. A celebration of the complexity and seemingly boundless depth of three-dimensional space.

At Ohio State University, using a cutting edge, real-time system from technology developed at the NASA space programme, Csuri became a crucial part of the foundation of modern computer graphics. 

He recognised very early on the importance that this tech was having not only upon the types of art produced, but also upon the changing attitudes of art itself and its place within society. His work marks the beginning of a whole new genre, one that would expand the boundaries of art and as such human expression and communication in an age of increasing digitality.

Csuri had to take a leap of faith. Could this new tool be used creatively? He asked, “Where is the sense of place and fun in this universe of linear logic?” He found this freedom and fun in the software environment that he shaped over a long career. 

Recognising that the art object could become many statements about the same thing, his code reflected his approach which allowed for numerous solutions to a problem. The Ordo series demonstrates well this process of iteration, which the computer facilitates, allowing the artist to explore innovations and express multiple ideas, by producing several outputs from one set of rules.

Csuri shows us a world of dynamic space, geometry, colour and light. Twentieth century modernism is redefined in an exciting and vital way.

Catherine Mason
21 September 2026

@cathcomputerarthistory has been recovering the history of computer and digital art since 2002 when she joined a research group at Birkbeck, University of London. 

Her first book A Computer in the Art Room: the Origins of British Computer Arts 1950-1980 (JJG: 2008 & ebook 2021), is the first comprehensive account of the history of British computer art. 

Over a long career she has worked in commercial galleries and public-sector arts organisations, adult education and exhibition curation. Today her main focus is research and writing; her latest book Creative Simulations (Springer 2024), tells the story of the early history of CAS, through George Mallen, one of the founders. She is a Visiting Research and Knowledge Exchange Fellow in the School of Computing at Goldsmiths, University of London.

text:
What I'm seeing across the industry right now is that the biggest bottleneck to AI adoption isn't model capabilities. It's data infrastructure.

Today, we're expanding the Eon Data Foundation with the launch of Eon Yukon, a new serverless data engine purposely built to change that.

AI agents need fresh, contextualized data to act. 
Specialized models need a continuous feed of data and feedback to improve. Both are still served by a stack, an architecture, and methods built for dashboards:

-Spark and Flink clusters sized for peak, plus compaction jobs to keep tables usable.

-A pipeline and a copy for every consumer, staged bronze to silver to gold.

-Hand-written jobs, wired together by an orchestrator and kept alive by specialists.

The result: shipping data is complicated, risky, and expensive. While coding agents ship apps in hours, they rarely build or run data pipelines. The data is too volatile, and a mistake costs too much.

With Yukon, data moves from ingestion to processing to serving in one continuous flow, without the infrastructure and pipelines traditionally required to connect them.

Events become compacted, sorted, deduplicated Iceberg tables within seconds.

Real-time aggregations run inline, with fully managed state. Agents and applications can access fresh data with sub-millisecond latency through a Redis-compatible API or through our SQL and spark compatible query engine.

Beyond moving and serving data, Yukon makes it continuously understandable - Live column-level statistics, accessible through MCP, give agents visibility into the data. Built-in monitoring, sampling, and data minimization help teams maintain control.

At 1M events/sec and equal freshness, Yukon used 4x less compute than Spark and 7x less than Flink. The benchmark is public: run it yourself with Eon’s ingest-bench.

This is another major step toward our vision of an Autonomous Data Foundation for the AI era, built to both protect enterprise data and unlock its full potential.

We've always believed that the real value of this club is its people. The friendships, the camaraderie, the willingness to show up for one another. That's the stuff that survives the cycles.

2,000 welcomes later, we believe in that simple idea more than ever.  

The club isn't just part of the journey. The club is the destination.

text:
UPDATE: Sei Labs says @SeiNetwork is safe from a newly discovered collision attack targeting LtHash, a hash function used in its state storage.

Researchers estimate the attack could find collisions with ~2⁸¹ hashes, but exploiting it would require a state size roughly 2 trillion times larger than Sei's current state.

According to Sei Labs, even adding 1 million entries per second would take approximately 130 million years to reach that scale.

The threat remains theoretical under current conditions.
author: TTT_News_
quoted_text:
ANALYSIS: @SeiNetwork is safe from a new collision attack vector targeting Lattice Hashes.

ePrint 2026/2083 describes a new collision attack on LtHash, the hash Sei's storage layer uses to fingerprint its data.

The attack finds two different states with the same LtHash in about 2^81 hashes. To succeed, it requires that those two states hold at least 550^8 entries between them. Roughly 8 sextillion.

Sei's state today has ~1 billion entries. A state big enough for this attack would be ~2 trillion times larger.

Even if Sei added a million brand-new entries every second, it would take about 130 million years before Sei was vulnerable.

Read the full analysis here: https://t.co/oeAg7bc8aB

For more details about the attack vector, read the paper "Two-Bit Lifting for Ternary SIS: Polynomial-Time Collision Attacks on LtHash": https://t.co/BKqkIc1qEg

author: ercwl
quoted_text:
Some personal news: I joined Lucid Computing (@LucidCompute) as Director of Research Partnerships & Standards.

My core focus will be to help foster more open source collaboration across the AI verification ecosystem, between the many teams working on similar / adjacent topics and pieces of technology.

I am so excited to finally be able to share this next chapter of my career. As I posted recently, I have been completely obsessed with AI safety.

It accelerated in March this year, when @ercwl put me in a group chat with @Kristian_Ronn. At the time, I was actively exploring the use of Zero Knowledge Proofs for critical AI use cases (mostly in insurance, defense, healthcare and robotics).

We immediately had great vibes together. We shared the same vision and the same enthusiasm, and we both saw AI safety as the most important thing humanity could work on.

Since then, I have met Greg, Lucid’s co-founder and CTO, and it was the same kind of connection, the same feeling of a shared vision and mission. And everyone I have met at Lucid since I joined is the same kind of person: talented, mission driven, and with a deep willingness to have a real impact with our work.

It’s a real honor to join them all on this epic journey.

I genuinely believe that cryptography and math are our only hope of avoiding a dystopian, totalitarian world with massive concentration of power, gatekeeping of intelligence, and abuse in many forms.

The beauty of cryptography and math, and Zero Knowledge Proofs in particular, is that they are tools that can break the asymmetry of power. This is precisely what we need for AI right now.

We also need solutions designed for the most adversarial conditions possible, including resisting superpowerful nation-state actors. That’s the only way to aim for credible international treaties to “pace AI”.

The threats and risks are immense, and AI safety is probably the greatest challenge humanity has ever faced. Despite that, I am hopeful, and I remain optimistic that we still have the power to change course. This will inevitably require cooperation and collaboration at many levels.

From what I have seen, there is a strong appetite for more open source collaboration in the AI verification ecosystem. That’s a great starting point, and I have high hopes that we can stimulate and nurture a very healthy, collaborative environment, with no zero-sum mentality. 

We need to join forces, more than ever.

The space is way too small today. It will have to grow massively over the coming months, and I am sure it will. That makes it even more important to build solid foundations and a strong culture in the ecosystem, so it can grow and scale the right way.

I will do my very best to help build that collaborative environment. I love building in public, I am an open source maxi, and I am used to working with many entities across distributed ecosystems.

The topics and primitives where I will focus and facilitate open source collaboration:
- ZK for provable inference
- Proof of exhaustion schemes
- Workload classification, via different techniques
- Hardware roots of trust, TEEs, hardware formal verification
- Formal verification

If you are working on any of these in AI verification, I would love to connect and see how we can join forces on our shared mission.

If you are not working on AI verification (or AI safety more broadly): first, you are missing out. Second, we need you. We need a lot more talent working on these problems.

Lastly, I will work on public communication and educational material about AI verification and our work at Lucid. More on this very soon. 

Follow @LucidCompute and @Kristian_Ronn, and stay tuned.

Let's build AI using tech to make it more verifiable and safer!
