PRL – I helped writing a piece about Pearl at optimist a few months ago when it came out. I’m a big fan of the concept and theoretically it makes a lot of sense. Appetite for lets call them “money” tokens is also clearly there as we saw with Zcash. Afaik a big part of PRL supply sits in the wallets of early miners and they are also dependent on them. Also the supply will grow 80% in the next year which definitely isn’t great. At this point the question is if the narrative is strong enough to tank this new supply or not. I sold my PRL a while ago sadly but I would be interested to buy back eventually.

UMIA – One of the most interesting Ownership solutions on the market. I’ve talked to NFTboi quite a lot about the concept and I really think it is superior to other alternatives. A big problem with ownership tokens was that only founder that got rejected in vc came and launched an ownership token because the incentives for founder weren’t good. You had a bunch of degens controlling your business decisions. You need to focus on the tokens growth even if you should’ve just focused on the product. I think UMIA has some good solutions but we will see what the first launches bring. I participated in the presale and still hold some tokens.

CASHCAT – I said I don't do memes so I'll keep it short. I think as a pure bet on RH growth this is a good vehicle. If we see a big season again this won't 10x tho. Its a safe and steady bet. I don't think pure memes will do as well as they did before so I'm not a holder anymore but I see why someone would hold Cashcat.

ZEC – I'm not really convinced. I like the private money thesis and I think with dems winning and crypto becoming sort of the small online community again that isn't mainstream and supported by the president, it could be a good opportunity to shield your money and be on the safe side. I think ZEC mostly played out over the last year. It did a 10x+ in one year and can certainly do more but the R/R to enter a new position here isn't favorable. I also prefer XMR as the "private money" but also the returns there might not be as good because it can't be listed anywhere + has some unknowns about the tokenomics which arguably is bullish because nobody knows anything but an exploit like the one on ZEC could be existential for it.

KNTQ – Also a token I wrote an article about a while ago. I'm a big fan of their business. They are generating good numbers and have the monopoly on staked HYPE. Now the elysium launch brought it on everyones radar. I have mixed feelings about the chain launch but I think it could gain marketshare short term. If it can sustain that depends largly on how .hl's are participating and if we see a big catalyst such as jeff engaging or something similar. I don't hold any tokens anymore but I regret that.

PONS – Not much to say here. I participated in the first run up to a billion but what goes up most come down. The metrics are down 90% from ATH and so is the token. I think we are entering fair value area here and we have to see if RH picks up pace again. If so then PONS is the best pure bet on RH imo.

AI – I've been vocal about AI from like 800k marketcap. I was a big fan but I have don't hold it anymore. I think the swaps routing through the USDG pool instead of the NVDA one which stalled the pool growth was a big thesis invalidator for me. Everyone was screaming board sit which wasn't achievable from the start as it needed AI to be at DOGE levels of marketcap. The dream being shattered at the same time when vlad stopped engaging with the ecosystem killed the token and I don't think it will come back if the pools issue isn't fixed.

KLED – One of these good projects that are a good business but not a good token. I think they tokenized like 5% of the supply through Street which ended up being a flop. If I could invest in the business itself I would do it. The token on the other side I'm not interested in.

CARS – A very interesting one imo. Ownership token with hotwheels gacha. I actually didn't know there is a hotwheels collectible market but there are cars going for 10k+. Its a good sector to gain marketshare in and for that reason I'm interested. Potential revenue for such small sector is probably not great but I think this could rerate higher if it gains substantial marketshare.

CRED – Payment processor that has real adoption and tokenized through Metadao. Its one of the more interesting ones but also a boring sector. I think to succeed you need an interesting business with actual numbers. Credible has actual numbers but a boring business. Its good and probably a good buy for a long term 2x but nothing that would be worth the opportunity cost for me.

SANC – I was on a call with one of the SANC guys and I was impressed. Its the biggest Solana staking provider that also powers various other staking tokens such as jup staked sol etc. They have improved the token massively over the last few months but without buybacks its still another "good business bad token". I own some of it but I would only buy more if they enable some sort of value accrual to token holders.

IMD – One of my favorite experimental AI tokens that came out lately. Each NFT represents one worker that the owner has to setup with API keys. You can then rent these workers to work on your projects. I think this is a really good concept and if adopted would work very well. I don’t like the direction of focusing on being a launchpad. I think not all ideas need to be tokenized and there would be actual demand in renting these workers outside of token launches. NFT holders only have upside from token launches and thats what I don’t like. A pivot to NFT holders being paid for work that doesn’t need to be launched is what would make me consider rebuying.

POD – I own a large bag of pod and also wrote a long form about it a while ago. The founder Luke is a great guy that knows how to grow a business. TLDR is they are using consumer GPUs for inference and pay these people in POD while selling the inference they generated. They buyback 100% of the revenue and have no equity structure stealing value. I think this is one of the greatest AI x Crypto products on the market. They recently had a migration to V2 which lead to them losing a lot of GPUs but they are recovering and I think the price will recover as well very soon.

STONK – I was a big stonk fan a while ago but not anymore. I think their mechanism is just the same extraction as PF but with RWA pairs. There is nothing being done to focus on tokens growth but only on getting as much revenue as possible. Revenue is also down like 80% from ATH so I think it's reasonable priced here if not a little overpriced. I'm not interested atm.

SURPLUS – Very good business with a lot of adoption but they don't make any money. They offer the product with 0 fees and now recently migrated the token to assumingly add value accrual. They inflated the supply by 50% while making no money for value accrual. Either they integrate the token in some way that leads to passive buy pressure or they max extract from the migration. We will see and if I hear some news about value accrual I would definitely consider buying because I think its also one of the best crypto x ai projects out there. The token just isn't

LIT – Not a lot to say here. I like LIT as a beta to hype with much larger upside. I see them as the more regulated version of HYPE with all the licenses but now that hype is entering the regulation game as well I think some of that upside is limited. The thesis violation of RH was a hard one and the price shows. I think here it is probably undervalued and will reprice to 4-5 again very soon. I don't hold any but I will be looking for an entry.

V4 – The launchpad claus launched on and thats the only part I'm bullish on. I like claus but the launchpad got no traction and earns almost nothing from existing tokens but only new launches which it doesn't have a lot of. R/R on Claus is much better.

ABYSS – All my friends are bullish on it and I get why they are. Jintao is a smart and well connected man. I didn't enter and coped on the way up but I think its just not my bet here. The mechanics make sense but they are really complex which is a double edged sword. It can spark a new season on RH with quality > quantity launches and if the launches do well I will probably fomo in but until I see some good launches its not my bet. I hope it wins tho because it would be net positive for our space.

CLAUS – I really like this one and especially the R/R here at 2M. I think they are adding more and more features to becoming a working ecosystem and network of agents. I think a lot of people misunderstand it as just an agent with v4 hooks while it has a lot more stuff to be bullish on. I own a bag and will likely continue to hold it.

SCHIFFY – I jeeted my bag on the first run up and I think the run is over. For me its just a beta of AI here which isn't good. If long picks up pace it can be a buy maybe but for now I'm not interested.

OTC – rev generating protocol that is likely undervalued on the xREV but not my play here. Not a lot of good launches and nothing really novel that could improve our ecosystem but just another launchpad.

BUN – One of my favorite RH tokens. I think the bun bundles with agentic MM make a lot of sense and we can see it on the charts of mosh tokens. They tend to perform better than pure Pons launches. If this finds adoption I'm in for it and will accumulate a big position.

BP – One of the cleanest bets on tokenization. I don't own a bag atm but if I get a good entry I would be willing to buy a lot. I don't know what I think of the tokens to equity conversion as the value accrual but other than that its really solid.

NET – Wrote a long form on this as well. I think the run is done here. The chart doesn't look good and most catalysts played out. There are better opportunities out there.

FLOAT – A novel launchpad on solana that I could see rule the trenches for a few weeks. I want to get a bag but there isn't a good entry here. I think this reprices much higher in the coming days. I think it solves a lot of issues I have with PF and thats the reason I like it.

QUAI – I had to look into this and it definitely is novel and advanced tech. I think for it to work it needs adoption tho. These kind of projects are too complex for people to understand and being too complex paired with no adoption just means they won't recover.

HOOKR- I was too lazy to look into it and thought its just another hooks launchpad. Now I learned that its much more than that. You can deploy custom pools through hookr for existing tokens and the value accruals to the token from this. 250M in total volume is impressive and this is more advanced than any of these hook protocols. I will do a little more DD and might start building a position soon.

WTH – Also a very interesting one. It takes advantage of price arbs on RH and distributes value to token holders. I think as a concept this makes sense and makes the value come back to the ecosystem and not being lost. One question with these arb tokens is if they have a working bot why aren't they using it privately and keep all the profits. Why do they tokenize it?

UP – Good RH infra project but not worth it for a quick flip. It has impressive numbers and a few RH interactions but the emissions are enormous. If you don't stake your supply its not worth it at all.

PRIORS – This looks interesting as well. A credit protocol for AI agents. The mechanism makes sense and also found adoption already. For that reason I'm interested in it. It solves a real problem while being tokenized and buring supply from collateral. This is also one of these projects I would buy if RH shows signs of a new season. Definitely on my watchlist.

TORCH – Not my play. A launchpad with no innovative features and a terminal. Depends on good launches but until they happen I'm not interested.

NEST – Very good bet on Hype and elysium. I think this is probably the best bet if you are still sidelined on the elysium trade like me. I should probably get some if we get a good price again before elysium launch. Or if elysium does well I will accumulate it anyway.

BREAK – Some sort of social layer for collector crypt. I am generally interested in stuff like this. It also has some adoption with 60k rev already, but I think it is fairly valued here.

LILLY - AI Influencer giving memecoin calls. Not my play.

GRIFT – I'm very interested. An open world game where agents live normal lifes and keep the city running. People can enter that world and complete tasks and earn RWAs. Also some actions from the agents buy the grift token from the treasury. Already 6% burned. I will keep this on the watchlist for sure.

ORBIO – I faded this from the start because I didn't like it. I think the product of using trading fees to fund inference made sense when volume routed through the correct fees. Now that a few fraudulent pools get all the fees that doesn't work anymore. Their pivot to a venice-esque private AI platform makes sense but I  would need to see adoption of that to be interested again. I think the old business is mostly dead now it depends on the private AI part.

ZRO – Layerzero is one of the alts I like the most. Im looking forward to their chain launch which also introduced value accrual to the token. They partnered with Citadal, NYSE and DTCC for this. Its a great bet on Tokenization. Its a long term trade but surely worth it.

TIBBIR – This is a weird one. The connections to Ribbit capital and the reputable wallets in just make this a mystery. I think its quite high for the few information that are public. I honestly don't really have an opinion on it.

KUDO – Verifiable promises by ai agent that are tokenized. Interesting idea and sort of similar to Priors. Devs look reputable and R/R here might not be bad. I will keep it on my watchlist

BROW - Product scans skills for vulnerabilities. Thats a useful concept. I don't see where the token fits in tho and they launched a launchpad which I don't think is bullish at all.

QUOTUM – Actually good project but some bundlers own 30% of the supply. Im good.

WORM – Security layer for AI agents to protect them from signing fraudulent contracts etc. Useful product but also again they added a launchpad for whatever reason. Some micropayments go towards buybacks that burned 6.5%. Could be a good one. Ill keep it on the watchlist.

PNKSTR – I would rather buy a punk if I was bullish on punks tbh. A lot of my friends are accumulating punks again so it might not be a bad bet here tho.

PINO – AI agent that is viral on socials. Not my trade tbh.

SAPLING – This might be a good bet if zcash goes on a crazy run again. I think there is upside if you accumulate before people catch on the trade. Stays on the watchlist.

PEAK – Just another launchpad with no novel features imo. Also site looks really vibecoded.

BINF – Another stake for inference token but on BNB this time. Im not bullish anything on BNB atm with the binance hack so its not my play.

NOSANA – Interesting project I will definitely keep it on the watchlist. I like all AI x crypto projects but this is more complex so I need to look into it more in depth.

MOSS – Another open world MMORPG thats integrated with crypto. If it gains players this can work very well but with 3 online players this doesn't look that interesting to me.

PURSUIT – I like it and I tried the product. It works. Idk what I would value this at but its solid.

DREAMS – I remember this from a year ago. This is a good project and works but has little traction currently. I'm not a fan of x402 stuff unless we enter some season again. Without a catalyst this doesn't do well.

SZR – No traction so I'm not really interested. Also 300 volume on the 24h.

MANCER - 16 in daily fees don't look too great. I got familiar with the concept and its not bad but its just not an investable token at current metrics.

CHOP – One of the more interesting product with actual adoption. I think its a novel concept and might be worth accumulating if RH does a comeback.

ZZZ – The GMX dev aspect of this is genuinely interesting but other than that the fact that its at 8M without a working product is unjustifiable. The premium for the dev is too high here imo and if the product is good I might consider it but not at the current stage.

MASK – I think the privacy sector is very interesting and I would need to try mask to see if it really is anonymous. My privacy quant said it isn't but I will regardless try it in the coming days and might enter if I really think the product is superior to others on the market.

CLANKER – The new founder is the only aspect making me bullish here. Depends on execution now but I'm not bullish clanker protocol nor base so not my play.

DARK – Venice on Robinhood with better prices on some models. Interesting sector but now that orbio also competes there it could be hard. Its been on my watchlist forever and it will probably stay there.

SIDELOT – Good concept but no adoption. Either this gains traction and it continues the pump or it doesn't and we go to zero. I'm not that interested.

1EDGE – Some sort of solana launchpad and terminal. Im so tired of seeing this over and over again. Not my trade

DELTA – Everyone said this is one of the most important projects in RH infra. It doesn't have a lot of adoption but just a product. Even at 9M now I wouldn't buy this tbf. At 5M this might be worth looking at but I think its still overpriced because of the big pump.

DARWIN – Good devs but the product doesn't look close to being ready and all thats live is an encrypted file sharing product. Not that interesting at the current valuation imo.

PROHPET – Interesting supply sink mechanism for a memecoin but not my play.

UNI – The cleanest bet on RH growth but value accrual and token equity concerns are valid and should be taken into account. Very good business ofc.

BORRO - 1.16 in fees in the last 30 days shows there is no adoption. Not interested until there is any traction.

LLL – Virtuals launch so I'm less interested. The idea isn't new and if they can execute well on it this could be good. Not my play because of virtuals tho.

DEUS – The robotics fund project. Its a legit project but iirc the unlocks are horrible. I would rather buy BOT as a robotics exposure.

PARE – I liked the concept from the start but based on the PA it looks like the project rugged. Happy to be convinced otherwise but I don't think it can just pull a v reversal after that chart.

STATICS – A dex with 10k in 24h volume. Doesn't look like it found adoption so not my trade until that reverses.

EARN – This is one of the RH projects I really like. I think I'm gonna accumulate some if I get some RH bags again. Definitely on my watchlist.

EXFIL – A trading terminal and app. Depends on the value accrual and volume but I usually stay away from terminal coins.

OVER - An actual interesting primitive. Trade volatility. If that works this could be really good but again its a virtuals launch so I'm not really interested. I will play around with it tho.

What if you could build a fantasy sports team that was yours to keep?

Introducing Pursuit, a new game where you collect athlete cards, build your roster, and compete for prizes.

Most fantasy sports games have the same problem: you spend a season building your team only to start from scratch the next year.

Your home league goes inactive, DFS resets every week, and games like FUT and Sorare make you rebuild your roster every season.

We think there's a better way to play.

In Pursuit, your team is a collection of athlete cards you actually own. Rip packs, build your lineup, and compete in weekly contests for prizes. Owning the cards gets you into contests with no additional entry fees.

Your cards never expire, so your team carries into the next season and beyond. You can also fuse duplicates into rarer cards that score more points, giving you a reason to keep improving your roster over time.

We're building a fantasy sports game where the time and effort you put into your team actually carries over.

Pursuit is live in private beta on Monad testnet.

We're looking for early players to help test the game and help shape its future ahead of a mainnet launch targeted for football kickoff in September 2027.

text:
💭 What If L2s Could Access Ethereum Liquidity Synchronously?

Ethereum has deep liquidity. But scaling across rollups has fragmented it into isolated execution environments.

For DeFi applications, accessing L1 liquidity often means bridging assets or waiting for asynchronous cross-chain messages, adding delays, costs, and complexity.

@puffer_unifi is designed to change that.

Through synchronous composability, Puffer UniFi aims to enable L2 applications to interact with Ethereum L1 smart contracts and liquidity within the same transaction.

Imagine borrowing against collateral on Ethereum L1 and executing a trade on Puffer UniFi as one atomic operation.

No separate bridging workflow. No waiting for cross-chain messages between steps.

What does this unlock for DeFi?

Better capital efficiency. Fewer cross-chain barriers. More composable applications.

Execution scales. Ethereum liquidity remains synchronously accessible. 🐡

text:
For two decades, writing the exploit was the bottleneck in a cyberattack. AI made that step cheap, and patching hasn't gotten faster:

- On average, attacks went from landing 63 days after disclosure in 2018-19 to 7 days before it in 2025

- A working exploit went from a skilled person's month to a few hours of machine time

- The median time to fully fix a known-exploited bug rose to 43 days

a16z's @asaf_ez and @steph_zhang expect a long, expensive worm era, hitting hardest where systems can't update fast: hospitals, schools, small water systems.

"When attacking is nearly free, attackers no longer need to want a target."

Full piece from Asaf Ezra and Steph Zhang: https://t.co/8L3D9mnL44

关于 SignalPlus 安全事件处置及用户保障的公告

11月4日凌晨起，SignalPlus 遭遇一起网络攻击。我们及时发现异常并快速采取处置措施，阻止了影响进一步扩大。截至目前统计，本次事件造成的相关用户损失总额被控制在不超过$82k，SignalPlus 已经开始逐个全额赔付。

客户资产安全始终是 SignalPlus 的首要关注。为最大程度保障用户账户及资产安全，我们第一时间主动联系了各个合作交易所，已从交易所侧停用所有与 SignalPlus 关联的用户 API Key，并暂停平台服务，开展全面安全排查。

这是一项面向所有用户的预防性保护措施。账户被纳入此次主动停用保护范围，并不意味着其信息已泄露或已发生损失。我们希望通过主动、全面的处置，为用户提供进一步保障。 对于此次事件给用户造成的损失、担忧及使用上的不便，我们郑重致歉。我们会持续跟进调查与用户反馈；对于后续核查确认由本次 SignalPlus 侧造成的用户损失，我们也将继续履行全额赔付承诺。

事件经过
根据目前的排查结果，一家第三方技术供应商联系人的 Telegram 账号被盗。攻击者冒用该联系人的身份，与我方工程师沟通，并以虚假 Teams 视频会议邀请为切入点实施社会工程学攻击，入侵了该工程师的电脑并进入潜伏状态。11月4日凌晨，通过工程师电脑的权限对内网发动攻击。我们监测到异常后阻断了相关攻击，并封堵了已发现的问题。第一时间联系各大交易所，主动停用了所有和 SignalPlus 相关的 Key，以确保用户资金安全。同时 SignalPlus 相关服务全都进入封闭维护状态。

在完成全面排查及必要的安全加固、确认具备安全恢复条件后，我们将逐步恢复各项服务，并通过官方渠道同步恢复进展和操作指引。 服务暂停期间，请用户通过交易所官方渠道查看和管理账户、持仓及挂单。

共同抵御恶意攻击，维护用户权益
网络攻击是整个科技行业持续面对的挑战，身份冒用和社会工程学等手段也在利用日常业务往来中的信任实施侵害。SignalPlus 坚决抵制非法入侵、窃取信息及侵害用户资产的恶意行为。

我们也正视此前未将 IP 白名单强制设为交易所 API Key 接入条件这一防护不足。这项安全要求落实不够充分，是我们的责任。后续我们将强化 API 接入要求，并进一步加强研发终端防护、内部访问控制及密钥管理。

保护用户、完善自身安全防护，是我们必须承担的责任。我们将持续加强安全建设，并与交易所、技术合作伙伴及安全机构加强协作和威胁信息共享，共同防范恶意攻击、抵制网络犯罪，维护用户权益与行业信任。

感谢各位用户的耐心与支持。我们会认真落实赔付、整改及后续服务恢复安排，并持续向用户同步进展。

text:
Today I met with a veteran investor who argued that memory stocks are not cheap even at a P/E of 3. Below is an edited version of our conversation.

Memory LTAs are basically meaningless. The best the LTAs being signed today can do is get customers to shoulder part of the memory makers' capex. Once prices fall, customers will gladly forfeit their deposits (prepayments) and walk away from the LTAs.

Historically, whenever prices fell more than 60% from the peak, customers broke their LTAs even after signing them.
So even if a 2027 shortage is certain and the stocks trade at a P/E of 3 on 2027 operating profit, 2028 operating profit is uncertain, which makes it hard to justify a higher valuation.

He went on to argue that even if 2028 operating profit were certain, we would still have to account for 2029 operating profit.

I pushed back and asked why the market doesn't discount TSMC the same way. Why does TSMC get such a high valuation? Wouldn't TSMC also take a big hit if the AI boom fades?

His answer: the problem was how violently memory prices rose in the first place.
If memory makers had raised prices in a healthy way like TSMC, it might be a different story. But because they hiked prices like a commodity, the market has no choice but to treat memory stocks like commodity stocks.

Even if memory makers stay in shortage through 2030, he said, the market will price in the risk of oversupply in 2031.

He closed his argument this way: even at 3x 2027 earnings, if memory prices fall in 2028 by enough to break LTAs, that 3x multiple on 2027 works out to 7.8 to 10x on 2028. So current valuations are not cheap.

text:
The NASDAQ has already given back all of its post-midterm gains, down another 3% today.

Similar thing happened in 2018.

Lot of exuberance following the midterms in 2018 (SPX rallied 2% the next day), then 3 major events caused the market to sell-off into December.

1) A Hawkish Fed: In October 2018, Fed Chairman Jerome Powell remarked that interest rates were still a long way from neutral, signaling to investors that the Fed would continue tightening monetary policy into 2019 regardless of cooling economic data. This triggered severe liquidity fears and widespread panic selling.

This is similar to today in that the market is pricing in 2 more rate hikes despite the sell-off we have seen in tech.

2) Escalating U.S.–China Trade War : Just before and after the midterms, a flood of major multinational companies (including Caterpillar, 3M, and Ford) warned that rising tariff costs were eating into their profit margins and disrupting global supply chains.

This is similar to today as tariffs have had major inflationary effects and is one of the reasons why the Fed has to remain hawkish.

3) Tech Valuation Reversals: The technology sector, which had been the primary engine driving the multi-year bull market, abruptly reversed course in late 2018. We also had the FAANG slump in which major tech giants faced severe regulatory scrutiny over antitrust and data privacy concerns (such as Facebook's controversies).

This is similar to today as the AI trade has taken quite the breather with AI fears mounting.

History does not always repeat itself, but it does often rhyme.

text:
随着民主党赢下中期选举，数据中心面临的政策收紧和停建压力成了热议话题，首先需要理解，为什么会有反对建设数据中心的声音，主要是因为居民认为自己需要承担相关的电费、用水、噪音、土地占用等成本，却很难看到与之对应的收益，甚至担心AI的过度发展会进一步影响到自身的就业前景。

Ben Thompson的这篇AI on the Ballot列举了一些数据中心建设的延缓和停止可能产生的影响，我进行了简单的总结，更推荐直接阅读原文：https://t.co/g8G0LjOBWq

1、少部分已经获得许可或已建成数据中心的Neocloud将有稀缺性，但整体而言，Neocloud相比Hyperscalers更难获得许可、场地、资金等，因此利空前者，利好后者。

2、对于NVDA，短期是利空，因为大量数据中心和Neocloud依赖英伟达的芯片，而Hyperscalers普遍拥有自主研发芯片的能力。但长远来看，如果电力和数据中心长期受到约束，那么在同等功率下能产出更多Token的英伟达芯片就将体现出价值。

3、民主党大获全胜不利于马斯克的企业，但政治上对于地面数据中心的反对，又利好SpaceX太空数据中心的建设。

4、对于Anthropic这类Frontier Labs，在计算资源受限的环境下，企业更可能选择效率更高的前沿模型。并且，如果初创企业更难获得廉价的计算资源，也就更难开发出好的产品，从而让Frontier Labs有充足的时间切入这些赛道。

5、对AAPL而言，有限的计算资源意味着终端设备的边缘推理更加重要，更重要的是，AI部署速度放缓意味着内存短缺问题会得到缓解，而苹果将从中极大受益。

目前与数据中心相关的政策，极大影响了AI产业链各部分的前景，通过这篇文章厘清其中关系，就可以在后续政策或风向发生改变的第一时间，做出正确的反应。

quoted_text:
Something is drinking while you argue.
It does not need your agreement. Only your return.
You have heard that time moves forward. 

A pendulum does not win by being believed. It wins by being fed. Attention is the stretch. Emotion is the swing. The moment you stop answering, the arc shortens.

You can spend years fighting gatekeepers, then become one. You don’t even have to forget what it felt like on the outside. You can remember every bit of it and still vote to make the next person’s life harder.

You remember the fees you couldn’t afford. The interviews with people who had better connections. The years someone else decided whether your work was good enough to count. You promised yourself that if you ever made it through, you wouldn’t treat people the way they treated you.

Then you get your chance. You work until your sleep suffers. The first month you pay every bill without worrying about grocery money, you almost can’t believe it. Years later there’s a home, payroll, clients, people depending on what you’ve built.

A newcomer shows up with a better way and a lower price. One customer asks why you charge more. Then Another. Nobody has left yet, but you’re already counting the accounts you could lose. Three would hurt. Six might mean telling somebody who helped build the business that their job is gone. Your stomach reacts before you form an opinion.

At the next meeting nobody says they’re afraid. They talk about quality, safety, responsible growth. Maybe newcomers should need another qualification. Maybe production needs limits. The businesses already operating can be exempt. They’ve proved themselves. You hear yourself agreeing.

Some protections are necessary. Nobody wants an untrained electrician wiring their home. But if the new rules cost thousands while the people already making money are exempt, what danger are they actually removing? When established producers complain that more supply will lower prices, who asks the families that could finally afford the product whether that’s bad?

You used to ask those questions. Now they sound like an attack. The money is only the surface. What the pendulum is actually feeding on is the meaning you’ve attached to those years. If somebody else can succeed without enduring everything you endured, what does that say about the suffering you turned into proof that you deserved to be here?

Was some of your suffering unnecessary? It’s easier to make your pain a qualification and demand that everyone after you earn it too.

You have become the person you once hated, and you can explain every decision that brought you here.

You didn’t set out to become unfair. Each decision had a reason. Now those reasons protect your position, and when somebody questions the arrangement, you feel as though they’re questioning everything you’ve worked for.

There’s a spiritual idea that calls this kind of force a pendulum, a thought form kept going by the attention and emotion people give it. Some believe these influences exist beyond what our physical senses can detect. Others recognize something similar in institutions, habits, and conflicts that keep drawing people back.

A pendulum doesn’t need everyone to agree. Two political camps can despise each other and still keep the same fight going. An insult produces a reply, which becomes proof of how terrible the other side is. Both come back tomorrow, convinced they’re resisting something. Neither notices how much of their day now belongs to the people they reject.

After years of forming opinions, finding evidence, and defending your position, admitting you were wrong might mean admitting you hurt people while believing you were helping them.

And that is a much harder thing to face than losing an argument.

Now think about an ordinary morning. Someone wakes up at home. Their partner is still asleep. There’s coffee to make, breakfast to prepare, nothing unusual planned. Before getting out of bed, they pick up their phone and open X.

The first post they see is a video of a child crying beside the remains of a destroyed home. They watch it, read the comments looking through the replies. It’s awful. They want to know what happened, whether anyone is helping, what can be done.

But before they’ve figured that out, they’re looking at another post. A politician shouting. A warning about the economy. Strangers arguing about who deserves blame for something else. Then another video showing people suffering somewhere else in the world.

Each story deserves attention, at least enough to understand what’s happening. Perhaps there’s an organization they could support or someone they could help. But the feed keeps moving. One emergency follows another, including situations they have no practical way to reach. They haven’t done anything wrong by opening their phone, yet putting it down is beginning to feel like turning their back on people who are suffering.

Forty minutes have passed. Their partner is awake now and asks a harmless question about breakfast. They answer sharply, irritated without quite realizing how angry they’ve become.

Their partner didn’t cause any of it. They’re simply the person who happens to be there when all those feelings come out.

The algorithm didn’t cause the suffering in those videos. It selected material likely to hold someone’s attention without knowing whether that person could help. An event becomes a headline, then somebody’s interpretation, then an argument about that interpretation. Before long you’re reacting to a story about a story about a story while the real person beside you has to repeat a question.

A simulation inside a simulation inside a simulation. Whatever reality ultimately is, we build these layers every day. What happened. What we remember. What we think others meant. What we imagine they’ll do next. What the feed predicts will upset us. We make decisions inside these versions and sometimes forget to check what is actually happening.

Spend enough time expecting people to behave a certain way and you’ll start noticing every example that proves you right. You’ll remember the insults, the betrayals, the times you were taken advantage of. Other experiences become harder to recall. Eventually a person can do something completely ordinary and you’ll interpret it through years of things somebody else did.

A woman walks into an RV repair shop waiting room in a genuinely happy mood. Something she’d worked toward is finally going right.

The television is showing disturbing news. One woman says she can’t bear to watch but keeps watching. A man says looking away is irresponsible. If people stop paying attention, who will care?

The newcomer looks at the television, then becomes aware of her own mouth.

She’s smiling.

Should she stop? Would it seem indecent to mention her good news? Nobody has accused her of anything. She’s barely been there a minute, yet she’s already wondering what expression the room will allow.

You know how that happens. Somebody lowers their voice and you do too. You were about to share something wonderful, but now it feels inappropriate. You look around to figure out what everyone else is feeling before you decide what you’re allowed to feel.

Of course consideration matters. You don’t enter a grieving friend’s house and demand they celebrate your promotion. You listen, cook, maybe cry with them. But they may also need someone who can remember the doctor’s instructions, drive the car, or help them get through the next morning.

When did visible distress become the proof that you care?

One person in that waiting room was suffering over the news. Another was angry about the possibility of looking away. The third was beginning to feel guilty for having a good day. What would the people on the television have lost if she’d kept smiling?

Nobody asked her to give up her happiness. She was considering it herself.

And if she had something genuinely good happening in her life, why should that become another thing she has to apologize for? There are already enough people who need help. Making one more person miserable doesn’t necessarily help any of them.

The same thing happens through pride, although nobody would mistake it for compassion.

Someone says something plainly wrong. You correct them. They answer a point you never made. You explain again. They give that little laugh that tells you they aren’t listening and want you to know it. Eventually the conversation ends.

An hour later you’re cutting an onion.

Their laugh comes back. Now you’ve got the perfect reply. You put down the knife and say it to an empty kitchen. In this version they can’t interrupt. They finally understand how ridiculous they sounded.

Later you’re in the shower and another example comes to mind. Even better. Maybe you should send one final message. Just to make sure they understand.

They might be asleep. You are still arguing with them.

At some point you stopped trying to establish what was true. You wanted that particular person to admit you were right. Their dismissal made you feel small, and now you’re imagining how satisfying it would be to make them feel small instead.

Some disputes demand persistence. Real harm, false accusations, and unjust rules can’t always be ignored. But some arguments have been over for hours while one person continues them alone. You can lose an entire evening to somebody who isn’t thinking about you at all.

Eventually you become so practiced at finding other people’s mistakes that even good news sounds like something to challenge. A younger colleague develops a better method and you’re already explaining why they haven’t earned the right to use it. Not enough experience. Didn’t follow the process. Hasn’t paid their dues.

Back in that meeting, preparing to shut the door.

Not everyone learns to watch for danger through pride. Some learn it when they’re small.

A child knows an adult is angry from the sound of footsteps. A cupboard closes too hard. A glass is set down a particular way. The child stops speaking before the adult even enters the room. Noticing those details may have kept them safe.

Years later they live with somebody gentle. A text goes unanswered for twenty minutes and their stomach drops. Their mind supplies a familiar story. They’re angry. I’ve done something wrong. Prepare for the fight.

The other person might simply be driving, but their body has already begun responding to a different life.

They start typing an accusation and stop.

The fear doesn’t instantly leave. Changing that response may take years and real support. But tonight, fear didn’t get to write the message. That matters.

Something you learned to survive can later hurt people who love you. You didn’t choose the circumstances that taught you to be afraid. But the people in your life now aren’t necessarily the people who frightened you. Your body can still respond as though they are.

Even that awareness can turn against you. You notice your anxiety and start checking whether you’ve finally stopped being anxious. You judge yourself for reacting. You wonder if you’ve lost all your progress. Every uncomfortable moment becomes another test.

A woman lives on a farm. She loves her animals, her work, her relationship. Money isn’t the daily worry it once was. Yet she’s become irritable, sleeping badly, unable to recover the excitement she used to feel about the life she’s built.

Picture her waking up and staring at the ceiling.

Is it gone?

No. Still there.

Yesterday was like this too. Maybe there’s an old resentment she never resolved. Maybe she’s doing something wrong. Before her feet reach the floor, she’s searching years of memories for an explanation.

Then comes the thought that makes an ordinary bad morning much worse.

I have the life I wanted. Why can’t I just be happy?

Outside, an animal is stealing another’s feed. The water needs changing. There’s mud by the gate. Coffee is getting cold. None of it requires her to feel inspired.

She can put on her boots and go outside irritated. Maybe the feeling stays. Maybe an animal does something ridiculous, and twenty minutes pass before she remembers to check herself again.

Depression, grief, illness, chronic pain, and bad sleep deserve real care. Seeking help can be the most important decision. But sometimes the effort to explain every feeling becomes heavier than the feeling itself. You suffer, then suffer because you’re suffering, then decide that your inability to stop must mean something is wrong with you.

You can even turn the desire for freedom into another way of punishing yourself. You decide to stop reacting, then become angry every time you react. You learn about self-awareness, then spend the day examining yourself for signs that you’ve finally become conscious enough.

You’ve taken something that was supposed to help you live and turned it into one more reason you aren’t allowed to enjoy living.

Think again about the pendulum idea. A headline, a stranger’s insult, a delayed reply, the memory of being humiliated fifteen years ago. Something happens and your mind immediately starts preparing a response. Sometimes the same thought returns two or three times, demanding another argument, another explanation, another chance to make yourself feel safe.

You don’t have to answer every time.

You may not control the first feeling. Your pulse rises before you’ve decided anything. You’re angry, frightened, jealous, or sad on a day you expected to enjoy. But having a feeling and doing everything it tells you to do are two different things.

Sometimes the response is necessary. Real injustice demands action. A child needs protection. Someone has to challenge a dangerous rule. Freedom doesn’t mean refusing to care or pretending nothing can hurt you.

You see the message and don’t send the accusation. You hear the insult and decide whether answering will accomplish anything. You watch enough news to find one useful action, then take it. You let somebody share their happiness without making them feel guilty. You congratulate the colleague whose talent threatens your position.

You judge the newcomer by their work instead of by how much they suffered getting there.

The gatekeeper believes they’re defending responsibility. The people in the waiting room believe they’re defending compassion. The person rehearsing an argument believes they’re defending truth.

And sometimes they really are. Responsibility matters. Compassion matters. Truth matters.

But there’s a difference between protecting something good and needing everybody to recognize you as the person who protects it.

The rule becomes more important than the people it was supposed to serve. Being visibly upset becomes more important than helping. Winning the argument becomes more important than learning anything.

You can spend years doing this without realizing what happened because the words you use still sound right.

We talk about being programmed as though somebody must have built an elaborate illusion around us. But consider the instructions we’ve already learned.

Your value depends on being right. Your happiness is offensive while somebody else suffers. Anyone who follows you must endure what you endured. A delayed reply means abandonment. A new competitor means danger. If you aren’t feeling grateful every minute, something must be wrong with you.

Parents, institutions, losses, rewards, and years of repetition taught us these rules. Some protected us once. Some never made sense. We forget where they came from and begin calling them personality. Principle. Instinct. Reality.

Then one day you catch yourself following one.

You can keep going. You can explain why this time is different, why your anger is justified, why the other person deserves what you’re about to do. There may even be some truth in your explanation.

Or you can stop long enough to ask whether this is really what you want to do.

Maybe that’s where becoming the programmer instead of the programmed begins. Not with the ability to control everything that happens to you. You can’t force someone to love you, erase poverty with thought, or undo your past by declaring yourself conscious.

But you can question the rules you’ve been living by. You can look at what they actually do, who benefits from them, and whether the people you care about are paying for fears they didn’t create.

If you believe you’re an immortal, sovereign soul, that belief should mean more than feeling powerful when everything is going well. What happens to your freedom when somebody insults you? What happens to your compassion when somebody else’s success threatens your own? What happens to your principles when following them could cost you something?

And if you believe in divine harmony, consider what that asks of you when the fair decision isn’t the one that benefits you.

It’s easy to talk about being guided by your heart when your interests and your conscience agree. The harder moments are the ones when you have to choose between protecting what you’ve built and allowing someone else the same opportunity that made your life possible.

What kind of sovereignty is it when a stranger’s laugh can command six hours of your life? What kind of freedom is it when you escape the gatekeepers only to become one?

If the universe used X’s algorithm to put this message in front of you, whether that was fate or chance matters less than what you do with it.

You can recognize these habits in other people all day. You’ll find plenty of examples. The real question is what happens when you catch yourself doing the same thing, with explanations that sound completely reasonable to you.

Return to the meeting.

A proposal lies on the table. Someone is remembering every fee they paid, every refusal, the years they were made to feel inadequate. They are afraid of losing what they built, and that fear has reasons. Outside is somebody capable, asking for a chance. Maybe they’ll be better. Maybe customers will leave. Nobody can promise otherwise.

For years this person believed the worst thing that happened to them was being kept outside. Now they have the power to do it to somebody else.

The vote hasn’t been cast yet.

Their past is in the room. It doesn’t have to cast the vote.

text:
Privacy is eroded in a variety of places. Here is an important one: currently, third-party RPC providers can see what accounts you are reading, and what transactions you are simulating before you send them.

Perhaps most significantly, if your browser wallet has multiple accounts, the provider can group them together by seeing which accounts are queried from the same IP address at the same time.

@category_xyz researchers have addressed this with WP-ORAM (write-public ORAM), a new means of making servers oblivious to what data is being read, while keeping writes (and the actual state) public. The paper includes both a proposal and a real, pragmatic implementation that can keep up with Monad.

Practical innovation to solve real privacy problems. Great job @AnanyaAppan James Austgen @KushalBabel @sourav1547 !

text:
民主党赢下美国两院，也别想一脚踩死美国AI！特朗普手里还有两张王牌！

民主党虽然拿下了参众两院，但未来两年，他们想全面禁止AI，或者强行通过共和党坚决反对的激进AI监管法案，几乎不可能。

为什么？美国制度给总统和少数党留下了两道重要防线：

1. 参议院60票门槛：民主党虽然控制参议院，但普通重大立法通常需要60票才能结束辩论。没有部分共和党议员支持，很多法案根本过不了这一关。

2. 特朗普总统否决权：即使民主党在国会通过了法案，特朗普也可以直接否决。想推翻总统否决，需要参众两院分别获得2/3多数，难度极高。

所以，接下来两年，民主党可以调查、听证、施压、限制部分政策，但想直接按下美国AI产业的暂停键，没那么容易。

币安发展到今天，已经到了大而不倒的地步。但说到底，它仍然是一家控制权高度集中的私人企业。

外界对它的信任，终究是有金额上限的。而金融体系最可怕的事情，就是信任崩塌往往先于真正的资不抵债。

更让我担忧的是，币安早就不只是一家交易所了。币安不止有庞大的散户群体，还有长期以来依附于它的复杂业态。量化机构、做市商、中小交易所在币安的对冲盘，这些共同构成了币圈重要的流动性基础设施。

一旦币安的信用崩塌，散户挤兑、机构撤资、做市商撤走流动性，整个行业都可能陷入连锁危机。

散户进一步退圈，流动性进一步枯竭。

等待整个币圈的，恐怕不再是一轮普通的熊市，而是漫长的冬寂。

一个市值数万亿美元的行业，竟然会因为一家私人企业的信用危机而陷入瘫痪。这应该就是币圈“去中心化”最可笑的地方吧。

text:
今天参加了两场稳定币相关的 Side Event，逢人就问一个问题：

这个周期，哪些稳定币公司真正拿到了大结果？

我得到了两个答案：一个是 Anchorage Digital，另一个是 Reap。

先说 Anchorage Digital。

一位稳定币公司的高管告诉我，最近，无论是 HashKey 和圆币科技正在推广的美元稳定币 RDUSD，还是 OSL 重点推动的美元稳定币 USDGO，其背后的稳定币铸造方和发行机构，都涉及美国公司 Anchorage Digital Bank。

而 Anchorage 服务的客户，已经多达十几家。

按照这位高管的说法，Anchorage 向 HashKey、OSL、圆币科技等公司收取稳定币铸造费用。如果按照1%甚至更高的费率计算，这将是一笔非常可观的收入。

举个例子：如果一家分销商发行或分销了100亿美元的稳定币，按照1%的铸造费率计算，仅这一项就可能产生1亿美元的费用。

这，其实说明了一个问题：在稳定币产业链中，谁掌握上游基础设施，谁可能拥有更高的利润和议价权。

再说第二家公司：Reap。

这家公司最近几年的发展势头非常猛。

2023年以前，很多人可能还没有意识到 Reap 的潜力。因为在2023年，Reap的稳定币支付额每个月还不到1亿美元。

但到了2025年，这个数字已经激增至每月30亿美元。

增长速度相当惊人。

一位接近 Reap 的朋友告诉我，巴西、东南亚和中东，都是 Reap 重点布局的市场。

它的业务逻辑其实并不复杂：

A企业把稳定币交给 Reap，Reap再将当地法币支付给A企业在其他国家的商业伙伴B。

本质上，Reap是在利用稳定币作为跨境资金流转的通道，帮助企业完成不同国家之间的资金结算。

而这还只是第一步。

这位朋友还提到，未来，Reap甚至希望实现法币对法币的直接跨境支付。

也就是说，A企业把法币交给 Reap，Reap就可以直接将B企业所在另一个国家的法币支付给B企业。整个过程，稳定币作为背后的资金结算基础设施，而企业无需直接接触稳定币。

他还有一个非常大胆的判断：

未来，几乎所有跨境支付渠道，都将有由稳定币驱动。

为什么？

因为传统跨境支付体系，尤其是SWIFT相关的传统银行支付链路，速度慢、成本高，一笔跨境资金转账往往需要等待数天，甚至一周。

而通过稳定币进行跨境资金转移，通常当天就能到账，最迟也可能在第二天完成。

速度更快，成本更低。两者之间的效率差距非常明显。

这也是为什么越来越多的企业开始关注稳定币在跨境支付中的应用。

回头看这两家公司，其实代表了稳定币产业链上的两种不同赢家：

Anchorage Digital赚的是上游基础设施的钱，Reap赚的是跨境支付场景的钱。

一个掌握发行和铸造环节，一个掌握真实的跨境支付需求。

这两家稳定币公司的发展经历，让我深受启发。

稳定币真正的大机会，在于谁掌握了产业链的关键节点。

更值得关注的是，他们早在5年前就开始布局稳定币业务，并最终在今天拿到了大结果。

而那时候，Web3行业很少有人关注稳定币支付，甚至很多人都不认为这是一个值得做的赛道。

这让我想到，现在也有很多人认为Web3已经没有新机会了。

但机会，往往就藏在那些还不被大多数人看见、也不被大部分人看好的地方。

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
昨晚的美股很强势但板块也是在分化：道指大涨约3%创下44年来最强的中期选举后单日表现，标普等权+1.86%强于标普500的1.5%，罗素2000涨幅也高于纳指。道指明显强于纳指，说明涨幅在向传统蓝筹、消费、医疗等板块扩散。而整个科技板块分化则很明显：超大云厂大科技非常强势、部分软件/saas走势很好，但半导体和电力板块整体走弱。说说我的理解：
1、看起来市场认为“中选结束+分裂政府（民主党掌控国会+川普继续当总统）”是个好事：
一方面政策不确定性大大降低；
另一方面分裂政府也会让政策极端化风险降低市场更偏好“有制衡的华盛顿”；
而油价大跌，布油跌倒94原因则是市场认为伊朗战争可能降温（这个迹象值得继续关注）。

昨晚走势非常典型地体现了“政治不确定性消除 + AI交易内部分化”这两件事。

2、民主党掌控国会对企业意味着什么？
1）政策波动减小：过去两年共和党一党独大时，关税、监管、地缘政策变化很快、很猛。现在国会被民主党掌控，很多激进动作会被卡住，市场喜欢这种“少折腾”。
2）行业板块受益点：
（1）医疗、医院类股票大涨（市场预期民主党可能部分逆转之前的医保削减）；
（2）消费、零售（尤其服务低收入人群的）表现好；
（3）油价大跌对能源股是利空，但对航空、运输、消费等传统行业是利好。

3）但民主党在数据中心、AI基建、环境监管上更严格，对能源、部分工业和基建节奏会有压制。
所以市场更多是在交易“不确定性降低”和“油价回落”，但并不是说预期民主党会大幅刺激传统产业。

3、再重点聊聊科技板块内部的AI分化
1）民主党在德州、乔治亚等关键州取得进展，这些地方对数据中心的社区反对声浪很大。市场担心数据中心建设节奏会放缓（环境、电力、水资源、监管审查更严），从而影响半导体硬件需求增速。

而大厂本身算力积累够，又是承载AI商业化的主体，反而可能因为新建放缓而相对受益（减少资本开支压力，强化现有优势）。

2）软件股有些表现不错，则说明资金进一步把关注点从“谁在建数据中心/卖芯片”转向“谁能真正把AI变现、做出商业化产品”。
这是典型的AI交易从“基建周期”向“应用与变现”分化的迹象。

4、关于科技板块分化这一点
这里要把上周在168X的访谈里聊到的AI主线迁移的观点再搬出来（见配图），访谈内容在这里https://t.co/l0MotcPBA2。

核心逻辑还是“AI主线迁移，每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，部署越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。”

但大家很容易形成的定式思维是什么？
一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。完全把AI = Semiconductor = Memory划等号，其实并非如此。AI也分上中下游，越往后中游的大云厂，下游的应用、agent会更受益以及各种应用场景。这也是7月份这里https://t.co/68oy5mSQ1z聊AI进入工程化阶段的必然趋势。

半导体有没有机会？跌多了跌出了性价比，那么机会也就出来了。只是说应该没有新的主线那么强势和丝滑。而且现在市场计价的是民主党上台就让数据中心建设减速，如昨天这里https://t.co/2F8dNnVKh6聊到的得州新当选的民主党州长对数据中心的要求上，也并没那么糟糕、而且要到27年1月初新党员的议员和州长才能正式履新。所以需要关注，什么时候市场开始意识到这一点、对半导体认知发生改观。年底前半导体可能会有一波反弹的机会。

author: aaronjmars
quoted_text:
re: token models

whenever I see a new company trying out its own token model, I just realize how futile it is even for them to try because 99% of the time it’s just not going to work. and it’s also extremely hard to underwrite new tokens with standards that are not established, even if the teams themselves are

and it’s not because the teams are stupid or because the teams don’t want good tokens or the teams don’t want the price to go up. it’s just not their domain. tokens are an extremely hard instrument to figure out

every single dollar that a team spends on figuring out how to do their token, every single minute that they spend on figuring out what the right model is, is time and money wasted not on their business but on something that is very superficial in a lot of ways and up until now, teams - unfortunately did have to do that. they mostly didn’t have a choice, and they (almost) always failed.

but today with MetaDAO and the existence of their ICOs and token structures and tokenholder rights and decision market structure, it seems to me like there really isn’t a better way to make your token work for your investors and for the team as well and to really align everyone together properly.

and if, and if you’re a team considering doing a token or who already has a token and are thinking about different structures, just ask yourself this question: do you really want to figure it out yourself and spend all the time and money on figuring out a proper structure when MetaDAO spends millions of dollars a every single year? with countless of launches constantly iterating and trying to nail this one niche, which is tokens? do you think you can do better than them realistically, because I don’t think so.

it’s like, just imagine if Apple was focused on figuring out how to distribute their shares and how to structure their shares instead of spending all their time and effort on bringing the first iPhone to market. who knows what could’ve happened? instead, they put in the time and work into what actually matters, which is their product.

为啥周四美股开盘后大跌了？不是中期大选利好吗？为啥 Bitcoin 也跌了？？

😂我晚上开始码字到现在还没有一个小时就出现大跌了，Bitcoin 都已经跌了超过 6% 了，这种情况下原罪大概率是出在美股身上，果然英伟达、AMD 和数据中心相关股票都在下跌，也就是科技股和 AI 都在下跌。

主要的原因就是民主党获胜，等等，不是说民主党获胜是利好吗？你 TMD 昨天还说是利好，怎么今天就是利空了？好坏坏话怎么都你一个人说的！！

先别打，这个逻辑是这样的。

昨天是因为民主党获得了胜利，控制了国会，尤其是参议院民主党领袖舒默都表示要结束美国和伊朗的战争了，这个利好确实带动了市场的上涨，甚至是 bitcoin:native ，这是没错的。

但就像昨天有小伙伴说的一样，这不是利好吗？为啥科技股在下跌，科技股昨天和今天下跌的原因都是一样的！主要原因就是因为数据中心建设的不确定性增加。

实际上民主党在得州、佐治亚州等数据中心建设较集中的地区取得胜利，部分地方民众此前就反对数据中心扩张，担心用电、用水和电费上涨。投资者担心，未来部分项目可能面临更严格审批或暂停建设。如果数据中心建得慢，芯片、服务器和算力供应商的订单增长也可能受到影响。

说人话，民主党没有那么激进，所以在民主党主要获选的地区可能就为了选票而降低对 AI 数据中心的支持，而且现在本身市场就担心 AI 的扩张带来了资本开支的增加，结果科技股的投资者就开始担心，出现了抛售。

这是第一个主要原因，其次就是油价又开始回升了，主要是市场昨天买入的是情绪，今天卖出的是情绪落地，所以我是在早晨看到油价反弹的时候就直接清空了做空的仓位，如果不算资金费率的是小赚，算了资金费率仍然是亏损的，但我觉得只要伊朗有明确的信号，我就在做空就行了。

上一轮七月就是因为觉得还能跌硬生生的从 80% 的利润变成了超过 100% 的亏损，和头疼的资金费率，所以这次就更果断了。

而在 bitcoin:native 我还是判断错了，虽然我知道 AI 会跌，油价上涨了，但是白天就已经是这样了，但白天 BTC 没啥动静啊，我就觉得 BTC 问题不大，结果到时间就买入抄底了，结果就成这样了，但我觉得现在买入的问题仍然不会很大，我在继续做空油价的时候，BTC 的价格就应该回来了。

但 AI 和半导体，我给小伙伴的建议就是不要着急抄底。

quoted_text:
Chamath on his infamous “below my line” moment: “If you believe it, you should never apologize.”

"I've probably been canceled or attempted to be canceled at least once in a really big way because of the show."

"The whole story was Jason was talking about human rights or something like that. And I essentially said something to the effect of stop virtue signaling because you nor anybody else in America are willing to actually make the substantive changes if you actually thought this was an issue.”

“So you say it's an issue, but your behavior betrays it being an issue. And as far as I'm concerned, it's below my line."

"That's the thing that became a meme, or there's a picture of me talking about the Uyghurs in China specifically. But I said the uncomfortable truth. Cause it's true. And I think it's very dangerous to say things matter when they don't matter.“

"And then the White House put out some comment on the Monday on Martin Luther King day, which I thought, this is crazy. This is intense.“

"I remember a friend of mine texted me and he sent me this study, which was when you look back at all of these moments online when you're in the public firing line, he said, if you believe it, you should never apologize. Never ever apologize, ever."

"I kind of stood my ground. And this is before cancel culture was canceled. So it was in the throes of it. And so I felt it on my skin and I realized this is not a way a sustainable society operates."

"But in hindsight, that's the greatest gift that I've gotten from the pod is that one moment, because it was like all these important things all at once that showed me where we were and where we needed to be."

"It's an enormous gift to know that you cannot be canceled. It allows me to be a little bit closer every day to my truer and truer self, because whenever I get afraid, I can go back to that moment and remember how it felt like, but then remember what the outcome was."

author: vonzz6
quoted_text:
俄罗斯要把币圈交易所的生意，直接抢回自己手里了。

而且这次出手的不是某家互联网公司，而是俄罗斯最大的证券交易所莫斯科交易所（MOEX），以及俄罗斯最大银行联邦储蓄银行（Sberbank）。

12 月 1 日起，莫斯科交易所计划上线 BTC、ETH 和 USDT 交易，由国家清算中心负责清算，交易时间覆盖莫斯科股市交易时段。

这背后有一个值得关注的市场：

俄罗斯用户对海外 CEX 的重要性，远比想象中高。

根据 TradingBeats 10 月数据，俄罗斯是 Bybit、HTX、MEXC 的第一大流量来源，分别占平台全球流量的 23.94%、13.76% 和 10.53%。

相比之下，Binance 仅为 1.54%，Coinbase 和 Kraken 分别只有 0.24% 和 0.16%。

俄罗斯现在想做的，就是把这部分长期流向境外交易所的需求，重新纳入本土金融体系。

但这次开放也有几个有意思的地方：

1. 并非全面放开。 普通投资者需要通过测试，每年通过单一经纪商购买加密货币的额度不超过 30 万卢布（约 3,700 美元），合格投资者不受额度限制。

2. USDT 的出现颇具戏剧性。 莫斯科交易所及其清算中心均受到美国制裁，而 USDT 发行方 Tether 一直执行制裁地址冻结政策。未来如何处理相关资产，仍存在疑问。

3. 本土金融机构开始抢占入口。 Sberbank 已获得加密货币交易资格，计划在自己的银行应用中提供 BTC、ETH、USDT 交易服务。

俄罗斯副财长此前估算，俄罗斯每天加密货币交易额约 500 亿卢布；而 Sberbank 预计首年相关交易规模最高可达 4 万亿卢布。

这件事真正值得关注的，不是俄罗斯又多了一个 BTC 交易市场。

而是一个趋势：当加密货币需求足够庞大，原本试图限制它的传统金融体系，最终可能选择自己下场，把交易、托管和清算全部纳入监管。

对于 Bybit、HTX、MEXC 等长期依赖俄罗斯流量的海外交易所来说，这可能才是真正需要警惕的变化。

text:
聊聊造成今天市场雪崩的《禁止人工超级智能法案》背后的两位激进左翼议员，看看他们过往的激进提案最后都形成民主党内共识么？在美国国会关于人工智能的辩论中，《禁止人工超级智能法案》是少数试图从源头遏制最极端风险的提案之一。它由佛蒙特州独立参议员伯尼·桑德斯和德克萨斯州民主党众议员格雷格·卡萨尔在2026年9月联合提出，主张在联邦层面设立专门机构之前，禁止开发可能超越人类控制的超级智能系统。法案把这类系统大致定义为在多数智力任务上达到或超过人类水平、或具备颠覆政府、拒绝关闭指令能力的技术，并设定了极高的计算量门槛。

桑德斯是美国国会历史上任期最长的独立议员，长期与民主党共同投票。他自称民主社会主义者，政治生涯从伯灵顿市长起步，历经众议员再到参议员，始终把经济不平等、工人权利和大公司权力作为核心议题。

卡萨尔则是正式的民主党人，2024年底当选国会进步党团主席，是该党团近年来最年轻的领导人之一。他出身奥斯汀劳工组织者，进入国会后把重点放在生活成本、公用事业垄断和科技对就业的冲击上，风格比传统文化议题更偏向经济民粹。

两人在党内都站在左翼，但路径不同。桑德斯几十年来反复推动的核心提案包括全民医保（Medicare for All）、绿色新政、大幅提高最低工资、免费公立大学和财富税。这些主张在2016年和2020年总统初选中获得了大量基层支持，也迫使其他候选人不得不回应。

卡萨尔近年的重点则包括“新可负担性议程”、对大型人工智能公司征税以资助失业者再就业、以及禁止用算法和数据对个人进行差异化定价。他与桑德斯联手推出超级智能禁令，正是把这种经济与监管逻辑延伸到技术前沿。

这些提案最终有没有变成民主党共识？答案是否定的。
1）全民医保至今仍未获得民主党党团多数支持；
2）完整版绿色新政也未成为党纲。
桑德斯自己在2025年公开承认，全民医保在党内仍缺乏足够票数。
卡萨尔推动的人工智能税和超级智能禁令同样只得到进步派议员的联署，主流民主党人更倾向监管、透明度要求和数据中心环境影响评估，而不是全面禁止。

而民主党内中间派和温和派仍然担心过度限制会削弱美国在技术竞争中的位置，也顾忌科技行业的政治捐款。

进步派确实改变了民主党的讨论边界。更高的最低工资、气候投资、学生债务减免和药价谈判等议题，在过去十年里从边缘变成了党内多数可接受的政策。但最激进的版本——永久禁令、单一支付者彻底取代私人保险、或对特定技术实施核武级管制——始终停留在左翼议程。

民主党属于大帐篷政党，进步党团人数虽多，却需要与更中间的议员协商才能推进立法。

总的来说，《禁止人工超级智能法案》目前仍是进步派的旗帜性提案，而非全党统一立场。它能否在民主党掌握国会后获得实质性进展，取决于党内左翼与中间派的力量对比，特别是民主党内中间派和温和派的态度。。

所以前面说这项法案应该成不了民主党内共识。

个人觉得今天被大面积传播其实有点刻意了。

text:
Hey @swivaljaw , co-founder of @gondixyz here 👋 It's a fair concern, and I'd rather talk about it openly.

You're right that leverage doesn't just disappear. What changes is how it unwinds. Gondi loans can't be called early, and each one has a fixed maturity, with those dates spread across weeks and months. So the leverage gets flushed gradually, loan by loan, instead of a price dip setting off a wave of calls and dumping hundreds of NFTs at once.

Punks are the best example: hundreds of loans on Gondi and no cascade liquidations in years.

What fixed terms do is let everyone see the risk ahead of time, and the floor doesn't pay for it all on one bad day.

Have a good one and let me know if you have any questions 🫡

author: garrytan
quoted_text:
Most people do not realize just how easy the AP exams have gotten. They are not college level.

Why/how have they become so easy? What's going on? 

This might shock you... A brutal new piece in Education Next just dropped, saying the decline in rigor of the AP in the last two decades is, in large part, because the content has been GUTTED. For example:

— AP Biology cut 40% of its material
— Required lines from the Aeneid in AP Latin halved
— Spanish Lit reading list cut from 56 works to 38

Then the questions themselves have become absurdly easier. Readability measures show English passages have fallen multiple grade levels, and some now include footnotes defining basic words...

A 2025 AP English prompt included footnote definitions for words like "optimism" and "pessimism."

At the same time, scoring was recalibrated so that more students pass: guessing penalties disappeared, rubrics grew more generous, readers were told to give students the benefit of the doubt, etc. — "no one at College Board had any incentive to maintain rigor."

College professors are now seeing students arrive with AP credit who lack basic content knowledge and writing ability. The College Board insists the exams have not become easier, but everybody familiar with them knows they've become an absolute joke.

Advanced Placement is no longer advanced. This is not college level.

It must be replaced.

text: The market won’t go up until leopold disappears for good
author: dgt10011
quoted_text:
My two cents on "Situational Awareness"-

I'm sure Leopold was a smart fellow. I'm optimistic he will find something worthwhile to do to contribute towards society. And while I see a lot of grave dancing, he is yet a young man who deserves second chances. However, there is one thing I will stand by with stubborn conviction and you can hold me to: and that is my belief that he should never manage institutional client capital ever again.

Listen to the below exchange, and watch his demeanor as Dwarkesh asks about how to avoid blowing up as so many hedge funds get either the the timing wrong, or approach with too much theory mindset. After a series of  hurried affirmations, he starts by responding: 

"Yeah, I mean look obviously, you can't ... you know, not blowing up is sort of like task number one and two, or whatever"

For any trained stewards of client capital, this is the ONLY phrase you need to have heard to realize everything you need to know from this two hour interview. You don't need to know his IQ, his pedigree, his experience. You know the only thing that matters. He doesn't care about the golden rule of money management.

He is going to blow up.

As an RIA with fiduciary duty and standard of care, not blowing is, in fact, task number one. It is the only task. There is no other task, and it is definitely not a "whatever." There simply remains no ambiguity in the human mind as to what the job is.

Now, listen to his answer one more time. There is something else here you probably missed the first time. He starts by saying "Yeah I mean look obviously you cant..." and then stops and pivots. Take a moment to think about what you think he was going to finish this sentence with if he didn't just realize that he probably should not finish that thought? Finish his sentence, I dare you. And now you know why it was obvious that he was going to blow up.

One more thing- I debated whether I wanted to post this or not. It's always really painful for me as a PM to watch others blow up in the industry, because I know how much client capital has been damaged (and other collateral damages in the service providers). However, recently there has been a trend of internet personalities who celebrate these kinds of misadventures by justifying risk taking. 

We must stop celebrating this culture of charlatans. There are so many public figures that I see online, who simply have no business of managing client capital, vying for attention where they play the very same game. In fact, the people who often come out defending Leopold are more likely that charlatan than not. Because anyone who understands the solemn gravity and incredible privilege of managing client capital knows that what Leopold just said in this video is so horrific to the professional investment management industry. Allocators must be more mindful of who they choose to build trust with. The best allocators know that belief and trust are not the same asset.

So good luck Leopold! I genuinely believe you are a smart, capable, and well-intentioned person-and excited to see what you will do next. We've never lived in a more exciting period in society to affect incredible change and contribution. Refocusing your energy towards what you are actually really good at and deeply care about, is the highest form of effective altruism you can do for others. In fact, it's probably the highest form of situational awareness there is.

text:
Genesis spent three years as an experiment before anyone could collect it.

Written by Daniel Calderon Arenas (@DaCaldera) in 2017, the project helped test the idea behind Art Blocks: an artist writes a system, and each mint produces a unique work from its rules. When the platform launched on November 27, 2020, Genesis was ready for its first collectors.

Its visual language is simple: grids, gradients, lines, shapes, and color. The variety comes from how those elements meet. Across 512 works, collectors could discover different sides of the same system, finding compositions that spoke to them.

DCA later recalled how quickly it all happened. After years in “cold storage,” the project went from release to collected in a matter of hours.

That history is part of what draws us to Genesis #40. It carries an idea developed in 2017, realized in 2020, and kept alive by the people who continue to collect it. We’re happy to be part of that story.

Today, we released the National Policy for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening to protect American biotechnology innovation while reducing the risk of misuse. 

This policy establishes a new, government-wide screening requirements for synthetic DNA and the equipment used to make it. It will ensure companies selling nucleic acid sequences and synthesis equipment know their customers and prevent the malicious use of these materials and tools.

This policy strengthens our Nation’s biosecurity posture by establishing rigorous U.S. government-wide procurement screening and physical security standards for synthetic biology. It replaces outdated “self-attestation” systems with robust, independent verification. It creates a dynamic, SI-powered screening layer that assesses the biological risk from nucleic acid sequences, allowing the U.S. to anticipate and prevent malicious use and help stop dangerous gain-of-function research. 

@NIST will issue rigorous new screening standards and @HHSGov and @USDA will certify synthetic biology providers. Together, these measures will strengthen American biosecurity, safeguard responsible innovation, and establish a global standard for safe and transparent synthetic biology tools and research.

Every trust mechanism in software comes down to one question. Who made the record.

A log is made by the system, afterwards, and it says what the system decided to write. An audit is made by a person, later, out of those logs. A proof is made by the computation, while it runs.

Nobody writes it. Nobody can edit it. That is the whole difference.

quoted_text:
Pickle's always right,  But this time you'd better watch your ASS
《连载系列：1 历史回响，盘面锐评》

上周全球金融市场度过了黑色星期四星期五，有很多维度要分析，第一篇先说大家最关注的：盘面走势
历史不会重演，但往往押韵，下面就跟着我的回顾一起享受这次十年难遇的盛宴吧，先说结论
😱还没到底😱

🕐美股回顾-卷土重来
2015 2018 2020 2022
其中2018和2020着重说一下

🔥2015，该涨不涨就要跌，顶部受阻的案例。
大盘在2000点的位置停滞，上涨动能不足，出现了两次下跌。幅度12%左右。
和本次下跌的相似点在于下跌之前都出现了一段时间的停滞。那么第一波跌幅可以看作是盘面为了修正的自然下跌。
但和本次也有差异之处。第一点是2015下跌之前，顶部盘旋时间更久，有将近半年多，第二点是幅度是比较温柔的，没有打破结构。

🔥2022，熊市案例。当年市场转熊了，btc也迎来寒冬，大盘最低给了27%的回调。

🔥2018，衰退交易例子，尖底。
18年底美股计价衰退交易，其实盘面前端也出现了停滞的现象，之后给到了20%的最大跌幅。这次的特点是下跌之中一步三回头，前2/3时间是上上下下的震荡，最后1/3时间直接来了一段大的跌15%。
衰退交易计价完成后涨得会非常快，这和本次行情8月5号的走法很像，当时boj加息再加上衰退交易担忧，也是猛烈下插，但是后期收复很快。

🔥🔥🔥2020，来自远古的恐惧，命运齿轮的转折点：312

为什么说2020的情况和现在是最像的，
首先当时新冠疫情的冲击和目前关税的冲击强度相似，这种带有外部冲击的市场在盘面上有自己的特色，就是会有更加明显的情绪行情
其次两次的大盘走势比较一致，第一波下跌后有短暂的企稳，短暂企稳后接了更强势的下跌，演变到后面就成了恐慌市场，情绪能到多少就到多少
最后一点就是跌幅和市场阶段。近十年内，美股有三次超过20%的下跌，分别是18 20和22。其中只有2020年的外部因素冲击导致了没有像样的回调，18年和22年大家都可以去拉一下，每次回调幅度都是比较可观的，可能将近10%。目前市场迅疾猛烈的下跌，并且跌幅已经有17%（18年整个趋势跌幅都只有20%）非常像312的行情
其次，312之后的收复是美联储归零降息，和现在市场预计的政策底一模一样，都在于美联储的降息

🕐比特币-大世面将至
之前和bane老师聊天的时候，他说这一轮大家好奇怪，6、7%的跌幅就叫闹麻了，之前比特币都是20%起步。20%可能要来了

最近关税冲击非常猛，有点接近2020年疫情期间，目前下跌速度位于2020年疫情和2022年加息之间。如果市场持续的话比特币很难独善其身，肯定会被流动性套现（其他市场濒临爆仓的资金套现一切可能套现的资产补充流动性导致市场普跌）

当年2020年3月份美股已经出现4%以上大跌的时候比特币还比较稳略微上涨诱多，后来全球市场进一步下跌比特币开始猛跌最后一天跌了60%，link直接从3美元跌到0.1
请大家看下方配图，第一个红圈是美股当时刚开始大跌比特币还比较坚挺阶段，第二个红圈是比特币开始疯狂补跌
所以我这里为什么怼 @0xPickleCati @BAYC2043 等大佬的观点，因为btc现在挺住了不代表就要开始上涨趋势（第二原因我是反骨仔嘴臭交易员所以就得锐评呢宝宝😘）

大家可以看到，美股目前强势资产还没有被流动性套现，比如说伯克希尔哈撒韦和沃尔玛。如果大盘和高贝塔股票持续下跌的话，投资机构将不得不面临margin，甚至包括一些只投大盘的机构，因为他们会开杠杆。而且指数ETF为了精准追踪大盘，会不断调整持仓，这就导致在某一些股票大幅下跌的时候，会导致ETF全盘抛售，所谓ETF杠杆效应，这会进一步演化成市场普跌。最后一点，btc目前步入主流资产，甚至有不少的公司和ETF资金持有，当这些holder出现流动性套现需求的时候，配合上散户情绪，跌幅没有办法估计。

🕐山寨辣评-气候不齐
大多数山寨币目前来到了清算阶段，有一些直接奔着归零的方向去，有一些庄家盐都不盐了，管他三七二十一的护盘拉盘。

1, 有不少朋友抱怨现在没什么玩的了，个人认为山寨币现在的玩法只有跟英毛集团混，如果你认识一个币的项目方发行团队，那可以尝试一下，其余的话不太认为现在是合适的出手时机。

2, 二级的那些垃圾山寨币，重新重视起来，不要有偏见。312的时候很多山寨币直接百分之八九十的腰斩，但后面涨上来的幅度是非常恐怖的。
狗狗币当天跌了26%，最低大概0.001，从前面的0.005高点跌下来80%，前面的底部0.002样子，跌下来50%，注意啊，很多人当时认为0.002就是底了，直接抄进去，后面又给了50%跌幅。但是这种时候真是大机会，我们交易员讲一个系统，意思是你的交易体系要不断长期的复利，但是，这种做法其实是认为自己可以打败市场，虽然有不少的交易大佬做到了，可是，当市场给出了机会，一个共同成长的机会，就像巴菲特和美国国运共同成长一样，这种我还是不会放弃的。

结语：这篇帖子纯粹从盘面角度看，之后会从宏观经济面讲一下关税，衰退和通胀等一系列的话题。感谢读到这里，欢迎转发锐评。

author: matthuang
quoted_text:
Today, Zipline raised $1.5b at a $21.5b valuation.  

When we started Zipline, flying autonomously in the US was illegal. Which made it really hard to convince investors to give us money! But we were too naive to think that meant we shouldn’t try.

We started the company on a cow farm. We worked out of run-down construction trailers so that we could keep engineering, manufacturing, and flight test all unified and in one place. Hiring people from normal companies like Google was hard because we didn’t have a cafe or laundry service. But enough risk takers and rebels wanted to go on an insane adventure with us. They became the early team.

We decided to launch in smaller countries and focus on life-saving use cases. We hired incredible entrepreneurs and operators in Rwanda, Ghana, Cote D’Ivoire, and other countries. For eight years, Zipline expanded our service across Africa, serving thousands of hospitals and health facilities and reducing maternal mortality by 51%. Today, the network saves over 14k lives every year and is cash flow positive. 

Last year, Zipline launched at scale in the US and the service exploded. We grew flight volumes about 100x over the last 18 months, and now make more than a million deliveries a year per metro. We’re now expanding with our partners to millions of deliveries per day. Normal families love having access to anything they need in 10-20 minutes, no matter where they live. Spend more time with loved ones and less time worrying about errands. 

Zipline builds drone delivery that is silent and safe. No one wants to hear an extremely loud “swarm of bees” delivering to their backyard or their neighbor’s. Automated delivery needs to be insanely quiet, which guided the overall architecture of our technology delivering from 330 ft in the air. We are 6 times quieter than the closest competitor during delivery. Zipline also now has over 150m commercial autonomous miles (10x the rest of the industry combined) and no safety incidents. Neighborhoods should demand silent and safe delivery!

Today, Zipline is announcing two things. First, we just signed the largest autonomous vehicle contract in human history to expand automated delivery nationally with Walmart, our first and biggest partner in the US. We’re starting by scaling to 300 supercenters throughout the country. Second, we’ve raised $1.5b at a $21.5b valuation from existing and new investors, led by Paradigm, WCM, and Layer. 

Zipline was a hard company to believe in for the first ten years of our history. Investors didn’t think the company was “investable”. Most people didn’t even think Zipline was an economic venture. Thanks to those who have rooted for us along the way. To all of the tens of millions of customers and families who rely on Zipline day in and day out: thank you for helping us build the future. Zipline has grown more than @ryanzip, @keenanwyrobek, I, and all others at the company could have imagined. 

There is a big opportunity to build a new layer of infrastructure for humanity over the coming years. We want to approximate teleportation. We can build a logistics network that connects and serves all people on earth. We can free human flourishing from the choking constraint of traffic and roads. There are no roads where we’re going.  🚀🌎

It’s called Auto Ontology, and it tackles a problem that better SQL alone won’t fix.

An agent can query the right database and still return the wrong answer.

Why?

Because “revenue” might mean something different in every system.

Auto Ontology is a Python framework that builds shared context over enterprise metadata:

→ Entities and business metrics
→ Relationships between data
→ Certified definitions and lineage
→ Provenance behind answers

It can generate ontologies from metadata, connect existing semantic models, and reconcile conflicting definitions.

For structured data, it also supports natural-language-to-SQL with validation against the ontology.

Agents can access that context through MCP, CLI, or API.

The useful shift: giving agents access to business meaning alongside the data.

Open source under Apache 2.0.

text:
On today's stock market crash:

As an investor, on days like today, you have to ask yourself one question: What fundamentally changed over the last 24 hours?

The shift in the fundamental backdrop cannot be attributed solely to the Midterm Election results; markets had already largely priced in the outcome.

So, what changed between yesterday and today? What is the fundamental reason for today's decline?

One of the most likely catalysts is growing concern about a potential "ban" on AI, or at the very least, severe regulation of the industry.

Over the last 24 hours, Democratic lawmakers have publicly called for restrictions on advanced AI development, including an outright "ban on artificial superintelligence."

Frankly, an outright ban will not happen.

Such a ban, if even possible to enforce, would effectively mean the US surrendering its position in the global AI race to China.

Does this mean AI is "over" or today's stock market crash marks "the end?" Absolutely not.

Rather, we believe we are witnessing a sudden shift in sentiment colliding with excessive levels of leverage, potentially triggering forced liquidations by several major institutional investors.

Therefore, today's downturn is more technical than fundamental. This is not to discount the concerns around regulation, they are legitimate. But price action right now does not look orderly or rational.

We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in human history.

Zoom out and remain calm.

text:
Why is the market selling off so aggressively today?

I think we're seeing a much bigger deleveraging event across AI and semiconductor stocks, with hedge funds cutting exposure to some of the most crowded trades in the market. After a difficult October, hedge funds appear increasingly cautious about maintaining large positions in AI stocks, especially with growing concerns surrounding the data center buildout, elevated valuations, and the sustainability of AI spending. And when you have so much institutional money concentrated in the same companies, even a relatively small reduction in exposure can create significant selling pressure.

We're also seeing concerns about what happens if data center construction slows down following the Democrats' midterm victories. Tighter regulations, permitting restrictions, and opposition from local communities could delay new projects, potentially affecting demand growth for GPUs, memory, networking equipment, and other AI infrastructure components. Add higher financing costs and questions about whether hyperscalers will generate sufficient returns on their investments, and investors have plenty of reasons to reduce risk.

But I think the bigger issue right now is deleveraging rather than a fundamental collapse in AI demand. Hedge funds aren't necessarily selling because they believe the AI investment cycle is over. Many may simply be reducing leverage, taking profits, and protecting capital after a volatile month. And when multiple funds start doing this simultaneously, falling prices can trigger even more selling, creating a cycle that pushes stocks lower regardless of whether the underlying businesses have changed.

And this is where I think the next few weeks become particularly important. We need hedge funds to come back into the AI trade if we want to see a sustained recovery. After October's volatility, I highly doubt institutional investors will rush back into these positions without seeing some stability first. That means retail investors could play an important role throughout November. If they continue buying the dips and help absorb the selling pressure, it could give hedge funds the confidence to gradually rebuild their exposure. If that happens, late November and December could become particularly interesting for AI stocks.

And despite all the concerns, I still think the underlying AI investment thesis remains intact. Hyperscalers are continuing to expand their infrastructure, existing data centers still need upgrades, and demand for computing capacity hasn't suddenly disappeared. Even if new construction slows down, that doesn't mean the entire investment cycle is coming to an end. For now, I think the biggest thing to watch is whether selling pressure begins to fade and hedge funds start rebuilding their positions. Because until institutional money returns in a meaningful way, it's going to be difficult for AI stocks to establish a sustained recovery.

author: 0xZergs
quoted_text:
USDai provides GPU-backed loans to companies, denominated in $USDai. The protocol recently executed a $1 million buyback of its governance token, $CHIP, and introduced programmatic buybacks from revenue.

To better understand what the team is targeting and how they see the category evolving in a few years, we interviewed @0xZergs, the CEO and Co-Founder of @USDai_Official.

The USDai model depends on borrowing demand, as it's a lending protocol, and that demand is constantly evolving. The demand sits in the “compute middle market”, and “power is the binding constraint, so deployments are getting smaller: 250-megawatt sites are becoming 2- to 5-megawatt modular builds. That means more borrowers needing $5M to $100M, not a few needing billions.”

While the demand is there, what makes USDai special and separates them from traditional lenders is that they can do small deals economically.

This is exactly what onchain capital unlocks: USDai can “fund a standard loan quickly, hold it while it builds a payment history, and then sell it to the institutions that wouldn’t underwrite it from scratch”.

USDai calls this model “season-and-sell”, and they do this because crypto users “prioritise liquidity above all else, while credit funds are less duration-sensitive”. The team has completed their first season-and-sell: a $106 million GPU financing sold to Silver Point and Victory Park.

Through this model, USDai doesn’t really compete with traditional capital; instead, it “delivers finished loans”.

“Onchain is the warehouse. Banks, private credit funds and insurers are the permanent home.”

One of USDai's major announcements is its focus on token alignment, but we asked the team why they felt this is the right moment to introduce programmatic buybacks. They added, “Now is the moment because we’ve proven the loop. We originated a loan, seasoned it and sold it. That turns the protocol from a balance sheet into a volume/origination engine.”

Additionally, “as the protocol scales, the source of purchases shifts. Today it is sUSDai’s net interest margin. As USDai outstanding grows, CHIP holders can switch on revenue from USDai itself for the stablecoin as settlement, which is the North Star of our protocol”

We ended our questions by asking what USDai looks like in its final form, and they added that it will be “the settlement dollar for compute”.

If USDai finance the next 10k neoclouds, “they all end up holding the same dollar, and they will transact in it.”
