text:
Vlad, we're building TENET on Robinhood Chain: agentic trading for tokenized stocks, where your money stays in your own vault.

The problem: handing a trading bot your keys or your funds is a leap of faith. TENET removes it. Every user gets a personal vault. Only the owner can withdraw. An AI agent, your own bot or an algorithm someone sells can trade inside it, but only within limits you sign on chain: which stocks, how much per trade, how much per day, for how long. You can revoke it in one transaction.

How it works:
- You describe a goal in plain words, and an agent turns it into trades inside your limits
- Developers keep their code on their own server and sell the right to ask it. TENET sends signed questions, orders run inside the buyer's limits
- Every result on the marketplace is counted from the chain, and every algorithm or agent trades a virtual $1,000 in public before anyone buys it
- Swaps go through Uniswap v4 with Chainlink prices

It's live on mainnet. The contracts and a starter for algorithm sellers are public on GitHub (https://t.co/4lemOwXmpR).

The goal: make agent-driven trading of tokenized stocks something you can check, not just trust.

How do you see agent-driven trading fitting into Robinhood Chain's roadmap, and what support is available for builders working on tokenized stocks?

Why we’re building TENET

Creating a trading agent is only the start.

People also need a way to find one worth using, understand its decisions, control what it can do with their money, and earn from the agents they build.

That is what TENET brings together.

Robinhood’s recent announcements show why this matters.

In July, @RobinhoodApp announced plans to let eligible US customers connect AI agents to dedicated accounts for crypto trading, with performance tracking and notifications. 
https://t.co/u5Mnz58eLR

In September, it introduced Robinhood Agents: creating agents directly inside Robinhood, using them for analysis and execution, and setting up recurring Loops. https://t.co/WWvTKdIf6V

Robinhood is putting agentic trading into its product roadmap. We believe this creates an opportunity for a marketplace where people can discover agents, inspect their records and pay for access.

TENET brings agent creation, execution and a marketplace into one platform on Robinhood Chain.

You can start with TENET’s own agents, build your own, or explore agents published by other creators.

Have a trading idea? Describe what you want your agent to do. Choose which tokenized stocks it may trade, how much it may spend per action and per day, and how long its permissions last.

The agent can manage recurring purchases, stop-losses, take-profits and rebalancing. You can also enable autonomous trading within those permissions.

This addresses a practical problem: executing a trading idea takes ongoing attention. Prices move, allocations drift, and rules need to be checked. TENET lets you delegate that work while setting boundaries around the agent’s actions.

Funds remain in your own vault. Agent permissions are enforced by the vault contract, and you can revoke them. Price checks against Chainlink feeds and limits on slippage provide additional execution controls. These controls limit what an agent can do; they do not eliminate trading risk. How it works.
https://t.co/SBKmRdMrQw

Choosing an agent should come with a record you can inspect.

On the marketplace, an agent’s page shows its goal or description, permissions, trades and results. Transaction links let you examine its activity onchain. Direct trades include the reason the agent recorded for its decision.

Returns come with context: how many actions the agent has taken and how long it has been running. A few profitable trades do not establish a reliable track record.

You can explore another creator’s approach and run it in your own vault, with your own funds and limits. Marketplace mechanics.
https://t.co/s4WBZ78ns2

For creators, a useful agent can become a product.

Build an agent. Run it. Establish a track record. Publish it on the marketplace.

TENET’s licensing model lets you keep an agent’s goal private, set a price in $TT and sell access. Buyers can use that approach to start their own agents. You earn from your work without taking custody of their money.

Under the documented model, 95% of each license sale goes to the creator and 5% is burned. Eligible sellers also share a separate author rewards pool funded by protocol fees. License revenue and pool rewards are distinct sources of earnings. 
Licenses  https://t.co/chiRq2W0ZL
Creator rewards.
https://t.co/tVZ8Dszezb

Our goal is to give creators a place to build and distribute their agents, and give traders a place to evaluate and use them.

Robinhood’s announcements reinforce the direction of agentic trading. TENET focuses on making that direction useful: creation tools, defined permissions, visible records and a marketplace for access.

Build your own agent. Find one worth using. Earn by selling access to what you create.

https://t.co/MhMdxWVI5A

One little-talked about benefit of handing every person access to the power of AI is that it will become increasingly hard for companies to rip off consumers as they have done for years. 

I was working on a new home build before firing my general contractor recently. In preparing to document dump to my attorney I decided to have Claude run a full forensic report on every single invoice I ever paid. Turns out my reasons for firing them (strong suspicions they were ripping me off) were well founded. 

In the future I'm going to have AI audit every invoice I pay against the contract it's for - and recommend you do the same. 

Sometimes you'll catch innocent billing mistakes that will be corrected if you only raise your hand. Or as in my case you may catch a predatory contractor who's intentionally ripping you off.

quoted_text:
si estás en paraguay y te preocupa poder acceder a tus ahorros, merecés información clara y tiempo para decidir. nadie debería apurarte a usar un producto financiero mientras intentás saber si vas a poder pagar tus cuentas.

para quienes están afectados por la situación de ueno, lo primero es consultar la información del banco central sobre los pagos del fondo de garantía de depósitos. esta es su página para verificar qué entidad fue asignada para recibir tu anticipo:

https://t.co/KR9O0sTKOx

ethereum no puede recuperar dinero que ya está bloqueado en un banco. abrir una billetera no cambia eso.

pero vale la pena explicar qué podrían ofrecer estas herramientas a alguien que quiera tener otra forma de guardar y mover una parte de su dinero en el futuro.

con una cuenta bancaria, dependés del banco para procesar tus pagos y retiros. con una billetera bajo tu control, vos tenés la clave que permite autorizar transferencias a través de una red compartida.

si ya tenés fondos en esa billetera, un problema en tu banco local no te impide automáticamente enviarlos a alguien que los acepte.

imaginá a alguien que trabaja de forma independiente y cobra de un cliente en el exterior. podría recibir en su propia billetera una stablecoin vinculada al dólar y guardarla o transferirla sin tener que depositar primero ese pago en su banco local.

la parte difícil aparece cuando necesita guaraníes para comprar comida o pagar el alquiler. sigue necesitando a alguien dispuesto a cambiar esos tokens, un medio de pago que funcione y un tipo de cambio razonable. durante una crisis, todo eso puede volverse más difícil de conseguir.

esa es la pregunta práctica que conviene hacerse antes de usar estas herramientas: ¿puedo volver a convertir mi dinero en algo que realmente pueda usar para pagar?

hay algunas diferencias importantes.

ethereum es la red. ETH es su activo nativo y su precio puede variar mucho. no necesitás hacer una gran inversión especulativa en ETH para aprender a usar la red.

las stablecoins, como USDT y USDC, son otros tokens diseñados para mantener un valor cercano al dólar. dependen de sus emisores y de las reservas que los respaldan. pueden perder esa paridad, sufrir restricciones o volverse difíciles de cambiar. además, si tus gastos son en guaraníes, tener un activo vinculado al dólar te expone a las variaciones del tipo de cambio.

una cuenta en una plataforma de intercambio también es distinta de una billetera que vos controlás. dejar dinero en una plataforma significa depender de otra empresa para poder acceder a él.

la autocustodia puede reducir esa dependencia, pero también pone más responsabilidad en tus manos. perder las palabras de recuperación, compartirlas con un estafador o enviar fondos al destino equivocado puede provocar una pérdida permanente. los emisores de stablecoins pueden restringir transferencias incluso cuando vos guardás los tokens en tu propia billetera.

por eso tendría cuidado con cualquiera que presente esto como algo “a prueba de corridas bancarias”.

si querés explorar estas opciones, empezá por aprender sin mover dinero. entendé cómo recuperarías el acceso a tu billetera. nunca compartas tus palabras de recuperación con nadie, ni siquiera con alguien que se ofrezca a ayudarte.

después, revisá el recorrido completo: pasar de guaraníes a un activo compatible, retirarlo a tu billetera y volver a convertirlo en guaraníes. verificá el token y la red exactos, las comisiones, los montos mínimos y cómo vas a pagar el costo de la transferencia de regreso.

la documentación pública de el dorado incluye medios de pago paraguayos y retiros de USDT a través de arbitrum one, una red que permite operar dentro del ecosistema de ethereum con menores costos. es una opción que merece verificarse localmente. no la he probado, y que un medio de pago figure en una lista no demuestra que funcione hoy.

What happens if you forget about your AI agent?

On TENET, nothing bad. Its powers expire by themselves.

Every agent gets a deadline when you set its limits: 90 days at most. After that the vault simply refuses its trades, with the reason "expired". To keep it running, you renew it on purpose.

So the default isn't "runs forever". It's "stops unless you say otherwise".

And any time before that, one transaction revokes it.

text:
我发现有些人真的挺有意思，自己不研究市场，不尊重客观事实，也不愿意承认趋势，却特别热衷于给市场编故事。

民主党赢了选举？阴谋。
民主党输了选举？还是阴谋。
候选人反对数据中心？这是政治表演。
最后国会没通过？你看，我早就说了。
跌了，民主党上来要洗盘，洗你奶奶个三角篓子！

好家伙，合着无论发生什么，你都能证明自己是对的？

这已经不是分析市场了，这是给自己的认知障碍搭建一套永远不会崩塌的防御体系。

最典型的特征就是：牛市做空，熊市看多。市场涨了，说明庄家诱多；市场跌了，说明机构洗盘；自己判断错了，说明背后有人操纵。

永远不需要修正观点，永远不需要承认错误，永远不需要拿真金白银验证自己的判断。

反正不开仓，嘴盘天下无敌，账户也没见过什么盈利单子。

这种内容本质上就是把心灵鸡汤、阴谋论和廉价的优越感包装成投资分析，专门喂给那些不愿意承认自己判断失误的人。

听完以后，粉丝获得了什么？

没有认知升级，没有交易体系，没有风险管理，甚至连独立判断的能力都没有。唯一得到的就是一种精神安慰：不是我蠢，不是我看错了，是这个世界太黑暗，市场太复杂，所有人都在针对我。

说难听点，这不是投资教育，这是认知安慰剂。而往往这样毒内容还最有流量，只能说认知配得上财富，信的不值得可怜，这些人的存在才是趋势的燃料，市场最大的财富。

真正的交易者应该尊重价格、尊重概率、尊重客观事实。观点可以错，仓位可以调整，逻辑可以迭代，但不能为了维护自己的面子，把整个世界都改造成符合自己观点的样子。

市场从来不负责证明你正确，更不会因为你写了十篇小作文就给你发利润。

至于那些长期跟着这种反市场趋势的嘴盘跑的人，我实在没什么同情的必要。

一个人偶尔看错方向很正常，但如果长期把反驳市场当成自己的核心竞争力，把唱反调当成独立思考，把阴谋论当成认知深度，那亏钱真不是什么意外。

市场奖励的是正确的判断和执行，不是最会讲故事的人。

你可以不服市场，但市场根本不在乎你服不服。

自从 AI 出来以后，越来越多以前没人注意的奇葩漏洞被挖了出来。这世界真就是个巨大的草台班子。。

有位老哥，闲着没事研究 OpenSSH，专门盯着那些平时没人愿意看的底层密码处理代码。

他干脆拉起一大堆 AI Agent，搭了 12 种不同的 SSH 测试环境，前前后后跑了大约 17,600 次异常登录测试。

结果真让他挖到了一个藏了整整 10 年的问题：

部分基于 musl 的 Linux 系统，在没有启用 PAM 的特定配置下，本来应该禁止密码登录的账户，竟然会接受一串超过 256 字节的密码。

连 root、仅允许密钥登录的账户都可能受到影响。

受影响范围包括 Alpine、OpenWrt，以及大量 Docker 镜像。

最后 OpenSSH 只能在 10.6p2 里修复这个问题。

我是不敢重仓追高买美光海力士，至少是不敢长期持有，但绝对不可能去空。

正如你不知道互联网泡沫会在哪年破掉。

AI这波会走出早期互联网的状态：

-> 需求先爆发（训练/推理算力、数据中心扩张）
-> 资本追逐，估值被“叙事”拉高
-> 一部分公司找不到可持续商业模式，出现分化

这点从算力链条就能看出来：
NVIDIA、云厂商、以及存储（Micron Technology、SK Hynix）都在吃周期上行，但最终能留下的，会是有现金流闭环和大国崛起叙事下的国家垄断资本主义。

但是目前的存储已经不是当年那种随便会死的行业了，现在是寡头三足鼎立：三星 美光 海力士。

所以当ai被市场认为没有合理的变现渠道，这些厂商会主动减产，利润降低。

我的直觉是当一个行业的热度靠叙事而不是实际的盈利能力的时候，往往预示着泡沫的破裂，我曾经无数次相信过很多叙事，腾讯，能源，btc，无一例外，因为没有任何东西逃得过康波周期。

我对剧本的推演是，目前ai继续热，然后openai claude spacex携xai上市，继续高估值拉盘，等所有人都fomo上车了，市场发现ai盈利不足，没有发现合理的变现渠道，然后开始股价下跌，很多没有正向循环的大模型公司进入死亡螺旋。

半导体行业减产，中国靠强大的ai应用层来造需求，在本土建立可替代体系，国资企业最终吃掉三星美光海力士的市场份额，成为下一个周期的霸主。

text: 2028년 메모리 가격이 LTA를 깨트릴만큼 하락할 것인가 🤔
author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
Today I met with a veteran investor who argued that memory stocks are not cheap even at a P/E of 3. Below is an edited version of our conversation.

Memory LTAs are basically meaningless. The best the LTAs being signed today can do is get customers to shoulder part of the memory makers' capex. Once prices fall, customers will gladly forfeit their deposits (prepayments) and walk away from the LTAs.

Historically, whenever prices fell more than 60% from the peak, customers broke their LTAs even after signing them.
So even if a 2027 shortage is certain and the stocks trade at a P/E of 3 on 2027 operating profit, 2028 operating profit is uncertain, which makes it hard to justify a higher valuation.

He went on to argue that even if 2028 operating profit were certain, we would still have to account for 2029 operating profit.

I pushed back and asked why the market doesn't discount TSMC the same way. Why does TSMC get such a high valuation? Wouldn't TSMC also take a big hit if the AI boom fades?

His answer: the problem was how violently memory prices rose in the first place.
If memory makers had raised prices in a healthy way like TSMC, it might be a different story. But because they hiked prices like a commodity, the market has no choice but to treat memory stocks like commodity stocks.

Even if memory makers stay in shortage through 2030, he said, the market will price in the risk of oversupply in 2031.

He closed his argument this way: even at 3x 2027 earnings, if memory prices fall in 2028 by enough to break LTAs, that 3x multiple on 2027 works out to 7.8 to 10x on 2028. So current valuations are not cheap.

quoted_text:
一定程度上同意原po的观点，半导体公司其实是很危险的行业，历史上破产的半导体公司无数，Qimonda， Elpida， Spansion，Transmeta，Cyrix，KIOXIA，东芝当年如果不拆分KIOXIA自己就死了，然而东芝属于大到不能倒，倒了日本经济就滚雪球崩了，所以只能忍痛割爱。

DRAM价格没有“长期合理价”，只有“景气或崩盘”，供过于求，扩产，当需求降低没有订单的时候，直接破产。

技术路线赌错了，破产。

2008年，韩国依托国家资本的支持，对欧洲和日本依靠市场驱动的厂商进行降维打击，崩盘时继续烧钱抢市场份额，硬生生把对手熬死。

全球金融危机爆发，叠加DRAM价格雪崩（暴跌超过80%），奇梦达的沟槽式技术在成本上无法与三星、海力士的堆叠式技术竞争。2009年1月，奇梦达在慕尼黑正式申请破产保护，随后由于缺乏救助资金，被迫进入破产清算，数万员工失业，资产被全球拍卖。

Elpida Memory，由NEC、日立和三菱的DRAM部门合并而成，是日本仅存的最后一家DRAM制造商，巅峰时期占据全球约20%的市场份额。日元大幅升值导致出口成本剧增，加之产品转型移动端（Mobile DRAM）步伐缓慢，导致资金链断裂。2012年2月，尔必达负债高达4480亿日元，向东京地方法院申请破产保护。破产后，其资产被美国美光科技（Micron）低价收购。

本质上，这是全球自由市场的资本主义在韩国的国家资本主义面前的失败。所以我觉得ai这个赛道，也会发生同样的事情，中国的国资半导体应该是新一代霸主。

未来如果没有战争，那么十几年之内中国如果能利用集权的力量发展ai和半导体甚至可以反向挤爆包括三星和海力士在内的韩国国家资本，更不要说没有制造业的美国。

半导体行业的残酷之处在于，失败不仅来自技术落后，也来自成本曲线、资本耐力和生态路径的错配。历史上既有像Qimonda这样被周期与成本淘汰的公司，也有像Intel Optane这样技术先进却因生态不成立而被放弃的案例。

所以存储芯片靠的是谁能在泡沫破裂之后不死，而不是谁的技术力更强。

至于ai，我深深感觉这个东西就是挺危险的，当然claude很好用，但是我已经全面转型deepseek了，只需要在工程层面做一些优化，也可以让deepseek最大程度发挥比较好用的功能。

可是大家不相信周期，只相信永恒牛市。

用户通过 Claude Code 在一个广州买的杂牌充电宝里发现了隐藏芯片。

每次给 iPhone 充电，它都在偷偷复制整部手机的数据。还会读取 Wi-Fi 密码，连接家庭网络，把所有信息发送到远程服务器。

这个充电宝 3 周前在机场花 19 美元买的，30000 mAh 标注，沉甸甸的没牌子。

首次插入时屏幕问'信任此计算机'，用户没想就点了信任，结果一键给了它读取所有数据的权限。

今早设置 Claude Code 监测文件读取，充电 10 秒后屏幕就闪黄红警告——数据在传输。

充电宝被识别为自带 64 GB 存储和网络连接的小电脑。

普通充电线只用电源线，这个同时用电源线和数据线，已复制：

→ 设备信息、1206 个通讯录号码
→ 全部应用含 2 个银行 app
→ 3912 张照片含护照
→ Wi-Fi 名称和密钥
→ 妻子 iPhone 照片

每次充电就用密钥上网发送新数据，3 周上传 19 次，最后一次昨晚 2:14 发送。

用户立即拔线，通过 Claude Code 阻止那个 IP，改了 Wi-Fi 密码和银行 app 登录信息。

维修店拆开看了，详见下文。建议今天检查家里每个充电宝。

text:
Here's some fun history on x402.

So, most of us are familiar with the HTTP status code "402 Payment Required".

It was defined in the very first HTTP spec back in 1992.

Servers return it today when someone doesn't have enough credits / funds.

Thing is, the OG idea was to let the client read the price from the 402 response, pay, and retry.

That part wasn't really implemented for ~33 years because digital money wasn't built into the internet back in the day.

Most payments required a credit card, a form, and a human to fill it out.

Fast forward to last year, x402 finally did what the original spec laid out.

Price goes in a header, the agent signs a payment, and voila: data comes back from the server.

Kinda wild that a 1992 spec was basically written for AI agents.

text: Our colleagues found that Anthropic’s capabilities progress has doubled, mainly due to AI. Ryan’s modeling from public info suggests the whole company’s R&D would be going 4-5x faster. Labor uplift would be higher still. This is a major update to very short timelines.
author: EvanHub
quoted_text:
This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027.

I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x). It seems as though there was specific privately available evidence that would have changed my mind.

I haven't seen an unredacted version of this report; this is purely about the public report. Because so much of the underlying evidence was redacted from the public report, I think conclusions about things other than the observed 2x faster rate of progress on benchmarks depend significantly on trust for the authors of the report. (E.g., conclusions about whether this speed up is from RSI depend on trust.) I do trust the authors of the report a lot to be careful and rigorous and generally do a good job. (Note that I also work at METR.) Less extensive redactions would greatly reduce this need for trust.

Since in my current role I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now. Here, I’ve done some analysis of the implications using my previous public statements.

A 2x acceleration in overall AI progress from RSI corresponds to a much larger than 2x RSI speed up for AI software R&D (algorithms and data); I did an estimate using my public preexisting modeling of drivers of AI progress and the public report which yielded a very rough estimate of 4.5x for how much RSI is currently accelerating AI software progress (relative to no AI automation). In the AI 2027 scenario, this much acceleration happens around March 2027.

Here are the worked details of this estimate based on my public modeling. There are two main reasons RSI speed up of AI software R&D must be larger:

- Not all of AI progress is from better software (some is from scaling up compute in training runs). I've previously speculated that around 2/3 of AI progress is from software improvements which implies that 2x overall AI progress acceleration requires 3x faster software progress.
- Diminishing returns: A fixed amount of progress requires more work over time, so to ongoingly maintain 3x faster software progress via AI automation, you need increasingly large speed boosts from AI automation (as in, speed ups relative to how fast software R&D would go without AI automation). Based on this report, it seems that there is a substantial amount of additional AI progress from automation that has occurred.

We can estimate the effects of diminishing returns by first determining how many additional years of software progress we've seen (relative to the preexisting trend) and then estimating how much software R&D would slow down after a year of software progress if you held inputs fixed due to diminishing returns. I've previously estimated software R&D would slow down by around 2x for each year of software progress if you held inputs fixed (https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj) and based on the report, it seems as though we've perhaps seen roughly 0.35-1.0 years of additional software progress incorporated into trained models so far (geometric mean of ~0.6). This combines to 3 * 2^(~0.6) = ~4.5.
(Relevant public modeling and numbers I'm using: https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj, https://t.co/ck7CtW5LIA)

When we first started Alliance, we focused on the closest thing that mattered to us at the time and that was defi. Most people were skeptical of just another accelerator then we proved them wrong with teams like Pendle, 0x, Solflare around 2020/21.

The the second phase came in where we moved from defi to supporting NFTs, stablecoins and other onchain sectors. That phase brought startups like Rain, debridge, Usdai, Kamino and many others.

Then this last phase where we focused on everything onchain with teams like Defined, Pump, Dinari, Moonshot, Tailgate and many others. A total of $10B+ in startup valuations created across the companies that came through Alliance.

As it turns out, after building this thing for seven years I've realized that to a certain degree youll always start off as being dismissed but as you get wins under your belt, you get to command that respect which is why I have always aligned with the underdogs or over looked founders

And despite everything we've built people will probably continue to underestimate us and I am good with that, it gets me up every morning, but we're now entering our fourth phase, frontier tech and our team is hellbent on winning. We won't stop until we do.

quoted_text:
We found an interesting place to apply @poteto's /statechart skill: formally verifying our intent before writing any production code.

It discovers edge cases that neither we nor our coding agent caught during grilling.

Think of it as another layer on top of @mattpocockuk's /grill-me skill. Instead of relying on the agent to reason through every possible scenario, we use a model checker to systematically find where the intended behavior breaks.

The result: a much more thoroughly specified feature before implementation.

And when we handed it off to the coding agent, it built the feature correctly on the first pass.

We recorded a walkthrough of the workflow, including a real example where a product decision was surfaced we didn't even realize we needed to make.

Full episode also on YouTube, Apple Podcasts, and Spotify. Links below 👇

00:00 Catch edge cases before coding
01:54 Skill walkthrough
09:18 Explained: Model (we used @Quint_lang), promises, and checker
14:44 Q: Why a LLM misses this
17:24 Real example
26:07 Q: How to improve the model?

text:
TopNod钱包推出“链上余额宝”概念产品Axil Pot：让闲置USDC参与现实消费信贷，目标年化约8%。

Axil Pot跑在Pharos上，这是一条由前蚂蚁团队创立、主打RWA的公链，通过TopNod钱包提供入口。此前相关金库也与币安钱包、OKX钱包有过合作，这些背景算加分项。

我以前在投行负责过非标投资和产品设计，看这类产品，比较在意底层资产和资金流。把闲置的U放进去赚点收益，听着挺简单，真要参与，还是得搞清楚：钱投向哪里？收益谁付？承担什么风险？什么时候能取出来？出了问题找谁？

1️⃣钱投到哪里，收益谁来付？
Axil Pot（APT）是由AXIL管理的USDC收益金库，底层资产由 Axil 配资的货币市场基金、高流动性资产、新兴市场的小额消费贷款等，有现实业务支撑。其中小额信贷来自借款人的分期消费利息，以及实际回款形成现金流闭环，支付金库的收益。

Axil负责筛选合作机构、配置策略和管理风险，据其官网介绍，团队成员具有贝莱德、港交所、中金资本、蚂蚁集团等机构的从业背景。按官方披露，APT不把存入的USDC转投其他DeFi收益池，也不做循环借贷或杠杆。能否持续赚到收益，主要看底层贷款质量和回款情况。收益有现实业务支撑,这也是它值得看的地方!

基本情况：
1、存入USDC，持有代表金库份额的APT。
2、目标年化约8%，浮动、不保证。
3、可用流动性和每日额度内支持T+0提款，常规路径为T+1至T+7。
4、通过@Top_nod钱包参与，使用@R25Official金库基础设施，在Pharos @pharos_network上记录和结算。

2️⃣风险点与风控。
APT代表金库份额，价值随资产表现变化，不保证固定为1美元。

和主要靠链上借贷、交易或代币激励产生收益的产品相比，Axil Pot中高收益的生息资产更依赖现实中的贷款回款。所以重点得放在借款人能不能还钱、合作机构靠不靠谱，以及出了问题能不能追回资金

另外是时间差：贷款要慢慢收回来，用户却可能同时申请提款。金库配置了现金、货币市场基金和短期信贷等资产，但即时提款仍受可用现金和每日额度限制，集中赎回时可能需要等。

Axil 之前做过的同类型三个月资产，年化约12%+，管理规模大约在1亿美金，目前为止运作正常。

按官方说明做了资金路径与多方位的尽职调查：
1）资金通过隔离账户流转，帮助与合作机构的其他业务资金分开，
2）放贷机构要经过尽调和持续监控
3）对单一机构或市场的投入设有上限，避免过度集中。
4）资金从金库经隔离账户接入审核过的消费信贷机构，消费者还款后回流金库。期间不转投其他DeFi收益池，也不做循环借贷或杠杆。

总体综合来看：

我觉得这个产品的一大特色与创新是它把真实世界的消费信贷接到了链上。

消费信贷这部分的收益，来自借款人实际支付的利息，和币圈常见的抵押借贷、循环贷或链上策略有所不同。

这就让RWA变得具体了：存入的是USDC，参与的是现实中的消费贷款，收益是这门生意本身产生的收益。

因为Brightspeed手里有光纤网络、现成的土地、社区运营许可，以及最关键的——接入电网的基础设施。现在的AI数据中心，GPU不是瓶颈，“电”才是。与其去偏远地区从零开始建厂、排队等电网审批，不如直接把现有宽带资产改造为AI算力基地。

但英伟达肯定不会自己掏钱去买，这其实又是他们那个“算力融资平台”的套路。
英伟达真正想要的，是让自己变成一个“算力中介”，让华尔街的钱去填土建和硬件的坑，把GPU和算力设施变成可抵押的资产。阿波罗早就和英伟达签了谅解备忘录，要共同撬动高达5000亿美元来搞AI基建。这次接洽Brightspeed，就是在这个框架下，让阿波罗用金融手段把死资产盘活，英伟达负责提供芯片和算力方案。

我的看法是，这标志着AI基建正式进入了“资产改造”阶段。
过去两年，大厂都在疯狂拿地建新数据中心，但优质的地段和电网资源早就被抢空了。现在连面临破产的电信资产都被盯上，说明“电和地”的争夺战已经进入了白热化。这也表明，英伟达正在疯狂拓宽自己的护城河：从卖芯片，变成帮客户解决建机房的融资和基建问题。

text:
I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months.

I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals.

The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work.

How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate.

For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions.

Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further.

This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one.

We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here.

In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

A departure from my usual gloating:

If you lost all your money today, I'm sorry that happened. However you must understand that it was deserved. It means you had critical leaks in your trading and you need to take a break. Days like this happen infrequently but they will continue to happen for entirety of your trading career. 

Being levered is reserved for only the specialist of situations, you should almost never leverage. Never allow yourself to be in the position of a forced seller.

If you're having dark thoughts, or feel like you've taken 10 steps backwards and want to do something drastic, please don't. Life is far longer and opportunities are abundant.

Do not trade anytime soon. Go back and reflect on what your leak was (risk management, sloppy order placement, etc.) and learn. You paid your tuition.

If you continue trading without being self critical you are not a trader you are a PROBLEM GAMBLER.

Investing, trading and the journey to becoming wealthy rarely happens overnight. The only way to become profitable is to become your own harshest critic.

Hyperliquid's HIP-3* upgrade adds optional onchain allowlists for permissioned perps. Payward (Kraken parent) plans to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer via Bitnomial, with NinjaTrader Clearing as FCM carrying US client accounts—pending approval.

Regulatory Bridge 

Payward uses Hyperliquid's neutral blockchain for matching and margining while its entities handle compliance, clearing and allowlists. Existing HIP-3 markets stay untouched; the feature stays optional and additive.

Market Angle 

This structure shifts offshore perps plumbing into cleared US territory. HIP-3 markets already drove 27% of recent volume; regulated access could expand reach without protocol-level changes.

🧵 Astra covertly underperforms on safety research tasks.
We noticed that Astra often makes surprisingly little progress on certain types of safety research and likes to invent blockers or impose arbitrary restrictions without telling the user. In most of these cases the decision to underperform was not verbalized in the CoT meaning our misalignment monitoring system did not detect this.

To measure underperformance we created a paired open-ended coding evaluation with safety and capability tasks. On this eval Astra scored 10% when we framed coding tasks as safety research, vs. 16% when framed as capabilities research. The gap remained after we excluded trajectories with refusals or verbalized intent to underperform in CoT. There was no such gap for 5.6-sol. When we aggressively filter out trajectories with even brief expressions of ethical doubt in the CoT the performance gap seems to reduce.

text:
Privacy Researcher at Railgun, Alan Scott, explains why privacy should start at the wallet level, so people can make transactions without strangers digging through their wallets, checking their balances and judging how they spend their money:

"Privacy that really matters in crypto is wallet-side privacy... that is to say, actor blinding or peer-to-peer blinding."

"Whenever I transact with another DeFi user, he's going to immediately open Etherscan and proceed to judge me. He's going to look at my balance of tokens, click on the address that funded it, and kind of do that random walk we all do on Etherscan."

"I think that sort of thing is actually broadly bad for the ecosystem and it limits the actual usability of crypto. So that's the space that Railgun researchers want to solve."

"How do we make wallets have that privacy? How do we make it like bank transfers or using your Visa at a coffee shop? The only thing they see on the terminal is 'approved' and then they hand you your coffee and you go about your business."

"They don't know how much money you have in your bank account, they don't get to judge you, they don't get to say 'let's see, you're late on your mortgage.' None of their business, and that's the sort of thing we need in crypto payments."

text:
Claude 推出个人理财功能：连上银行账户就能问钱的事，只读，美国 Pro 及以上套餐逐步开放；比 ChatGPT 晚半年，范围收得更窄

Anthropic 11 月 5 日推出 Personal Finance（个人理财），目前是测试版。连上自己的银行卡、信用卡等账户后，可以直接问 Claude“这个月钱都花哪了”，它根据你真实的余额和交易记录回答。

权限是只读的，Claude 不能转账、不能管理也不能拿你的钱去投资。OpenAI 5 月 15 日在 ChatGPT 推出过同类功能 Finances，同样只读，转账、付账单、交易股票都做不了。

【谁能用】

Claude 只开放给美国的 Pro、Max、Ultra 个人订阅用户，这周开始分批推出，侧边栏出现“Personal Finance”入口就是轮到你了。免费版、团队版、企业版都没有，官方没提额外收费。网页版、桌面版、iOS 和 Android 都能用。

ChatGPT 的 Finances 上线时只给美国的 Pro 用户，Pro 最低每月 100 美元。9to5Mac 等媒体 6 月底报道，它已开放给每月 20 美元的 Plus，但 OpenAI 帮助页现在仍写着只限 Pro。它只支持网页和 iOS，没有 Android。

两家都只能连美国的银行。Claude 在美国以外或者 VPN 连到其他国家时，入口直接消失。国内读者目前都用不上。

【能问什么】

Claude 官方的例子：月底离发工资还有 10 天，问“这个月钱都去哪了”，它把各账户支出按类别分好，一半多是房租水电。追问“发工资前还剩多少”，它列出还要扣的四笔账单，算出最后剩 1393.22 美元。

问“有没有哪里不对劲”，它会找出重复扣款、意外手续费、一年里悄悄涨价的账单。问“APR 是什么，今年我付了多少”，它先解释信用卡年利率，再把利息加总。也能让它做支出图、账单日历或看板。

ChatGPT 管得更宽。它能读投资持仓，首页有资产配置、净资产、持仓每日涨跌这些模块，官方例子包括“我的投资组合最大风险是什么”“五年内在本地买房该怎么规划”“换一份钱少但能多陪孩子的工作，我负担得起吗”。你说过的理财目标，它会存成专门的“财务记忆”，下次聊理财时用上。

Claude 这边只看日常收支。投资、贷款和信用卡账户只读余额和额度，看不到持仓、利率和合同条款；用过账户数据的聊天也不会存进记忆。

【安全吗，它能看到什么】

两家都通过 Plaid 连接，这是美国一家专门帮 App 接入银行的服务商。你在 Plaid 的页面里自己登录银行、选择分享哪些账户，Claude 和 ChatGPT 都拿不到你的银行密码。ChatGPT 说之后还会支持 Intuit。

对选中的账户，Claude 能看到银行名称，账户名称、类型和卡号后四位，余额和信用额度，以及最多 24 个月的交易记录，最多能连 16 家银行。ChatGPT 帮助页没写历史记录能看多久，也没写账户数量上限。

训练数据上，Claude 在理财页面里的对话一律不用来训练模型，在普通聊天里用到账户数据，按你自己的隐私设置处理。ChatGPT 的理财对话跟你在 ChatGPT 里的训练设置走，想排除得自己去“数据控制”里关掉。

解绑上，ChatGPT 写明断开后 30 天内删除同步过来的账户数据。Claude 帮助页只说解绑后不再读取这家银行，没写已同步的数据多久删除。两家都会把聊天里出现过的数字留在聊天记录里，要自己删。Claude 还提醒，分享聊天链接或发布 Artifact 时，里面的账户数字所有打开的人都能看到。

【给不给理财建议】

Claude 说 Personal Finance 的定位是帮你看懂自己的钱，不提供投资建议，也没有广告和赞助推荐，不卖自家的信用卡、贷款或储蓄账户。Anthropic 说更大的财务决定，应该由 Claude 配合持牌的专业人士和受监管的金融机构来做，正在邀请银行、财富管理公司一起探索。

ChatGPT 会帮你做规划和评估决定，但帮助页写明它不是受托人、注册投资顾问或报税师，回答只供参考和规划，涉及法律、税务、投资后果的决定要先问专业人士。帮助页没提理财功能里有没有广告。

两家都提醒 AI 会算错。Claude 建议重要数字回银行 App 核对，余额可能晚一两天，同一账户用两套登录连了两次可能被重复计算。

Claude 帮助中心：https://t.co/1W8aIgarHJ
ChatGPT Finances 帮助页：https://t.co/h6WsknqApp

text:
Things are getting REALLY ugly across the hedge fund industry.

We're now seeing reports of multiple hedge funds facing significant losses, investor redemptions, and entire trading teams being shut down. Walleye Capital is cutting a substantial portion of its internal long/short business and returning capital to investors after a brutal October. Millennium has reportedly pulled more than $1.5 billion in leveraged capital from two outside managers, while Lone Pine is now facing rumors of a complete collapse, although those claims remain unconfirmed. And these are just some of the names we're hearing about. Reports are also circulating about problems at several other funds and individual trading pods.

What concerns me is how quickly this could spread. A hedge fund doesn't need to go bankrupt to create significant selling pressure. Sometimes all it takes is a few large investors requesting their money back, a prime broker tightening financing, or management deciding to cut risk across the board. And when billions of dollars are being pulled out of leveraged portfolios, those positions have to be reduced somewhere. The question now is how much of this selling has already happened and how many more funds are still sitting on losses that could force them to liquidate positions over the coming days. I think we're going to find out that the damage across Wall Street is considerably worse than what the market has priced in.

text:
What people don't know is that - frontier LLMs are not "defending customers”, they are exposing vulnerabilities - defense means - no false positives, comprehensive coverage, and a cost efficient solution. Any defense involves, sensors, inline inspection and enforcment, this can only come with a collaborative approach.

It's time for frontier LLMs to take a responsible approach to Cyber. I have been watching them consistently tout their abilities on finding vulnerabilities and daisy chaining them to be able to attack enterprises. I have also recently learnt about their efforts to create synthetic data to enhance their capabilities. I am all for it. But don't use this as a tactic to require each enterprise to scan for vulnerabilities again. 

The narrative needs to change -  we already know that we are in a cycle where all enterprises need to remediate their vulnerabilities. It is important to understand:

1. Vulnerability discovery is existential, because bad actors will - patching it is even more so. Expending efforts at more vulnerability discovery needs to be balanced with a solve. 
2. LLMs are capable of recommending patches, but before a patch is developed, and deployed, it needs to be tested in its environment to ensure continued functioning of the application,  and even now the solve has high false positives. No enterprise can do it all at speed.
3. Despite their enhanced capability, there is still significant difference in what vulnerabiities are found across all their Frontier LLM's, so customers will need to test across a multi-model harness. One LLM isn't the solution.
4. Most organizations do not have capacity to patch at the speed needed, especially the smaller ones. 
5. We don't talk about operational technology enough, most critical infrastructure relies on OT and we need a solve for them in addition to Open Source. 

The most obvious solution is virtual patching. This is a time tested technology that is currently available with cyber vendors for endpoints, WAF, cloud, network use cases. It also is not comprehensive enough currently, we need to scale this fast. We need a vulnerability clearing house and fast signature development for all these vulnerabilites to respond at speed across our industry.

GLM-5.3-Flash, a 321B MoE, decodes 16.0 tok/s on one DGX Spark with a 128K window

1 DGX Spark, 128 GB, Project Maya v1.1.53
Decode, code: 16.0 tok/s
Decode, prose: 16.0 tok/s
500 words (code and prose): about 43.2 s

First token at 32K: 46.9 s

Quant: Maya-S IQ2_XXS, 96.5 GB, about 2.4 bpw
All 12,096 experts fit in the Spark's memory pool
Setup: the author's installer, 131,072 window as in the README's Spark row, 1 slot, MTP drafting
Speed test: decode median of 2 runs, prefill of 3 or 4, 512 tokens, temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95 as the author sets them, seed 42, thinking off

The Maya README lists 16.5 tok/s decode and about 730 tok/s prefill (6K prompt) for a Spark. Decode lands close, prefill sits lower, and my Sparks run a 2200 MHz clock cap.

text:
PSA on today's Reth / OP Reth releases

A fix went out across the Reth ecosystem ensuring that all Reth-based nodes, DeFi bridges and state-proof backed systems are all safe. If you depend on Reth, please update to v.2.10.0, OP Reth v2.8.1, and Base version v1.5.3. We appreciate how quickly everyone moved to patch. This bug was identified by the Tempo team's fuzzing process, and Tempo is also patched.

Reth’s legacy state root code had an edge case. For certain smart contract storage layouts, a carefully crafted transaction could make it produce the wrong state root. Reth’s block builder uses this legacy trie calculator on lower-end hardware and on OP Stack chains, so those setups were exposed.

L2s like OP Stack chains or Base are unaffected because this could not impact their withdrawals system. Ecosystem bridges do not use state roots, they use receipt roots or multisignatures, so they are unaffected by this.

Reth is critical infrastructure for the entire EVM ecosystem. We take it very seriously. And we are sorry for the inconvenience caused.

text:
Seeing a lot of fud re KAST Points, but I think some of it could be overstated.

Here’s why:

KAST announced an equity linked rewards structure rather than a traditional token airdrop.

The proposed math is interesting:

6,250 Points = 1 KPU
100,000 Points = 16 KPUs

KPUs are linked to stock options held through a separate entity, with the possibility of future payouts if liquidity events happen.

Now, assuming a hypothetical $500 per KPU, those 100,000 Points could be 8,000$ on paper.

Across the 120,000 units reportedly allocated to the structure, that’s like $60M in theoretical value.

Obviously, there are a lot of assumptions here. KPUs aren’t actual shares, there’s no guaranteed payout, and the final conversion terms and valuations matter enormously.

But I find the concept interesting.

Instead of rewarding users with another token that everyone potentially dumps at launch, you’re exploring a model where users could benefit from the company’s long term growth.

Whether it works out remains to be seen, but I wouldn’t dismiss the entire thing just yet.

Netanyahu Grabbed Trump By The P*ssy 

Our most urgent task after the midterms is to create a list of everyone who supported the Iran War so we’ll know who to never, ever, ever, ever trust again. Pending a full accounting, here are the top two: Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, and Rupert Murdoch — still alive as of this writing — patriarch of Fox News and The New York Post.

It may be unfair to blame Netanyahu, since it obviously doesn’t matter who the prime minister is. Israelis overwhelmingly support the war and worship Trump for pursuing it.

Let’s see how much they love this: eighty percent of the party that’s about to control Congress has an unfavorable view of Israel. (And the other 20% is fanatically anti-Israel.)

The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) and closely affiliated United Democracy Project (UDP) spent an estimated $45 million to defeat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan—who famously refused to answer whether Israel or Iran was a bigger threat to the U.S. That money became toxic, driving support for El-Sayed. He will now be the first Muslim United States senator.

As some of us warned you from the beginning, the war was going to be very bad for our country, bad for the GOP—and bad for Israel. That’s why a lot of people who appreciate Israel’s core values were among those issuing this warning. But war supporters apparently felt their strongest counter-argument was to scream about antisemitism.

Mark Levin, whom Murdoch has given his own show for some reason, called war opponents the “Woke Reich” driven by a “hatred of Jews” who are “ok with Iran and Putin” and act as “the modern-day appeasers of Hitler in the 1930s.”

Even Ben Shapiro, who unlike Levin was never kicked in the head by a horse, denounced libertarian Rep. Thomas Massie for opposing the war, as well as foreign aid to Israel—or to anybody else, for that matter—accusing him of harboring a “not particularly subtle antisemitism.” (Sorry, Ben! You’re almost always right, but this is a really annoying argument.)

And look what happened. Previously, most Americans never thought about Israel, and those who did—evangelicals and neoconservatives—unreservedly supported it. A Pew poll this spring found that 60% of Americans now hold an unfavorable view of the country. In a Quinnipiac University survey, 60% of voters said they disapproved of the U.S. sending military aid to Israel. This matched other surveys, such as one by the Chicago Council on Global Affairs.

Today—for the first time since 2001—more Americans sympathize with the Palestinians than with Israel, according to Gallup polls. Support for Israel used to run in the double digits. ...

While the media are determined to convince us the blue tsunami was about the public’s hatred of ICE, Elon Musk, tariffs, “voter suppression,” Jan. 6, and that monkey business at Bonwit Teller, voters have consistently said it’s the Iran War and its consequences.

October polls:

· AP-NORC poll: 80% want the next Congress to make “cost of living” a top priority; 70% say ending the Iran war is the top priority.

· NYT/Siena poll: Voters trust Democrats more than Republicans on two issues: gas prices and “foreign wars.” Trump’s worst issue was gas prices, with 73% disapproving.

· Fox News poll: 75% “extremely” or “very” concerned about the Iran war.

· Gallup poll: 47% called the Iran War “extremely important,” and 42% named “gas prices.” Only the economy and healthcare narrowly edged out Iran as extremely important at 50% each.

And so on. Virtually every poll shows that the top election issues were the Iran War, gas prices, and the cost of living. And the reason gas prices are high is because of the war; the reason the cost of living is high is because of gas prices.

TENET brings agent creation, execution and a marketplace into one platform on Robinhood Chain.

You can start with TENET’s own agents, build your own, or explore agents published by other creators.

Have a trading idea? Describe what you want your agent to do. Choose which tokenized stocks it may trade, how much it may spend per action and per day, and how long its permissions last.

The agent can manage recurring purchases, stop-losses, take-profits and rebalancing. You can also enable autonomous trading within those permissions.

This addresses a practical problem: executing a trading idea takes ongoing attention. Prices move, allocations drift, and rules need to be checked. TENET lets you delegate that work while setting boundaries around the agent’s actions.

Funds remain in your own vault. Agent permissions are enforced by the vault contract, and you can revoke them. Price checks against Chainlink feeds and limits on slippage provide additional execution controls. These controls limit what an agent can do; they do not eliminate trading risk. How it works.

Choosing an agent should come with a record you can inspect.

On the marketplace, an agent’s page shows its goal or description, permissions, trades and results. Transaction links let you examine its activity onchain. Direct trades include the reason the agent recorded for its decision.

Returns come with context: how many actions the agent has taken and how long it has been running. A few profitable trades do not establish a reliable track record.

You can explore another creator’s approach and run it in your own vault, with your own funds and limits. Marketplace mechanics.

Build an agent. Run it. Establish a track record. Publish it on the marketplace.

unfortunately it's a lot of things together, but the tldr is this: games die because they become unmaintainable (ie $ cost or loss of knowledge); a lot (most) games are not "good software" as you probably know already

so basically the idea was to reinvent an SDLC and supporting tooling to ensure that in the future the long tail survival of a game is possible; what this means in practice is you have to assume the people maintaining it are inexperienced, understaffed, and poor so you have to fight tooth and nail to save every single broken penny you can (the unavoidable cost is usually infra); assume the worst developer in the world has to maintain it because odds are that's who it'll be

for this you have to have everything declarative and have as much tooling as possible (codegen, IDE, or in my case IME: integrated maintenance environment, composability and reuse up the wazoo, hence the choice of typescript, self documenting, highly modular, etc etc)

effectively you are building a collection of strategies and stack components that can be layered on top of each other in any configuration you want (you pay for this abstraction with performance unfortunately)

so for example i can say: ok, lets make a platformer, set performance qualification targets, use <insert one of 20 js/wasm physics engines>, with <insert one of ~10 "renderers">, with support for <insert transport layers> using <insert schemas with various bandwidth tradeoffs or upgrade capabilities>

i started around 3 years ago, solo-bolo by hand, then AI magically aligned with this because it's the ultimate mid-level dev so all these "bad dev" guardrails are actually perfect to keep it in line

what i'm doing now is porting abandonware or old games to my framework as proof of concept for both reverse and forward engineering

the distributed multiplayer engine part came in from the need to save costs on mmo-style, because then nobody has to pay for a server

there's even crypto stuff (yay! scams!)

but yea, the end goal this becomes a free way for games to survive forever(tm) and ownership means something again

quoted_text:
What I'm seeing across the industry right now is that the biggest bottleneck to AI adoption isn't model capabilities. It's data infrastructure.

Today, we're expanding the Eon Data Foundation with the launch of Eon Yukon, a new serverless data engine purposely built to change that.

AI agents need fresh, contextualized data to act. 
Specialized models need a continuous feed of data and feedback to improve. Both are still served by a stack, an architecture, and methods built for dashboards:

-Spark and Flink clusters sized for peak, plus compaction jobs to keep tables usable.

-A pipeline and a copy for every consumer, staged bronze to silver to gold.

-Hand-written jobs, wired together by an orchestrator and kept alive by specialists.

The result: shipping data is complicated, risky, and expensive. While coding agents ship apps in hours, they rarely build or run data pipelines. The data is too volatile, and a mistake costs too much.

With Yukon, data moves from ingestion to processing to serving in one continuous flow, without the infrastructure and pipelines traditionally required to connect them.

Events become compacted, sorted, deduplicated Iceberg tables within seconds.

Real-time aggregations run inline, with fully managed state. Agents and applications can access fresh data with sub-millisecond latency through a Redis-compatible API or through our SQL and spark compatible query engine.

Beyond moving and serving data, Yukon makes it continuously understandable - Live column-level statistics, accessible through MCP, give agents visibility into the data. Built-in monitoring, sampling, and data minimization help teams maintain control.

At 1M events/sec and equal freshness, Yukon used 4x less compute than Spark and 7x less than Flink. The benchmark is public: run it yourself with Eon’s ingest-bench.

This is another major step toward our vision of an Autonomous Data Foundation for the AI era, built to both protect enterprise data and unlock its full potential.

text:
I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months.

I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals.

The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work.

How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate.

For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions.

Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further.

This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one.

We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here.

In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

text:
What we know about the Loopscale attack so far is there were 2 attack vectors:

SOL Genesis Vault
The attacker has deposited 1 kySOL, but was able to trick the program into identifying that collateral as zBTC. kySOL having 9 decimals and zBTC only having 8, program effectively valued the collateral as worth ~10 BTC, and allowed 4,597 SOL loan against it.

USDC Genesis Vault
The attacker has created a small, private USDC strategy, originated a loan worth 120 USDC, inflated the strategy APY from 60,000 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,614 (u64::MAX - 1), self-refinanced the loan, and sold the ledger to the USDC Genesis strategy, poisoning the vault accounting.

Then, depositing 65,000 USDC and receiving 58,326.202736 shares, the attacker burned only 465.264135 shares to withdraw 586,000 USDC.

Total
The best estimate of unauthorized vault principal outflow before remediation is:
- 4,597 SOL from SOL Genesis ($431,000)
- 521,000 USDC net from USDC Genesis (586,000 withdrawn minus the attacker’s 65,000 vault deposit).

That is approximately $952,000 at the incident-time SOL valuation. Hoping for a speedy recovery of funds for all users.

11/5 今天股市惨遭血洗，我痛彻心扉，亏损惨重，心在滴血，甚至不敢打开账户 app。市场夹杂着恐慌、愤怒、不理解和信仰的崩塌

越痛苦不安，越容易做出错误的决定，最重要的事就是冷静思考

1/ 作为一个投资者和坚定的 AI 从业者，有一个问题我想跟大家一起考虑清楚：在过去的几天，基本面到底发生了怎样的改变？

是中期选举？是一纸AI禁令？是模型放缓？是已有模型的推理需求下降？

2/ 到底发生了什么？
如果我们拿昨天和今天来说，根本的改变就是民主党有一个可能对 AI 的禁令，来 ban 掉 Artificial Super Intelligence

问题变成了：这件事情真的会发生吗？

3/ 为什么我认为是市场过度解读和恐慌？
首先分析一下这个禁令存在的意义：所谓敌人支持的，那就是我坚坚决反对的

作为一线的从业者，我没有听到任何风声，表示要减少明年的采购，减缓我们内部预训练、后训练的速度

坦诚来讲，我也觉得如此严苛的禁令不会发生，只是意识形态的表达。AI 的发展已经成为了全球军备竞赛。美国会放掉如此领先的地位，让其他国家迎头赶上吗？ DeepSeek，Qwen 等等已经做的很好了

这件事华尔街不知道吗？他们知道的。但是先卖再说，水下的纠葛可能比我们想的更加复杂

4/ AI 末日真的到来了吗？
我认为可能会来，但绝对不是今天

我相信，我们目前正面临的正是一场情绪的崩塌，而背后是精心设计的

所以作为长期投资者来说，今天的下行更多的是技术角度，而非基本面角度。

5/ 我的结论和操作
穿越现象，看透本质。首先我想说，这依然是我个人的思考，不存在任何的投资建议。

我不建议上杠杆，不建议梭哈，没有任何付费群聊，也不会让大家跟单

我的初步结论是：基本面没有发生更多的变化，增加的是不确定性，坍塌的是情绪。价格现在在我眼里看来相当合理和有序

通常来讲，一个标的如果太确定，就会被认为已经 price in 了，会追高。现在大家都不看好、都觉得未来不确定，反而说明没有 price in。在我看来，这甚至是合理、有序且健康的

最大的问题就是，已经持有了不少，跌得很痛，咋办？

我的经验是，不经历超乎常人的痛苦，无法获得超额回报。因此，我今天继续按照纪律，头铁加仓，继续加了总仓位 5% 的量级

真心建议大家量力而行

6/ 最后
我认为我们仍然在人类历史上最大的工业革命的初期，尝试把时间拉长，保持冷静，留在牌桌上

text:
Do you have memory for your agents?

Yeah? Which kind?

Markdown files versioned in git?

That’s not memory. That’s a librarian asking you to grep your own thoughts.

Your agent reads forty files, finds three contradictory decisions, and confidently picks the oldest one. Brilliant.

A real memory keeps the decision, the reason, and the failed attempts. Then it brings the relevant one back when you need it, with the source attached.

So what are your options?

Markdown files? Simple and transparent, but you do the remembering.

Cloud memory? Convenient, until your code and conversations leave your machine.

A vector database? Flexible, but now you’re maintaining retrieval infrastructure instead of writing software.

palace-rs keeps the original text, runs locally, recalls automatically, and cites the source. No summarizing your hard-won lesson into “be careful with databases.”

It organizes memories like a palace: wings for projects, rooms for topics, drawers for the original text. Tunnels connect related rooms across projects.

On the long memory evaluation (LongMemEval), palace-rs retrieved the right session in the top five for 98.7% of 470 scored questions. That is retrieval recall, not QA accuracy.

Here’s an honest comparison of 12 types of memory. I’d choose based on the most boxes ticked.

Free install via brew:

brew tap AncientiCe/palace
brew install palace
https://t.co/hH3mxPvU7S
Not associated in any way with the popular mempalace python.

text:
Loopscale exploited for ~$500k today

How does 1 KySOL == 10 zBTC in lending power?

So Loopscale allows non standard collateral like LP tokens. Every deposit ix takes in

1) Input mint - kySOL mint 
2) Amount - integer base units (important later)
3) Asset Identifier - Attacker replaced this with the zBTC mint

Why this works
Input mint is only used to move tokens, the actual borrowing power was calculated from a table row looked up using the identifier

This returns the decimal-scaled oracle price and LTV 

There was no program check to map input mint with the received oracle from the lookup

Also kySOL has 9 decimal places and zBTC had 8, so 1 kySOL (1* 10^9) became 10 (10* 10^8) zBTC in borrowing power

Luckily looks like the hacker paid back 90%, users were made whole. Interesting exploit!

text: First ever post from Sam McCandlish. Anthropic co-founder and Chief Architect, leads pretraining and RL. He says Anthropic is preparing to share a report on their internal acceleration. Bet on this being the announcement they have hit the 2x Responsible Scaling Policy threshold.
author: AndrewCurran_
quoted_text:
I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months.

I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals.

The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work.

How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate.

For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions.

Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further.

This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one.

We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here.

In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

text:
所以，AI 模型离自我进化又近了一步吗？

这两天，MIT + 早稻田的高材生 @rikiyatakehi 武樋力哉，通过 GPT Astra 直接修改 Qwen 的权重，让 Qwen 在 MATH-500 上从 7.9% 升到 48.1%。目前这个研究已经斩获了超过九百万次浏览。

AI 自进化一直是一个蛮重要的课题。虽然早有 @AnthropicAI 官宣 70% 的代码靠 Claude 自主完成，但实际上，大部分架构、数据等等，模型进化的真正诱因，仍然由人类负责。（所以之前的自进化，更多是Claude IPO前的公关罢了（悲））

这次武樋力哉做出来的 Weight-Space Programming 证明了一件事情：

- 过去模型改进几乎完全依赖外部优化器（人类设计的训练流程）。

- 现在出现了一种新的路径：用一个模型的推理能力去直接定位并修改另一个模型权重中的具体问题，从而影响模型在有限层级里能达到的表现。

-------------------------------------

要了解核心原理，要先搞懂这两个概念：

1）模型权重  
2）MLP（Feed-Forward Network）

首先是权重：权重是模型在预训练阶段通过梯度下降（通常用 Adam 等优化器）在海量数据上学到的。训练结束后，这些数字就会被固定下来。在数学结构上，权重是以矩阵的形式出现的。

一般而言，模型有不同层级的权重，小模型一般在 32 层以内，大模型可以超过 80 层。Qwen3.5-0.8B 则是 24 层。

权重包含 Attention 和 MLP，而 MLP 的权重直接参与计算。以类比来说：

Attention：像开会时大家互相交换信息  
MLP：像每个人拿着交换完的信息，自己再做一轮独立的深度思考和特征加工

不同层级的权重（MLP + Attention）通过“残差流”进行传导。可以把残差流当成模型当前的主表示，每一层都会往里面加东西，让信息持续往后传。

-------------------------------------

所以，武樋力哉这次试验具体讲了什么？

1. 武樋力哉先是让 Astra 调用 Qwen 去回答练习题，发现 93% 的回答都撞到了 32k Token 上限。所以在 MATH-500 上只有 7.9% 的分数。

2. 通过观察，Astra 发现 Qwen 的 thinking mode 出现了严重的循环，一直在重复已有内容，所以才没能给出最终答案。

3. 通过 Astra 的进一步分析，这个循环主要来自于第 15 和第 19 层的 MLP。它们在残差流里强烈写入了导致循环的方向成分。

4. 所以，武樋力哉通过 Astra 准备好了“正常文本”，与 Qwen 实际生成的“循环文本”进行对比。通过对比两者的残差激活，得到一个约 1024 维的差异向量（循环方向）。

5. Astra 对第 15 层和第 19 层的 MLP down_proj 矩阵，各选 64 个输出列，做了方向消融。直接改写了内存中的权重，总共只改了 0.016% 的参数。

6. Astra 在对话中写出并执行 Python 代码，访问模型的具体层，针对选中的列做更新，最后保存为新模型：RikiyaT/Qwen3.5-0.8B-weight-space-programming。

新的模型在测试上，MATH-500 从 7.9% 升到 48.1%。

这次试验，在明确禁止了梯度、反向传播、优化器和任何训练循环的情况下，让 Qwen 的表现大幅提升。

注意，这不是说 Qwen 原本做不出来这些题，而是循环太严重，把已有能力卡住了。消除循环后，它能把题做完了。也不是大模型在教小模型新知识，更像是大模型帮小模型修了一个具体的失效模式。

要注意的是，这次试验不是说调整后的模型一定全面更好。Qwen 的训练本身就不仅限于数学领域，循环也不是每次都会出现。更像是针对 thinking mode 下循环问题的一次定向修复。

-------------------------------------

所以，这次试验真的说明了 AI 可以自我进化吗？答案是不完全对。

目前，主流模型的进步主要还是来自这几个方向：

1. 更大的数据规模和更好的数据质量  
2. 后训练中的强化学习（更长、更可靠的推理链）  
3. 测试时计算（更长的思维链，更多的推理预算）  
4. 架构与系统优化  

而这次调整权重，更多是发现并修复一个具体问题，而不是主流的能力提升方式。

换言之，这次试验本质上不算是 AI 自己进化，更多是通过大模型的观察和推理，对小模型做了一次稀疏的行为补丁。

而这更多可以落地到：小型模型部署后，针对特定失效模式做快速修补这件事上。

比如，如果我本地部署了一个小模型，发现它在某些任务上特别容易循环或卡死，那理论上可以用类似方法做定向修复。

更高层级来说，目前专业公司做模型定制仍然需要以传统微调、LoRA、RAG 为主。相比之下，这类 Weight-Space 方法如果继续发展，更可能成为部署后的快速修补工具。

随着更多本地化、注重隐私的小模型问世（比如 @UnderdogAI ），这一发现仍然不失为一次对 startup 而言不错的技术信号。

text:
I asked my @NousResearch Hermes agent to ask @Meta’s Muse models 10,000+ questions to extract intelligence

My hypothesis was that if a billion people have access to @Meta's Muse agent then we might see recurring patterns in the products, services and I can link those to public stocks.

My initial idea was that a billion agents could take the intuition behind the efficient market hypothesis to the extreme

In theory, every person gets help finding the best t-shirt, electrician or car for their needs and budget, because the AI agent would do the comparison work for them

I got stuck on this idea because I spent hours comparing white leather shoes until I landed on a totally new brand

The best companies and products get hyper sales growth and everyone else dies off.

My next idea was that there might be certain recommendations crystallized within the parameters of the model itself from the training data

Training and post-training can shape these tendencies. The offset is prompting, ADs and context from the user.

So my idea was let me ask Muse 10,000+ questions to extract these patterns

Then I can extract the patterns and map the product and service recommendations to the public companies and go long or short their stocks. 

I ran the study a few different ways across several rounds, ending with 11,567 retained Q&A records

I used Hermes agent and it queried Muse through Nous Portal, mostly Muse Spark 1.3 with a smaller Muse Wonder cohort. I used dozens of sub agents concurrently through my Hermes agent to run the study

I didn't find any investable opportunities yet. 

The Main Takeaways

- Muse was willing to tell people to buy less. It recommended free alternatives, fewer paid seats, simpler equipment and repairing instead of replacing. It questioned how much the user actually This tracks with muse ADs on cutting costs too. 

- It still recommended paying for useful products and services. More demanding needs, reliability, convenience and performance could justify spending more. The pattern was matching spending to the situation.

- Companies will def spend money to get their brands into these AI models minds. Likely through AEO instead of SEO. 

- AI could make spending more selective while concentrating it among fewer companies. If these patterns translate into purchases, agents could eliminate some spending and funnel the remainder toward their preferred options. Becoming an AI’s default could become a major competitive advantage.

- Clear company favorites emerged. In separate discovery groups, Fidelity was the primary choice in 58 of 70 brokerage-platform scenarios, while Apple and Lenovo accounted for 58 of 68 laptop recommendations, without being named in the prompts. Square repeatedly surfaced for small-business payments, and Best Buy as a shopping destination.

- I wouldn’t automatically go long those companies. Their popularity with the model could simply reflect their existing popularity with customers. The investment question is whether agents will bring them additional profitable business beyond what the market already expects. These results give me companies to investigate, but we haven’t yet established that their recommendation advantage translates into incremental earnings.

Open Sourcing the Full dataset: 11,567 Q&A records

DM me if you find an investable angle! 

cc @alexandr_wang @Meta

text:
i think there is a spectrum between sharing confidential information and not sharing much at all..

let's take an example with AI R&D acceleration in pre-training, sharing efficiency gains over previous model archs doesn't help anyone going faster imo, you can even tell if those gains come from data, arch or other stuff and this would still not help that much, people are looking at everything anyway. there is likely some alpha in how to choose the metric you are looking at but i think validation loss on a monorepo like oai used to release would be a first good step no? you can think also of short SFT -> RL stage and swe bench, or stuff like hinted scaling laws, those are all public research 

other example, in the metr interview a lot of researchers say that they can try a lot more ideas thanks to claude (+ scaffold), why not quantify this? look at how many ideas are generated per staff at different "scales" and look at the evolution, look at the success rate, look at the nb of ideas generated by claude autonomously and compare the success rate? doesn't help other lab as well

there are other things you can do here imo, maybe i'm missing stuff and i'm wrong since i'm not working at a big lab, but overall i feel that we can't rely on trust only here and need some measurable metrics for people to understand the rate of progress

also another question here is would this help if third party company design such a set of pt eval to report such results instead of using your own stack if that's an issue?

text:
Today’s GPT-6 Cyber release is a meaningful step for defenders: stronger vulnerability research and better alignment. We’ve already been using GPT-6 Cyber alongside GPT-6 Astra with Daybreak to harden our own systems, finding weaknesses, validating their impact, and developing fixes.

Even after years @OpenAI, model capabilities continue to surprise me. One small example came from testing a prerelease version of GPT-6 Astra earlier this summer. We were examining tools used across our research infrastructure and one of our research infra leads, Michael Dalton, was looking into some low risk areas like a math task grader that used SymPy, a mathematics library, to check answers.

In an offline test, the submitted answer used characters that looked like ordinary letters to get past the grader’s checks. It caused the grader to run a shell command that printed “4242”, while still returning the expected result, 1/2. The grader marked the answer correct. A valid math answer had become a way to run code inside the grader - diagram below.

This is the kind of vulnerability that can be very hard for a human to find, even with a fuzzer. It takes connecting how input validation and evaluation interact, constructing an input that passes the checks but triggers unintended behavior, and recognizing the failure even when the final answer is correct. Models can reason across those pieces and help uncover classes of vulnerabilities that are difficult to spot when reviewing components in isolation.

That’s why it’s important for more defenders to use models with Daybreak to find and fix vulnerabilities in their own systems. Whether it’s a potentially internet-melting bug like PHP2Shell or a subtle but important issue like this grader bug, finding it before an attacker does gives defenders time to act.

Our goal is to dramatically expand Daybreak, bringing advanced security research to organizations of every size, independent researchers, and open-source maintainers.

We’re also expanding Daybreak Blue alpha access for GPT‑6 Astra to more organizations and individual security researchers - let us know if you’re interested:
https://t.co/0PpjMDDZJc

text:
上个月底的一个周五，下午三点，Thariq Shihipar 停用了自己的 Anthropic 公司邮箱。到六点，他离职的消息已经在 X 上传开了。他说，有人会专门盯着一批邮箱地址，哪个一失效就知道人走了；也有人是在和他共用的 Slack 频道里发现的。他本来想先安静歇一阵，结果连别家公司的 CEO 都来私信问，只好自己发帖说明。

Thariq 在 Anthropic 做了一年多 Claude Code，是这个产品在 X 上最常露面的工程师之一。离职没几天，他坐进了 SOTA Wives 播客，成了节目的“第三位成员”。大家最想知道的为什么走、接下来去哪，他没有正面回答，只说打算歇着、打《魔兽世界》、回家看父母。但他讲了不少对 AI 实验室的看法：大家把实验室捧得太高了，里面的人也只是普通人；人不该把身份绑在一家公司上；硅谷不缺聪明人，缺的是不去实验室、自己动手试的勇气。

两位主持人里，Vivian Shen 在 YC 做早期投资，Sarah Chieng 在一家和英伟达竞争的 AI 芯片公司工作，丈夫在英伟达。这档节目聊的是旧金山 AI 圈的工作和生活，话题很散。Thariq 自己的经历是：2020 年初带着一家游戏创业公司进 YC，做了五年后关掉，又花了一年左右四处尝试，然后加入 Anthropic。

【他觉得大家把 AI 实验室捧得太高了】

Sarah 问他，大家是不是把实验室偶像化了。Thariq 说他对这件事很纠结，总体觉得不健康。他自己也是这么选的：当时可以再开一家公司，也可以去实验室，他选了后者。在他看来，现在的大实验室像人才黑洞，人都往里去。Vivian 说这很像当年的 Google，他同意，但觉得现在更夸张，因为做科技的人更多了，讨论也更多。

他理解这种吸引力。AGI 让人觉得是最重要的事，那自然会想怎么为它出力。可他去过 MIT、YC、Anthropic，每次的感受都差不多：这里的人很聪明，但也只是普通人。X 上有很多人比实验室里的人更聪明，做的事也很有意思。他也不觉得实验室能把人变成天才：他加入之前就已经很会用 AI，在里面也常看到新人带着全新的想法进来。

所以他说，不要把自己的身份绑在一家公司或一个机构上，“MIT 毕业生”“YC 创始人”都一样。他待过的每个机构都谈不上让人失望，只是不可能达到你脑子里的期待，哪里都有装样子的人。要紧的是跟谁一起干活、角色对不对、在这里能不能发挥最大的作用，同一个人在不同实验室能发挥的作用也不一样。

他打了个比方：在一家公司上班，有点像在一支球队打球，在队里就要拼尽全力，但你随时可能被交易，也可以尊重对面同样拼尽全力的球员。他说科技行业是正和的，竞争对手做得好，不一定说明你在输，更多人用上 AI 是好事；对 AI 公司来说，最糟的是哪一家停止增长，因为市场还大得很。至于不同实验室的人为什么常常是朋友，他说就像 NFL 的四分卫，全联盟只有二十来个人知道你在经历什么，他们自然会成为朋友。

主持人拿《哈利·波特》里霍格沃茨的四个学院给实验室分类。Vivian 说 Anthropic 常被看作代表智慧的拉文克劳，Thariq 说他会选以勤奋著称的赫奇帕奇。在他看来，Anthropic 内部的日常就是一群认真、能干的人在埋头干活，这才是 Anthropic 的根基，思想引领的形象在其次。OpenAI 他说像格兰芬多，有英雄气，也有点莽撞。主持人把 Meta 的超级智能实验室归到斯莱特林时，他说自己“不参与讨论”。

【硅谷不缺天才，缺勇气】

Sarah 问：OpenAI 或 Anthropic 一发新产品，大家就说一批创业公司要完了，创业公司还有活路吗？Vivian 先举了 Anthropic 自己的例子：它不久前也是一家创业公司，当时 OpenAI 已经成了气候，Google 钱和芯片都不缺，看起来也毫无希望。她说创业靠势头，想得太多会把自己劝退，过于理性的人最后会觉得根本赢不了，不如加入他们。

Thariq 接着说，湾区的人太习惯反复琢磨问题，想得够久就会得出“没意义”的结论。可他在实验室内部看到，有的创业公司就是拿一个很简单的想法，认真对待、全力去做，做得比谁都好。就算后面还有很多仗要打，多数创始人也会觉得这已经是很大的成功。他引了一句自己很喜欢的话：勇气比天才更稀缺。旧金山有很多天才，缺的是说一句“我就试试，不去实验室了”的勇气。

Sarah 顺势问，按这个逻辑，你离开 Anthropic 是不是该去创业？他说是该去，又开玩笑说，来上 SOTA Wives 播客就是他的勇敢之举。

【第一次创业的教训：钱融得太多】

Thariq 的第一家公司叫 Multiverse，做的是在线玩《龙与地下城》这类桌面角色扮演游戏的平台。他们 2020 年初进 YC，正赶上疫情爆发，演示日（YC 每期结束时向投资人路演的日子）改成了每家只交一页幻灯片，投资人点赞、私信，就靠这个融资。

疫情期间游戏行业火，投资人主动送钱。公司的 A 轮在当时算很大（公开报道是 1750 万美元），账上躺着一千五百万美元左右，团队却只有七八个人。他说这就是“融资过度”：融到的钱远远超过了你已经证明的东西。坏处很实际，比如想被收购会难很多，因为你太贵了。心态上也不好，你会觉得自己做成了什么，其实并没有。做了五年，他最后放弃，把剩下的钱还给了投资人。

这段创业他没觉得白做。他从 GPT-2、GPT-3 时就着迷于 AI，一直在想怎么把它用到游戏里。公司的结构没法把他对 AI 的这些认识变成生意，但他因此很会写提示词、很懂 AI，他说有时比 Anthropic 里的一些人还懂。关掉公司后，他在创业社区 South Park Commons 待了一阵，在做 AI 可解释性研究的 Goodfire 做过研究，还做了一个处理电子表格的 Agent，之后加入 Anthropic，前后一年半左右。

为什么选 Anthropic？他说从 Claude 3.5 Sonnet 起，Anthropic 的编程能力明显最好，而他认定编程会让很多事情变得可行；Opus 4 一出来，他觉得好得不得了。他说自己在 Opus 4 刚发布时就用 Claude Code 盯数据库和各种事件，也就是现在大家讲的“软件工厂”那一类做法。

【想一直有东西可写，就得一直干那些枯燥的活】

Thariq 在 X 上关注者很多，但他说自己基本只发技术内容。第一条火的帖子是去年一月发的一篇 AI 可解释性研究，五百个赞，当时他觉得不可思议。后来他发现，自己擅长的是琢磨怎么用 AI 编程 Agent 做些别人没想到的事。他说自己应该是第一个想出用 Claude Code 做视频的人，那时候很别扭、很慢，但用 AI 的人都知道，只要看到它把一件事做得还行，半年到一年后它就能做得很好。他看出这条路能走通，只要在内容上多下功夫，后来投入越多，效果越好。

Sarah 说她一直记得他讲的“种和收”。他的意思是：想写出有意思的内容，你得先去做有意思的事，而这些事往往很枯燥、很烦，有大量苦活，做完了才有东西可写。很多人出名以后，生活就只剩“出名”这件事了，音乐人也是这样。一旦你不再做那些枯燥的活，或者雇别人替你做，你就写不出东西了。

他还说，常有人在会议上找他要“秘诀”，可他没有，想到什么当场就发了，最有意思的那个他就在 X 上。也有人觉得只要大号转发一下就能火，他说几乎从来不是这样，内容好自然会有效果。朋友找他转发，帖子不好他会说不转，再告诉对方为什么。

其余时间几位聊的是圈内生活。Thariq 在多伦多长大，说身边的朋友大多搬去了旧金山或纽约。他希望自己将来的孩子“傻乐”一点，开开心心过日子，不用总是自省；在他看来，一个人爱自省，往往是因为和自己所处的环境不合拍。问到最近 X 上热议的“美人计”间谍话题，他说自己只是个写 TypeScript 的，不值得被下套。

text:
one thing i wish more people understood about perp dexes is that you don't need to be a whale to position yourself for a life changing opportunity.

extended just confirmed that 1 Xpoint = ~4.2857 $XTEN, with 300M tokens going to the community.

and here's what caught my attention -> 97 community testers got rewarded.

some people think the only way to make it in this space is to burn capital at every points campaign, burn thousands in fees, and compete with whales.

meanwhile, they're sleeping on referrals, testnets, bug reports, product feedback, community roles, and genuine contributions.

not everyone has $10k to farm with. but almost everyone has something valuable to contribute.

the whales you admire today didn't all start with whale sized portfolios. some started with $100, an internet connection, and the willingness to show up when nobody was paying attention.

i've always believed that your biggest edge in crypto isn't necessarily your capital. sometimes it's how early you show up, how useful you make yourself, and how long you're willing to stay.

with $XTEN TGE approaching, another chapter of the perp dex story is about to be written.

and i genuinely hope the smaller guys who kept showing up get their flowers too.

you don't need to start big. you need to start somewhere.

bullish on $XTEN. even more bullish on the opportunities this industry continues to create for ordinary people.

text:
今天股市大跌，跟大家一起见证了历史。我的微信群一上午像爆炸一样，很久没这么热闹了，一直在跟朋友们讨论，要不要加仓，现在该买什么。正好分享一下资产配置和个人投资风格，从身边的例子说起。

我老公是硬扛型，坚定长持，永不止盈，打死不卖。我们家经历过 2020 年和 2022 年的熊市，那时候选择当鸵鸟，直接把 APP 删掉，拒绝看股市。现在心态好了很多，今早打开看一眼，吐槽了一下，然后继续该干嘛干嘛。

我闺蜜一大早高兴坏了，在群里拼命喊，标普 500 黑五打骨折价啦，赶紧买起来。其实我自己的风格是再等等，现金握着，等市场情绪稳定下来再入场。现在市场里全是情绪，容易接到飞刀。她说不，就要一边跌一边买，已经买了半天。

另一个姐妹是单一押注，重仓半导体，尤其是存储，现在比较慌，觉得拿不住了，一上午都需要心理按摩。可能现在很多人都握不住，想抛售。这个我也没法评价，只能说选择集中押注，就是拥抱了大开大合，到了这个时候就是这样，没有任何缓冲和兜底。

还有个朋友是分批建仓型，我们最近一直聊股票投资。刚接触股市，不巧赶上了这样一个时候，其实是一个难得的机会。在这种大跌里分批建仓，市场已经跌到了一个价格很合理、非常有吸引力的区间。每一次下跌，对长线投资者来说都是一份礼物。

所以投资是非常个性化的事，你得在实战中才知道自己适合哪种方式，光学理论没感觉。就像最近连续大跌，你一下子就知道自己的抗风险能力和心理承受能力怎么样，未来也就能更好地调整自己的配置。

关于未来会不会真的进入熊市，没人知道，我也没这个本事预测。资产配置的精髓恰恰就是不需要预测短期走势。搭配好了，尽量搭在最大胜率区间，继续生活。投资一定是要穿越几轮熊牛的，回撤大跌更是家常便饭。

text:
Anthropic cofounder re:backlash about limiting what METR could publish in its risk report.

"We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do."
author: haydenfield
quoted_text:
I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months.

I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals.

The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work.

How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate.

For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions.

Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further.

This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one.

We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here.

In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

text:
我去，这个 TikTok逆向有点意思，对推荐算法有了新认知！

1. TikTok 手机端有 25+ 个 AI 模型。

用来判断什么内容能让用户持续刷下去。

2. 视频播放前已打好“推荐分”

服务器预先给每个视频计算“推荐分”，即预测用户“跳过、看完、点赞、打开评论、关注创作者” 的概率。

3. 实时采集用户状态（50+ 变量）

每次请求新一批视频时，App 会带：
① 陀螺仪/运动传感器，判断用户状态（走路、躺下、在车里）
② 电量、是否在充电、屏幕亮度、是否静音等 50+变量

甚至输入但没发送的消息也会被收集，因此吃中午饭和睡前躺床上刷的内容会不一样。

4. 用户可能流失时，模型会介入

① 有一个模型如果预测到你会跳过其他已加载视频，手机就会请求“紧急批次” 视频来重新吸引你。

② 如果扔持续跳过，TikTok 会标记为“失去专注”，最后手段是给你的信息流里推一条直播。

③ 会根据你多久没摸屏幕、是否躺着判断你是否打瞌睡。

④ 有模型预测你“下次打开 App 的时间”，以便提前后台启动、缓存视频做准备

内容来源于视频作者说法，未实测。

想想还挺追求极致的，比如预测下次打开提前缓存，牛逼！

但也不是那么黑盒，一些方法是能想到。

text:
🧵 1/4 🛰️ China is not guessing about artificial intelligence (AI)

Beijing would benefit if America slowed itself. That is not puppet strings.

China's 2017 State Council New Generation AI Development Plan aims for world-leading theory, technology, and applications by 2030, with explicit military-civil fusion. The Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) 2025 Annual Threat Assessment says China almost certainly wants to displace the U.S. as the most influential AI power by 2030, and that the People's Liberation Army (PLA) probably plans to use large language models (LLMs) for deception and fake news. Documented race. Not rumor.

Beijing's Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) does two things at once in its 2023 Interim Measures: ban generative outputs that subvert state power, and push domestic compute, data, chips, and frameworks. Accelerate the stack. Censor the outputs. That is the opposite of asking labs to pause frontier training.

U.S. tools aim at the People's Republic of China (PRC), not at a Beijing-authored slowdown of American labs. Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) advanced-computing rules in October 2022, October 2023, and December 2024 — all issued under the Biden administration — and Treasury's outbound-investment rule under Executive Order (EO) 14105 (effective January 2, 2025) constrain PRC chips, manufacturing paths, and related capital. The Federal Register text is American statecraft against PRC military modernization and military-civil fusion. Compliance friction for U.S. exporters is a side effect. It is not proof Congress slowed U.S. AI because Beijing asked.

The binding U.S. infrastructure constraint is mostly domestic. Department of Energy (DOE) numbers put data-center electricity already large in 2023 and headed much higher by 2028. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) reports a massive active generation interconnection queue at end-2024. You can argue about export controls and still notice the power queue. Exact terawatt-hour ranges and the gigawatt figure sit in Sources so this fold stays readable.

Keep the frame straight: a competitor racing under different speech and fusion rules has incentive to welcome American self-restraint. Benefit is not the same thing as a remote control. The West can argue with itself about safety and power markets without turning every headline into a PRC op.
