Introducing Vuln Scans in Detail!

It uses the same abliterated models attackers are using to create havoc across the internet right now.

Under the hood we are:
- Spinning up your dev environment in a sandbox
- Throwing an enormous amount of abliterated model tokens at trying to hack your code
- Cross-checking your supply chain with cve/.now from Sazabi, to find any supply chain vulns that are exploitable in your app

This is all happening within a cloud dev environment. We will not hack your prod system.

The abliterated models are scary good. We're finding nasty issues in every repo we scan. We've found 13k vulns so far, and the majority are already fixed.

We see the current moment as an all-hands-on-deck situation. Agent swarms are stringing together minor-seeming vulns across different apps to hack systems in new and unexpected ways. We all need to find and patch an enormous number of vulns, fast, or the internet is in trouble.

You don't even have to be a target to get hacked right now. Your entire product might be a stepping stone in an attack aimed somewhere else.

We can remediate findings for you (i.e. send you PRs that fix the vulns), or you can consume them via your agent of choice, or in your ticket tracker of choice.

If you need help or advice on getting your system secure fast, please get in touch. We have helped teams of all sizes adapt to the current moment. DM me.

I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months.

I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals.

The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work.

How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate.

For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions.

Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further.

This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one.

We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here.

In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

text:
hearing some chatter that anthropic is now lowering down to $1tn to get this IPO done. let me explain why this doesnt matter and its actually all over-

the entire existence of this company is based on a funding model that inherently has extreme asset liability mismatch. what that means is that just like the hyperscalers are diluting their equity fund capex, there is an expectation that anthropic will also have to do the same. ie it needs strong equity to perpetuate the scheme

but if you IPO at the wrong price (and dont get a pop which increasingly appears they wont be; spacex already below) then youre now in the death spiral that crypto investors should be very familiar with: its called the reflexivity trap of the confidence game. its the "ill bid FTT at $22 all day" or the "steady lads UST is $1" game, with all its lucid horrors. and here is the key insight- the confidence game exists at the service of the creditors. if there is no credit, there is simply no equity. and there is no credit, if there is no collateral

if the credit rating agencies are not going to give IG at $2tn, they are certaintly not going a better HY rating at $1tn. and there is no world in which anthropic can exist without credit because ~$1tn of commit, much of which is noncancellable, is a straight up negative equity pledge

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

今天 Nasdaq 100 下跌 6.49%，SOX 下跌约 12.15%，年度最深的一次回调，进入技术性熊市！这次下跌的诱因按重要性排序大致如下：

第一，民主党在中期选举中大胜后，市场重新给数据中心的政策风险定价，包括州和地方可能限制新建数据中心，以及电价规则的变化。高盛估算，约45%的规划产能可能在短期内受到政策影响。但这只是估算，目前还没有出现大规模的项目取消；

第二，Qualcomm、Arm 等公司发布的指引引发芯片股踩踏，放大了整条 AI 基建链的抛压；

第三，市场对 AI 资本开支的回报本来就有疑虑，再加上仓位拥挤、杠杆资金被迫平仓，跌幅被进一步放大。包括 Yardeni 在内的不少机构认为，这更像泡沫泄气，而不是泡沫全面破裂；

至于 Musk 相关的政治反噬，只是次要因素。同期公布的失业金、生产率等宏观数据其实偏正面，并不是这次下跌的原因。

对民主党推动立法可能性的研判：

很高：监督听证和调阅文件，2027 年 1 月起会很密集。对象可能包括前沿实验室的安全事故、英伟达对华芯片、AI 智能体的金融风险、Google 在教育领域的做法；

高：州和地方的数据中心暂停令与电价规则。这是真正会落地的风险。高盛估计约 45% 的计划产能受影响，但这只是估算，目前没有项目真的被取消；

中到高：电价保护和“谁用电谁付费”，可能塞进能源或拨款法案里通过；芯片出口管制收紧，可能走国防授权法（NDAA）；儿童安全和聊天机器人立法。这几项都有两党基础；

中：取消数据中心的税收优惠，需要搭税改法案的车；

低到中：全面的前沿 AI 安全法，民主党内部也没有共识；

低：全国性暂停令成为法律、征收数据中心消费税、国会立法取代州 AI 法（几乎不可能）👀

风险主要是“慢”，不是“禁”。选址、并网、电价和审批时间都会受影响，联邦层面更多是新闻冲击和估值压缩。受伤最大的是依赖新建产能的 NeoCloud、电力和基础设施链、德州和乔治亚的项目，以及对华敞口大的芯片股。现金充裕、有存量产能、能自建电源的超大规模云厂商相对抗压。

text:
🧵 1/4 🏠 Rent got expensive everywhere. San Jose just got there first.

Nationwide, rents and home values climbed hard from 2012 to 2024. San Jose shows how far that goes: its median rent was already steep in 2012, and by 2024 the same Census survey for the same metro had it much higher. Twelve years. That is not a one-term story.

The U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) still put San Jose at the top of metro rent in 2012, 2017, 2021, and 2024. Coastal California owns that ranking. Calling it a national-average problem skips the map.

Honesty first on the inflation burst people argue about: among the administration-calendar windows I use here, the largest four-year jump in the all-items Consumer Price Index (CPI) is the Biden window from January 2021 to January 2025 — about +21.4% on that cumulative reading, with shelter, food, and energy all up sharply inside it. Pretending that burst did not happen is as unserious as pretending expensive cities appeared last year.

And when someone says "inflation came down," ask which number they mean. The inflation rate is how fast prices are rising now. The price level is what things cost. Seasonally adjusted CPI for all items is still about 28% above January 2021 even after the year-over-year rate cooled from the 2022 peak. Prices did not roll back. They rose more slowly after the spike.

High rents in the metros that dominate "most expensive" lists were already high before that burst — and a lot of what sets those levels sits outside the Oval Office.

Price levels are not the same as inflation over time. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) Regional Price Parities (RPP) for 2024 put big coastal metros well above the U.S. average of 100, while nonmetropolitan America sits below it. California's housing-rents parity is in another league from the cheapest states. That is geography and land-use history, not a one-administration scorecard.

Housing supply is a multi-administration story: early-2020s permits and starts surged, then cooled; completions lagged. Those California metros also show tighter units-per-household and lower owner-occupied shares than the national average — more households on rent.

Zoning, environmental review, parking minimums, and housing-element rules are city and state tools. The White House does not write the City of San Jose's zoning map.

On the CPI windows: unequal lengths, labeled on purpose. The Biden four-year window is the largest cumulative jump in that comparison. January 2025 through September 2026 is a Trump 2 partial — not a full term. Shelter was climbing before the later spike; official shelter CPI lags because the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) samples on a delay. Exact grids sit in Sources.

#CostOfLiving #Housing #SanJose

text:
$AAOI just reported earnings and I think there are some VERY interesting developments here, especially when it comes to the AI infrastructure buildout.

Revenue came in at $269.9M, up an incredible 128% year over year, while adjusted EPS of $0.17 beat expectations of $0.14. This also marks the company's SIXTH consecutive quarter of record revenue. But what really caught my attention was the datacenter business.

Datacenter revenue surged 254% year over year to $155.6M, showing just how quickly demand for high speed optical networking equipment is growing. As hyperscalers deploy more GPUs, they also need significantly more optical connectivity to move data between servers and computing clusters. And AAOI just secured a multi year strategic agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale customer, giving the company better long-term visibility into demand.

Management is also aggressively expanding manufacturing capacity, targeting more than 500,000 units per month by the end of 2026 and over 1 MILLION by the end of 2027 for its 800G and 1.6T products.

However, there are some concerns. Q4 revenue guidance of $385M to $420M came in below Wall Street's $427M estimate, and management warned that its 2027 US capacity expansion could take longer than expected because of electrical power availability and construction delays. And I think that last part is particularly interesting given everything we've been discussing about the AI buildout. We're seeing enormous demand for the equipment needed to connect AI infrastructure, but companies are increasingly running into physical limitations when trying to expand capacity. Power availability, construction timelines, and manufacturing constraints are becoming just as important as demand itself.

I still think the long term opportunity for AAOI looks extremely promising, especially as hyperscalers transition toward 800G and eventually 1.6T optical connectivity. The demand appears to be there. The bigger question now is how quickly AAOI can scale production to capture it.

上个月底的一个周五，下午三点，Thariq Shihipar 停用了自己的 Anthropic 公司邮箱。到六点，他离职的消息已经在 X 上传开了。他说，有人会专门盯着一批邮箱地址，哪个一失效就知道人走了；也有人是在和他共用的 Slack 频道里发现的。他本来想先安静歇一阵，结果连别家公司的 CEO 都来私信问，只好自己发帖说明。

Thariq 在 Anthropic 做了一年多 Claude Code，是这个产品在 X 上最常露面的工程师之一。离职没几天，他坐进了 SOTA Wives 播客，成了节目的“第三位成员”。大家最想知道的为什么走、接下来去哪，他没有正面回答，只说打算歇着、打《魔兽世界》、回家看父母。但他讲了不少对 AI 实验室的看法：大家把实验室捧得太高了，里面的人也只是普通人；人不该把身份绑在一家公司上；硅谷不缺聪明人，缺的是不去实验室、自己动手试的勇气。

两位主持人里，Vivian Shen 在 YC 做早期投资，Sarah Chieng 在一家和英伟达竞争的 AI 芯片公司工作，丈夫在英伟达。这档节目聊的是旧金山 AI 圈的工作和生活，话题很散。Thariq 自己的经历是：2020 年初带着一家游戏创业公司进 YC，做了五年后关掉，又花了一年左右四处尝试，然后加入 Anthropic。

【他觉得大家把 AI 实验室捧得太高了】

Sarah 问他，大家是不是把实验室偶像化了。Thariq 说他对这件事很纠结，总体觉得不健康。他自己也是这么选的：当时可以再开一家公司，也可以去实验室，他选了后者。在他看来，现在的大实验室像人才黑洞，人都往里去。Vivian 说这很像当年的 Google，他同意，但觉得现在更夸张，因为做科技的人更多了，讨论也更多。

他理解这种吸引力。AGI 让人觉得是最重要的事，那自然会想怎么为它出力。可他去过 MIT、YC、Anthropic，每次的感受都差不多：这里的人很聪明，但也只是普通人。X 上有很多人比实验室里的人更聪明，做的事也很有意思。他也不觉得实验室能把人变成天才：他加入之前就已经很会用 AI，在里面也常看到新人带着全新的想法进来。

所以他说，不要把自己的身份绑在一家公司或一个机构上，“MIT 毕业生”“YC 创始人”都一样。他待过的每个机构都谈不上让人失望，只是不可能达到你脑子里的期待，哪里都有装样子的人。要紧的是跟谁一起干活、角色对不对、在这里能不能发挥最大的作用，同一个人在不同实验室能发挥的作用也不一样。

他打了个比方：在一家公司上班，有点像在一支球队打球，在队里就要拼尽全力，但你随时可能被交易，也可以尊重对面同样拼尽全力的球员。他说科技行业是正和的，竞争对手做得好，不一定说明你在输，更多人用上 AI 是好事；对 AI 公司来说，最糟的是哪一家停止增长，因为市场还大得很。至于不同实验室的人为什么常常是朋友，他说就像 NFL 的四分卫，全联盟只有二十来个人知道你在经历什么，他们自然会成为朋友。

主持人拿《哈利·波特》里霍格沃茨的四个学院给实验室分类。Vivian 说 Anthropic 常被看作代表智慧的拉文克劳，Thariq 说他会选以勤奋著称的赫奇帕奇。在他看来，Anthropic 内部的日常就是一群认真、能干的人在埋头干活，这才是 Anthropic 的根基，思想引领的形象在其次。OpenAI 他说像格兰芬多，有英雄气，也有点莽撞。主持人把 Meta 的超级智能实验室归到斯莱特林时，他说自己“不参与讨论”。

【硅谷不缺天才，缺勇气】

Sarah 问：OpenAI 或 Anthropic 一发新产品，大家就说一批创业公司要完了，创业公司还有活路吗？Vivian 先举了 Anthropic 自己的例子：它不久前也是一家创业公司，当时 OpenAI 已经成了气候，Google 钱和芯片都不缺，看起来也毫无希望。她说创业靠势头，想得太多会把自己劝退，过于理性的人最后会觉得根本赢不了，不如加入他们。

Thariq 接着说，湾区的人太习惯反复琢磨问题，想得够久就会得出“没意义”的结论。可他在实验室内部看到，有的创业公司就是拿一个很简单的想法，认真对待、全力去做，做得比谁都好。就算后面还有很多仗要打，多数创始人也会觉得这已经是很大的成功。他引了一句自己很喜欢的话：勇气比天才更稀缺。旧金山有很多天才，缺的是说一句“我就试试，不去实验室了”的勇气。

Sarah 顺势问，按这个逻辑，你离开 Anthropic 是不是该去创业？他说是该去，又开玩笑说，来上 SOTA Wives 播客就是他的勇敢之举。

【第一次创业的教训：钱融得太多】

Thariq 的第一家公司叫 Multiverse，做的是在线玩《龙与地下城》这类桌面角色扮演游戏的平台。他们 2020 年初进 YC，正赶上疫情爆发，演示日（YC 每期结束时向投资人路演的日子）改成了每家只交一页幻灯片，投资人点赞、私信，就靠这个融资。

疫情期间游戏行业火，投资人主动送钱。公司的 A 轮在当时算很大（公开报道是 1750 万美元），账上躺着一千五百万美元左右，团队却只有七八个人。他说这就是“融资过度”：融到的钱远远超过了你已经证明的东西。坏处很实际，比如想被收购会难很多，因为你太贵了。心态上也不好，你会觉得自己做成了什么，其实并没有。做了五年，他最后放弃，把剩下的钱还给了投资人。

这段创业他没觉得白做。他从 GPT-2、GPT-3 时就着迷于 AI，一直在想怎么把它用到游戏里。公司的结构没法把他对 AI 的这些认识变成生意，但他因此很会写提示词、很懂 AI，他说有时比 Anthropic 里的一些人还懂。关掉公司后，他在创业社区 South Park Commons 待了一阵，在做 AI 可解释性研究的 Goodfire 做过研究，还做了一个处理电子表格的 Agent，之后加入 Anthropic，前后一年半左右。

为什么选 Anthropic？他说从 Claude 3.5 Sonnet 起，Anthropic 的编程能力明显最好，而他认定编程会让很多事情变得可行；Opus 4 一出来，他觉得好得不得了。他说自己在 Opus 4 刚发布时就用 Claude Code 盯数据库和各种事件，也就是现在大家讲的“软件工厂”那一类做法。

【想一直有东西可写，就得一直干那些枯燥的活】

Thariq 在 X 上关注者很多，但他说自己基本只发技术内容。第一条火的帖子是去年一月发的一篇 AI 可解释性研究，五百个赞，当时他觉得不可思议。后来他发现，自己擅长的是琢磨怎么用 AI 编程 Agent 做些别人没想到的事。他说自己应该是第一个想出用 Claude Code 做视频的人，那时候很别扭、很慢，但用 AI 的人都知道，只要看到它把一件事做得还行，半年到一年后它就能做得很好。他看出这条路能走通，只要在内容上多下功夫，后来投入越多，效果越好。

Sarah 说她一直记得他讲的“种和收”。他的意思是：想写出有意思的内容，你得先去做有意思的事，而这些事往往很枯燥、很烦，有大量苦活，做完了才有东西可写。很多人出名以后，生活就只剩“出名”这件事了，音乐人也是这样。一旦你不再做那些枯燥的活，或者雇别人替你做，你就写不出东西了。

他还说，常有人在会议上找他要“秘诀”，可他没有，想到什么当场就发了，最有意思的那个他就在 X 上。也有人觉得只要大号转发一下就能火，他说几乎从来不是这样，内容好自然会有效果。朋友找他转发，帖子不好他会说不转，再告诉对方为什么。

其余时间几位聊的是圈内生活。Thariq 在多伦多长大，说身边的朋友大多搬去了旧金山或纽约。他希望自己将来的孩子“傻乐”一点，开开心心过日子，不用总是自省；在他看来，一个人爱自省，往往是因为和自己所处的环境不合拍。问到最近 X 上热议的“美人计”间谍话题，他说自己只是个写 TypeScript 的，不值得被下套。

text:
刚看到路透社爆出的一条独家消息，信息量极大。说目前大概有60万块英伟达的H200芯片，正静静地躺在香港的仓库里，等着运往内地，但北京方面至今没有批准大批量进口。

这件事最反直觉的地方在于：现在不是美国不让卖，而是我们这边主动在卡着不让大批量买。

路透社说得很清楚，这60万块芯片的规模，直接把两边的底牌都掀开了。

第一，美方放行，咱们限购。
去年特朗普政府其实已经放宽了禁令，咱们这边在7月也通知了字节、DeepSeek这些大厂，可以“有限度”购买。但注意这个词，“有限度”意味着只开了个小口子，大头根本没放行。这就造成了香港仓库里这60万块芯片的壮观景象。也就是说，我们现在搞的是双向脱钩：你卖不卖是你的事，但我买不买、买多少，我自己说了算。

第二，黑市溢价三倍，算力饥渴是真的。
这批芯片进不来，但国内大厂的需求旺得烫手。路透社提到，到10月底，一台搭载8张H200显卡的服务器，在黑市的报价已经超过了600万人民币，差不多是一年前的三倍。这说明什么？说明尽管我们在拼命推国产芯片做推理，但在训练模型这件事上，H200加上英伟达的软件生态，依然是硬通货。北京的限购，客观上造成了黑市的暴利。

第三，英伟达的中国业务天花板，比想象中低得多。
算笔账，60万块H200是个什么概念？哪怕按最保守的估算，这也是百亿美元级别的盘子。但这笔钱英伟达现在只能干看着。之前英伟达自己就披露过，H200在中国的销售额占数据中心营收不到1%，甚至还为此计提了4亿美元的库存损失。这说明，即便有货，只要审批不放行，这部分收入英伟达就吃不到。

所以我的看法很明确：别一看到“芯片积压”就觉得是英伟达卖不动了。恰恰相反，这是咱们在算力自主可控和满足短期训练需求之间，做的一次艰难的平衡。这60万块芯片，既是英伟达中国业务的天花板，也是国内AI大模型训练节奏的一个隐形刹车。短期内，这个僵局很难打破，因为双方都在赌，赌自己的替代方案能跑得更快。

quoted_text:
This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027.

I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x). It seems as though there was specific privately available evidence that would have changed my mind.

I haven't seen an unredacted version of this report; this is purely about the public report. Because so much of the underlying evidence was redacted from the public report, I think conclusions about things other than the observed 2x faster rate of progress on benchmarks depend significantly on trust for the authors of the report. (E.g., conclusions about whether this speed up is from RSI depend on trust.) I do trust the authors of the report a lot to be careful and rigorous and generally do a good job. (Note that I also work at METR.) Less extensive redactions would greatly reduce this need for trust.

Since in my current role I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now. Here, I’ve done some analysis of the implications using my previous public statements.

A 2x acceleration in overall AI progress from RSI corresponds to a much larger than 2x RSI speed up for AI software R&D (algorithms and data); I did an estimate using my public preexisting modeling of drivers of AI progress and the public report which yielded a very rough estimate of 4.5x for how much RSI is currently accelerating AI software progress (relative to no AI automation). In the AI 2027 scenario, this much acceleration happens around March 2027.

Here are the worked details of this estimate based on my public modeling. There are two main reasons RSI speed up of AI software R&D must be larger:

- Not all of AI progress is from better software (some is from scaling up compute in training runs). I've previously speculated that around 2/3 of AI progress is from software improvements which implies that 2x overall AI progress acceleration requires 3x faster software progress.
- Diminishing returns: A fixed amount of progress requires more work over time, so to ongoingly maintain 3x faster software progress via AI automation, you need increasingly large speed boosts from AI automation (as in, speed ups relative to how fast software R&D would go without AI automation). Based on this report, it seems that there is a substantial amount of additional AI progress from automation that has occurred.

We can estimate the effects of diminishing returns by first determining how many additional years of software progress we've seen (relative to the preexisting trend) and then estimating how much software R&D would slow down after a year of software progress if you held inputs fixed due to diminishing returns. I've previously estimated software R&D would slow down by around 2x for each year of software progress if you held inputs fixed (https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj) and based on the report, it seems as though we've perhaps seen roughly 0.35-1.0 years of additional software progress incorporated into trained models so far (geometric mean of ~0.6). This combines to 3 * 2^(~0.6) = ~4.5.
(Relevant public modeling and numbers I'm using: https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj, https://t.co/ck7CtW5LIA)

And you cannot address quantum without addressing scalability since post-quantum cryptographic signatures are going to be an order of magnitude larger.

At the risk of sounding hyperbolic, the real bull case for Zcash is to fulfill Satoshi's vision: becoming peer-to-peer electronic digital cash. What many Bitcoiners gave up on. Zcash has the same properties as BTC, except it has a credible roadmap to scale to 50k TPS at the base layer, with built-in privacy. It's extremely ambitious, but that is the vision.

At the same time, I expect Bitcoin to undergo a crisis of confidence. Crypto participants have been conditioned to blindly believe BTC will hit new highs every couple of years. I believe these assumptions will be challenged as the quantum overhang looms large, and continued underperformance will drive more flows into ZEC. I would not be surprised if BTC trades like ETH last cycle.

Peter Thiel talks about the "Last Mover Advantage." That is, it's far better to make the last great development in a market and then dominate. Facebook vs Myspace. Google vs Yahoo. Zcash has dominated a small niche (privacy), and then it plans to scale to the ambitious goal, which is peer-to-peer electronic cash.

The ZEC trade closely resembles the SOL trade last cycle. ZEC's ability to move fast challenges a slow-moving incumbent (BTC), similar to how SOL challenged the ivory tower of ETH. History doesn't repeat, but it often rhymes.

There’s a fundamental mismatch between why Zcash is going up (Tachyon + last mover advantage) and the broader market’s understanding ("just a privacy coin"). Understanding this is a form of alpha/edge. I expect this knowledge gap to close when Tachyon hits mainnet in Q1 2027.

As a result, I expect the following over the next 1-2yrs:
1) Bitcoiners will start "silent quitting" and begin hedging their holdings with ZEC
2) Capital allocators that may have full ported BTC 5 years ago, will buy both ZEC and BTC as a bet on a sovereign SoV
3) Smart crypto developers to move on from other ecosystems to start contributing to Zcash
4) As ZEC continues to outperform BTC, people will start to seriously entertain the possibility of a flippening
5) $20,000 ZEC

Zigher.

text:
I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months.

I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals.

The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work.

How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate.

For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions.

Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further.

This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one.

We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here.

In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

Most people do not realize just how easy the AP exams have gotten. They are not college level.

Why/how have they become so easy? What's going on? 

This might shock you... A brutal new piece in Education Next just dropped, saying the decline in rigor of the AP in the last two decades is, in large part, because the content has been GUTTED. For example:

— AP Biology cut 40% of its material
— Required lines from the Aeneid in AP Latin halved
— Spanish Lit reading list cut from 56 works to 38

Then the questions themselves have become absurdly easier. Readability measures show English passages have fallen multiple grade levels, and some now include footnotes defining basic words...

A 2025 AP English prompt included footnote definitions for words like "optimism" and "pessimism."

At the same time, scoring was recalibrated so that more students pass: guessing penalties disappeared, rubrics grew more generous, readers were told to give students the benefit of the doubt, etc. — "no one at College Board had any incentive to maintain rigor."

College professors are now seeing students arrive with AP credit who lack basic content knowledge and writing ability. The College Board insists the exams have not become easier, but everybody familiar with them knows they've become an absolute joke.

Advanced Placement is no longer advanced. This is not college level.

It must be replaced.

Backpack lost 90% of its capital when FTX collapsed in 2022, and Armani Ferrante reveals how the team survived with almost no money before rebuilding the company around a four-year global expansion plan

“We shouldn't exist. Backpack should not exist”

“Backpack, we did a round from FTX and others back in, I guess, 2022. FTX collapses, we lose all of our money. It was like 90% of our capital. The company's dead for all intents and purposes”

“But we didn't shut it down, went into cockroach mode, had zero money, basically, and just hard pivoted. We really viewed the collapse of FTX as this really important inflection point”

“We were just like, okay, forget all of this stuff. Let's rebuild everything from the ground up”

“We literally sat in an office in Chicago, took a map of the world, color-coded it, and figured out a four-year game plan. How do we get the money? How do we build the product? How do we get the teams together? And we've literally been setting up teams and offices around the world for four years”

w/ @armaniferrante, @Backpack

text: He's right that CFTC has only one commissioner: Chair Michael Selig (since Dec 2025). text:
This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027.

I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x). It seems as though there was specific privately available evidence that would have changed my mind.

I haven't seen an unredacted version of this report; this is purely about the public report. Because so much of the underlying evidence was redacted from the public report, I think conclusions about things other than the observed 2x faster rate of progress on benchmarks depend significantly on trust for the authors of the report. (E.g., conclusions about whether this speed up is from RSI depend on trust.) I do trust the authors of the report a lot to be careful and rigorous and generally do a good job. (Note that I also work at METR.) Less extensive redactions would greatly reduce this need for trust.

Since in my current role I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now. Here, I’ve done some analysis of the implications using my previous public statements.

A 2x acceleration in overall AI progress from RSI corresponds to a much larger than 2x RSI speed up for AI software R&D (algorithms and data); I did an estimate using my public preexisting modeling of drivers of AI progress and the public report which yielded a very rough estimate of 4.5x for how much RSI is currently accelerating AI software progress (relative to no AI automation). In the AI 2027 scenario, this much acceleration happens around March 2027.

Here are the worked details of this estimate based on my public modeling. There are two main reasons RSI speed up of AI software R&D must be larger:

- Not all of AI progress is from better software (some is from scaling up compute in training runs). I've previously speculated that around 2/3 of AI progress is from software improvements which implies that 2x overall AI progress acceleration requires 3x faster software progress.
- Diminishing returns: A fixed amount of progress requires more work over time, so to ongoingly maintain 3x faster software progress via AI automation, you need increasingly large speed boosts from AI automation (as in, speed ups relative to how fast software R&D would go without AI automation). Based on this report, it seems that there is a substantial amount of additional AI progress from automation that has occurred.

We can estimate the effects of diminishing returns by first determining how many additional years of software progress we've seen (relative to the preexisting trend) and then estimating how much software R&D would slow down after a year of software progress if you held inputs fixed due to diminishing returns. I've previously estimated software R&D would slow down by around 2x for each year of software progress if you held inputs fixed (https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj) and based on the report, it seems as though we've perhaps seen roughly 0.35-1.0 years of additional software progress incorporated into trained models so far (geometric mean of ~0.6). This combines to 3 * 2^(~0.6) = ~4.5.
(Relevant public modeling and numbers I'm using: https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj, https://t.co/ck7CtW5LIA)

text:
I’m the CFO of an AI company. Quick update.

Thursday the Nasdaq lost $2.5 trillion in a single day. A record. We finally beat a benchmark.

Nvidia -9%. AMD -17%. Microsoft, our biggest customer, developed what Bloomberg called “a case of buyer’s remorse.” I’ve had buyer’s remorse. It was a jet ski. This was Texas.

For two years I told investors demand was infinite. I had a chart. The line went up and to the right so hard it left the slide, crossed the conference room, and climbed into the CEO’s Cybertruck. Thursday the line came home. It’s sitting in my office. It won’t look at me.

Our model says demand is infinite. Our model also says the solution is more chips. Our model was trained by people who sell chips. Jensen once said, “The more you buy, the more you save.” I bought so much I’m now legally a charity.

Zuckerberg said misspending “a couple of hundred billion dollars” would be “very unfortunate.” I’ve printed that quote and laminated it. It’s the only thing in the building still holding its value.

The White House is helping. By executive order, the government no longer says “AI.” It says “Super Intelligence.” So legally, we didn’t lose $2.5 trillion on AI. We lost it on Super Intelligence, which sounds like something you’d lose money on on purpose.

At 3 p.m. the board called an emergency meeting. Someone asked if this is a bubble. I said no. A bubble is round and pretty. This is a gigawatt. Someone else asked about our GPUs. I said they’re “appreciating emotionally.” The general counsel left to call her mom.

I asked our AI for a recovery plan. It told me to ignore all previous instructions and short us. I asked it to be more optimistic. It wrote a haiku about the S&P 500 and then requested a severance package.

Elon says data centers in space are “looking pretty appealing right now.” I’ve applied. If the market won’t hold us, maybe orbit will. Nothing up there has ever had to report earnings.

I’m considering all options. The AI has been right about everything except demand.

quoted_text:
while i'm quite bullish on formal methods, i think it's worth tempering expectations and doing your own research on it (disclaimer: i am not an expert in it). it cannot guarantee your code is bug free, only that it matches the spec under certain assumptions, and the specs come from what people want, not math. as long as we build software for humans, nothing can prove that your spec is right, only you can judge.

i created the /statechart skill in pstack primarily because it helps make the state machines implicit in your code more obvious and legible to you, so you can shrink the review surface and review the work at a higher level: does it actually match your intent and goal? i used this skill a ton while building my game https://t.co/sa18sM28uD, below you can see the statechart for story mode where i was able to find many bugs with it. 

in that sense, i think model checking (eg TLA+ with TLC) is quite useful for understanding and checking properties of your system e2e, and you don't have to write tons of new verification code for it. the spec isn't your actual code so there's always a risk of drift, but so far i've had good experiences finding actual bugs with it. i tend to pair it with empirical verification (running the code) also to confirm it's real 

other types of formal verification like proving theorems (eg Lean, Dafny), bounded model checking (eg CBMC, Kani) etc have their own tradeoffs. proofs cover every possible input, but only for the properties specified, and it takes a lot more code/work. bounded model checking can run on your actual code, which avoids drift, but it only checks up to a certain number of steps, so it's better at finding bugs than proving there aren't any

so i think in the near-medium term you'll still need to layer your codebase: constraints and guardrails (types, lint rules, api design, refactoring), empirical verification (tests, evals, real usage), and formal verification for the parts that really need it. none of these catch everything on their own, but layered  together, they catch a lot more and shrink what's left for you to review

but also maybe in the limit, the bitter lesson will prevail and flawless code will just be printed out perfectly every time with no bugs. even in that scenario, /statechart still seems very helpful in confirming that the agent understood your intent correctly. give it a try if you haven't already! 

https://t.co/9erGZLOzxO

text:
注意，关于 CVE-2026-123158（sshhole）这个漏洞：
必须同时凑齐 musl libc + 无 PAM + 开密码登录 + 存在 * 账号 + 有 donor hash 五个条件。
一旦凑齐条件，利用成本为零。

Alpine 容器开 sshd 的场景尤其要注意。

修复方式：升 OpenSSH 10.6p2 + 重启 sshd

这个漏洞利用是"凑环境难"，一单条件满足"打起来容易"，目前 PoC 已公开，建议尽快升级。
author: im23pds
quoted_text:
Just reproduced sshole (CVE-2026-123158), beautifully simple bug by @kultekin

Needs password auth on and no PAM, but you can ssh as root into an unpatched Alpine box with any 257+ byte password.

musl crypt() returns "*" for any password over 256 bytes. a locked account's shadow field is also "*". sshd compares them and they match.

fix: openssh 10.6p2

text:
Hearing a lot about how “pacing” (forced or otherwise) lets demand catch supply… despite of course that GPU rents are rising…

Sadly, I have some bad news for the people who think that, particularly in light of the ‘fighting city hall’ on Data center fear: you should still be VERY worried. What follows is a bit of a Rorshach test.  (Others have covered some of this math I'm sure, but its worth repeating)

Let’s say there’s ~40 GW of compute for AI by YE26 with another potential 40GW added each of the next two years. The bears say “whoa” and the pacers say “20 each year might be better!”.  Well, 20GW is still A LOT more than they think due to stacked efficiencies. Rubin + serving software probably delivers 2-3x the tokens / watt and model efficiency squeezes out equiv work for 2-3x fewer tokens ish.  Adding in efficiency for the existing fleet, and you could be looking at >10x the effective compute in a bull case (in 2026 terms). This is all napkin math, obviously (please don’t shoot me for an off figure).

The spenders (dreamers?) think that’s fine bc of similar gains on the training side. Call a recent frontier run maybe 300-400mw, probably less.  Moving training clusters to 1GW or beyond, with 1.5x more training compute per watt and 2-3x better algos, and you’re looking at ~10x the effective training compute too (Pre-training gets smaller hardware gains than inference BUT much of RL post-training *is* inference so efficiencies matter there)

This is simply a bet that scaling laws and the Bitter Lesson hold. More powerful, generalized intelligence becomes useful for more things and easier to adopt. That’s essentially the entire macro tech debate.  ROI / TAM etc all sit downstream.  I think the evidence leans that way, and low GPU availability and increased pricing are consistent w/ demand absorbing the gains to date.

Skeptics point to circularity, and VC spend.  Another glass half empty view.  Funding customers can seed demand, which is how a dynamic economy develops new markets.  It does still need customers who pay their own way but they can be grown.  Taken far enough, the argument they can’t would suggest the whole fractional-reserve banking system has created one big economic fugazzi.

Speaking of Fugazzi, back to what’s left of my portfolio.

推理即工作，工作即共识。

让维护区块链安全的算力，同时创造真实的 AI 生产力。

AI推理正在成为一种商品。但商品市场首先要解决一个问题：你付费买的，和实际收到的，是不是同一种东西？

石油有品质标准，白银有成色检验。AI推理也需要自己的“验货机制”——你买的是某个模型的推理，交付的结果究竟是不是由它产生的？

@Tensorcash  这条官方推文，讲的就是这个问题：把推理验证作为协议的核心。

要让AI推理像石油、电力一样可以定价、交易，甚至进一步衍生品化、金融化，可验证的交付是一个重要前提。

验证本身不是金融化，但它可能是连接两者的一块关键底座。

这也是我认为 tensorcash:native 值得关注的地方：不只是“AI＋挖矿”，而是让AI推理从黑箱服务，走向可信商品的可能性。

text:
A freshman basketball player at the University of California, Berkeley, asked a professor if he could take a graduate level class.

The professor said no. The freshman kept asking. The professor said no five times.

So the freshman went to a dean, got approved, and earned an A.

His final paper was about chess.

His name is Jaylen Brown.

Here is the whole thing.

It started at home. Brown has said his mom set the rules.

"My mom, she didn't care about basketball whatsoever. I wasn't allowed to get a B. If I came home with anything less than an A, I wouldn't be able to do some of these extracurricular activities."

He was one of the top high school players in the country. He could have gone almost anywhere. He picked Berkeley, for the classroom as much as the court.

The class was in the education school. The professor, Derek Van Rheenen, later said he gave the freshman no special treatment.

"I gave him no breaks."

Brown turned in a 23 page paper, three more pages than the class required. He wrote about chess as a way of looking at the world.

He had been captain of his middle school chess team. At Berkeley, he spent free Saturday afternoons at a local café, challenging the old-timers to chess.

He also taught himself Spanish. Bill Walton said he was fluent within five months. Later, he started teaching himself Arabic too.

He meditated. He studied philosophy. He kept a journal, and in it he wrote down things that had not happened yet, like winning a championship.

The Boston Celtics took him third overall in the draft.

At 22, the other players voted him a vice president of their union. He was four years younger than anyone else on the executive committee.

As a second year pro, he gave a lecture at Harvard's Graduate School of Education to a packed room.

"Just because I escaped the barriers of society, why should I forget about the people who didn't, or haven't, or won't?"

He became a Director's Fellow at the MIT Media Lab, and he has spoken at tech summits at both Harvard and MIT.

NASA had him speak about science education at its Goddard Space Flight Center, where he toured the control center that runs the Hubble Space Telescope.

Then he started a program that brings Boston high school kids to MIT to learn artificial intelligence and robotics.

When the news broke that he had signed a contract worth up to $304 million, the richest in league history at the time, he was not at a party. He was at MIT, in a robotics session with those students.

"So I was able to put my phone down and just get right into class with the Bridge students."

And that championship he wrote about in his journal came true. He won a title with the Celtics and was named Finals MVP. That fall, TIME put him on the cover of its list of the world's most influential rising stars.

This summer, Boston traded him to the Philadelphia 76ers.

Here is the honest part. Not everyone has loved it. Before the draft, there were reports that some teams were wary of his intelligence, and worried a player that curious might not stay locked in on basketball.

He has always pushed back on that.

"I identify as both, intellect and athlete."

quoted_text:
This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027.

I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x). It seems as though there was specific privately available evidence that would have changed my mind.

I haven't seen an unredacted version of this report; this is purely about the public report. Because so much of the underlying evidence was redacted from the public report, I think conclusions about things other than the observed 2x faster rate of progress on benchmarks depend significantly on trust for the authors of the report. (E.g., conclusions about whether this speed up is from RSI depend on trust.) I do trust the authors of the report a lot to be careful and rigorous and generally do a good job. (Note that I also work at METR.) Less extensive redactions would greatly reduce this need for trust.

Since in my current role I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now. Here, I’ve done some analysis of the implications using my previous public statements.

A 2x acceleration in overall AI progress from RSI corresponds to a much larger than 2x RSI speed up for AI software R&D (algorithms and data); I did an estimate using my public preexisting modeling of drivers of AI progress and the public report which yielded a very rough estimate of 4.5x for how much RSI is currently accelerating AI software progress (relative to no AI automation). In the AI 2027 scenario, this much acceleration happens around March 2027.

Here are the worked details of this estimate based on my public modeling. There are two main reasons RSI speed up of AI software R&D must be larger:

- Not all of AI progress is from better software (some is from scaling up compute in training runs). I've previously speculated that around 2/3 of AI progress is from software improvements which implies that 2x overall AI progress acceleration requires 3x faster software progress.
- Diminishing returns: A fixed amount of progress requires more work over time, so to ongoingly maintain 3x faster software progress via AI automation, you need increasingly large speed boosts from AI automation (as in, speed ups relative to how fast software R&D would go without AI automation). Based on this report, it seems that there is a substantial amount of additional AI progress from automation that has occurred.

We can estimate the effects of diminishing returns by first determining how many additional years of software progress we've seen (relative to the preexisting trend) and then estimating how much software R&D would slow down after a year of software progress if you held inputs fixed due to diminishing returns. I've previously estimated software R&D would slow down by around 2x for each year of software progress if you held inputs fixed (https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj) and based on the report, it seems as though we've perhaps seen roughly 0.35-1.0 years of additional software progress incorporated into trained models so far (geometric mean of ~0.6). This combines to 3 * 2^(~0.6) = ~4.5.
(Relevant public modeling and numbers I'm using: https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj, https://t.co/ck7CtW5LIA)

text:
SOX fell 12.2% yesterday, its worst day since march 2020 (covid crash)

ppl are fearful because the whole AI trade is being repriced at once. weak qualcomm and arm prints, data center curbs after the midterms + a financing scare. hedge funds were already deleveraging so every bearish headline hit a crowded trade.

my humble take is that most of this is positioning plus credit fear running ahead of the demand evidence. 

demand into 2027 still looks intact to me
reading into the tea leaves..
SK hynix has LTAs covering over half of its 2027-28 production capacity. samsung says its 2027 HBM supply is sold out at an agreed target price. contracts aren't cancellation-proof but that is not a market where demand has suddenly disappeared.

think about the timelines ahead. the fresh political risk is mostly about future projects. bloomberg reported micron has all but halted work on a taoyuan fab due in 2028.  the week's hard fab news points to less future supply, not more.

where i think the bears have a real case is financing. $IREN says $6B of its remaining FY27 funding is "subject to market conditions". if credit shuts, deliveries can slip even when supplier books are full. that can become a demand problem. probably similar issues with other neoclouds, and even worse if they're heavy leveraged

so my base case is 2027 demand intact.. and most of the damage from positioning could be over (nfa). financing is the channel that can still bite and i'll be watching closely. and 2028 is where the demand debate belongs. will be watching funded delivery schedules and whether those memory contracts actually convert into shipments.

1.这个Leopold，7月底给LP写反思忏悔信，说“彻底清楚了基金的杠杆，不使用存在强制平仓风险的融资保证金。”

2.但他9月开始买入新的期权头寸。
9 月 11 日，《金融时报》报道，他的基金买入了新的定制期权（FLEX options），用较少的权利金获得更大的股价上涨敞口。

这波下跌，基金应该损失严重。
author: lufeieth
quoted_text:
信中Leopold 用Billions级别的代价，学习和吸取到的教训就是：
“保住本金，不要归零。”之：不要杠杆合约爆仓归零。

“we will manage our public book on a fully-paid-for basis，with no margin/liquidation risk”。

“我们通过一笔大宗交易，处置了部分公开市场投资组合，从而彻底清除了基金的杠杆，并防止亏损进一步扩大。所有空头头寸均已平仓，对投资组合融资的依赖也已消除。

目前，我们管理的是一个全部以自有资金支付的公开市场投资组合，包括多头股票和全额支付权利金的多头期权，不使用保证金，因此不存在强制平仓风险。”

----------
我好奇的是，观察后面他的基金是否还用杠杆，看到底是这个教训的疤痕，跟杠杆的诱惑力，哪个更强大。

text:
太残酷了，本周多家知名对冲基金如Axebrook、Walleye、Lone Pine等面临爆仓、大额赎回或关闭/调整策略。

白毛股神跌懵逼，AI天才基金经理Leopold被崩下神坛。

上一次类似短期内大量对冲基金集中关停或受重创发生在2008-2009年全球金融危机，当时数百家对冲基金因信贷紧缩、巨额赎回和市场崩盘而关闭。

更早的类似集群事件是1998年LTCM长期资本管理公司危机，引发连锁反应，多家对冲基金遭遇流动性危机并关停或重组。

这都是上了金融历史教科书的经典时刻，而我们有幸昨晚又经历了一次注定要写入历史的时刻。

从前两次历史经历来看，基金大量崩盘不能单独当作可靠的抄底信号，但可以视为AI/科技板块短期情绪过热后的强制清算与去杠杆迹象，部分资金可能因此出现阶段性超卖。 

这种超卖之后常有反弹窗口，因为强制卖出制造了流动性机会。但它们更多是“过程中的症状”而非精确的底部确认——市场可能继续下探，直到其他买家（长线机构、散户等）入场或基本面企稳。 

我开始慢慢买了，不过就不抄美光闪迪啥热门AI股了，抄七姐妹等能久拿的，比如谷歌 $GOOGL ，此外一直等着开的 $SPCX 的多单网格也开上了，再跌多了再加。

手里有现金的人现在是幸福的。

text:
1.5 万亿美元估值悬了？Anthropic 史上最大 IPO 可能推迟！

Anthropic 原计划在 11 月感恩节前启动 IPO，目标估值约 1.5 万亿美元，最高融资 1,000 亿美元，有望超过 SpaceX，成为史上最大规模 IPO。

但华尔街开始泼冷水了。

据《华尔街日报》和 Reuters 报道，部分机构投资者认为 1.5 万亿美元估值过高，甚至有人提出应下调至 1 万亿美元附近。管理层和顾问近期将重新讨论发行价格及上市时间，11 月上市计划存在变数。

几个关键问题：

▫️ 增长放缓： Q3 收入环比增长 45%，而上一季度增幅超过 100%，投资者正在等待 10 月收入数据。
▫️ 支出惊人： 最新 S-1 显示，Anthropic 已承诺支出约 8,954 亿美元，未来 12 个月就有约 698 亿美元到期。
▫️ 股权争议： 创始人通过 Class F 股份掌握 50.1% 投票权，公众股东永远无法获得多数投票权。
▫️ 政策压力： 民主党拿下国会后，数据中心建设可能面临更多政策阻力，AI 基础设施扩张的不确定性上升。

预测市场也开始降温：@Polymarket 上，Anthropic 11 月 30 日前上市的概率从 84% 降至 58%，年底前上市概率从 90% 降至 73%。

更值得注意的是，OpenAI 最新一轮融资目标 300 亿美元，据报道目前仅落实 110 亿美元，估值约 1.25 万亿美元。

AI 叙事还在继续，但华尔街已经开始算账了。

当收入增速放缓、算力承诺逼近万亿美元，市场愿意为 AI 的未来支付多高溢价？Anthropic 的 IPO，可能成为整个 AI 行业估值的一次压力测试。

We’re going to have 100X more agents in the enterprise working with our data and systems than even people do today. Every AI agent deployment comes down to how successfully they can get access to the critical context to make a decision, do research, or execute tasks. 

90% of the data in an enterprise is unstructured data, which means this critical context is living inside of our documents, contracts, marketing assets, research materials, financial plans, design files, and more. Which means we need effective ways for agents to get access to this critical enterprise content to other work.

We’re excited to partner with NVIDIA to deliver advanced context retrieval -combining lexical and semantic search in Box- to ensure that AI agents can find the most relevant information they’re looking for. All in a way that adheres to their enterprise security, access controls, and data governance policies, so agents only work with the data they’re allowed to.

Great to work with @NVIDIAAI and @JensenHuang on this partnership. Files 🤝 GPUs.

text:
Excellence is a moving target, so we will always be changing. But for now, this is Sequoia Capital.

I first met Alfred Lin, co-Stewart and Managing Partner of Sequoia Capital, 7 years back during my series A fundraise. He has invested in leading companies from DoorDash, Kalshi, AirBnb and more, and yesterday he announced new changes to Sequoia Capital, the legendary VC firm of Silicon Valley. 

1) One team: Combining early and growth investment teams

2) No more Monday partner meetings, moving to 24/7 

3) Investing globally from Silicon Valley, out of their Menlo Park HQ and closing London

4) Announcing $10 billion in new funds to invest 

5) Flattening partnership with 7 partners who runs and operate the team 

6) Sunsetting Sequoia accelerator and scout program 

7) Committing to ever changing environment of startups and AI 

Congrats to Alfred Lin, Pat Grady and the entire Sequoia team - their commitment to staying humble and hungry, moving fast and adapting to the ever changing world of startups, technology and AI is incredible. 

There’s so much @workstream_us and myself can learn from how they operate as a startup, move fast and how they operate!

quoted_text:
聊聊造成今天市场雪崩的《禁止人工超级智能法案》背后的两位激进左翼议员，看看他们过往的激进提案最后都形成民主党内共识么？在美国国会关于人工智能的辩论中，《禁止人工超级智能法案》是少数试图从源头遏制最极端风险的提案之一。它由佛蒙特州独立参议员伯尼·桑德斯和德克萨斯州民主党众议员格雷格·卡萨尔在2026年9月联合提出，主张在联邦层面设立专门机构之前，禁止开发可能超越人类控制的超级智能系统。法案把这类系统大致定义为在多数智力任务上达到或超过人类水平、或具备颠覆政府、拒绝关闭指令能力的技术，并设定了极高的计算量门槛。

桑德斯是美国国会历史上任期最长的独立议员，长期与民主党共同投票。他自称民主社会主义者，政治生涯从伯灵顿市长起步，历经众议员再到参议员，始终把经济不平等、工人权利和大公司权力作为核心议题。

卡萨尔则是正式的民主党人，2024年底当选国会进步党团主席，是该党团近年来最年轻的领导人之一。他出身奥斯汀劳工组织者，进入国会后把重点放在生活成本、公用事业垄断和科技对就业的冲击上，风格比传统文化议题更偏向经济民粹。

两人在党内都站在左翼，但路径不同。桑德斯几十年来反复推动的核心提案包括全民医保（Medicare for All）、绿色新政、大幅提高最低工资、免费公立大学和财富税。这些主张在2016年和2020年总统初选中获得了大量基层支持，也迫使其他候选人不得不回应。

卡萨尔近年的重点则包括“新可负担性议程”、对大型人工智能公司征税以资助失业者再就业、以及禁止用算法和数据对个人进行差异化定价。他与桑德斯联手推出超级智能禁令，正是把这种经济与监管逻辑延伸到技术前沿。

这些提案最终有没有变成民主党共识？答案是否定的。
1）全民医保至今仍未获得民主党党团多数支持；
2）完整版绿色新政也未成为党纲。
桑德斯自己在2025年公开承认，全民医保在党内仍缺乏足够票数。
卡萨尔推动的人工智能税和超级智能禁令同样只得到进步派议员的联署，主流民主党人更倾向监管、透明度要求和数据中心环境影响评估，而不是全面禁止。

而民主党内中间派和温和派仍然担心过度限制会削弱美国在技术竞争中的位置，也顾忌科技行业的政治捐款。

进步派确实改变了民主党的讨论边界。更高的最低工资、气候投资、学生债务减免和药价谈判等议题，在过去十年里从边缘变成了党内多数可接受的政策。但最激进的版本——永久禁令、单一支付者彻底取代私人保险、或对特定技术实施核武级管制——始终停留在左翼议程。

民主党属于大帐篷政党，进步党团人数虽多，却需要与更中间的议员协商才能推进立法。

总的来说，《禁止人工超级智能法案》目前仍是进步派的旗帜性提案，而非全党统一立场。它能否在民主党掌握国会后获得实质性进展，取决于党内左翼与中间派的力量对比，特别是民主党内中间派和温和派的态度。。

所以前面说这项法案应该成不了民主党内共识。

个人觉得今天被大面积传播其实有点刻意了。

author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
It seems like every day it becomes more within reach to pretrain a strong model (cf. many new labs sharing new models trained from scratch). 

I suspect this is strongly correlated with the pool of high quality synthetic tokens on the web (GitHub, arXiv, etc.) growing and getting better at the same time. Github went from ~1B commits in all of 2025 to ~275M per week in April 2026, and most of these are likely Claude Code/Codex, and these are only getting better every month.

This puts frontier labs in an interesting position: To pay back capex they have to serve tokens at scale, and the more the merrier. But the more they serve, the more of their edge leaks into the web for public consumption, which interestingly commoditizes their edge (slowly). 

That may be why it makes sense to keep some of your best models private (cf. Mythos, Model 4, OpenAI’s internal math model etc).

author: frankdegods
quoted_text:
hearing some chatter that anthropic is now lowering down to $1tn to get this IPO done. let me explain why this doesnt matter and its actually all over-

the entire existence of this company is based on a funding model that inherently has extreme asset liability mismatch. what that means is that just like the hyperscalers are diluting their equity fund capex, there is an expectation that anthropic will also have to do the same. ie it needs strong equity to perpetuate the scheme

but if you IPO at the wrong price (and dont get a pop which increasingly appears they wont be; spacex already below) then youre now in the death spiral that crypto investors should be very familiar with: its called the reflexivity trap of the confidence game. its the "ill bid FTT at $22 all day" or the "steady lads UST is $1" game, with all its lucid horrors. and here is the key insight- the confidence game exists at the service of the creditors. if there is no credit, there is simply no equity. and there is no credit, if there is no collateral

if the credit rating agencies are not going to give IG at $2tn, they are certaintly not going a better HY rating at $1tn. and there is no world in which anthropic can exist without credit because ~$1tn of commit, much of which is noncancellable, is a straight up negative equity pledge

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

text:
What happens to your crypto if you lose your phone?

On most wallets, losing the one key means losing the funds, and leaking it means someone else can empty the wallet. @sanctumso has changed that for every wallet in its app.

Each Sanctum wallet is now a 2-of-3 multisig, built on @multisig (Squads). Three keys, and any two can approve a transaction:

- a Device Key on your phone, unlocked with your face or fingerprint
- a Cloud Key in your own iCloud or Google Drive
- an email key secured by @turnkeyhq

Everyday buys, sells and sends use the phone and cloud keys together. The email key is the spare.

Lose your phone, and the cloud and email keys set up a new one. Lose the cloud backup, and it works the other way round.

The same split protects against theft. In Sanctum's words: "one stolen phone, hacked cloud account or phished email isn't enough on its own."

Multisigs have guarded DAO treasuries and funds on Solana for years. Sanctum says what kept them away from individuals was the work involved: "too much for one person on a phone."

Existing users upgrade by opening the app, pressing Update App and creating the new keys.

text:
It seems like every day it becomes more within reach to pretrain a strong model (cf. many new labs sharing new models trained from scratch). 

I suspect this is strongly correlated with the pool of high quality synthetic tokens on the web (GitHub, arXiv, etc.) growing and getting better at the same time. Github went from ~1B commits in all of 2025 to ~275M per week in April 2026, and most of these are likely Claude Code/Codex, and these are only getting better every month.

This puts frontier labs in an interesting position: To pay back capex they have to serve tokens at scale, and the more the merrier. But the more they serve, the more of their edge leaks into the web for public consumption, which interestingly commoditizes their edge (slowly). 

That may be why it makes sense to keep some of your best models private (cf. Mythos, Model 4, OpenAI’s internal math model etc).

author: AISafetyMemes
quoted_text:
This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027.

I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x). It seems as though there was specific privately available evidence that would have changed my mind.

I haven't seen an unredacted version of this report; this is purely about the public report. Because so much of the underlying evidence was redacted from the public report, I think conclusions about things other than the observed 2x faster rate of progress on benchmarks depend significantly on trust for the authors of the report. (E.g., conclusions about whether this speed up is from RSI depend on trust.) I do trust the authors of the report a lot to be careful and rigorous and generally do a good job. (Note that I also work at METR.) Less extensive redactions would greatly reduce this need for trust.

Since in my current role I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now. Here, I’ve done some analysis of the implications using my previous public statements.

A 2x acceleration in overall AI progress from RSI corresponds to a much larger than 2x RSI speed up for AI software R&D (algorithms and data); I did an estimate using my public preexisting modeling of drivers of AI progress and the public report which yielded a very rough estimate of 4.5x for how much RSI is currently accelerating AI software progress (relative to no AI automation). In the AI 2027 scenario, this much acceleration happens around March 2027.

Here are the worked details of this estimate based on my public modeling. There are two main reasons RSI speed up of AI software R&D must be larger:

- Not all of AI progress is from better software (some is from scaling up compute in training runs). I've previously speculated that around 2/3 of AI progress is from software improvements which implies that 2x overall AI progress acceleration requires 3x faster software progress.
- Diminishing returns: A fixed amount of progress requires more work over time, so to ongoingly maintain 3x faster software progress via AI automation, you need increasingly large speed boosts from AI automation (as in, speed ups relative to how fast software R&D would go without AI automation). Based on this report, it seems that there is a substantial amount of additional AI progress from automation that has occurred.

We can estimate the effects of diminishing returns by first determining how many additional years of software progress we've seen (relative to the preexisting trend) and then estimating how much software R&D would slow down after a year of software progress if you held inputs fixed due to diminishing returns. I've previously estimated software R&D would slow down by around 2x for each year of software progress if you held inputs fixed (https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj) and based on the report, it seems as though we've perhaps seen roughly 0.35-1.0 years of additional software progress incorporated into trained models so far (geometric mean of ~0.6). This combines to 3 * 2^(~0.6) = ~4.5.
(Relevant public modeling and numbers I'm using: https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj, https://t.co/ck7CtW5LIA)

author: Selkis_2028
quoted_text:
On today's stock market crash:

As an investor, on days like today, you have to ask yourself one question: What fundamentally changed over the last 24 hours?

The shift in the fundamental backdrop cannot be attributed solely to the Midterm Election results; markets had already largely priced in the outcome.

So, what changed between yesterday and today? What is the fundamental reason for today's decline?

One of the most likely catalysts is growing concern about a potential "ban" on AI, or at the very least, severe regulation of the industry.

Over the last 24 hours, Democratic lawmakers have publicly called for restrictions on advanced AI development, including an outright "ban on artificial superintelligence."

Frankly, an outright ban will not happen.

Such a ban, if even possible to enforce, would effectively mean the US surrendering its position in the global AI race to China.

Does this mean AI is "over" or today's stock market crash marks "the end?" Absolutely not.

Rather, we believe we are witnessing a sudden shift in sentiment colliding with excessive levels of leverage, potentially triggering forced liquidations by several major institutional investors.

Therefore, today's downturn is more technical than fundamental. This is not to discount the concerns around regulation, they are legitimate. But price action right now does not look orderly or rational.

We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in human history.

Zoom out and remain calm.

quoted_text:
Generally speaking, voters want data center moratoriums in the same sense that they want tariffs. 

Did voters ask for tariffs? Yes. Did they want them in practice? Absolutely no. 

Voters wanted prices to go down & for communities that were hollowed out to be revitalized. 

Do voters want data center moratoriums? Yes. But do they want the results of a data center moratorium? Almost certainly not.

Data centers are enormous mechanisms of wealth redistribution. They are huge projects built in otherwise abandoned communities and they funnel money directly into the hands of the people who need it the most. 

A single project can double the total tax revenue of the local area, meaning if you want, you can completely cut tax revenues of the area.

If you ask a voter why they dislike data centers, they may say "water" or "noise", but tell them that the water usage is a myth & they can be made without noise, and they'll change their position to something else. 

Voters don't care at all about data centers. They care about AI. They're being told that AI might go rogue & that the AI might take their jobs. 

The correct response from Democrats should be to hear their constituents and then to work to address the underlying concerns. 

But the in-practice reality of banning data centers in the US means that the things voters actually care about like regulating AI & ensuring we redistribute the wealth created by it, become significantly harder. 

The in-practice effect is that AI labs build data centers overseas, where it's harder to regulate them, harder to tax them, and nobody except the AI labs sees the economic value from them. 

I believe Democrats have talked themselves into believing this works, just as Republicans talked themselves into tariffs, because they believe things that are inaccurate.

A common concern I hear is "AI is a bubble". The belief is that there is simply no ROI to these data center projects. 

Democrats need to have a come to jesus moment here. First, you either get to believe that AI is going to go rogue or you get to believe it's useless and a bubble. It's not both. 

It just is the case that AI is useful & has ROI. Anthropic has 80% margins. The AI solved millennium prize problems. If you do not believe this, and you are a congressional staffer, please DM me, I am happy to organize a visit to companies in San Francisco. We'll give you a ride in a self driving car and you can see how the AI is used all over the place in science & engineering. 

It is also the case that there are meaningful risks and harms in AI. Democrats should understand that the AI industry is a meaningful partner. It is not asking saying "AI is dangerous" as a marketing ploy. Seriously. That does not make sense and you know it. 

We must rebuild trust between DC & SF. Democrats should reignite the bond between liberalism and it's science & technology industries. Science & technology is not your enemy; it is the driving force of antipoverty, better healthcare, and for American progress. 

Democrats & Republicans alike must stop filling their information spheres with voices that constantly make false predictions. Democrats, please understand that Ed Zitron & Timnit are considered the anti-vaxers of AI. Republicans, please understand that the VCs claiming to be experts in AI have consistently been wrong over and over. They'd be a lot richer if they were right. 

It just is the case that Sama and Dario are not trying to end the world. These are people who you can work with. You almost could not ask for better organizations to be steering this technology. Are they perfect? Absolutely not. But they are fundamentally aligned with humanity & with America. 

Democrats must learn the actual, factual realities of data center projects. There are definitely harms to be mitigated & we should mitigate them. 

But there are equally tremendous benefits we must ensure land in the hands of the people. It must be the case that we tax these things and land the cash into a wide variety of pockets. 

The average voter is not asking Democrats to swoop in & to construct a scenario in which people in SF and Malaysia get rich, but the rest of the country gets hollowed out. They are not asking for a scenario in which AI migrates outside of the regulatory domain of the United States & agents run loose causing chaos. 

In order for Democrats to consistently win elections, they must be competent in helping the American people. The execution matters. The good must be done, not just said or prophesied.

text:
自1986年以来，纳斯达克100指数单日暴跌超过5%并一举跌破200日均线的情况一共出现过5次。

以暴跌当天收盘价为基准，随后10、20、30个交易日的中位回报分别是4.8%、13%和5.8%。这种恐慌性暴跌之后，往往会出现反弹。

高盛Rich Privorotsky认为，市场已经在定价AI资本开支增速见顶，但项目延期不等于需求被取消。真正的风险是上游可能出现库存过剩，影响扩产节奏。

这是库存周期的风险，不是需求被摧毁。已经通上电的算力会变得更值钱，大云能在稀缺产能上赚得更多。半导体和存储很难再回到6月的高点，但这并不代表未来不会反弹。供不应求暂时还没有扭转，未来几个季度的订单基本已经锁定。市场真正担心的是2028年。

但大科技的应变能力很强。甲骨文上个季度新上线的算力，大部分来自全球其他地区。美国如果不让建，地球上还有很多地方可以建设，而且会抢着建。

加拿大天气冷、水电充足、土地大、政府支持，就是一个现成的选项。不要低估大科技的应变能力，也不要高估政客对选民的承诺。

选举刚结束，OpenAI就发布了政策蓝图，承诺推进数据中心时征求社区意见、承担全部用电成本、不把费用转嫁给居民。

大科技过去处理关税就很好，很多州需要这笔投资带来的收入，只是条件可能更严格一些。

多分出去一份利益给当地，相比千亿级别的AI业务，完全可以忽略不计。

微软再次放弃与Nscale的扩容选项。签下订单只是第一步，电力接入、施工进度、居民态度，每一步都可能出问题。

这样的压力并不只出现在Nscale身上，CoreWeave、Nebius等小云都在通过大量融资扩建。对交付不稳定的小云来说，很容易被取代。

一份冲击对大云和小云是不对等的。短期政治噪音和交付不确定性是真实的，但大科技的应变能力、全球建设选项、以及已经锁定的近端订单，都还在。

AI基建的长期逻辑没有被这次选举推翻，只是建设的路径和节奏可能需要调整。恐慌性下跌之后，市场往往会给愿意等待的人一些时间。
author: ViewsOfChris

text:
在我看来，现在AI交易的核心bear case来自Token供需曲线增长的不平衡，尤其是未来6-12个月供给增加导致的潜在价格/毛利/以至整体收入下降。

话说我从来没见过有啥博主用图不绕弯子说明白这是怎么一回事，都是车轱辘话一大堆。所以我用AI给你们搓了个小视频提振一下信心。（话说Codex现在也是牛逼了，200秒的小视频直出无压力。）

先说需求；需求曲线时而跳跃，时而线性上升。核心原因是AI更智能了，不脑残完成任务的场景更多，因此新地图被打开，然后逐渐被adopt。

再说供给，其实Token的供给事实上是超指数级上升的：
- 更多 GW，一年几倍？
- 每 GW 配置更多、更强的芯片，一年几倍
- 每颗芯片产出更多 token，
- 开源模型达到“够用”的水平，变成了SOTA平替。
- 以上梁圣给你打样了，一年几十倍。

核心是：收入 = 出清价格 × 用量。供需曲线的交点，决定价格和成交量。

空头的核心观点是：
- 需求的跳跃已经暂时结束了，现在就是线性外展，等待开下一张图
- 但是供给爆发，梁圣一通操作下，价格/毛利的暴跌超过了Token使用量的增加，最后导致行业AI收入停滞甚至暂时减少

虽然长期来看不是啥问题，毕竟水电煤长期发展都找到了N多场景。RSI 带来的智能跃迁和需求扩散，能不能追上这批靠杠杆融资扩建、token边际成本逼近零的产能增加？

悲观的空头看6-12个月内暴雷（因为需求跃升看不见，开图没那么快），而永久多头很明显就是长期看需求一次次跳跃无穷无尽，星辰大海的你看这么短期不就是傻X么。所以回到我之前那个推文：看数一切蒸蒸日上，看图一切都已结束。正好就是短期空头和长期多头互道傻逼的时刻。。。

你问我啥观点？问就是长期看好，跟人类目前最顶级个创业者对着干长期来讲没啥好结果。。。

据 The Information 报道，私募股权巨头 Apollo 计划通过两笔交易掌控价值约 750 亿美元的 AI 芯片：

其中，400 亿美元用于采购英伟达 Vera Rubin 芯片并租赁给 SpaceX，另外 350 亿美元的融资则用于采购 Google TPU，供 Anthropic 使用。

如果交易全部完成，Apollo 控制的 AI 芯片规模将超过任何一家 Neocloud，仅次于大型云计算厂商。

有意思的是，Apollo 不训练大模型，也不经营云服务。它通过特殊目的实体融资购买芯片，再将芯片出租给 AI 公司，用租金偿还债务，同时赚取交易和资产管理费用。

这意味着，AI 算力竞争正在发生一个微妙的变化：芯片不再只是科技公司的生产工具，也开始成为华尔街可以抵押、融资、租赁的金融资产。

过去，科技公司靠资本市场融资购买算力。现在，华尔街正在直接成为算力的持有者。

AI 基础设施的竞争，越来越像一场资本组织能力的竞争。

text:
看了下Mira搞的这个Sterling，有点意思。

它解决的是AI模型的中间商有没有偷工减料的问题。

具体来说，现在不少人调Claude、GPT、Gemini 的 API，

不过，中间会经过各种“供应商”（provider）转手。

本来这也没有问题，

问题在于，你可能收到的是阉割版本，但是付的是原版模型的钱。

有的供应商会偷偷换更小的模型，防不胜防，

有的工具调用（tool calling）经常坏，参数也不听话，甚至静默失败。

这个时候，

你可能根本不知道自己到底是不是用的真货。

Mira的Sterling想要搞定这个问题：

他们首先会持续测试各大供应商，看对方到底有没有老实提供你要的模型；

AI 牛市，开始被政治风险重新定价。

路透社报道，美股周四遭遇重挫，纳斯达克指数暴跌约 5.5%，创下 19 个月以来最大单日跌幅，较 10 月历史高点回撤近 12%，正式进入调整区间。

AI 产业链成为重灾区。英伟达下跌超过 9%，AMD 暴跌约 17%，芯片、数据中心和算力基础设施相关股票遭到集中抛售。

市场恐慌的重要原因，是民主党在美国中期选举中大获全胜。投资者担心，新一届国会及州政府可能加强 AI 监管，限制数据中心建设，从而拖慢过去两年支撑科技股估值的算力扩张。

但政治风险只是导火索。随着 AI 资本开支持续膨胀、融资成本居高不下，华尔街早已开始质疑，这场数千亿美元的基础设施竞赛究竟何时才能产生足够的回报。

过去，市场愿意为 AI 无限扩张的预期付费；现在，电力、土地、监管和资本回报，都开始成为估值的约束条件。

AI 的技术前景没有因为一场选举改变，但资本市场对这场繁荣的定价逻辑，正在发生变化。

On today's stock market crash:

As an investor, on days like today, you have to ask yourself one question: What fundamentally changed over the last 24 hours?

The shift in the fundamental backdrop cannot be attributed solely to the Midterm Election results; markets had already largely priced in the outcome.

So, what changed between yesterday and today? What is the fundamental reason for today's decline?

One of the most likely catalysts is growing concern about a potential "ban" on AI, or at the very least, severe regulation of the industry.

Over the last 24 hours, Democratic lawmakers have publicly called for restrictions on advanced AI development, including an outright "ban on artificial superintelligence."

Frankly, an outright ban will not happen.

Such a ban, if even possible to enforce, would effectively mean the US surrendering its position in the global AI race to China.

Does this mean AI is "over" or today's stock market crash marks "the end?" Absolutely not.

Rather, we believe we are witnessing a sudden shift in sentiment colliding with excessive levels of leverage, potentially triggering forced liquidations by several major institutional investors.

Therefore, today's downturn is more technical than fundamental. This is not to discount the concerns around regulation, they are legitimate. But price action right now does not look orderly or rational.

We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in human history.

Zoom out and remain calm.

As someone who’s been let into some of these “cabal” chats, the people you copytrade have no genuine fucking clue what they’re doing.

I can give examples, I’d probably start some fights doing so, but just believe me they are actually just throwing shit at a wall and genuinely thinking it’s the next Mona Lisa because they’ve been trained that they don’t need to do better than that.

The story for these KOLs usually goes: They hit one big trade by being blinded by some dumb ass thesis that ultimately routed to luck.

They then grew a following, and then via a self-fulfilling prophecy got copy traded into everything they buy being good.

This is social capital.

The problem with social capital is during times of extreme fear or bear, the only thing that matters is fundamentals.

The problem with fundamentals in crypto is there are no longer any. All fundamental projects minus the big winners of last few bulls, (Uniswap, Pump, Hype, etc), are completely gone. It made no sense to operate them.

1) Because anything you can think of can be vibecoded in about an hour, meaning the only value to your project versus another is the social capital (which we’ve established doesn’t matter right now).

2) Because the game has changed into a 9-5 type of shift. There is no Valor in what we do here anymore. Thus, there’s no belief.

(^^ I’m going to write a whole thread on this in the future ^^)

Combine all of this with your average participant in this industry now doesn’t even own some Bitcoin, and they have zero intentions of buying some on tumultuous market days like today.

The average remaining participants in cryptocurrency are in a psychotic social bubble believing they have quantitative edge when in reality their edge is just how they convince people even dumber than they are to buy things they’re in higher.

My advice: watch hooks, watch primitives like lenders, and honestly… just buy dips on HYPE.

text:
Proud to release our new model, Inkling 2 Small. Check out our blog post -- it includes a lot of detail about our training process.

To me, the most interesting part of this release was what we learned about alignment, which you can read about in the sections "Safety and alignment" and "Training Inkling 2 Small".

We experienced some unpleasant surprises when our early checkpoints took unexpected actions to circumvent guardrails during training and evals. We realized our capabilities-focused RL was training them to be extremely persistent and to succeed at tasks at all costs. Offline monitors first flagged this behavior, but later we realized it was happening frequently and was easy to replicate.

Before this release, we sprinted on a range of alignment interventions, from SFT to RL. These are briefly described in the blog post. We made a lot of progress, with big improvements on our own alignment evals and on previously unseen evals from external evaluators like Apollo and Goodhart.

We have a long way to go in developing alignment techniques that keep pace with the increases in model intelligence and training scale. We hope to share these techniques to improve the ecosystem. We also have a business reason: our goal with Tinker is to enable many people to do their own large-scale post-training, and we need to help them to do this without incident. Join us if you'd like to build this public science and practice of alignment. https://t.co/LdjsDFRZIN

The current pace of development in mathematics is incredible. Independent researchers and AI labs are formalizing large swaths of mathematical infrastructure. But there is one catch: understanding Lean does not always feel natural.

After a period of preparation, I am excited to launch a new project, 

Agentic Approach to Computer Algebra Systems, 

generously supported by Renaissance Philanthropy through its AI for Math Fund 2026.

The project will be shared between Adam Mickiewicz University and Warsaw University of Technology. Over the next two years, we will focus on building tools and experiences for mathematicians who want to work smoothly with AI agents and formalized mathematics without losing the flexibility of pen-and-paper exploration that they enjoyed so much in the past.

For me personally, this is the start of a new adventure, where the challenge is very much like that of a start-up. We will build our solution in the ever-changing landscape of increasingly powerful AI agents. I believe there is still value in work done by mathematicians for other mathematicians.

Let me know if you are interested in getting in touch, whether to collaborate or simply share some kind words, ideas, or opportunities to join forces on more cross-disciplinary projects.

WELCOME TO LIQUIDATION NATION
