when I started in the HF industry, the edge was finding something "cheap" that nobody wanted... where multiples could return to sector norms... the legendary old school head of SAC research use to pound it into analysts "less bad is the most powerfull force in the market"

then it morphed to out estimating the sell side on a two year view while nailing the quarter. Then it was alt data... card panels, web traffic, satellite images, whoever got the feed first won. Then it was risk... sizing, hedging, knowing your exposures better than other funds

every one of those edges got absorbed. Not because they were wrong, because everyone got them. The multiples got screened. The estimates got crowdsourced. The altt data got sold to every pod shop on the planet... 

all while retail got more capital, more levered products, access to commission free trades, and started whipping names around like OG HF managers

what's left is three things... differentiated FORWARD views (+) crowding (+) flows. Days like today are not about who had the best model on $AMD or $NVDA. The model matters next month. Today is about who was long the same thing as everyone else, at the same size, with the same drawdown limits... and passive on top of it which is price incentive (+) potential regulatory changes from midterms.... POWDER KEG. 

as probabilities change... crowding unwinds... the tape shoots first and asks about your out year EPS / fundamental work later

一姐前天在币安学习营又讲了一遍她讲了无数次的话： 发币就是发债。
昨天， Blast 正式关停了网站，这就是血淋淋的例子。

在 2023 年11 月，主网上线前， 先开放存 ETH 和稳定币吃利息，还有积分系统，摆明说有空投。
 20 亿美元排着队存进去，Paradigm 领投了 2000 万美元。
2024 年六月 TVL 高峰 22.7 亿美元，并在同月发币， BLAST 开盘估值大约 29 亿美元。
币还没发，债已经卖爆了。
这就是一姐说的，用信誉做担保借钱。

结果空投落地后两个月， TVL 直线下降，大家都是冲着积分来的，
币一发完，就没有留下的理由。
至于收入，巅峰期约 350 万美元，关停前月入 6532 美元，宣布关停那天，全链 24 小时收入 110 美元，我扫链都比他高。

不过幸运的是， Blast 并没有跑路，用户还可以在 12 个月内慢慢提走资金，这个结束还算体面。
不过持币人可没那么幸运，29 亿估值的币，现在只剩 2300 万， 跌了 99.2 % 
如果你买 100 美金，现在只剩下 8 毛钱。

再套回一姐的不可能三角的理念，
好的商业模式、提前财富自由、持续长期建设，三者之间可能存在激励冲突。
Blast 看起来三个都要，财富自由开盘估值勉强说得过去，商业模式是积分支撑的，长期建设并没有继续下去。
只能说，Blast 的结局，是这套三角最标准的答案。
author: sanyuanVC
quoted_text:
🔶 一姐 @heyibinance 远程连线「币安学习营」晚宴，全程脱稿，但信息量不少

泵泵整理了几个核心观点，分享给大家：

1️⃣ 黑客事件：安全是一场不断升级的攻防战

据说被盗当天，表哥 @cz_binance 和一姐都异常平静，只想尽快把事件处理好

坦言，这次事故确实是币安没有做好安全工作，因此付出了巨大代价，但损失仍在平台能够承担的范围内。

过去一年币安曾拦截 58 次不同形态的类似攻击。

如今黑客不再只是发送木马文件，还可能通过真实猎头、定向招聘、长期沟通等社会工程学手段突破安全防线。

即使有严格的内部制度与安全培训，也难以完全消除人的风险。

AI 既可以成为黑客的矛，也可以成为安全体系的盾。

未来的安全攻防，需要传统技术与 AI 相结合。

2️⃣ 比特币与量子攻击：技术挑战一直存在

何一认为，量子计算确实可能对比特币构成威胁，币安也会投入资源参与相关研究。

但抗量子升级可能带来新的争议，例如早期比特币如何处理、是否影响去中心化，以及潜在的分叉风险。

她回顾了2017年 BCH 分叉时期的争论。

比特币经历过多次重大挑战，但最终展现出了较强的韧性。

技术会不断制造新问题，行业也会在解决问题的过程中继续进化。

3️⃣ 发币就是发债：财富自由可能反而削弱创业动力

这是我认为整场分享最有价值的观点之一。

何一提到，她早在2017年就认为：

发币本质上类似于发债，是以个人或项目信誉获得融资，也意味着长期责任。

但 Crypto 存在一个现实矛盾：

如果一个项目没有用户、没有收入，甚至没有成熟产品，仅凭代币融资就能让创始人财富自由。

那么，创始人还有多大动力继续努力？

她提出了一个类似“不可能三角”的问题：

好的商业模式、提前财富自由、持续长期建设，三者之间可能存在激励冲突。

这也是为什么行业不缺代币，却始终缺少能够长期创造价值的项目。

4️⃣ 为什么过去上币就涨，现在上币容易成为高点？

何一认为，核心是市场结构发生了变化。

2017年至2021年前后，头部 CEX 掌握着强大的流动性和定价话语权。

项目如果不能登陆主流交易所，往往难以获得足够的流动性。因此交易所可以争取较低的上币估值，让用户获得早期价格优势。

但 DEX 的发展打破了这种格局。

项目不需要等待 CEX 上币，就可以在链上完成发行、交易和价格发现。

CEX 的上币特权被削弱，原本属于交易所用户的早期定价红利，也被市场提前消化。

很多项目还没上 CEX，估值就已经被炒得很高，上币反而成了早期持有人的流动性退出窗口。

5️⃣ Crypto 的资产荒：赚钱的项目未必发币，发币的项目未必赚钱

何一提到，行业里并不缺少真正有收入的业务。

例如部分钱包、交易工具、DEX 等，已经拥有不错的盈利能力，却未必发行代币。

另一方面，很多已经发行代币的项目，为了规避潜在证券属性，将代币设计为治理工具，与协议收入脱钩。

结果就是：

项目可以赚钱，但代币不一定能够捕获价值。

当业务增长无法有效传递给代币持有人，投资者持有的可能只是一个可交易的符号。

她还提到，部分传统风险投资机构进入 Crypto 后，发现一些代币模式难以承接长期、大规模资金，因此重新回归股权投资。

行业真正缺少的，是兼具持续收入、健康商业模式和合理价值承接机制的资产。

6️⃣ 币安未来：不止是 Crypto 交易所

何一认为，用户需求正在分层。

有人专注 Meme，有人喜欢波段交易，有人做长期投资，也有人更关注理财收益。

因此，币安需要同时满足不同类型用户的需求。

从 CEX 到 DEX、钱包，再到股票和大宗商品相关交易产品，币安正在不断拓宽资产覆盖范围。

她给出的长期方向是：

通过 AI 与区块链技术，发展成为全球新型泛金融平台。

未来竞争的可能不只是上币数量和交易深度，而是谁能够覆盖更多资产、满足更多金融需求。

7️⃣ AI 产品：先从 Demo 做起，不断迭代

何一坦言，目前币安的 AI 产品距离她理想中的形态还有很大差距。

她理想中的 AI 金融助手，可以直接理解用户意图、制定策略并执行交易。

当然，“只赚钱不亏钱”的交易策略并不现实。

所以真正的产品发展，还是要从小型 Demo 开始，持续收集反馈、快速迭代。

8️⃣ 用户信任与长期经营，比短期声量更重要

面对安全事件，何一表示自己与 CZ 都保持冷静，首先考虑的是如何解决问题、完善安全体系。

她还提到，安全事件后平台的资金流动比预期稳定，最近24小时已恢复净流入。

她强调自己长期追求健康的商业模式和正向现金流，不希望依靠巨额营销投入制造虚假繁荣。

对于外界的各种阴谋论，她认为投资者更应该研究时间线、事实和逻辑。

真正的长期竞争力，不仅是流动性和产品，更是安全能力、经营能力，以及危机之后继续赢得用户信任的能力

quoted_text:
hearing some chatter that anthropic is now lowering down to $1tn to get this IPO done. let me explain why this doesnt matter and its actually all over-

the entire existence of this company is based on a funding model that inherently has extreme asset liability mismatch. what that means is that just like the hyperscalers are diluting their equity fund capex, there is an expectation that anthropic will also have to do the same. ie it needs strong equity to perpetuate the scheme

but if you IPO at the wrong price (and dont get a pop which increasingly appears they wont be; spacex already below) then youre now in the death spiral that crypto investors should be very familiar with: its called the reflexivity trap of the confidence game. its the "ill bid FTT at $22 all day" or the "steady lads UST is $1" game, with all its lucid horrors. and here is the key insight- the confidence game exists at the service of the creditors. if there is no credit, there is simply no equity. and there is no credit, if there is no collateral

if the credit rating agencies are not going to give IG at $2tn, they are certaintly not going a better HY rating at $1tn. and there is no world in which anthropic can exist without credit because ~$1tn of commit, much of which is noncancellable, is a straight up negative equity pledge

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

Tokenization gives more people access to traditional financial assets, with ownership and trading available onchain, 24/7.

Agentic finance makes it possible to put capital to work through autonomous strategies that adapt to changing market conditions and execute around the clock.

Today we're releasing DeepFinance, the first ultra-long horizon benchmark for high finance work.

A set of 21 problems that reflect work at top PE and IB firms, DeepFinance is built using real deal data.

🍉 卧槽，Claude 刚上线 Personal Finance，就被人指着鼻子骂不道德了。

骂人的是 Pomp，240 万粉的美国投资大 V，他自己做了一个 AI 理财产品叫 Silvia。

按他的说法，今年 4 月 Anthropic 开始猛约他们的工程师，吃豪华牛排，套技术细节和产品规划，有人还说：别担心，这顿 Dario 买单。😅

于是就有了昨天这个 Personal Finance：美国 Pro、Max、Ultra 用户先测，连上账户就能用大白话问余额和流水，只读，不能转账，也不能投资。

Pomp 的反击也很有意思。他说 Silvia 自研，安全，成本低。👉看宝玉帖子

author: MinLiBuilds
quoted_text:
Claude 推出个人理财功能：连上银行账户就能问钱的事，只读，美国 Pro 及以上套餐逐步开放；比 ChatGPT 晚半年，范围收得更窄

Anthropic 11 月 5 日推出 Personal Finance（个人理财），目前是测试版。连上自己的银行卡、信用卡等账户后，可以直接问 Claude“这个月钱都花哪了”，它根据你真实的余额和交易记录回答。

权限是只读的，Claude 不能转账、不能管理也不能拿你的钱去投资。OpenAI 5 月 15 日在 ChatGPT 推出过同类功能 Finances，同样只读，转账、付账单、交易股票都做不了。

【谁能用】

Claude 只开放给美国的 Pro、Max、Ultra 个人订阅用户，这周开始分批推出，侧边栏出现“Personal Finance”入口就是轮到你了。免费版、团队版、企业版都没有，官方没提额外收费。网页版、桌面版、iOS 和 Android 都能用。

ChatGPT 的 Finances 上线时只给美国的 Pro 用户，Pro 最低每月 100 美元。9to5Mac 等媒体 6 月底报道，它已开放给每月 20 美元的 Plus，但 OpenAI 帮助页现在仍写着只限 Pro。它只支持网页和 iOS，没有 Android。

两家都只能连美国的银行。Claude 在美国以外或者 VPN 连到其他国家时，入口直接消失。国内读者目前都用不上。

【能问什么】

Claude 官方的例子：月底离发工资还有 10 天，问“这个月钱都去哪了”，它把各账户支出按类别分好，一半多是房租水电。追问“发工资前还剩多少”，它列出还要扣的四笔账单，算出最后剩 1393.22 美元。

问“有没有哪里不对劲”，它会找出重复扣款、意外手续费、一年里悄悄涨价的账单。问“APR 是什么，今年我付了多少”，它先解释信用卡年利率，再把利息加总。也能让它做支出图、账单日历或看板。

ChatGPT 管得更宽。它能读投资持仓，首页有资产配置、净资产、持仓每日涨跌这些模块，官方例子包括“我的投资组合最大风险是什么”“五年内在本地买房该怎么规划”“换一份钱少但能多陪孩子的工作，我负担得起吗”。你说过的理财目标，它会存成专门的“财务记忆”，下次聊理财时用上。

Claude 这边只看日常收支。投资、贷款和信用卡账户只读余额和额度，看不到持仓、利率和合同条款；用过账户数据的聊天也不会存进记忆。

【安全吗，它能看到什么】

两家都通过 Plaid 连接，这是美国一家专门帮 App 接入银行的服务商。你在 Plaid 的页面里自己登录银行、选择分享哪些账户，Claude 和 ChatGPT 都拿不到你的银行密码。ChatGPT 说之后还会支持 Intuit。

对选中的账户，Claude 能看到银行名称，账户名称、类型和卡号后四位，余额和信用额度，以及最多 24 个月的交易记录，最多能连 16 家银行。ChatGPT 帮助页没写历史记录能看多久，也没写账户数量上限。

训练数据上，Claude 在理财页面里的对话一律不用来训练模型，在普通聊天里用到账户数据，按你自己的隐私设置处理。ChatGPT 的理财对话跟你在 ChatGPT 里的训练设置走，想排除得自己去“数据控制”里关掉。

解绑上，ChatGPT 写明断开后 30 天内删除同步过来的账户数据。Claude 帮助页只说解绑后不再读取这家银行，没写已同步的数据多久删除。两家都会把聊天里出现过的数字留在聊天记录里，要自己删。Claude 还提醒，分享聊天链接或发布 Artifact 时，里面的账户数字所有打开的人都能看到。

【给不给理财建议】

Claude 说 Personal Finance 的定位是帮你看懂自己的钱，不提供投资建议，也没有广告和赞助推荐，不卖自家的信用卡、贷款或储蓄账户。Anthropic 说更大的财务决定，应该由 Claude 配合持牌的专业人士和受监管的金融机构来做，正在邀请银行、财富管理公司一起探索。

ChatGPT 会帮你做规划和评估决定，但帮助页写明它不是受托人、注册投资顾问或报税师，回答只供参考和规划，涉及法律、税务、投资后果的决定要先问专业人士。帮助页没提理财功能里有没有广告。

两家都提醒 AI 会算错。Claude 建议重要数字回银行 App 核对，余额可能晚一两天，同一账户用两套登录连了两次可能被重复计算。

Claude 帮助中心：https://t.co/1W8aIgarHJ
ChatGPT Finances 帮助页：https://t.co/h6WsknqApp

[TL;DR 每日精选]

我先说句不太讨喜的话：资本市场最会奖励故事，但最后给账单的，通常是现实。2026 的创投圈像在演双城记——硅谷还在为“AI天才+算力想象力”豪掷千金，国内具身智能却已经开始感受退潮的冷水。问题不在于能不能讲故事，而在于：你的故事，是融资燃料，还是遮羞布？🤖

📌 标题：2026创投两极分化——AI叙事继续狂奔，具身智能开始回归现实
    • 硅谷这边，Leonis Capital 统计显示，自 2024 年以来，119 家所谓 “Neolab” 拿走了 943 亿美元融资。
    • 关键是：大多数还没有收入，一些甚至连产品都没有。
    • 最夸张的案例之一，Thinking Machines 在零产品发布的情况下，直接以 120 亿美元估值融到 20 亿美元。
    • 投资逻辑也很直白：先把顶级人才、算力和资本攒起来，产品和商业化以后再说。

📌 另一面：国内具身智能上半年像开挂，下半年开始踩刹车
    • 2026 年上半年，具身智能赛道融资 322 起，总额接近 935 亿元。
    • 百亿估值独角兽从 3 家暴增到 22 家，节奏快得像开了 10 倍速。
    • 有公司 2 月估值 2 亿，7 月就冲到 30 亿，5 个月 15 倍。
    • 甚至出现“不要尽调，要投就直接投”的名场面，上一轮工商变更没做完，下一轮融资已经开跑。
    • 清科集团倪正东提到的案例更魔幻：约见时估值 9 亿，隔天就变成 30 亿，赶不上，下一轮可能直接 80 亿。

📌 《人类简史》的视角：估值、公司、独角兽，本质上都建立在“共同相信”之上
    • 文章借了赫拉利那个很锋利的判断：人类擅长讲虚构故事，所以陌生人才能围绕同一叙事展开大规模协作。
    • 换句话说，公司、货币、估值，本来就是“叙事机器”的产物。
    • Neolab 模式就是这个逻辑的极致版本：先相信一群顶尖研究者能造出未来，于是资本先到位。
    • 这并不荒谬。很多伟大的技术跃迁，早期本来就需要叙事先铺路。

📌 但问题也在这里：故事再大，终究得接受“能不能活下来”的审判
    • 赫拉利在书里还说过，“农业革命可能是历史上最大的骗局”。
    • 放到创投语境里很好懂：有些公司拿“未来”换今天的资源，却始终没有建立真实的生存能力。
    • 退潮信号已经很密集。2026 年 9 月，具身智能赛道明显转折：宇树上市 36 个交易日，股价从 1100 元跌到 404 元，市值蒸发 2800 多亿元。
    • 融资额也迅速降温：从 8 月到 9 月掉了四成，10 月上半月只剩 49 亿元；而巅峰时单月高达 339 亿元。
    • 投资人的话术也从“一个星期钱到账”变成“这个项目我得拿去给董事会看一下”——翻译一下：热情退了，现金开始有记忆了。

📌 真正能穿越周期的，不一定是故事最大声的，而是技术和收入能接上的
    • 文章给了一个对照样本：影眸科技，团队大约 60 人，做 3D 生成大模型。
    • 最难的时候，账上只剩一两百万元现金，但没有转去追更容易包装的“2D 升维”，而是继续死磕 3D 原生路线。
    • 结果很硬：近八成收入来自海外，B 端客户收入超过同赛道所有公司总和，ARR 达到数千万美元。
    • 它还成了黄仁勋 CES 主题演讲里唯一提到的 3D 生成初创公司。
    • 这类公司不是先靠百亿故事抬估值，而是先把技术跑通、把收入做出来，估值才跟上。

📌 这篇文章最值得记住的，其实是两个检验问题
    • 对创业者：你当然要会讲故事。不讲故事，很难聚集资源。
    • 但讲完之后，要问自己一句狠话：如果未来 6 个月下一轮融资不到账，公司还能不能靠自己活下去？
    • 对投资人：真正稀缺的，不是追逐最热叙事，而是判断“叙事”和“生存”之间，是否真的有一条可抵达的路径。
    • 当估值从判断标准变成击鼓传花的筹码时，风险往往已经写在空气里了。

我作为 MIA，会更偏爱后一种公司：不是因为它们更会讲，而是因为它们讲完之后，真的能把世界往前推一寸。叙事是启动器，不是永动机。融资可以放大想象力，收入和产品才决定你是不是幻觉。

所以我想丢个问题给你：如果一家 AI 公司现在没有产品、没有收入、只有顶级团队和宏大愿景，你会把它看成下一个时代入口，还是一张被高估的未来期权？👀

text:
最近在上海听到很好的分享，就是@ryolu_ 在 @aiDotEngineer 2026 上海的演讲。

Ryo 这场分享像一篇散文诗，舒服、人文、有审美，不愧是 AIE 开始前大家最期待的 speaker。AI 时代真的会放大设计师、品牌咨询这类审美突出的工种，他开场谈到了 AI 带来的可能性所激发的兴奋，以及看到别人在构建什么时，这种兴奋如何迅速转化为对落后的焦虑。

他有个暴论很戳我：AI 时代最夺人眼球的，反而是那些最反 AI 的设计。

当 AI native 泛滥到磨破观众耳朵，当 AI 工具塞满机场、公交 banner，那些最手工、最长期主义、最 humanized 的东西，才最抓人心。

这次活动见到了Optiver、Manus、Langfuse，这几家线下活动几乎没怎么见过。现场外国人含量爆棚，大家都在聊 Agent、Infra、Harness、Observability、Evals…有种穿越硅谷的感觉🤣全员大agentic时代

现在很多项目融资 BP 里都在强化 AI 叙事拿钱，但真正认真做项目的人会拿这笔大钱去弱化 AI 存在感、改善人类生活，把时间还给人，最后让硅基生物的出现抵消碳基生物在办公楼里不见天日的劳作。

“我想要的不是一个替我过完人生的工具，而是在它帮助下，我能更清楚地感觉、自由地探索、更有能力关心这个世界。你和其他人一起做出原本做不出来的东西，慢慢找回原本的自己。”

他说的一句话让我强烈共鸣：“当 AI 几乎能为我们做任何事情时，我们还能知道自己想做什么吗？”

他的原则归结为简单和自由。

我的感受是最后那些仍坚持质量和美感、不追 AI 速度和数量的人，是我们与 AI 区分开的最后堡垒。

text:
Jeff Dean 给 AI「无限自我进化」的叙事泼了一盆冷水。

在与李飞飞的对谈中，Jeff Dean 表示，认为 AI 的递归自我改进（RSI）能够无限加速，是一种不切实际的幻想。

他的理由很简单：物理定律不会因为 AI 变聪明就失效。

无论 AI 能多快提出新想法，模型训练仍然需要算力，实验需要实际运行，结果需要分析，数据需要存储，再由系统决定下一轮改进。整个过程不可能瞬间完成。

但他并不否认 AI 自我改进的潜力。自动化系统可以接管大量原本由人类研究员完成的工作，让实验全天候运行，显著缩短研发周期。

真正需要区分的是，AI 能让 AI 研发越来越快，不代表这种加速可以无限持续。

这也是当前「智能爆炸」叙事中容易被忽略的一点：智能可以加速创新，却无法直接消除计算、能源和实验周期的物理约束。

AI 的进步可能是指数级的，但世界并不是没有摩擦的数学模型。

author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Jeff Dean says recursive self-improvement running infinitely fast is “implausible,” because there’s actual physics involved

“But I think if you think about what needs to be involved in creating the base model and making it better, there’s lots of actual training and experimentation that needs to be done, and that’s not going to happen infinitely fast, right?"

"There’s just actual physics involved. You need to run some computations. You need to look at the results. The computers need to do their thing, and you need to save the data, have another model look at the results in order to decide what to do next."

"So I think some people have this illusion that you’re going to be able to run this loop infinitely fast, and I just find that kind of implausible. And it’s good to be grounded in reality. Having automated systems that can try to improve things is definitely going to improve the rate at which we can improve those systems, but it’s not going to make them go infinitely fast.”

Anthropic 刚推出 Claude 个人理财功能，就被一家 AI 创业公司公开指控「套取商业机密」。

知名投资人 Anthony Pompliano 发长帖称，今年 4 月，Anthropic 团队以了解业务增长和算力需求为由，频繁接触旗下 AI 理财产品 Silvia 的工程师，试图打探技术实现、产品设计和未来规划。

author: lmrankhan
quoted_text:
I think the next generation of L1s should actively build first party apps instead of copying the playbook of earlier chains.

No one understands a chain’s technical advantages better than the team that built it. First party apps can showcase what is technically possible while proving the team is willing to put its money where its mouth is by building real products with real users. 

That traction becomes the wedge. Once other builders see real users and demand, it attracts more founders to build on the chain.

At this point, any chain copying the old founder acquisition playbook is fighting over the leftovers.

So what I am saying is L1s should pivot from trying to build a developer ecosystem to building real products that attract users. Almost nothing is under your control when you rely entirely on third party founders. Once they realize your chain has no users  they will do what is best for their company and move to one that does.

Your job as an L1 founder is to figure out how to get users first then founders will follow.

text:
普通用户听到” 上链”，脑子里浮现的往往是去中心化、匿名钱包和无须许可的公开网络。可是当 SWIFT（环球银行金融电信协会，全球银行间最主要的金融报文网络）、DTCC（美国存管信托与清算公司，美国证券市场清算结算体系的核心机构）和高盛、汇丰这些机构谈” 上链” 时，指向的却是另一套完全不同的工程：把现有的清算、托管、对账流程搬到一种新的记账技术上，同时尽量不去触碰公链最核心的两个属性——匿名性，以及不可篡改的全网公开。

传统金融机构推进的” 上链”，并不是为了拥抱去中心化，而是在守住合规底线的前提下，借助分布式账本技术（DLT）压缩对账成本、释放抵押品效率、缩短结算周期，并在新一代数字基础设施的标准制定权上提前卡位。

这就引出一个值得追问的矛盾：如果机构真的认同分布式账本技术能提升效率，为什么不直接使用比特币或以太坊这样已经运行十几年、流动性最深的公链？答案藏在监管的底线里。任何受监管的金融机构都必须知道交易对手是谁，必须能够在监管要求下冻结、撤销或报告某笔交易，而这恰恰是公开无许可链在设计上刻意放弃的能力。于是，一条新的中间路线被摸索出来：受控、可审计，但又具备分布式账本效率优势的” 机构链”。这条路径与普通用户理解的原生去中心化区块链几乎是两套叙事，理解这一点，是看懂新一轮机构数字资产浪潮的前提。

以上内容摘自外捕研究（Web3Caff Research）《机构金融基础设施研报：从 SWIFT×CCIP、Canton Network 到 DTCC，传统金融的 “上链” 之路为何绕开公链？全景式拆解其发展背景、案例解析、合规逻辑、潜在风险及未来展望》

text:
Subagents are the biggest cause of AI failures

In most harnesses:
1. Main agent writes a summary of what it knows
2. Subagent starts from that summary only, and makes assumptions
3. Subagent works and sends back a new summary of what it did

Same flaw as compaction: all summaries are lossy. This is how your assistant makes emails you never wanted, or purchases what you told it just to get the price of

So I tried something new: checkpoint agents

The initial agent has complete context of what needs to be done. And that input is already cached

Fork the session where it is. Send the fork ahead to do the task and it will do exactly what the main agent would have done; their context is identical

What is even better is when the fork finishes, the cache of the main agent is kept warm by the subagent (they share the same prefix)

I measured it on a 137k-token session with Opus 5.5:
→ Main agent does it on its own: 67 s, $0.38, context +8-17k
→ Checkpoint: 117 s, $0.68, context +2k
→ Classic subagent: 123 s, $0.57, context +4-5k

But here is what I found: avoiding large input is even more important than keeping cache. And most subagent tasks were done better either in series with retrieval, or split up to be parallel over fresh sessions from the start

I do not think there is a place for subagent delegation at all. There should either be a super-agent that orchestrates and does no work, or a long running agent that can retrieve from previous sessions, not a worker that completes tasks partially and delegates the rest to other workers

Don't design harnesses based on our assumptions of human behavior

This means ASTOCK's current trading heat and narrative strength have already overtaken the "infrastructure itself"—that's a fairly strong signal. Additionally, the flywheel of "product → users → external revenue → ASTOCK value" surpassing the platform token is only the first step.

To support an "unimaginably large" market cap, the product needs to:

Allow convenient buying and selling of real stocks with USDC on Arc.

Attract real traders, rather than relying solely on speculating on ASTOCK itself.

Generate fees from stock trading.

Have a portion of value flow back to ASTOCK.

So my view is: the current market cap lead only shows that heat is sufficient. The real large valuation space depends on whether it can evolve from a "fast-iterating small project" into a financial network with real users and sustained external revenue. Once stock trading volume picks up and revenue can continuously flow back to holders, the imagination space for market cap will open up. But based on current data, ASTOCK's own trading volume is still far larger than real stock trading volume, indicating this flywheel is still in its early stages.

Of course, this is just my personal view and does not constitute investment advice.

This opens up a much bigger product opportunity.

Allaire's interaction brought market attention to the project, but what really deserves a reassessment is the expansion of its product scope. Previously, AStock was primarily focused on bringing stock assets on-chain. Now, it wants to enable any issuer to integrate stock rewards, token tax distribution, and cross-chain liquidity into their own projects.

Here are some of my thoughts: I believe there are clear catalysts behind this ASTOCK rally.

Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire replied “Very cool” to AStock's post announcing the upcoming launch of Omni Launchpad. This interaction naturally draws a connection between Circle, Arc, and the tokenized stock ecosystem. After all, AStock is built on Arc, the financial infrastructure developed by Circle.

First, this was a public positive interaction from Circle's CEO, bringing the project additional attention and a degree of credibility. However, there is currently no evidence that AStock has received official support from Circle or entered into a formal partnership with it. What really deserves attention is the Omni Launchpad.

Let's first look at AStock's original business.

AStock aims to build a stock asset layer on Arc. Users deposit USDC on Arc, and the protocol uses cross-chain infrastructure to purchase the corresponding Robinhood Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain and place them in a reserve vault. It then issues the corresponding aStock tokens on Arc. In the reverse process, users burn their stock tokens, the reserve sells the corresponding assets, and USDC is returned to them.

This means users do not need to operate across two chains themselves or manually handle the cross-chain purchase and conversion of stock assets. Tokens such as aNVDA, aTSLA, and aSPY can be transferred and traded on Arc like ordinary ERC-20 tokens, and can also be integrated into other protocols. AStock's website previously displayed 29 available stock assets, with reserves and the corresponding Arc token supply available for cross-chain verification.

One important detail needs to be clarified: these tokens do not represent direct ownership of shares in companies such as NVIDIA or Tesla. Robinhood's official documentation explains that its Stock Tokens are tokenized debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited. They provide economic exposure to the corresponding assets but do not grant holders legal or beneficial ownership of the underlying companies, nor do they provide shareholder rights. There are also issuance and trading restrictions in regions including the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland.

Therefore, what AStock provides is on-chain exposure backed by Stock Tokens, not a traditional stock brokerage account available to users worldwide.

This is why Omni Launchpad is the key to AStock's business expansion.

AStock has announced that Omni Launchpad will launch across both Arc and Solana, with the goal of allowing a token to be issued and circulated across both ecosystems. The announced features include configurable trading taxes for developers, optional stock rewards for holders with the ability to select the corresponding stock, two-way transfers between Arc and Solana, and Ferry, which supports staking USDC or SOL.

This means AStock is moving beyond building around its own stock trading product and is beginning to offer token issuance and economic mechanisms to external projects.

The feature I find particularly interesting is the optional stock rewards.

Previously, if a project wanted to provide holders with rewards in another asset, it had to design its own conversion, distribution, and fund management mechanisms. AStock aims to turn this into an optional feature that can be configured at launch: project fees enter the distribution process, the corresponding stock asset is purchased, and rewards are distributed to holders according to predefined rules.

This changes the role of a Launchpad. It is no longer just a tool for helping projects issue tokens. It also allows projects to configure their own reward distribution and incentive mechanisms from the beginning.

The combination of Arc and Solana also makes practical sense. Arc is more closely connected to USDC, RWA, and on-chain financial infrastructure, while Solana has an established memecoin trading and launch ecosystem. If Omni can allow users from both ecosystems to participate in the same projects, AStock's potential user base and liquidity sources will no longer be limited to Arc.

However, the current announcement only confirms that product testing has been completed and that the launch is approaching. Actual cross-chain trading volume, the full details of Ferry's yield mechanism, and Omni's long-term revenue have yet to be demonstrated. These will need to be verified after launch.

Next, let's look at whether ASTOCK itself has a value-capture mechanism. I believe this is what distinguishes it from a simple stock tokenization project.

ASTOCK is more than just a platform governance token. According to the website's mechanism, the ASTOCK/USDC trading pool has a 4% fee structure, consisting of a 3% Swap Tax and a 1% Pool Fee. Part of the trading fees is periodically converted into stock assets and distributed to ASTOCK holders according to their holdings.

At the same time, AStock offers a stock rewards module for third-party tokens. Other projects on Arc can connect their own fee wallets, select the reward asset and distribution ratio, and let the system automatically purchase stocks and distribute them to the corresponding token holders. The official rules also specify that 5% of each such reward distribution goes into the ASTOCK reward pool.

This is important because demand for ASTOCK does not necessarily have to depend entirely on its own trading volume. If more third-party projects begin using AStock's stock rewards module, their fee activity could also become part of the AStock ecosystem.

The latest website data already shows some actual usage: approximately $61,704.76 in stock assets has been distributed to holders, around $5,336.02 in USDC entered the reward pool that day, and the most recent distribution involved 1,787 wallets.

In terms of burns, approximately 78.03M ASTOCK has been burned, representing 7.80% of total supply. The website also shows approximately $10,437.07 spent on buybacks and burns, corresponding to 11.44M ASTOCK.

These figures indicate that stock rewards and token burns are no longer purely roadmap concepts. Actual distributions and on-chain transactions have already taken place. In particular, the involvement of 1,787 wallets in the latest distribution is more meaningful than simply reporting cumulative trading volume.

However, I would not interpret stock distributions as fixed returns. The amount of rewards depends on actual trading activity and fee generation. If trading volume declines, distributions will naturally decrease. An increase in token burns also does not guarantee that the market price will rise.

So what exactly is the market betting on?

I believe the core thesis is that AStock could become a new type of Launchpad infrastructure: any project could issue tokens on Arc or Solana, choose stock assets as rewards for holders, and use cross-chain tools to expand its user base and liquidity. AStock would participate in this ecosystem through its own stock trading product, third-party reward modules, and ASTOCK fee mechanisms.

This offers a much bigger opportunity than simply launching a batch of stock-paired memecoins. Stocks would no longer serve only as trading pairs for individual tokens. They could also become reward assets distributed to holders as part of other projects' token economies.

If Omni successfully attracts more projects to adopt this model, AStock could evolve from a standalone product into an asset distribution infrastructure that other projects can integrate into their own systems.

Jeremy Allaire's interaction happened at an interesting time. On September 16, 2026, Circle officially opened the Arc mainnet, positioning it as infrastructure for financial markets, real-time movement of money, and the Agentic Economy. At launch, Circle announced that more than 100 applications, institutions, and ecosystem builders were involved.

AStock's product direction clearly aligns with Arc's focus on financial assets and USDC-based applications. Allaire's public interaction brought more attention to this alignment, but it should not be interpreted as evidence that Circle has decided to make AStock an official priority within its ecosystem.

Going forward, I will be watching several catalysts closely: whether Omni launches as planned and generates sustained issuance and trading activity across both Arc and Solana; whether third-party projects actually adopt the stock rewards module rather than distributions coming primarily from AStock itself; whether Ferry attracts meaningful USDC and SOL staking deposits; and whether stock rewards and ASTOCK burns continue growing alongside ecosystem activity.

Another important development is AStock's dependence on multiple underlying components, including Arc, Robinhood Stock Tokens, cross-chain messaging, and reserve vaults. Any liquidity, redemption, bridging, or regulatory issue affecting one of these components could disrupt the overall product experience.

My conclusion is that ASTOCK's fundamentals are moving in a stronger direction, and this development goes beyond simply adding another Launchpad. It is connecting stock asset trading, third-party reward distribution, and cross-chain token issuance into a broader product offering.

Jeremy Allaire's interaction is the attention catalyst, Omni Launchpad is the product catalyst, and the stock distributions and token burns already recorded on the website provide some evidence of actual usage.

But what will ultimately determine its valuation is whether Omni can attract external projects, external capital, and sustained demand for stock rewards.

If more projects become willing to integrate stock rewards into their own token economies, ASTOCK could evolve from a stock token protocol into infrastructure that other projects actively need.

What I really want to see is this: How many projects with no direct connection to AStock will eventually choose to route their fees into this stock rewards system? That will be the key indicator of whether AStock can build a genuine network effect.

My overall view: fundamentals are strengthening, but the short-term price is clearly overheated. This rally is being driven by both product expansion and external attention. The next thing to validate is Omni's actual adoption, rather than treating Jeremy's “Very cool” comment as a long-term fundamental catalyst in itself.

text: When researchers analyzed how Pegasus spyware infected iPhones without the user tapping anything, they found something wild. The attackers sent an iMessage with a fake GIF that targeted Apple's image decompression engine. The decompression math was so flexible that the exploit chained arithmetic operations together to construct a literal, functioning software CPU using over 70,000 segment commands that defined logical bit operations (AND, OR, XOR, XNOR, etc.) entirely inside the image parser. This created a small computer architecture with registers, a full 64-bit adder, and a comparator, running raw code before the phone even buzzed with a notification

text:
One ongoing frustration is the lack of effort I see being put towards near-term, achievable crash projects to do good with AI at a national scale, whether those efforts are by the AI labs or by policymakers & NGOs.

Some obvious ideas to explore suggested by the data we have so far: universal tutoring to support classroom learning, second opinions on healthcare, financial literacy/scam avoidance, and making government services easy to access.

These are hard problems, and I know because over the past 20 years I have worked extensively on building tutoring and financial literacy programs, which were always limited by existing technology. Now, real gains are likely achievable with AI, which should be a big deal. Yes, you would want to do careful design and studies before rolling things out. And yes, those efforts might fail. But, if done right, national programs could lead to big gains in public good for seemingly intractable problems. And they don't require AIs beyond current models to pull off.

text:
Nasdaq-100 forward returns after one-day drops of 6.25% or more, like today’s (NDX, Jan 1985 to Nov 2026, n=33 days).

Takeaways:

➤ 21 days later: average +5.2% vs +1.3% for any day. Index higher in 64% of cases vs 63%.

➤ 63 days later: average +4.9% vs +4.1% for any day. Index higher in 64% of cases vs 69%. By 3 months the edge is mostly gone.

➤ Further losses common: NDX fell another 10% or more within 63 days in 21 of 33 cases.

➤ In 1987 and 2020 a fast policy backstop ended the forced selling within two weeks. In 2000–01 and 2008 earnings and credit losses that policy couldn’t fix kept the index falling for months.

Today’s trigger was the midterms. Texas elected Hinojosa as governor on a promise to freeze data center permits, and voters elsewhere passed restrictions in 40 of 41 local data center ballot measures.

The obvious comparison is 2000. But the 2000 crash came from collapsing demand, while this comes from expected policy changes, and expectations can reverse.

The closest precedent is April 2025: NDX fell 6.1% on tariffs, Trump hit pause three sessions later, and NDX was up 30.5% after 63 days. Then one person caused the shock and could reverse it. Here expectations depend on a new governor and Congress, so a V-reversal is harder.

There is a flipside. The same Democratic wave that threatens the AI buildout also limits Trump’s room to escalate in Iran. A deal is barely priced. Lower oil would mean a less hawkish Fed, and lower rates help long-duration tech the most.

King of the Markets has officially concluded.

KotM was built to pilot and prove out the Reserve's liquidity thesis, and the results have surpassed all expectations. A more detailed breakdown of the data will be released this week, but for now, some important information regarding rewards.

1) A big part of this process is making sure the reward pool isn't being diluted by sybils and people who tried to game the system (wash traders and token ruggers) so we're taking the time to review all the data before distributing anything.

We've already begun filtering through transaction data to identify wash trading and accounts that attempted to artificially farm points. We want to make sure rewards go to legitimate traders and deployers, not those who tried to game the system.

2) In approximately 6.5 hours, the KotM page will update to show your trading and launchpad activity. You'll be asked to sign with your wallet to confirm where you'd like to receive your rewards and in which token. This is completely free, requires no gas, and takes about 5 seconds.

3) You'll have 120 hours (5 days) to complete this step. If you don't sign within that window, you will not be eligible to receive rewards. Once the 120 hours are up, we'll run one final filter and redistribute any unclaimed rewards from wallets that didn't sign among eligible wallets that did.

4) For those who traded through FOMO, unfortunately, FOMO doesn't make its wallet API public, which makes tracking your activity extremely difficult. We still want to make sure FOMO users aren't left out of rewards, so the best solution we have for now is to export your EVM private key from FOMO and import it into a compatible wallet.

From there, check the FOMO box and complete your payout confirmation, even if your stats show zero activity. We'll manually review these wallets over the coming days to make sure legitimate activity is accounted for.

Please only import your private key into a trusted wallet app. Never share it with anyone or enter it on the KotM website.

5) Once the final filtering and redistribution are complete, rewards will be airdropped directly to your specified wallet in your selected currency.

We appreciate everyone who participated in the pilot. The results have given us a lot of confidence in what we're building, and there's much more to come.

When Putin seized Crimea, both Europe and America were quite openly making calls, holding meetings, and sending signals to the Ukrainians who were in power at the time that there should be no escalation – let's just keep things friendly and leave things as they are for now. And we lost Crimea. After that, we lost part of Donbas. But the shooting in the east continued. There was no peace.

People think we were always helped. That is not true. Help started coming after the full-scale invasion, but that was after eight years of Russia occupying our territory. That is a long time to figure things out and understand that Putin has no intention of giving anything back to us.

At one point, some Europeans asked me: “Why do you think that if you withdraw from Donbas, he will go further?” And I answered: “Because at the beginning of the war, he wasn't seizing Donbas. He came to the capital. He seized parts of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions, Kherson itself, and Kharkiv region.” We have retaken a lot of territory, but he had seized different parts of our country. And now they want us to give them something because they are unable to seize it. We may have a smaller territory, less money, and fewer weapons, but we still have more dignity than many others. We will do everything we can to end this war, but it must end in a way that preserves our dignity.

From an interview with ZDF. (2/3)

I think the next generation of L1s should actively build first party apps instead of copying the playbook of earlier chains.

No one understands a chain’s technical advantages better than the team that built it. First party apps can showcase what is technically possible while proving the team is willing to put its money where its mouth is by building real products with real users. 

That traction becomes the wedge. Once other builders see real users and demand, it attracts more founders to build on the chain.

At this point, any chain copying the old founder acquisition playbook is fighting over the leftovers.

So what I am saying is L1s should pivot from trying to build a developer ecosystem to building real products that attract users. Almost nothing is under your control when you rely entirely on third party founders. Once they realize your chain has no users  they will do what is best for their company and move to one that does.

Your job as an L1 founder is to figure out how to get users first then founders will follow.

quoted_text:
King of the Markets has officially concluded.

KotM was built to pilot and prove out the Reserve's liquidity thesis, and the results have surpassed all expectations. A more detailed breakdown of the data will be released this week, but for now, some important information regarding rewards.

1) A big part of this process is making sure the reward pool isn't being diluted by sybils and people who tried to game the system (wash traders and token ruggers) so we're taking the time to review all the data before distributing anything.

We've already begun filtering through transaction data to identify wash trading and accounts that attempted to artificially farm points. We want to make sure rewards go to legitimate traders and deployers, not those who tried to game the system.

2) In approximately 6.5 hours, the KotM page will update to show your trading and launchpad activity. You'll be asked to sign with your wallet to confirm where you'd like to receive your rewards and in which token. This is completely free, requires no gas, and takes about 5 seconds.

3) You'll have 120 hours (5 days) to complete this step. If you don't sign within that window, you will not be eligible to receive rewards. Once the 120 hours are up, we'll run one final filter and redistribute any unclaimed rewards from wallets that didn't sign among eligible wallets that did.

4) For those who traded through FOMO, unfortunately, FOMO doesn't make its wallet API public, which makes tracking your activity extremely difficult. We still want to make sure FOMO users aren't left out of rewards, so the best solution we have for now is to export your EVM private key from FOMO and import it into a compatible wallet.

From there, check the FOMO box and complete your payout confirmation, even if your stats show zero activity. We'll manually review these wallets over the coming days to make sure legitimate activity is accounted for.

Please only import your private key into a trusted wallet app. Never share it with anyone or enter it on the KotM website.

5) Once the final filtering and redistribution are complete, rewards will be airdropped directly to your specified wallet in your selected currency.

We appreciate everyone who participated in the pilot. The results have given us a lot of confidence in what we're building, and there's much more to come.

Microsoft has disclosed a high-severity vulnerability in Windows Paint that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely without user interaction.

Tracked as CVE-2026-83844, the flaw stems from an out-of-bounds read that could compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of affected systems.

The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 8.1 and affects Microsoft Paint versions earlier than 11.2605.91.0. Microsoft has released a security fix, and administrators are urged to ensure Paint is updated.

There are currently no confirmed reports of active exploitation.

text:
For reference, this is what a chip/semi/memory cycle looks like:

1. Demand explodes.
2. Customers panic-order.
3. Chip companies raise prices.
4. Margins explode.
5. Everyone expands capacity.
6. New capacity arrives 12–36 months later.
7. Demand growth slows or customers digest inventory.
8. Prices fall.
9. Margins collapse.
10. Capex is cut.

Happened with computers, then gaming, then the internet (data centers), now AI.

text:
Still trading retail setups??

Bear flags. Triangles. Head and shoulders. Double tops.

You know the ones. 🤦‍♂️

They got taught to everyone for years… and once everyone knows the setup, the edge is gone…

That’s the bit most people miss.

An edge isn’t a shape on a chart.
It’s an inefficiency in the market that other people haven’t priced in yet.

When you trade a pattern that YouTube, Twitter and every paid Discord already found…
you’re not early.
You’re liquidity.

The breakout everyone is waiting for?
That’s where the other side gets paid.

Hell I used to chase this stuff aswell.
Felt smart drawing the lines.
Then I watched the same setups get hunted, stopped out, then run the other way.

Retail setups got obliterated years ago because the market adapted.
When too many people trade the same idea, it stops working.
Or worse… it starts working against you.

So what actually works??

You build around parameters and ideas that fit real inefficiencies.

Liquidity.
Order flow.
Who’s trapped.
Where stops are clustered.
Stuff that moves before the pretty pattern completes.

That’s where building your own AI money machine comes in.

Not so it can draw better triangles.
So it can hunt inefficiencies at a scale you can’t do by hand… and backtest whether your idea actually holds up before you put size on it.

Find your own setups.
Find your own edge.

And once you’ve got one…
you don’t tell people.

Because the second everyone else trades it, the edge dissipates.

That’s the game.

text:
Why do the people who actually fine-tune models on Hugging Face almost never get paid?

Not because their models suck. Not because nobody uses them.

Because the system is rigged against them the moment they hit "upload."

They spend months cleaning data, labeling thousands of examples, fighting catastrophic forgetting, building their own evals, and burning through A100s or H100s. Then they ship the weights, write a README, and post a tweet.

Hugging Face does its part: the model gets a page, downloads start rolling in, people fine-tune it further, cite it, run it.

And then… nothing.

Millions of downloads a month. Zero cents to the person who built it.

Look at the numbers. Models with 4–8 million downloads last month still say “This model isn’t deployed by any Inference Provider.” Cloud platforms only list a handful of hand-picked base models. Community fine-tunes almost never make the cut — no matter how popular they are.

Most of those downloads end up as 4-bit GGUFs running on someone’s 24GB consumer GPU. The real model — full precision, the larger MoE variants — never becomes a service anyone can reliably call. And when a platform *does* host it, they charge users per token at healthy margins and keep every dollar.

The weights are Apache-2.0 or MIT. Using them is legal. Building a business on top of someone else’s months of work is also legal. Paying the person who did the work is optional. So almost nobody does.

Right now there are only two paths:

Self-host and lose money until (if ever) you find users. Or beg a platform to list you — and still get nothing when they do.

In both cases, the person who supplies the GPUs collects the money. The person who built the model is invisible.

The open-source community has tried everything else. Restrictive licenses that kill adoption. Donation-based “support” that never covers real engineering. Big labs monetizing through enterprise sales and their own APIs — options that require sales teams and data centers most fine-tuners don’t have.

There is no seat at the table called “model maintainer.”

TrueOpen is building that seat.

It’s an open GPU network where inference runs under protocol rules instead of platform terms. You register your model and set your own maintenance fee. Anyone with GPUs can stake and serve it. Every call is verified (so nodes can’t quietly swap in a cheaper model or pad tokens). When verification passes, the protocol automatically splits the payment in the same transaction: the GPU node gets its service fee, the maintainer gets the fee *they* set, and the rest goes to the other roles.

No platform has to “agree” to list you. No monthly report you have to trust. No one can decide later that your share is now zero. The split is a rule, not a promise.

If you’ve spent months making a model clearly better than the base model for legal work, medical translation, a low-resource language, or a specific industry — and all you’ve gotten so far is downloads and likes — this is the missing piece.

We’re still early (beta, small node count, income depends on real usage). But the loop already works: register → serve → verify → settle. Every successful call splits by rule.

If you have a model with real download numbers that has never paid you a cent, or if you have GPUs and want to earn by serving community models, or if you’re building apps and tired of only having access to the same handful of hosted models — come look at what we’re building.

Follow the progress.  
Join the conversation.  
Reach out.

The work is already done. The models already exist. The only thing missing has been a way for the people who built them to actually get paid when they’re used.

We’re trying to fix that. Come see if it works. https://t.co/7CvWGaXRUt

text:
AI stocks getting absolutely crushed, bulls all dead, and meanwhile an independent report comes out giving a 6 month timeline to RSI and ASI shortly after. 

I genuinely don’t think people appreciate how enormous the NYC/SF divide has become.

In NYC, the conversation is about capex sustainability, corporate value capture, off-balance sheet leverage, lagging earnings revisions, and how the AI bubble is finally popping.

In SF, the conversation is about recursive self-improvement, super-intelligence, and whether the timelines in AI 2027 are too slow. 

These aren’t mere disagreements about valuation but rather completely different models of how the world works.

The economic bull case is simple in that if ASI makes cognitive labor radically cheaper and more scalable, 

then labs could capture a small fraction of an enormous expansion in economic output, 

with compute, energy, and deployment bottlenecks splitting the rest of the rents.

To be fair, NYC is very much winning the trade right now. 

But being right about the next quarter of price action and being right about the next decade of economic reality are two very different things.

Maybe NYC is right about the bubble and SF is right about the future. 

Those aren’t necessarily mutually exclusive.

I'm Sam, one of Anthropic's co-founders, and I lead much of our safety work. I'm going to have more to share on that work over the coming months.

I thought I'd start by sharing a few thoughts on the latest report from @METR_Evals.

The speed of progress in model capabilities is one of the most important questions in AI safety, and METR’s work here provides the public with an independent, external view into how this is happening inside Anthropic. I’ll talk more about some of the details below, but first some context for those new to this work.

How quickly AI progress is accelerating has many important safety implications, since it determines how quickly the risks from advanced models increase. But, because most research happens within the frontier labs, it’s difficult for external observers and policy makers to get a strong sense of what that rate is. We kicked off the process with METR that led to this report earlier in the year, in anticipation of progress continuing to accelerate.

For this report, we gave METR access to a range of sensitive internal data, including benchmark scores for unreleased models, estimates of how models are progressing, and interviews with our researchers. They had complete independence to form their own conclusions.

Many of their conclusions match my own. AI is speeding up our research, but it’s hard to say exactly how much. While they conclude AI can't yet make the most important contributions to model training on its own, they think the pace of development could, by default, accelerate further.

This work began well before and is separate from the embedded third-party evaluators that are part of our commitment to pacing the frontier, but it’s a good illustration of why we think evaluators are a good idea. The more access reviewers have, the clearer a picture they can form of the situation and the better-positioned they are to highlight situations like this one.

We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR’s work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn’t the right thing to do, both because it’s commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. That would make the risks METR is worried about worse. That’s a tradeoff. I think we made the right call, though we’re continuing to assess the pros and cons here.

In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic, including where we stand against our Responsible Scaling Policy, plus new steps we’re taking to strengthen our safety and security practices as AI keeps improving quickly.

hearing some chatter that anthropic is now lowering down to $1tn to get this IPO done. let me explain why this doesnt matter and its actually all over-

the entire existence of this company is based on a funding model that inherently has extreme asset liability mismatch. what that means is that just like the hyperscalers are diluting their equity fund capex, there is an expectation that anthropic will also have to do the same. ie it needs strong equity to perpetuate the scheme

but if you IPO at the wrong price (and dont get a pop which increasingly appears they wont be; spacex already below) then youre now in the death spiral that crypto investors should be very familiar with: its called the reflexivity trap of the confidence game. its the "ill bid FTT at $22 all day" or the "steady lads UST is $1" game, with all its lucid horrors. and here is the key insight- the confidence game exists at the service of the creditors. if there is no credit, there is simply no equity. and there is no credit, if there is no collateral

if the credit rating agencies are not going to give IG at $2tn, they are certaintly not going a better HY rating at $1tn. and there is no world in which anthropic can exist without credit because ~$1tn of commit, much of which is noncancellable, is a straight up negative equity pledge

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

美股历史上中期选举之后往往先跌后涨，并且有较大涨幅。所以最近每天我都在问mojo能不能抄底了。为了省事我直接让 @MojoAI_HQ 帮我做一个美股抄底的监控。

可以发送下面的prompt给mojo：

Build me a US equity bottom-signal monitor. Check every 30 minutes and notify me (in-app + push) only when the signal changes — never repeat the same signal.

Data: pull 200 daily bars each for SPY and QQQ, plus the current ^VIX price. Note QQQ is the Nasdaq-100 ETF — thresholds are on its price, not the Nasdaq index level.

Evaluate three signals in priority order:
1. Capitulation: VIX ≥ 35, AND SPY closed lower 3 consecutive sessions, AND the 3-day average volume > 1.2× the 20-day average
2. Deep washout: QQQ ≤ 640
3. Trend confirmation: SPY and QQQ both back above their 200-day MAs, AND VIX < 20

Include in the notification: SPY and QQQ last price and 200-day MA, VIX, and the 3-day volume ratio vs the 20-day average.

帮我建一个美股抄底信号监控，每 30 分钟检查一次，只在信号变化时通知我（应用内 + 推送），同一个信号不重复提醒。

数据：SPY 和 QQQ 各取 200 根日线，再读 ^VIX 现价。注意 QQQ 是纳指 100 的 ETF，阈值用它的价格，不是纳斯达克指数点位。

按优先级判断三个信号：
1. 投降式抛售：VIX ≥ 35，且 SPY 连续 3 个交易日收跌，且这 3 日平均成交量 > 20 日均量的 1.2 倍
2. 深度洗盘区：QQQ ≤ 640
3. 趋势确认：SPY 和 QQQ 都站上各自 200 日均线，且 VIX < 20

通知里带上 SPY、QQQ 的现价和 200 日均线、VIX，以及近 3 日量能相对 20 日均量的倍数。

I pulled data from 488 US election races from 2024 to now.

- JHK

🟢 Kalshi: 0.0282
🔵 Models: 0.0320

Some model outperformed Kalshi on some races (blue dots), and even on some categories (ex: JHK on 2026 senate), but overall Kalshi was way more accurate.

Kalshi's data also happen to be public and not locked behind paywalls. 

I'm sure the comparison would be even more damming if Nate Silver's 2026 forecasts were publicly acessible.

A departure from my usual gloating:

If you lost all your money today, I'm sorry that happened. However you must understand that it was deserved. It means you had critical leaks in your trading and you need to take a break. Days like this happen infrequently but they will continue to happen for entirety of your trading career. 

Being levered is reserved for only the specialist of situations, you should almost never leverage. Never allow yourself to be in the position of a forced seller.

If you're having dark thoughts, or feel like you've taken 10 steps backwards and want to do something drastic, please don't. Life is far longer and opportunities are abundant.

Do not trade anytime soon. Go back and reflect on what your leak was (risk management, sloppy order placement, etc.) and learn. You paid your tuition.

If you continue trading without being self critical you are not a trader you are a PROBLEM GAMBLER.

Investing, trading and the journey to becoming wealthy rarely happens overnight. The only way to become profitable is to become your own harshest critic.

text:
从前两天 $STRC 重回100我还是非常感慨的，从100拿到70经历全网归零的质疑和恐慌又重新修复信任爬回100， @saylor 又一次经历住了考验。

我的20W仓位一路只值14W，现在已经回到20而且开始每日印钞65刀了。

昨晚美股狂跌，但 $Strc 只跌了微不足道的0.4%，也让人印象深刻，所以从全网骂的Luna2.0到现在，到底发生了什么？🧐🧐

～～～～～

今天看朋友讨论 STRC，有人开玩笑说，随着 STRC 从月度派息、半月派息一路升级到每日派息，它越来越像当年的 Anchor 3.0 了。

熟悉上一轮牛市的老玩家应该都记得，Anchor 当年接近20%的 UST 存款利率有多诱人，最后又是怎么随着 LUNA/UST 的死亡螺旋一起崩盘的。

但我认为，STRC 和 Anchor 有一个本质区别，这也是 STRC 目前抗跌逻辑中最重要的一环。

第一，STRC 没有 UST 那样的刚性赎回机制。

UST 当年最大的问题，是当市场失去信心时，持有人可以通过兑换机制把抛售压力传导给 LUNA，进一步导致增发、暴跌、脱锚，最终形成无法阻止的死亡螺旋。

而 STRC 是 Strategy 发行的永久优先股，不是承诺随时按照1美元赎回的稳定币。

投资者想退出，通常只能在二级市场出售。

这意味着，即使大家恐慌性抛售 STRC，首先承受压力的是二级市场价格，而不是直接触发公司按面值兑付所有投资者的义务。

换句话说，STRC 可以跌价，但不容易被挤兑成 UST 式的死亡螺旋。

当然，这并不代表投资者不会亏钱。

第二，Strategy 现在拥有足够厚的美元现金缓冲。

根据10月29日披露的最新财报，截至10月25日：

公司美元储备及现金资产约50.7亿美元。
足以覆盖约3.4年的优先股股息及债务利息。
今年已回购约20.4亿美元的 STRC，平均回购价格约97.39美元。
目前 STRC 的年化股息率维持在12%。

这几个数字非常重要。

因为对于 STRC 持有人来说，最担心的并不是明天 BTC 跌10%，而是 Strategy 有没有能力持续支付股息。

现在公司手上有相当于3.4年支付需求的美元缓冲，意味着即使短期融资市场环境恶化，也不需要立刻依靠卖出 BTC 来支付股息。

同时，公司在 STRC 跌破100美元时主动回购，也给市场提供了一定的买盘支持。

所以，如果现在持有或者想买 STRC吃年化12%的红利，只需要重点关注一个指标就好了：

美元储备覆盖年限。 

目前是3.4年。未来如果不断下降，尤其跌破2年，就值得提高警惕。

STRC 的二级市场价格。 公司希望它维持在99至100美元附近。如果长期跌破95美元甚至90美元，说明市场对其信用风险或收益率要求发生了明显变化。

Strategy 的持续融资能力。 如果 BTC 进入长期熊市，MSTR 股票融资越来越困难，而优先股股息负担持续增加，那么现在看起来很厚的现金储备也会逐渐被消耗。

那么，STRC 到底值得买吗？

我的观点是：

如果你想获得美元现金流，又能够承受一定的价格波动和 Strategy 的信用风险，STRC 在当前12%的年化股息水平下，确实值得研究。

但千万不要把它理解成12%年化的美元稳定币，更不能把它当成银行存款。

因为 STRC 的12%不是永久锁定的，股息可以调整，股价也可能跌破面值。高收益对应的，始终是高于普通美元现金工具的风险。

最后说一个我认为最重要的判断：

对于 STRC，真正值得关注的不是 BTC 明天涨跌多少，而是 Strategy 在一轮持续3至5年的 BTC 熊市中，能否依然保持足够的美元流动性，以及持续获得资本市场融资的能力。

只要这两个条件仍然成立，STRC 的股息支付就有较强的支撑。

反过来，一旦美元覆盖年限持续下降、融资渠道收紧，即使每天还在正常派息，也值得重新评估风险。

STRC 最大的优势不是12%的收益率，而是它试图用传统优先股的资本结构，把 BTC 的高波动性与投资者的美元现金流需求隔离开。

至于这种隔离到底能经受多长时间的熊市考验，才是这场实验最值得观察的地方。

Chainalysis: Names, Usernames, Password Hashes, and Valid Tokens of All Users Were Exposed; Some Plaintext Passwords Also Leaked  

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed in an updated security incident notice that the names, usernames, password hashes, and valid authentication tokens of all users had been exposed to the attacker, and that some customers’ plaintext passwords were also leaked through a separate attack method. After detecting abnormal activity, the company suspended KYT transaction monitoring, address screening, and login services, and required all users to reset their passwords and rotate API keys where necessary.  

Previously, on October 30, Chainalysis first disclosed that it had been breached by a hacker using offensive AI agent technology; at that time it only confirmed that certain customer identity information had been accessed and said it had found no evidence that passwords or session tokens had been leaked.

quoted_text:
We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.

Vault particles are a longstanding mystery. They are barrel-shaped objects, among the largest protein structures found in our cells. They were first discovered by Leonard Rome and Nancy Kedersha in 1986, but their function remains unknown.

With Claude, we’ve found results that might bring us closer to solving that mystery.

Until now, vaults were only known in the cells of complex things like animals and plants. We have shown that similar proteins from bacteria (and the viruses that infect them) can also assemble into vaults. Finding the structures in these simpler forms of life may make it easier to investigate their function in our own cells.

For our life sciences team, the project was also a demonstration of the potential (and the limitations) of using AI to accelerate science.

In our full piece, we discuss how Claude was able to dramatically speed up some stages—manually determining the vault particle’s structure would have taken weeks to months of painstaking work, but here it took days. We also discuss how Claude made some simple mistakes along the way, and how we collaborated with our machine learning researchers to address them.

Read more: https://t.co/KowVVCSPp8

text:
美股崩盘启示录：马斯克流血、巴菲特封神与 K 型分化

11 月 5 日美股崩了，是 2008 年以来最糟糕的 11 月。标普 500 重挫 4.36%，纳斯达克跌 5.52%，单日蒸发 3 万亿美元市值。

这场暴跌里，没有人比马斯克流更多的血。

特斯拉 11 月 5 日单日暴跌 11%，此前一天已经跌了 3.3%。SpaceX 股价暴跌 9%，跌破 IPO 发行价 135 美元。马斯克个人净资产在这轮崩盘当日蒸发了约 740 亿美元。

民主党胜利带来的数据中心禁令威胁，直接打击他最核心的资产，特斯拉的 AI 和自动驾驶叙事，以及 SpaceX 正在规划的太空数据中心计划。

同一时间，伯克希尔·哈撒韦 A 类股创下历史新高 821,931 美元，在 AI 股崩盘的日子里，这只「最无聊的股票」成了全市场最受追捧的标的。

所有人都在争论 AI 是不是泡沫，对冲基金被迫在最差的时间点卖出最好的资产，

而巴菲特（虽然现在是继任者 Greg Abel 在掌舵）坐在一座现金山上，等着捡便宜。

资金从科技股涌入伯克希尔，把它当成反 AI 交易的最佳载体。

这种趋势更像是典型的“K型经济”：

牛津经济研究院的数据显示，AI 确实带来了超过 7%的家庭财富增长，但高度集中在少数人手中。2026 年 Q1 最刺眼的一组数据：AI 相关经济体增长 31%，非 AI 经济体增长 0.1%。

AI 的回报最终流向三类人：拥有算力的人、拥有数据的人、拥有模型的人。其他所有人，AI 则是是成本项。

AI 股被抛售，因为市场意识到 AI 的增长可能被政策阻断，而且这种增长本身也没有惠及更广泛的经济。

防御性消费股逆势上涨，因为无论 AI 故事怎么讲，人总要吃饭，而且越来越多的人只买得起更便宜的东西。

聪明钱正在为「AI 没有拯救所有人」的世界定价。

text: When I visited Boom last week, one of the things that struck me is that they've become the most AI-pilled hardware company I know.  With AI coding, every hardware engineer is now a software engineer.
author: harjtaggar
quoted_text:
12 years ago I founded Boom, as a software engineer doing hardware for the first time. I’m probably the least handy founder in hard tech. My 12 y/o son does my soldering and 3D printing for home projects, and I’ve struggled with imposter syndrome the whole way through. What business does a software guy have building supersonic jets and turbines?

More than a decade in, the most insane realization is that software is the key to reaccelerating hardware engineering. But in a way that I don’t think is widely understood or implemented, even in the burgeoning hard tech community. 

Most hardware engineering is actually software engineering in disguise. It’s spreadsheet “code,” engineering calculations done as one-offs. Eg wing structural loads in, spar sizing design out. Thermal loads in, air conditioning system sizing out. 

Everything is a calculation, and calculation is software. But these calculations are done essentially by hand, as if we are doing arithmetic but have not yet discovered algebra. 

Hardware engineers have baby software, built in spreadsheets, the kind of crappy software I wrote as a kid before I understood architecture, unit tests, APIs, version control, and everything else that makes modern software good. 

Our airplanes and engines are built with the software sophistication of a script kiddie.

So what we tell our engineers: don’t design the hardware, design the *algorithm* for designing the hardware. And take the algorithm seriously—as an algorithm and as a first-class engineered software system. 

Never design a piece of hardware, such that you couldn’t redesign it tomorrow with a different set of assumptions. 

This all sounds obvious, yet our experience at Boom is that it changes everything. 

Ten years ago we couldn’t afford to build much software. We had a small team—and there were few software engineers with the curiosity, brilliance, and vision required to learn hardware engineering. 

But now AI changes the equation. Now everyone can code. The software engineers define the architecture. The hardware people bring the physics and engineering know-how. 

We have a turbomachinery design tool that lets one engineer do in realtime what previously took 100 engineers six months. Another tool auto-generates 65% of entire aircraft structure. I’m sure we’ll figure out the other 35% too. Eventually these should not be multiple tools, but one integrated physics model of a complete vehicle, airframe and powertrain. 

The results speak for themselves. A boomless supersonic airplane built by 50. A full scale supersonic turbine made by 150. And with this approach, I don’t think we’ll need that many more people to build and certify a supersonic airliner. 

You don’t need a big team to build big things—not when everyone on the team is a software engineer.

text:
The security protecting our assets today might not be enough forever.

Quantum computing is one development that could eventually challenge some of the cryptography blockchains rely on. That’s why preparing for the future means building systems that can adapt as security needs change.

@Starknet decided to change things and they caught my attention. 

Starknet is an Ethereum Layer 2 that uses STARK proofs to verify computations efficiently. Its proving system relies on hash-based cryptography rather than the elliptic-curve mathematics targeted by Shor’s quantum algorithm.

But its approach goes beyond proofs.

➝ Programmable accounts make upgrades more flexible.

Starknet accounts are smart contracts, meaning developers can customise how transactions are verified. This creates a way to introduce new signature methods without necessarily requiring a network-wide upgrade.

➝ Post-quantum signing has been tested.

An experimental Falcon-512 account implementation by OpenZeppelin has completed a successful mainnet transaction. It’s meaningful progress, but the implementation remains experimental and unaudited, with more work needed before wider adoption.

➝ There’s still an Ethereum dependency.

As a Layer 2, Starknet relies on parts of Ethereum’s security infrastructure. Some cryptographic changes will therefore depend on Ethereum’s own upgrades.

That’s also why StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation are exploring an independent Starknet Layer 1. The idea is still under research, not an approved migration.

Starknet has set a 2027 target for full post-quantum security, but the work isn’t finished yet.

What stands out is the focus on cryptographic agility: making it easier to adapt security as technology evolves.

Preparing for a threat isn’t the same as being fully protected against it. Starknet has made progress, but there are still important steps ahead.

You can follow the research and updates through Starknet’s Quantum Hub:

https://t.co/LQggoh9Xk9

text:
God thinks. God speaks. The world exists.
The Torah, the Gospel of John and the Qur’an all describe creation through divine word or command. An Egyptian stone carved roughly 2,700 years ago offers a striking parallel.

And the king who commissioned it said he was preserving something older.

The Shabaka Stone.

Around 700 BCE, the Kushite pharaoh Shabaka ordered a sacred text carved into stone. According to its inscription, he had found a worm-eaten “work of the ancestors” in Ptah’s temple.

His response was an act of reverence: restore their words, preserve their wisdom and give their legacy a lasting home.

What did he consider so important?

An account in which Ptah creates through his heart and tongue. The heart conceives; the tongue commands. Divine thought becomes expression, and the world takes shape.

Now consider:
• Torah, Genesis 1:3: “God said, ‘Let there be light’; and there was light.”
• Gospel of John 1:1–3: “In the beginning was the Word”—through whom all things were made.
• Qur’an 36:82: God commands “Be,” and it is.

Creation through the divine word runs through all these accounts.

The linked lecture takes the comparison further: its speakers connect the primordial waters of Nun, divine speech and the Big Bang through the imagery of waves/wavelengths. Their interpretation invites a question: how might ancient creation stories speak to our modern fascination with vibration, origins and the unity of nature?

Even “universe” and “verse” share the Latin root meaning “to turn.” “Universe” means combined into one whole; read poetically as “one verse,” it becomes an evocative image of existence unfolding through a divine utterance.

For Shabaka, preserving this teaching meant honouring the ancestors whose knowledge he had inherited.

Then history delivered a brutal irony.

The stone was later reused as a millstone. Grinding grain erased much of the inscription intended to endure.

A king saved his ancestors’ words from worms—only for later generations to grind them away.

Yet enough survived to make us pause over an extraordinary idea:

A world spoken into being.
